Delete returns early on Storage NotFound and leaves stale legacy copies — Skipping `d.Legacy.Delete` on NotFound leaves stale legacy copies that can resurface if reads fall back to legacy storage. Only short-circuit non-NotFound errors so legacy cleanup still runs when storage reports NotFound.

Delete sets context logger to d.Log instead of log — Passing the bare `d.Log` loses the name/kind/method fields for `klog.FromContext` calls inside `d.Storage.Delete`. Pass the just-built `log` to `klog.NewContext` like every other mode-3 method.

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Watch broadcaster starts after search index, dropping writes during index build — Writes made during the index build are permanently missing for Watch clients because the snapshot is taken after those events occur. Move `initWatcher` before `search.init` so it captures the earlier resource version.

NewResourceServer leaks watchers when Init fails — The search watcher and backend poller started by `search.init` keep running forever after the error return. Call `s.Stop(ctx)` before returning nil to cancel them.

Concurrent BuildIndex calls can overwrite cached index and drop events — A later cache assignment can hide an index that already received events, making those writes invisible in results. Reuse a single in-flight build per key so `handleEvent` and the cache always reference the same index.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Federated rules not marked immutable in useAllAlertRuleAbilities — Federated rules from Mimir source_tenants become editable and deletable, which can corrupt externally managed alert state. Reapply the isFederatedRuleGroup check by overriding Update, Delete, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently to NotSupported.

Dead Silence menu item when rulerRule is missing — The Silence item renders but its drawer never opens because RuleActionsButtons requires a Grafana rulerRule. Hide the item when rulerRule is unavailable, or wire the drawer to work from promRule alone.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Abstract getShortcut() breaks binary compatibility for existing grant factories — Pre-existing grant factories compiled against older Keycloak versions will throw `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()`, breaking all access-token issuance. Make `getShortcut()` a `default` method so existing providers remain compatible.

isAccessTokenId matcher never verifies grant shortcut — The matcher never rejects a non-matching grant shortcut because `substring(3, 5)` reads the wrong indexes and the condition is inverted, so it only validates the UUID part. Use `substring(4, 6)` and return false when it does not equal `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Client-credentials access tokens are encoded with grant type 'na' instead of 'cc' — Tokens minted for this grant type carry `na` instead of `cc` because `ClientCredentialsGrantType.process` never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on `clientSessionCtx`. Set it to `OAuth2Constants.CLIENT_CREDENTIALS` before calling token generation.

Reader thread is not joined before assertion — A reader exception raised after the deletion loop can be appended after the assertion, letting the test pass despite the NPE regression. Join the reader thread before calling `assertThat` so every `caughtExceptions` entry is visible.

getSubGroupsCount returns null when group is concurrently deleted — A concurrent delete makes `getSubGroupsCount()` return null, violating the `GroupModel` contract and leaking null into `GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount`. Return `0L` for a missing model instead of null.

PropertyResourceBundle decodes UTF-8 message files as ISO-8859-1 — Non-Latin translations are read as mojibake, so `verifySafeHtml` operates on corrupted strings and its `Illegal HTML` output is garbled for those locales. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`, including the English bundle nearby.

santizeAnchors compares translation and English anchors by position — A translation that reorders two links is reported as `Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string` and fails the build even though the anchors are unchanged. Match each translation anchor against the set of English anchors rather than requiring identical order.

totpStep1 contains Italian text instead of Lithuanian — Lithuanian-locale users see Italian instructions in the OTP setup flow. Replace `totpStep1` with the correct Lithuanian translation of `Install one of the following applications on your mobile:`.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties:71-71`

Use i18next {{n}} interpolation for error-invalid-multivalued-size — The single-brace placeholders and the Java `{2,choice,...}` pattern are not interpolated, so `error-invalid-multivalued-size` renders as literal `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` text when shown via `setUserProfileServerError`. Revert to `{{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}}` or use real i18next pluralization.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties:188-188`

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: getClientsWithPermission returns 'Clients' instead of actual client IDs — Because individual client resources are created without a resource type, `findByType` only matches the "all-clients" resource, so the method returns literal names instead of client IDs and `AvailableRoleMappingResource` can NPE on `realm.getClientById("Clients")`. Set the type on individual client resources, as V1 `ClientPermissions.initialize` does with `setType("Client")`, or iterate `realm.getClientsStream()` as in the improved code.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Base theme login-password.ftl missing passkey conditional UI include — Realms using the base theme silently lose passkey re-authentication because this template still renders only the password field. Add the same `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />` include here as in `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/login-password.ftl`.

Login-cache invalidation skipped when original IDP model is organization-aware — The wrapped model returned by getById() can report disabled when the IDP's organization is disabled, so the early return skips invalidation for changes like hideOnLogin or linkOnly and a stale entry may later appear on the login page. Compare against the raw delegate via idpDelegate.getById(original.getInternalId()) so both sides use the same eligibility.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Table widgets render empty with use-table-widget-visualization flag — This branch discards `result.data` and `result.meta`, so every table widget renders empty for orgs with the flag enabled. Pass `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the real columns into `TableWidgetVisualization`.

zip error IDs with nodestore values misaligns missing entries — Missing or reordered nodestore entries will attach the wrong title, message, and timestamp, and trailing errors get dropped entirely. Look up each generated `node_id` in the returned dict instead of zipping `events.values()`.

Zero-valued age or timestamp bypasses mutual-exclusion validation — A `0` age or timestamp is treated as absent, so validation is skipped when the other field is also present. Use membership checks like `"age" in self.initial_data` so zero-valued fields still raise the error.

Error timestamps are not converted to replay-relative time — The comparison is always false because error timestamps are absolute epoch seconds while breadcrumb timestamps are replay-relative, so errors are appended after all breadcrumbs instead of interleaved. Convert error timestamps to replay-relative offsets before comparing.

Assemble analytics event recorded before feature gate and schema validation — Requests that fail the feature gate or schema validation still increment the assemble metric, over-counting actual assemblies. Move the `analytics.record` call after those checks succeed.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Negative flusher_processes results in zero flusher processes — A negative value makes `num_processes` negative, `range(num_processes)` empty, and zero flusher processes are spawned, leaving segments unflushed. Clamp it with `min=1` on the option or `max(1, ...)` when computing `num_processes`.

Subset shard count inflates per-shard cap and exceeds global flush limit — The per-shard cap becomes a subset fraction of the total shard count, so a flush can exceed `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` by up to `num_processes`× and `any_shard_at_limit` trips less often, weakening backpressure. Compute the cap against the total shard count instead of the subset size.

Flusher processes not terminated when join deadline is exhausted — When the deadline is consumed, remaining processes are left running indefinitely. Remove the early `break` so `process.terminate()` runs for every flusher process regardless of `remaining_time`.

Redis cluster memory query repeated per sub-buffer in submit — `iter_cluster_memory_usage` returns whole-cluster INFO, so repeating it per sub-buffer just repeats the same full-cluster query with scaled values. Fetch `get_memory_info()` once from one buffer and reuse that list.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import time — All instances built via `from_integration` will share the module import time, since the default is evaluated once at class definition. Set `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own creation time.

OAuth state uses deterministic pipeline signature, enabling CSRF — A deterministic state provides no CSRF protection: an attacker can precompute it and inject their own authorization code into a victim's active pipeline. Generate a per-session token with `secrets.token_hex()`, bind it via `pipeline.bind_state("state", ...)`, and validate with `pipeline.fetch_state("state")` on return, as `OAuth2LoginView` and `OAuth2CallbackView` already do.

KeyError when GitHub integration metadata lacks sender — Integrations without `sender` exist and crash this path with a 500. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and return `error(...)` when the login is absent instead of indexing directly.

GitHub sender validation is skipped when Integration row does not exist — When the Integration row does not exist, the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch returns `pipeline.next_step()` before this validation, so the user match is never enforced if the webhook loses the race against the redirect. Move the sender check before that early return, or enforce it in `build_integration` before the integration is created.

get_user_info call can raise unhandled exceptions during OAuth — `get_user_info` can raise on 401/403/5xx via `raise_for_status()` and on invalid JSON via `resp.json()`, surfacing as an unhandled 500 rather than the user-facing error page. Wrap the call in try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is abstract but declares a `pass` body — Any detector typed `metric_alert_fire` now fails at construction because `Detector.detector_handler` cannot instantiate this abstract subclass. Implement `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, or restore a concrete `evaluate()` stub instead of `pass`.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Dereference of possibly-undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar throws — `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, so every Google Meet booking without a destination calendar throws a TypeError and aborts event creation. Add optional chaining before `.integration`, matching the previous `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`.

Calendar references lose externalCalendarId for non-credential destinations — `createEvent` only sets `result.externalId` when passed a third argument, which only the `destination.credentialId` branch does, so references from the type-based and no-destination branches lose `externalCalendarId` and cannot be matched later. Fall back to the matching entry in `evt.destinationCalendar` for `result.externalId`.

Video credentialId is dropped when creating booking references — `createMeeting` returns a video `credentialId`, but this branch hardcodes `undefined`, and cancellation only calls `deleteMeeting` when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so Zoom/Webex/Daily meetings are never deleted. Use `result.credentialId` in the non-calendar branch too.

Collective team destination calendars dropped when organizer has none — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when both the organizer and event type have no destination calendar, discarding the co-hosts' calendars, which is the bug this PR targets. Build `evt.destinationCalendar` as `[...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]` instead of optional-chained `push`.

Fallback never matches, passing undefined calendarId to events.update — The fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so its predicate can never match and `calendarId` reaches `calendar.events.update` as `undefined`, failing updates for references lacking `externalCalendarId`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` as the fallback, as before.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`

updateLocation drops calendar credential and external IDs from references — `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns no `externalId` or `credentialId`, so `updateLocation` persists references with both fields `undefined` and later updates and cancellations cannot resolve the right calendar. Fall back to the matching entry in `booking.references` when `result` lacks them, as the previous code took these from `evt.destinationCalendar`.

Recurring calendar deletion sweep repeats for each booking reference — The sweep is nested in the new `bookingCalendarReference` loop but does not depend on `reference`, so a booking with N references issues N× the identical `calendar.deleteEvent` calls and duplicates in `apiDeletes`. Run the sweep only once, not per reference.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team admins rejected because admin/owner checks are combined with && — Since `isTeamAdmin` already matches ADMIN or OWNER, the `&&` with `isTeamOwner` rejects admins who are not owners. Use `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`, so team admins can add guests.

addGuests allows adding guests to cancelled or rejected bookings — Without a `booking.status` check, a cancelled or rejected booking gets new attendees and a CONFIRMED invite, resurrecting it in every calendar. Reject `CANCELLED` and `REJECTED` bookings before adding guests.

Guest email blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive — Because `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is not, changing the casing bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. Lowercase both sides as in checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts, and normalize the attendee duplicate comparison too.

Attendees can append guests to someone else's booking — The `isAttendee` clause lets any attendee append arbitrary addresses to someone else's booking, sending invites and branded emails as the organizer. Restrict this mutation to `isOrganizer` or `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, or require organizer confirmation.

Add guests action bypasses disableGuests and seatsPerTimeSlot — Guests can be added to event types with `disableGuests` or `seatsPerTimeSlot`, bypassing those constraints and creating seatless `Attendee` rows. Guard both the `add_members` action and `addGuestsHandler` against both fields.

Non-atomic duplicate attendee check allows concurrent duplicate guests — The `booking.attendees.some` check and `createMany` are not atomic, so concurrent calls insert duplicate attendee rows. Run the check and insert in a transaction with a unique index on (bookingId, email), or lock per booking.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests — Passing raw `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends a second full confirmation to addresses already filtered out of `uniqueGuests`. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

Deduplicate guest emails inside the addGuests request payload — `uniqueGuests` never dedupes against itself, so repeated emails in one payload are inserted twice by `createMany` and get two invites. Dedupe `guests` through a `Set` before filtering.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: App metadata lookup uses public slug instead of metadata key, causing 404 — `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by directory name while `app.slug` holds the public slug, so most apps resolve to `undefined` and return 404, breaking credential sync. Look up the entry by `dirName` (selected alongside `slug`) instead.

Refresh response without refresh_token overwrites stored token with placeholder — When the response omits `refresh_token`, this writes the literal `"refresh_token"` over the stored credential; for Office 365 (optional `refresh_token` in `refreshTokenResponseSchema`) it is persisted and permanently breaks later refreshes with `invalid_grant`. Keep the caller's existing refresh token instead of injecting a placeholder.

Refresh token wrapper stored as credential key breaks Google auth — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `SafeParseSuccess` wrapper, so storing it as the credential key makes `googleCredentialSchema.parse` fail in `googleAuth` on the next read and breaks Google Calendar after the first refresh. Persist `key.data` instead.

Sync path returns raw fetch Response instead of parsed token JSON — Callers like `googlecalendar`, `hubspot`, `zoho-bigin`, and `zohocrm` expect provider-native token shapes, so returning the raw `Response` makes them no-op, crash, or overwrite the stored credential in shared mode. Return `await response.json()` or normalize each caller.

refreshOAuthTokens receives credentialId instead of owning user id — `refreshOAuthTokens` is passed `credentialId` as its `userId`, so the sync endpoint fetches another user's tokens or none and persists them onto this credential. Pass the credential's `userId` instead.

Connection is built with stale access token after refresh — The `jsforce.Connection` is built right after refresh from the pre-refresh `credentialKey.access_token`, so an expired token still fails despite the fresh one being saved. Use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and the refreshed `instance_url` when constructing it.

Salesforce token refresh validates via statusText instead of response.ok — `statusText` is empty for HTTP/2 and for servers omitting a reason phrase, so a valid 200 response throws `HttpError` and every Salesforce calendar operation fails. Check `response.ok` and read the body for the error message.

Salesforce client creation always refreshes token regardless of expiry — `getClient` runs on every constructor call, so each booking and calendar fetch now triggers a Salesforce token round trip and a `prisma.credential.update` write. Only refresh when the stored token is actually expired.

Webhook secret compared with timing-unsafe string inequality — The strict inequality short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret prefix through timing on this unauthenticated endpoint. Compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers after confirming the header is a string.

Race condition can create duplicate app credentials — Without a transaction or a unique constraint on userId+appId, concurrent webhook deliveries both `create`, leaving duplicate credentials where `findFirst` returns an arbitrary stale row. Add a unique constraint and `upsert`, or wrap the check-and-write in a serializable transaction.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Do not increment retryCount when SMS sending is locked — `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` when sending is locked, and `checkSMSRateLimit` sets that state automatically once the monthly limit is hit, so a temporarily locked user permanently loses all reminders after two cron runs. Only increment `retryCount` for genuine provider errors and skip when sending is locked.

SMS cleanup deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders with retryCount > 1 — Without a `method` filter this SMS cron hard-deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP `WorkflowReminder` rows whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. Scope the branch with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` so only SMS reminders can be deleted, matching `scheduleWhatsappReminders.ts`.

Unguarded retryCount update in catch can abort reminder batch — If `prisma.workflowReminder.update` throws — say P2025 after the new `deleteMany` removed the row — the exception escapes the loop and skips every remaining reminder in the batch. Wrap the increment in its own try/catch or use `updateMany` so error handling cannot abort the batch.

Missing index on WorkflowReminder retryCount causes cron full scan — No index supports `retryCount`, per `schema.prisma`, so this `deleteMany` full-scans the multi-million-row `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron run. Add an index on `retryCount` or on `(method, retryCount)` in the migration.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup-code login bypasses password when TOTP code is supplied — A request with a valid backup code and any `totpCode` logs in without the password, so a copied backup code alone unlocks the account. Verify the password unconditionally in the backup-code path before accepting the code.

Backup code comparison is case-sensitive, rejecting uppercase codes — Codes are stored as lowercase hex but `indexOf` matches them case-sensitively, so a user typing uppercase codes gets `IncorrectBackupCode` and is locked out. Normalize both sides with `toLowerCase()` before comparing, and apply the same fix in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`.

Backup code redemption has a non-atomic read-modify-write — Two parallel requests with the same code both pass `indexOf` and both authenticate, and concurrent redemptions of different codes can overwrite each other, breaking the single-use guarantee. Consume the code with an atomic conditional update, such as `prisma.user.updateMany` guarded by the original `backupCodes`, and fail when the count is not one.

resetState not called when modal is dismissed via X, Escape or backdrop — Closing the dialog with X, Escape, or the backdrop leaves `step` at `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening shows the previous codes with no Cancel button to escape. Call `resetState` from the dialog's open/close handler, not only from the footer buttons.

2FA backup-code dismissal skips onEnable and leaves stale step — Once the enable request succeeds, dismissing the dialog never calls `onEnable`, so the security page still shows 2FA as disabled, and the stale backup-codes step reappears on reopen. Call `onEnable` and `resetState` on dialog dismissal after the request succeeds.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: Deleted caching tests leave authorization/filter caching unverified — Without these tests, nothing asserts that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` cache their results, so a regression that recomputes conditions on every call would pass the suite. Restore the two caching assertions using the new `Prisma.sql` expectations.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Raw HTML cook method bypasses sanitization for imported feed content — Because `cook_methods[:raw_html]` returns `raw` untouched, third-party HTML from `TopicEmbed.import` reaches the page unsanitized, letting `<script>` or `onerror` run in the Discourse origin. Sanitize the imported HTML with a tag, attribute, and scheme allowlist before storing it, rather than relying on the cook bypass.

Invalid `end if` in embed/best template causes SyntaxError — ERB compiles the whole view into one method, so `<%- end if %>` leaves it unbalanced and every render of `embed/best` raises a SyntaxError, including the empty-topic branch. Change it to `<%- end %>`.

nil feed content raises NoMethodError and aborts the poll — `i.content` is nil for items that only carry `<description>`, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborts the `each` loop, and skips all remaining items with no retry. Read the body defensively from `i.content` or `i.description` and skip blank items.

add_column with default rewrites posts and blocks access on PostgreSQL — On PostgreSQL before 11 the default and NOT NULL force a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads and writes to posts for the whole migration. Add `cook_method` nullable without a default, backfill in batches, then set the default and NOT NULL afterward.

Unguarded embed.post causes NoMethodError for orphaned topic embeds — A `topic_embeds` row outlives hard-deleted posts, so `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises NoMethodError, aborting the `rss.items` loop in `Jobs::PollFeed` and leaving all later items unimported. Return early when `post.blank?` or delete the stale embed.

Feed poll runs inline for every distinct embed URL retrieval — `perform_retrieve` pays the full O(feed items) poll inline for every distinct `embed_url`, since the `retrieved:` throttle is per URL and `feed_key` is unused. Enqueue the poll as its own throttled job instead of running it inline per request.

Remote embed fetch lacks timeouts and size cap — A slow remote response blocks the worker indefinitely and an oversized body is loaded entirely into memory by `open(url).read`, reachable from the embed endpoint. Pass explicit `open_timeout` and `read_timeout` and cap the bytes read.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Migration dereferences nil PG rows for missing site settings — The migration aborts with `NoMethodError` whenever no matching row exists, which is the normal case for `embed_category` and blocks the upgrade. Guard both lookups with a `cmd_tuples` check like the block below already does.

SQL injection in embeddable_hosts migration via string interpolation — A stored host containing an apostrophe crashes the migration, and other SQL fragments are executed with migration privileges. Pass the value through `connection.quote` instead of interpolating it.

Migrated embeddable hosts keep URL scheme and never match — Values stored with `http://` bypass the model's `before_validation` normalization, so `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` never matches the scheme-free `uri.host` and embedding silently stops working. Strip the scheme and path before inserting, or route the insert through the model.

Missing embeddable host causes NoMethodError in update and destroy — A stale or crafted id raises `NoMethodError` and returns a 500 instead of a JSON error. Raise `Discourse::NotFound` unless the `EmbeddableHost` lookup returns a record before calling `save_host` or `destroy`.

before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil — A request that omits `host` raises `NoMethodError` in this callback and 500s before `validates_format_of` can report the field error. Skip the `sub!` calls when `host` is blank so validation handles it.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Duplicate OptimizedImage.downsize breaks 5-argument emoji call — The 4-argument `downsize` at line 149 shadows the 5-argument version, so `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` calling it with 5 arguments will raise `ArgumentError` and custom emoji stop being downsized. Remove the dead definition and convert the emoji caller to a single `"100x100"` argument.

Animated GIF form uploads are downscaled to a static frame — `allow_animation` never matches because `downsize_instructions` tests the extensionless tempfile path, so animated GIFs collapse to a static frame. Pass the original `filename` into the downsize call as `app/models/upload.rb` already does.

Upload size validation ignores admin-configured max size settings — Hardcoding 10MB drops the `max_<type>_size_kb` lookup, so client-side validation no longer honors admin limits and `utilities-test.js.es6:52` can no longer trigger `file_too_large`. Keep the `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup.

Oversized images not rejected after failed downsize attempts — A file still oversized after 5 passes is only rejected later by `Validators::UploadValidator#maximum_image_file_size`, wasting up to 5 conversions before the user sees an error. Derive the scale from `tempfile.size / SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` and abort explicitly if it stays too large.

Oversized uploads run up to five ImageMagick passes — Each oversized upload runs up to five full ImageMagick cycles plus `ImageOptim` in `convert_with` (app/models/optimized_image.rb), multiplying CPU cost for large files. Resize once with a factor from the size ratio rather than iterating relative 80% steps.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Public group members endpoint truncates default member list — Groups with more than 50 members silently hide the rest because the public members template has no pagination and never sends `limit` or `offset`. Page the endpoint from the client or return the full list for visible groups.

add_members fails when adding existing group members — Adding an existing member or repeating a name raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and the request 500s, which is common since the admin UI never filters existing members. Skip usernames already in the group before calling `group.add`.

remove_member raises RecordNotFound when user is not a group member — A stale list, concurrent removal, or double submit turns this into `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` instead of a no-op. Look the user up through `group.users.where(id: user_id).first` and delete only when found, still returning success.

totalPages overcounts pages when user_count is a multiple of limit — An exact multiple of `limit` reports a page that does not exist, so `showingLast` stays false and the next arrow loads an empty list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` so the last-page guard matches the real page count.

group.users.delete bypasses primary group cleanup and counter cache — Deleting the join row directly bypasses `destroy_deletions`, so a removed user keeps `primary_group_id` set and `user_count` drifts. Route removal through `usernames=` or explicitly clear `primary_group_id` for the removed user.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises NoMethodError when default_locale is nil — A nil `default_locale` raises `NoMethodError` inside `I18n.fallbacks[]` during translation lookups, since `compact` runs after `to_sym`. Build the array first and guard before calling `to_sym`.

Translation cache is not invalidated when default_locale changes — Users keep seeing text from the previous site locale after an admin changes `default_locale`, since the `translate_accelerator.rb` LRU key omits the resolved fallback chain. Include the current `SiteSetting.default_locale` in the cache key or clear `@cache` when it changes.

Fallback chain loaded only on controller path, not in jobs or rake tasks — In Sidekiq threads and rake tasks the `SiteSetting.default_locale`/`:en` fallbacks are looked up against locale files that were never loaded, so missing keys render "translation missing" instead of fallback text. Call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` wherever the locale is changed for a context.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Rejected device stays cached, bypassing the device limit — A device that was just rejected gets cached by `localCache.SetDefault` before the store call, so its next request returns early and the limit is bypassed. Move that cache write after the store call succeeds.

Non-atomic device limit check allows exceeding the limit — Concurrent requests all see `count < deviceLimit` before any write lands, so bursts can exceed the limit by any amount. Make the check and insert atomic with a transaction, lock, or unique constraint.

Anonymous auth blocks on TagDevice DB round-trips — Every uncached anonymous request now pays a `SELECT COUNT(*)` plus a write against `anon_device` on the auth path, and blocked devices still do a COUNT and failing UPDATE each time. Move `TagDevice` back off the request path.

Retry closure reassigns captured args, duplicating query on retry — `WithDbSession` retries the callback on lock errors, and reassigning the captured variable prepends the query again, sending it twice. Build the args slice locally inside the callback.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Missing cache re-check causes duplicate manifest parses — Goroutines that raced past the `RLock` check repeat the whole manifest parse while holding `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`, serializing concurrent requests behind a blocking parse on cold starts and whenever the parse fails. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` under the write lock and return early if it was populated by the goroutine that won the race.

Async legacy writes use request context canceled after response — The legacy `Create`/`Update`/`Delete`/`DeleteCollection` run under the request context, which Go cancels as soon as `ServeHTTP` returns, so each aborts with `context.Canceled` right after the response and the dual write never happens. Detach the goroutine with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` while keeping request values.

Async legacy update reuses raw objInfo instead of persisted result — `Legacy.Update` re-invokes `objInfo.UpdatedObject` on the legacy store's own old object, so the legacy copy can diverge from unified storage. Wrap the persisted `res` in `updateWrapper` as modes 1 and 2 do and pass that to `d.Legacy.Update`.

Async legacy writes in mode 3 can be applied out of order per object — Fire-and-forget goroutines drop the ordering guarantee: a create-then-delete, as in `playlist_test.go:506-576`, can reach legacy reversed and leave the row orphaned. Serialize the async legacy writes per object with a single worker queue keyed by kind+name.

Legacy DeleteCollection records to storage histogram instead of legacy — Legacy latency lands in the storage histogram and legacy failures stay invisible in `grafana_dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds`. Call `d.recordLegacyDuration`, as the other legacy calls do.

Delete storage duration metric uses object name as kind label — `recordStorageDuration` gets the object `name` in the `kind` label, so every deleted object adds a new `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` series (unbounded growth, unusable filtering). Pass `options.Kind` instead.

Create error path records legacy duration instead of storage duration — The storage failure goes to the legacy histogram, so `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` never shows `is_error=true` and legacy gets a false spike. Record it with `d.recordStorageDuration` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:125-129`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Concurrent cache misses can build duplicate indexes for same key — `getOrCreateIndex` now checks `GetIndex` outside any per-key lock, so two concurrent misses build separate indexes in the same directory and one caller keeps writing to an index already replaced in `b.cache`, making those documents unsearchable. Add per-key deduplication or an in-flight map so only one build per `NamespacedResource` runs at a time.

Logging TotalDocs races with watcher cache writes — The watch goroutine started just above can write the same cache under `cacheMu` while this call reads it, causing a concurrent map read/write panic. Synchronize `TotalDocs` with the cache writer or run it before the watcher starts.

Eager Init leaks watcher on unmanaged in-process servers — In-process servers from `restoptions.go` and `legacy_storage.go` have no `Stop` call site, so each construction starts a broadcaster goroutine and appends a subscriber to `dashboardSqlAccess.subscribers` that is never removed. Keep initialization lazy for servers that are not lifecycle-managed, or trigger shutdown for those construction paths.

Init failure leaks watcher and event-pump goroutines — The discarded instance never gets `Stop`, so the broadcaster and the `backend.WatchWriteEvents` subscription from `initWatcher`, plus the search event pump, keep running against the database forever. Call `s.cancel()` and close the started watchers on the error path before returning.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Silence menu item shown in list view but cannot open drawer — In the list view the visible "Silence notifications" item does nothing, because `RuleActionsButtons.V2` only mounts `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` when a ruler rule is present and the list view passes no `rulerRule`. Gate the silence item on a ruler rule being present, or make the drawer work from the promRule/uid.

Federated Mimir rule groups are treated as editable — Federated Mimir rule groups are read-only server-side, yet every view going through `useAlertRuleAbility` now reports Update/Delete/Pause as supported and shows actions that fail. Thread the federation check through from `rule.group` or pass a flag into this hook.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: New abstract getShortcut() breaks binary compatibility for custom grants — Any externally deployed custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` compiled against the previous SPI throws `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()`, so the server fails to start after upgrade. Give `getShortcut()` a default implementation, such as deriving it from `getId()` or returning the UNKNOWN `na` value.

Duplicate null check on grantType means rawTokenId is never validated — Because `grantType` is checked twice, a null `rawTokenId` is silently encoded as the literal "null" suffix instead of failing fast. Change the second check to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

Grant shortcut length is not validated before token ID encoding — A grant factory returning a 3-character shortcut mints access tokens whose IDs always throw `IllegalArgumentException` in `getTokenContextFromTokenId`, which requires exactly 6 characters. Validate that the shortcut is exactly 2 characters in `encodeTokenId`, or make the decoder length-agnostic.
client_credentials tokens encoded with UNKNOWN grant type — Set it before `generateAccessToken()` so the new `cc` shortcut is emitted.

isAccessTokenId checks wrong grant substring and inverts the comparison — `substring(3, 5)` reads the token type's second character plus the grant's first character, so the grant shortcut is never validated. Use `substring(4, 6)`, otherwise every valid encoded token ID is rejected once the inverted comparison is fixed.

getSubGroupsCount returns null for deleted group, violating SPI contract — Consumers that unbox or aggregate the count now throw an NPE on a concurrently deleted group, moving the crash to a harder-to-diagnose layer. Return a non-null value such as `0L`, or re-resolve through the delegate and signal a controlled failure.

Reader thread can hang test JVM if group deletion throws — Any exception from `group(groupUuid).remove()` leaves the non-daemon reader thread spinning forever and hangs the whole test JVM. Wrap the deletion loop in `try/finally` that always sets `deletedAll`, and preferably make the thread a daemon.

Reader thread not joined before asserting caught exceptions — A failure from an in-flight `groups()` request is appended after the assertion already passed, so the regression this test targets can be missed. Join the reader thread before checking `caughtExceptions`.

Reader thread busy-spins on full group listings and unbounded errors — The unbounded `caughtExceptions` list and full-hierarchy reads on every iteration can saturate CPU or fail with OOM instead of reporting the assertion. Add a small delay and record only the first failure.

Choice-format normalization hides embedded markup from sanitizer — Dropping the whole `{N,choice,...}` segment in `normalizeValue` lets embedded markup like `` bypass the sanitizer for `error-invalid-multivalued-size` and `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`. Neutralize only the `<` characters in the choice pattern so choice literals are still sanitized.

Lithuanian account messages totpStep1 replaced with Italian text — Lithuanian users of the account and login TOTP setup pages now see Italian instructions. Restore the Lithuanian translation in `totpStep1`; the same wrong-language string is also in `messages_lt.properties` under the login theme.

error-invalid-multivalued-size uses MessageFormat syntax breaking i18next — i18next only interpolates `{{ }}`, so `error-invalid-multivalued-size` displays raw `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` text in the admin UI and conflicts with existing translations. Keep `{{0}}`/`{{2}}` here and in the account `messages_en.properties`; the `choice` form belongs only in server-side theme bundles.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties:188-188`

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: getClientsWithPermission returns bogus entry instead of client ids — The set ends up with the all-clients resource's literal name instead of client ids, so AvailableRoleMappingResource throws a NullPointerException on `realm.getClientById(cid)`. Iterate real clients and add `client.getId()` when `hasPermission` passes.

Existing realms miss upgrade for new CLIENTS admin resource type — Realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 already enabled never get the new scopes or the CLIENTS resource type, and `getOrCreateResource` fails with ModelException("No scopes found."). Add reconciliation for existing admin-permissions resource servers when the schema grows.

ClientPermissionsV2 throws on live token-exchange and permission paths — Every token-exchange request in a V2 realm now throws a 500 through `canExchangeTo`, and the client `management/permissions` endpoints fail the same way. Return false for exchange checks and a no-op for `setPermissionsEnabled` instead of throwing on live paths.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77-95`

Client permission listings return null display names — The CLIENTS type isn't handled in the name resolution, so `getDisplayName()` stays null and PolicyResourceService returns null displayNames for every client permission listing. Resolve the client UUID to a readable label for this type.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Passkey-only users bypass required password factor via configuredFor — `configuredFor` lets a passkey satisfy a required password factor, so possession-only passkeys replace the knowledge factor in step-up flows. Restrict the `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` shortcut to re-authentication or require a UV-checked passkey.

Passkeys widget missing from base login-password.ftl — Themes inheriting from `base`, including the legacy `keycloak` login theme, render no passkey UI because `base/login/login-password.ftl` lacks the macro. Add the `passkeys.ftl` import and `passkeys.conditionalUIData` call there too.

Organization clause in shared login predicate hides org-linked IDPs — `getLoginPredicate()` also backs `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()`, so this clause silently hides org-linked IDPs without `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` from the linked-federated-identity list when organizations are disabled. Move the organization clause into the cache layer's invalidation predicate, not the shared login predicate.

Login cache invalidation uses org-aware enabled state for original IDP — For an IDP bound to a disabled organization, `original.isEnabled()` is false even though the IDP sits in the login cache, so an update to `hideOnLogin` or `linkOnly` returns early and leaves stale entries. Test `getLoginPredicate()` on the stored model from `idpDelegate.getById(...)` instead of the wrapped `original`.

Login IDP cache key omits organizationId, causing unbounded entry growth — Keying the login cache by realm and `FetchMode` only lets each new `organizationId` grow the same `IdentityProviderListQuery` and evict the whole entry cluster-wide via `invalidateObject`, forcing DB reloads. Include `organizationId` in the key, as `cacheKeyOrgId` does for `getByOrganization`.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Feature-flagged table branch renders empty data, discarding result and fields — With `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, the hardcoded empty `tableData` and `columns={[]}` discard `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the widget fields, so every table widget renders empty. Pass the real result and fields, or keep `StyledSimpleTableChart` until the migration is wired up.

Unbounded nodestore fan-out in replay breadcrumb summary error fetch — `fetch_error_details` loads every error id from nodestore per request, and `NodeStorage.get_multi` issues a backend read per id, so large replays cause unbounded fan-out. Bound the ids (e.g. the most recent N) or batch the lookup before building `node_ids`.

Error timestamps compared against replay-relative offsets — Comparing an absolute `ErrorEvent` `timestamp` against the replay-relative `event["timestamp"]` offset makes the merge test always true or always false, so errors flush as one block instead of interleaving. Normalize both to the same base before comparing.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Sleep patch makes flusher delay a no-op causing flaky test — The `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", ...)` patch also intercepts `time.sleep(0.1)`, so the delay never happens and `(msg,) = messages` can raise `ValueError`. Bind the real function with `from time import sleep`, as `test_flusher.py` does, or patch `time.sleep` only inside the flusher module.

Redis memory INFO fanout is repeated for every flusher buffer — Each flusher buffer repeats the identical cluster-wide `iter_cluster_memory_usage` fanout, so the summed `used`/`available` are N-times-duplicated cluster totals. Query the cluster memory once per `submit()` instead of iterating over every `self.buffers` entry.

wait_produce timer uses "shards" tag key while sibling metrics use "shard" — The `shards` tag key prevents the `wait_produce` timer from being correlated with the `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` timers that use `shard`. Use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` to match.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: queued default evaluated once at import, not per instance — Every `AssignmentSource` built during the worker's lifetime reports the same import-time timestamp, so `queued` cannot measure latency or distinguish two sources. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own queue time.

sync_status_outbound's assignment_source is never passed by its only caller — The status path gets no source-based cycle prevention because the only caller in `tasks/sync_status_outbound.py` never forwards `assignment_source` or passes it to `should_sync`. Thread the source through the status task and `should_sync`, or drop the parameter from the abstract contract.

OAuth state uses pipeline signature instead of per-flow nonce — `pipeline.signature` is a constant md5 of the view class names, so it can't bind the callback to the browser that started the flow, leaving the login-CSRF open. Generate a per-flow nonce with `secrets.token_hex()`, bind it via `pipeline.bind_state`, and compare against `pipeline.fetch_state`.

OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri and grant_type — The exchange omits `redirect_uri`, so it no longer matches the authorization request per RFC 6749 and relies on GitHub's registered callback; if `absolute_uri` differs there, users hit the generic failure page. Pass the same `redirect_uri` and `grant_type=authorization_code` into the exchange `data`.

GitHub install skips ownership check when Integration row is absent — When the webhook hasn't created the `Integration` yet, the `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch calls `next_step()` and `build_integration` without checking that the authenticated GitHub user owns the `installation_id`, letting an attacker link another account's installation. Resolve the installation's `sender` from the GitHub API, or require the webhook-created `Integration`, and run the comparison on both branches.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481-482`

Missing sender metadata crashes GitHub installation pipeline — Pipeline-created integrations never get a `sender` key in `integration.metadata` (only `build_integration` sets it), so indexing `["sender"]["login"]` raises and returns a 500 instead of the failure page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value as failed verification.

GitHub OAuth token and user-info errors cause 500 — `safe_urlopen` and `get_user_info` can raise (HTTP errors, connection errors, the 30s timeout) outside the guarded block, producing a 500 instead of the `github-integration-failed` page. Wrap both calls in try/except and return `error(...)` on failure.
