Decoder's fixed 6-char context check conflicts with variable-length grant shortcut SPI — The `getShortcut()` SPI advertises variable-length shortcuts, so a compliant provider produces token ids the decoder rejects with `IllegalArgumentException`, breaking the round-trip. Validate shortcut lengths in `encodeTokenId`, or relax the decoder to a variable-length grant segment.

testIncorrectGrantType passes via NPE instead of exercising shortcut validation — The test still passes if validation regresses: without `postInit`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` throws a `NullPointerException` that the broad `RuntimeException` catch swallows. Call `postInit` and catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically.

Null modelSupplier result still dereferenced in sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads — The same null from `modelSupplier.get()` still reaches the `getSubGroupsStream` overloads, including one used by the group-children endpoint in `GroupResource`, so the NPE this PR fixes remains reproducible. Apply the same null handling to all three sibling overloads.

getSubGroupsCount() returns null, violating GroupModel's never-null contract — The null propagates through `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` and is serialized as a null `subGroupCount` in admin API responses, breaking clients that expect a number. Return `0L` instead — a group that no longer resolves has no subgroups.

Reader thread not joined before asserting no exceptions were captured — A request still in flight when `deletedAll` is set can append to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already run, so the test passes despite capturing the exact concurrent-deletion failure it should detect. Join the reader thread before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

Reader thread spins forever if a group delete throws before deletedAll is set — If any `remove()` call throws, `deletedAll.set(true)` is never reached and the reader thread loops forever issuing admin requests, hanging the test JVM and discarding the collected exceptions. Wrap the deletion loop in try/finally so `deletedAll` is always set.

Revert message to i18next interpolation syntax broken for account console — i18next in `setUserProfileServerError` cannot substitute `{0}` or evaluate `{2,choice,...}`, so English users see the raw pattern instead of attribute names and counts. Restore `{{0}}`-style placeholders as community translations keep them; choice pluralization only works in server-rendered MessageFormat themes.

Java MessageFormat syntax rendered literally in admin console message — English admins see the raw MessageFormat syntax instead of attribute names and counts because the admin console interpolates this key via i18next in `setUserProfileServerError`. Restore `{{0}}`-style placeholders; the `{2,choice,...}` pluralization only works in server-rendered themes.

`santizeAnchors` pairs anchor tags by order, rejecting reordered translations — A valid translation that reorders anchor tags fails the build with `Didn't find anchor tag` because `englishMatcher.find()` only advances on exact positional matches, and `replaceFirst()` also strips the first occurrence rather than the matched one. Collect the tags into sets and compare membership and counts instead.

Lithuanian totpStep1 contains Italian text instead of Lithuanian — Lithuanian users see Italian on the OTP setup page; the same Italian also replaced `loginTotpStep1` in the login theme's messages_lt.properties. Replace both with a Lithuanian rendering of the new English wording; anchors are no longer needed since the source dropped them.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties:71-71`

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: getClientsWithPermission returns the all-clients type resource as a client id — Delegated admins holding an all-clients map-roles-composite permission get a 500 because the caller `getRoleIdsWithPermissions` dereferences the bogus id via `realm.getClientById` without a null check. Skip resources whose name equals `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` in `getClientsWithPermission`.

canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token exchange — With `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` enabled, every cross-client token exchange fails with an unhandled 500 because `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` calls this method unconditionally. Evaluate the permission as V1 does instead of throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`.

Cleanup listener gates on V1 flag but management() dispatches to throwing V2 implementation — Both flags can be active at once — `Profile` auto-enables the V1 flag for the token-exchange V2 features — so `ClientRemovedEvent` reaches `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` and every client deletion rolls back. Also require that `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is disabled.

getClientsWithPermission misses per-client grants and returns bogus id — Per-client grants like map-roles stay invisible because resources from `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` carry no type attribute, so `findByType` matches only the all-clients resource. Look up per-client resources by name instead of via `findByType`.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Base theme login-password.ftl missing passkey conditional-UI include — Passkey re-authentication silently fails on themes inheriting the base theme, since `PasswordForm.authenticate` sets up WebAuthn context but the page renders no passkey button. Add the `passkeys` import and `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />` here, as base `login.ftl` and `login-username.ftl` already do.

Update skips login cache invalidation when org-aware wrapper masks original state — When the organization is disabled, `getLoginPredicate()` fails on the wrapper's `isEnabled()` even though the raw fields changed, so the `.idp.login` cache isn't invalidated and login pages keep showing an IDP that should be hidden. Evaluate the predicate on the raw original loaded via `idpDelegate` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Table widget renders empty data under use-table-widget-visualization flag — Hardcoded empty props silently discard the query results, so every dashboard table widget renders as an empty grid under the flag. Pass the real `result.data` and `result.meta` with derived `columns`, or gate the branch until `TableWidgetVisualization` is actually wired up.

Truthiness check on sibling field lets timestamp: 0 and age: 0 coexist — Zero is falsy, so a report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes the mutual-exclusivity check and is accepted and counted. Test presence with `"age" in self.initial_data` in both validators instead of a truthy `get`.

Error IDs are paired with wrong event data when nodestore omits missing ids — The Django backend's `get_multi` omits missing ids, so zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` pairs every later id with the wrong event's data, corrupting titles, timestamps, and the breadcrumb timeline. Look up each id with `events.get(node_id)` instead of zipping the values.

Client-controlled field params cause KeyError and drop error_ids from summary — An unknown `?field=` value raises an unhandled `KeyError` for a 500, and omitting `error_ids` silently empties the summary's error context. Stop accepting `field` params on this endpoint, or whitelist known fields instead of projecting blindly.

Snuba query runs even when error context is disabled — Requests that disable error context still pay the cross-service Snuba query, whose result is then discarded. Move the `query_replay_instance` call and `process_raw_response` below the `disable_error_fetching` early-out.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Redis memory info sampled once per buffer, P× redundant cluster INFO fan-out — `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` already queries every Redis master in the cluster, ignoring `assigned_shards`, so looping over `self.buffers.values()` repeats that blocking `INFO` fan-out per flusher process and stalls the consumer loop. Sample memory once from a single buffer; the used/available ratio is unchanged.

Inconsistent shard tag key between produce and wait_produce timers — Per-shard dashboards and alerts will silently fragment, since `wait_produce` tags `shards` while `produce` and the segment-size metric tag `shard`. Use the `shard` tag key for both timers.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: queued defaults to module import time instead of per-instance time — Every `AssignmentSource` built via `from_integration` carries the worker's boot timestamp, which `to_dict()` serializes into each `sync_assignee_outbound` task; `test_to_dict` misses it by only asserting non-None. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so `queued` is evaluated per instance.

KeyError on missing metadata["sender"] in GitHub install check — Integrations built by the install pipeline never get a sender, so the whole install flow turns into a 500; installation.py already treats the key as optional. Switch to `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` so a missing sender lands on the error page.

Token exchange omits redirect_uri sent in authorize request — GitHub requires the token-step redirect_uri to match the authorize-step value, so real installations can fail at the exchange while tests pass because the endpoint is mocked in `_stub_github`. Add the same `absolute_uri` value the authorize leg builds to `data`.

CSRF state uses predictable pipeline signature instead of per-flow nonce — Because `pipeline.signature` is a deterministic md5 of class names, identical for every flow and derivable from source, this gate verifies nothing — any caller can supply the constant. Generate a random nonce, bind it with `pipeline.bind_state`, and compare against `pipeline.fetch_state`, as identity/oauth2.py does.

Unwrapped get_user_info call raises unhandled exception on GitHub API errors — A rate limit or transient 5xx makes `get_user_info` raise through `resp.raise_for_status()`, showing a 500 in the install dialog, unlike the guarded token exchange just above. Wrap it in try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated — `MetricAlertFire` exposes this class as its handler, so evaluating any metric_alert_fire detector crashes with `TypeError` when `Detector.detector_handler` tries to instantiate it. Implement or stub the abstract methods inherited from `StatefulDetectorHandler` — at minimum `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, `get_dedupe_value`, and `get_group_key_values`.

Expected occurrence built with wrong group key in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe — The mismatched fingerprints leave the two `IssueOccurrence` objects unequal under `__eq__`, so the assertion fails on every run. Pass `"group_key"` to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` instead of `"val1"`.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Transformed config discarded; raw config returned with unconverted schedule_type — Consumers get the raw `schedule_type` value instead of the human-readable one because the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, discarding the transformed copy. Return the mutated `config` so the conversion takes effect.

Dereference of possibly undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar crashes EventManager.create — Whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty — as callers like `handleNewBooking.ts` produce — dereferencing `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError that crashes the booking/payment flow instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

References created by updateLocation lose externalCalendarId and credentialId — `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`, so every reference `updateLocation` creates stores undefined, and later reschedule/cancel operations can't resolve the right calendar. Return those fields or fall back to `evt.destinationCalendar` values.

Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition drops slug or bypasses requestedSlug flow — The ternary is inverted: with billing disabled, self-hosted orgs get no slug even though `vercelCreateDomain(slug)` registered their subdomain, making them unreachable via `getSlugOrRequestedSlug`; with billing enabled it bypasses the `requestedSlug` approval flow. Restore the `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition.

createEvent posts to first destination calendar regardless of which host credential was invoked — Each host's credential is now invoked per destination, yet `createEvent` still posts to `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, so a member's token 404s on another host's calendar id; `LarkCalendarService` makes the same mistake. Match the destination whose `credentialId` equals the invoked one, as `GoogleCalendarService` does.

destinationCalendar initialized to null drops member calendars for collective events — When no event-type or organizer destination exists, `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops and `createAllCalendarEvents` falls back to organizer credentials only. Initialize the field to `[]` like the other handlers.

updateEvent fallback never matches, leaving calendarId undefined — The fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it never matches and `calendar.events.update` receives `calendarId: undefined`, silently failing reschedules for bookings whose reference lacks that field. Use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`

Video meeting references lose credentialId, preventing meeting deletion on cancellation — `handleCancelBooking.ts` only calls `deleteMeeting` when `credentialId` is set, so canceled Zoom/Teams/Daily rooms are left orphaned. Use `result.credentialId` for the video branch — `createMeeting` in `videoClient.ts` returns it.

Destination calendar without credentialId never matched; event created on "primary" — `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable (see `schema.prisma`), so destinations without one never match and events are silently created on `"primary"`, breaking the follow-up `hangoutLink` patch. Fall back to the first destination calendar's `externalId` when no match is found.

Duplicate events when destinations share integration without credentialId — For collective events with several destinations of the same credential-less integration, the no-credentialId branch in `createAllCalendarEvents` re-runs the same credentials per destination, creating duplicate events on one calendar. Deduplicate credentials across destinations, e.g. with a Set of used credential ids.
Sequential createEvent awaits make booking latency scale with host count — Resolve the per-destination creations with `Promise.all`, as the no-credentialId branch already does.

Recurring-event deletion sweep re-runs for every calendar reference, duplicating delete calls — The recurring-event sweep never reads `reference`, yet it re-runs per calendar reference, multiplying delete API calls and re-deleting already-removed events. Hoist this block out of the per-reference loop since its inputs don't depend on it.

Reschedule merge path deletes only first old calendar reference, orphaning others — On reschedules with `newBookingId`, the merge path still deletes only the first old calendar reference via `booking.references.find(...)`, leaving other hosts' events orphaned with stale times. Iterate all old `_calendar` references for deletion, mirroring the per-reference loop added here.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team permission check uses && so admins (non-owners) are denied adding guests — Team admins get `FORBIDDEN` on their own team's booking because `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` demands both roles. Use `||` — or just `isTeamAdmin`, which already returns true for ADMIN or OWNER.

Guest emails bypass blacklist and duplicate check due to case-sensitive comparison — A mixed-case guest like `Spam@Example.com` slips past the lowercased `blacklistedGuestEmails` and receives the full booking details and video link. Compare against `guest.toLowerCase()`, and normalize the `booking.attendees` duplicate check the same way.

No booking status check allows adding guests to cancelled/rejected bookings — Attendee rows are created, CONFIRMED ics attachments are emailed, and calendar updates run against deleted events, since `booking.status` is never checked. Throw `BAD_REQUEST` unless the status is `ACCEPTED`, before any state changes.

Guests array is not deduplicated, allowing duplicate Attendee rows — Submitting the same email twice in `guests` inserts two identical Attendee rows — the model has no unique constraint — causing duplicate emails and calendar entries. Dedupe case-insensitively before `createMany`; the server schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` drops the client-side uniqueness refine.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests, re-sending scheduled email to existing attendees — An existing attendee who is re-submitted still gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the add-guests notification, since `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `email-manager.ts` treats raw `guests` as new. Pass `uniqueGuests` so only added guests are notified.

Unbounded `guests` array enables resource exhaustion and mail bombing — One authorized request with thousands of emails triggers an unbounded `createMany`, a huge email fanout, and a bloated calendar update — a repeatable mail-bombing vector from any attendee account. Bound the `guests` array in `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with `.max(25)`.

evt CalendarEvent never sets team, so team members never get add-guests emails — Team members silently miss the add-guests notification: `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `email-manager.ts` only notifies when `calEvent.team?.members` is populated, leaving that loop dead code. Populate `evt.team` from `booking.eventType.team` with its members, as `handleCancelBooking.ts` does.

Stale validation error banner reappears when dialog is reopened — Since the dialog stays mounted in `BookingListItem`, one failed validation makes the error banner reappear on every reopen, even after a successful add. Clear `isInvalidEmail` in `onSuccess`, and reset both it and `multiEmailValue` when closing via `onOpenChange`.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: refreshAccessToken persists zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of parsed tokens — `googleCredentialSchema.parse` throws on the next `GoogleCalendarService` construction because the persisted key is the `{success, data}` wrapper, not the tokens — permanently disabling Google Calendar after each user's first token refresh. Unwrap with `.data` before persisting, e.g. `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`.

Credential-sync path returns raw fetch Response, breaking token-parsing callers — With `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `Response`: googlecalendar reads `res?.data` and silently keeps the expired token, hubspot persists the Response as the credential key, and zoho callers crash. Parse the endpoint's JSON into a normalized token object, or pass it through each app's parser.

Updated credentials never reset the invalid flag, leaving app disabled — Fresh keys never revive a credential marked `invalid` — `getCalendarsEvents.ts` filters those out, so a user whose app was disabled stays broken despite the sync, defeating the app store as source of truth. Add `invalid: false` to the `prisma.credential.update` data payload.

Token refresh checks unreliable statusText instead of response.ok — `statusText` is empty for HTTP/2 fetch responses and varies across 2xx codes, so a valid refresh can throw `HttpError` 400 with an empty message, breaking every Salesforce operation. Check `response.ok` instead.

msteams refresh via sync endpoint marks token expired, causing refresh loop — The sync endpoint's response has no `expires_in`, so `expiry_date` becomes `Date.now()` and `getToken()` re-runs the sync POST plus a credential write on every Teams call, gradually overwriting the key's `refresh_token`. Map the endpoint's expiry into the `expires_in` offset the caller expects.

Sync-config-driven schema strips instance_url from Salesforce token response — On sync-enabled instances the saved key loses `instance_url`, so the next `getClient` builds `jsforce.Connection` with `instanceUrl: undefined` and every Salesforce call hits the wrong host. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` picks `minimumTokenResponseSchema` from the global sync config; since this response comes straight from Salesforce, use `salesforceTokenSchema` here.

Computed schema keys collapse to one literal key, stripping token response fields — Both computed keys collapse to the single literal `"[object Object]"` and `z.object` strips unknown keys, so callers persist only `access_token` plus the placeholder `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` — office365calendar overwrites users' real refresh tokens, zoomvideo stores a NaN expiry. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` and stop forcing the placeholder.

Unconditional Salesforce token refresh + DB write on every getClient call — Services are constructed per operation via `getCalendar()`, so eager `getClient` adds a blocking `login.salesforce.com` round trip and DB write to each one — and the new token goes unused since `Connection` still gets stale `credentialKey.access_token`. Gate refresh on token expiry, or let jsforce's built-in lazy refresh handle it.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !==, leaking timing info — Plain `!==` leaks match-length timing on this Internet-reachable endpoint, where the secret is the only authorization for overwriting any user's credentials. Compare SHA-256 digests of both values with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

refreshOAuthTokens called with credential row id instead of user id — Passing `credentialId` (the credential row id) as `refreshOAuthTokens`'s `userId` parameter makes the sync endpoint resolve the wrong user — Bigin refresh fails or returns another user's tokens; every other caller passes `credential.userId`. Do the same here.

Race condition in webhook creates duplicate credentials without unique constraint — Two concurrent deliveries both see `findFirst` return null and both `create`, since `schema.prisma` has only `@@index` — no unique constraint — on `Credential(userId, appId)`; later syncs update just one row, leaving a stale duplicate. Add `@@unique([userId, appId])` or upsert semantics.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Unprotected prisma update in catch block aborts the reminder loop and 200 response — A row deleted mid-run by `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (or a transient DB error) makes this update throw P2025, escaping the loop, skipping remaining reminders, and losing the 200 response. Wrap the catch-block `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in its own try/catch.

Transient SMS failures counted as retries, deleting reminders that could still be sent — Both the `else` branch and `catch` increment `retryCount` even when `twilio.scheduleSMS` failed transiently — `smsLockState` LOCKED or a rate limit — so `deleteMany` irreversibly purges reminders that could still be sent. Increment only for non-retryable errors like invalid phone numbers.

`retryCount` read-modify-write loses updates on overlapping cron runs — Overlapping cron runs both read the same snapshot and write the same `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, undercounting failed attempts and letting duplicate SMS go out before `deleteMany` purges the reminder. Use atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in both update calls.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup-code login skips password verification, allowing access with leaked backup code — Anyone holding a leaked backup code can sign in without knowing the password, since this branch never calls `verifyPassword` and the earlier `user.password` check is skipped when `totpCode` is set. Verify `credentials.password` here, as disable.ts does, or make the check unconditional.

2FA success path never calls onEnable(); parent state stale after dismiss — Dismissing via ESC, X, or overlay at the backup-codes step never refreshes the parent — the Switch still shows 2FA disabled and reopening shows stale codes. Call `onEnable()` when enable succeeds, or invoke it from `onOpenChange` when `step` is `DisplayBackupCodes`.

Backup code burn uses check-then-act race allowing same code twice — Two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both pass `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` before either write lands, so the code authenticates twice. Burn it atomically with `updateMany` keyed on the unchanged `user.backupCodes`, requiring `count === 1`, or use a locking transaction.

Backup code comparison is case-sensitive; uppercase input is wrongly rejected — Codes are generated as lowercase hex, but the `XXXXX-XXXXX` placeholder invites uppercase, so a correctly typed uppercase code is rejected with `IncorrectBackupCode` — locking users out of recovery. Apply `.toLowerCase()` before `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` (disable.ts needs the same), or unify generation and display.

Backup-code input constraints never enforced, invalid codes silently dead-click — The `required` and length constraints are never enforced — the host form is `noValidate` and the zod schema uses `.passthrough()` — so an empty or short code submits with no feedback. Pass validation rules to `methods.register("backupCode", ...)`, or add the field to the zod login schema.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: Multi-condition Prisma.sql assertions fail against flat expected templates — Because `Prisma.sql` only flattens nested fragments when a query compiles, the results of `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, and `buildFilterConditions` never `toEqual` the flat expected templates, failing these tests in CI. Have each builder emit a single flat template, like the user-scope branch, or assert on the compiled query instead.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Invalid `<%- end if %>` tag in embed template causes SyntaxError on every render — The `<%- end if %>` ERB tag compiles to a trailing `if` modifier with no condition after `end` — stdlib ERB joins compiled segments with `;` and the Rails Erubis handler likewise appends `;` after the tag body, producing invalid Ruby (`end if;`) and a SyntaxError when ActionView compiles the template. Every `/embed/best` request for a URL that already has a topic returns a 500, so the embed widget can never render comments (the controller specs never render views, so this is uncaught).

poll_feed crashes on Ruby 2.0 and nil content: String#scrub is undefined — `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError: `String#scrub` does not exist on Ruby 2.0.0 (the version this project runs and tests on per `.travis.yml`; the method was added in Ruby 2.1), and `i.content` is nil for feed items that lack a content element. The exception aborts `poll_feed` at the first item — with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the hourly job fails silently forever, so no feed items are ever imported and the RSS branch of `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` can never succeed (the specs stub `poll_feed`, so this path is untested).

NOT NULL default column add rewrites posts table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` forces a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL 9.x (the no-rewrite optimization for constant defaults only landed in PG 11), blocking all reads and writes on the forum's largest, hottest table for the duration of the copy during deploy. Add the column as nullable with the default, backfill existing rows in batches, then attach the NOT NULL constraint.

Protocol-relative URLs (//host/...) are broken by absolutize_urls — Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` satisfy `href.start_with?('/')`, and `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, so the URL is rewritten to `http://<embed-host>/cdn.example.com/img.jpg`. Imported articles that use protocol-relative links or images (common in RSS/WordPress feeds and CDN assets) get every such link broken.

Double HTML-unescaping corrupts escaped HTML in imported feed items — `CGI.unescapeHTML` decodes the feed item's HTML a second time: SimpleRSS already returns XML-unescaped HTML, so content-level escapes such as `<div>` in an article's code sample become literal `<div>` markup, which is then stored via the `raw_html` cook_method and rendered with `raw post.cooked`. Every imported article containing escaped HTML examples or entity-encoded text is silently corrupted (and escaped tags become live tags) — drop the `CGI.unescapeHTML` call and pass `i.content` through as-is.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when no 'embed_category' setting row exists — On any site without an `embed_category` row, `[0]` returns nil and `nil['id']` aborts `db:migrate` before the `uncategorized_category_id` fallback can run. Guard the query result as migration 20140929204155 does, checking `cmd_tuples > 0` before indexing.

Migration inserts unnormalized hosts, breaking exact-host matching for scheme/path-qualified entries — Migrated rows like `https://example.com/1234` are stored verbatim, so `record_for_host`'s exact `lower(host) = uri.host` match fails and previously-allowed hosts get `Discourse::InvalidAccess` on `/embed/comments`. Apply the model's normalization, stripping the scheme and path, to each line before inserting.

Unescaped host value interpolated into INSERT breaks migration on quotes — A single quote in an old setting value produces invalid SQL and aborts `db:migrate` mid-run. Escape `h` with `PG::Connection.escape_string` as sibling migration 20140929204155 does, or use bound `exec_insert`.

Hosts saved with a port never match in record_for_host, rejecting valid embed requests — A host saved as `example.com:8080` passes the validation regex but is stored with the port, which `uri.host` never includes, so `record_for_host` rejects every embed request from it. Strip the port in `before_validation` with `sub!(/:\d+$/, '')` or compare including it in `record_for_host`.

Update and destroy raise NoMethodError on stale embeddable host id — A stale id makes `save_host(nil)` call `nil.host=` and `destroy` call `nil.destroy`, returning a 500 instead of a 404. Add `raise Discourse::NotFound` when the `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` lookup is nil.
before_validation callback raises NoMethodError when host is nil — Guard with `self.host = (self.host || '').sub(...)`.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Downsizing loses GIF animation because tempfile path lacks .gif extension — Animated GIFs are silently flattened to one frame: `OptimizedImage#optimize` detects animation only when the source path matches `/\.GIF$/i`, which the extensionless multipart tempfile never does, so `allow_animation` is ignored. Downsize from a tempfile carrying the original extension, as `OptimizedImage.create_for` does, or match on the original filename.

Hardcoded 10MB limit drops per-type site setting checks in client validation — Attachments above `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client-side and fail only after a full upload, and sites configured above 10MB reject valid files, because `maxSizeKB` drops the per-type setting lookup. Restore the settings-driven limit for attachments, keeping the 10MB cap for images only; the 413 handler repeats this hardcode.

Duplicate downsize definition shadows 5-arg version, breaking ResizeEmoji — Every custom-emoji upload now fails its `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` job with `ArgumentError` (5 for 4), leaving the emoji un-downsized: the second `downsize` definition takes only 4 parameters and shadows the original. Keep one signature accepting both the width/height form and the dimensions string.

Unvalidated downsize loop exposes ImageMagick to decompression bombs and banned types — Any logged-in user can force up to five full ImageMagick decode/re-encode passes on a 10MB file with huge pixel dimensions, since the downsize loop runs before size and `authorized_extensions` validation and gates only on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. Downsize only after those checks pass, and cap accepted pixel area first.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Public group members page silently hides members beyond first 50 — Add next/previous controls like the admin page, or restore the unbounded listing for this consumer.

`automatic` resolves against member context, not group; remove icon shown for automatic groups — Since `automatic` is undefined on the member context, the remove icon appears even for automatic groups, where the server always rejects removal with 422. Resolve the flag against the group, e.g. `controller.automatic`, so the icon only renders when removal can succeed.

Stale offset after member removal can reload an empty members page — After removing the only member on the last page, `findMembers` reloads with the stale `offset`, so the server returns an empty list and the UI shows a blank page. Reset the offset when the current page empties or clamp it against the freshly returned `meta.total`.

Group member add/remove failures are silently swallowed — When the server rejects the request, the unhandled promises in `removeMember` and `addMembers` swallow the error, so the admin gets no feedback and the list silently stays unchanged. Add a rejection handler that displays the error, as the replaced save flow did.

add_members raises RecordNotUnique when adding an existing member — The unique index on `group_users` means `group.add(user)` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` — a 500 — whenever a username is already a member, and nothing on the client prevents resubmitting one. Guard each add with a membership check or reuse the diffing semantics of the old `Group#usernames=` setter.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Translation LRU cache key omits default_locale, serving stale cross-tenant fallbacks — Fallback-resolved translations are cached under a key that omits `SiteSetting.default_locale`, even though `FallbackLocaleList#[]` now makes the result depend on it. The no-args fast path in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72` caches under `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}"` and nothing in the repo clears it (no `I18n.reload!` call sites exist), so after an admin changes the default locale, hot (key, locale) entries keep serving the old fallback text indefinitely — and on multisite, where `SiteSetting.default_locale` differs per tenant but the LRU cache is process-global, tenant A's fallback resolution is served to tenant B for the identical (key, locale).

Fallbacks only loaded in web requests; background jobs miss English fallback translations — `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is wired only into the web `set_locale` filter, so fallback locales are never loaded in background processes — `app/jobs/base.rb:151` and the `I18n.with_locale` callers (`app/services/post_alerter.rb:138`, `lib/post_destroyer.rb:102`) set a thread locale but never ensure the chain is loaded, and `I18n::Backend::Base#load_translations` is patched to a no-op without explicit filenames (translate_accelerator.rb:25-29). On any site with `default_locale` ≠ en, keys missing from the current locale render as `translation missing: xx.key` strings in emails and notifications instead of falling back to English, until the process happens to translate with en as the thread locale.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Over-limit device is cached on failed write and bypasses the limit for 29 minutes — In `tagDeviceUI` (impl.go), the device key is cached before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs, so an over-limit rejection still leaves it in `localCache` and the cache hit makes `TagDevice` return nil on later requests. Move `a.localCache.SetDefault` after a successful `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, or evict the key on error.

Anonymous device limit bypassable by omitting X-Grafana-Device-Id header — `TagDevice` (impl.go) returns nil when the header is missing, so clients that omit or rotate `X-Grafana-Device-Id` authenticate freely and never count against the quota. Anchor enforcement to a server-side signal, or document that the cap only meters cooperative frontends.

Count-then-insert race in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` exceeds the device limit — In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, `CountDevices` and the insert run as separate statements with no lock, so concurrent requests each see `count < deviceLimit` and all insert, exceeding the cap. Make the check atomic with a transaction that locks the counting range, or a conditional insert that re-checks the count.

TagDevice runs synchronously on the auth path, blocking every anonymous request — Auth now waits on a device round-trip for every anonymous request, amplifying latency on the hottest path. Run `TagDevice` asynchronously so authentication doesn't depend on it.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Missing double-check of cache after acquiring lock causes duplicate manifest loads — Concurrent requests that raced past the nil check each re-read and re-parse `assets-manifest.json` under the lock, serializing callers behind K duplicate loads. After `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`, re-check `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` and return it before rebuilding.

TestLogger.FromContext returns a throwaway logger, dropping captured logs — Tests logging through `FromContext` — for example `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` in `logger_middleware.go` — capture nothing, silently defeating assertions on the fake. Return the receiver `f` instead of a fresh `NewTestLogger()`.

Async legacy writes use request context, canceled when handler returns — Legacy Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection writes are aborted mid-flight whenever they outlast the response, silently drifting the two stores and risking data loss if reads ever fall back to legacy. Derive the goroutine contexts from `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, ...)` so only the deadline applies.

Legacy Update recomputes patch on stale object instead of unified result — PATCH/Apply requests write different content to legacy than to unified storage, because raw `objInfo` makes legacy `Update` recompute the patch on its own possibly stale copy (see `legacyStorage.Update` in `pkg/registry/apis/playlist/legacy_storage.go`). Wrap the unified result in `updateWrapper`, as `dualwriter_mode2.go` still does.

Delete no longer tolerates NotFound from unified storage, orphaning legacy-only rows — Objects existing only in legacy (pre-migration rows) now return 404 and stay orphaned forever, blocking mode 3-to-4 migration, since every storage error returns immediately. Restore the `apierrors.IsNotFound` fall-through so legacy cleanup still runs.

Mode 3 records unified-storage errors as legacy duration metrics — `grafana_dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds{is_error="true"}` gets inflated by unified-storage failures recorded through `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`, skewing the legacy health metrics operators use for mode migration. Replace both error-path calls with `recordStorageDuration`, as `dualwriter_mode2.go` does.

Async legacy delete-collection recorded under storage metric instead of legacy metric — Every async legacy delete-collection is hidden: `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` attributes it to the storage metric, so `grafana_dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds` shows zero delete-collection traffic in mode 3. Call `recordLegacyDuration` instead, matching `dualwriter_mode2.go`'s counterpart.

Delete success path uses object name as metric kind label causing unbounded cardinality — Each distinct deleted object name creates its own `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` series via the `name` label — user-chosen names mean unbounded Prometheus cardinality. Pass `options.Kind` like every sibling call.

Mode-3 tests never assert the async legacy write actually happened — Mode 3's defining async legacy write can be deleted or broken without failing any test — no `AssertCalled` verifies the legacy mock after the goroutine. Synchronize on the goroutine (mock channels or a WaitGroup) and assert `LegacyStorage.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection` ran with the unified-written object.

Mode-3 playlist tests assert legacy state without waiting for async dual-write, causing flakiness — The mode-3 subtests only pass when the async legacy write beats the next HTTP request — `doPlaylistTests` asserts legacy state immediately with no synchronization against the goroutine. Poll for legacy convergence with a timeout instead.

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Removing whole-function lock exposes data race and lost errors in searchSupport.init workers — With `cacheMu` gone, the `group.Go` workers race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed`, tripping CI's `-race` detector and letting a `nil` overwrite a build failure so `init` reports success with missing indexes. Declare a local `err` per closure and make `totalBatchesIndexed` atomic or mutex-protected.

TotalDocs reads bleve cache without lock, racing with index-building goroutine — An unlocked iteration of `b.cache` while the event goroutine's `BuildIndex` writes it is an unrecoverable concurrent map crash. Acquire `cacheMu.RLock()` inside `TotalDocs`, which also covers the lockless prometheus read in bleve_index_metrics.go.

Blocking Init in NewResourceServer stalls Grafana startup on search-index build — Since `ProvideUnifiedStorageClient` wires this into the main Grafana server, the synchronous `Init` blocks wire-graph and HTTP/metrics readiness behind the full index build, risking probe failures and crash loops. Keep eager init for the standalone storage-server; build asynchronously with a readiness gate when constructed in-process.

Postgres skip disables only CI coverage of changed StorageServer startup path — The commit history shows this test now fails under Drone with postgres after these changes, so the skip masks a live regression in the eager `Init` startup instead of fixing it. Resolve the underlying startup or timing failure and remove the skip.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Silence action no-ops in new list view because drawer only renders for ruler rules — Users get a visible Silence action that does nothing: `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, always false when only `promRule` is passed. Build the drawer input from `promRule`/`identifier` instead of gating on the ruler rule.

GrafanaPauseAbility/grafanaDeleteAbility are dead code; Pause and Delete items hidden in list view — Grafana-managed rules lose Pause and Delete even for fully-permitted users: both items are gated on `rulerRule`, which `GrafanaGroupLoader` no longer supplies. Gate Delete on `canDelete && identifier`, and pause from `promRule.uid`/`isPaused` via `usePauseRuleInGroup`.

Federated rule check hardcoded to false, allowing edits of federated Mimir rule groups — Users can open the edit form on a federated group and save changes that clobber its federated configuration. Propagate the group's state into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` — e.g. carry `source_tenants` from `rule.group` — before removing `isFederatedRuleGroup` from this path.

skipToken fails to disable abilities; Duplicate menu wrongly shown for cloud rules — Cloud rules can now show a Duplicate item whose clone flow cannot succeed: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` still evaluates global Grafana permissions, and `AlertRuleMenu` ORs the result in. Return `[false, false]` for `skipToken`, as `useCanSilence(undefined)` does.

GrafanaRuleListItem missing key prop causes React state reuse across rules — An in-flight clone redirect or open delete modal can hit the wrong rule after filters change or polling updates. Add `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`, matching the other switch branches.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: isAccessTokenId slices wrong chars and inverts grant-shortcut comparison — The grant check in `matchesSafely` never fires, so `expectRefresh` and sibling matchers degrade to a bare UUID check that accepts any grant, and short prefixes throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. Slice the grant segment with `substring(4, 6)` per `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` and return false only when it differs from `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Grant-type token ID encoding always emits "na" for client-credentials, UMA and token-exchange tokens — The registered "cc" and "pg" shortcuts stay dead because client-credentials, UMA, and token-exchange issuance (check `ClientCredentialsGrantType`, `AuthorizationTokenService`, `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider`) never set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on `clientSessionCtx`, defeating the introspection and admin optimizations. Set the attribute in those paths or derive the grant centrally in `initToken`.

Constructor re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, leaving null rawTokenId unchecked — A null `rawTokenId` slips through, and `encodeTokenId` would later concatenate it into a token ID ending in ":null". Pass `rawTokenId` to the final `Objects.requireNonNull` call.

getSubGroupsCount() returns null when backing group is gone, violating GroupModel contract — A null `subGroupCount` can reach admin group listings via `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, and callers unboxing the `Long` will NPE, breaking the documented `GroupModel` invariant. Return `0L` from `getSubGroupsCount()` when `modelSupplier.get()` finds no backing group.

Reader thread is never joined, so late exceptions can slip past the assertion — An exception from the reader's final in-flight request can land in `caughtExceptions` after `assertThat` already passed, letting this regression test false-pass. Capture the thread reference and call `join()` after `deletedAll.set(true)` before asserting.

Choice block stripping hides injected HTML from the sanitizer — Because `[^}]*` deletes the whole choice block before `santizeAnchors` and `policy.sanitize` run, hidden anchor markup passes verification yet `MessageFormat` re-emits it at runtime where `kcSanitize` still permits `a[href]`. Strip only the numeric `N<` separators so any other `<` is flagged.

MessageFormat placeholders in client-side bundle are never substituted by i18next — `error-invalid-multivalued-size` is rendered client-side by `setUserProfileServerError` in `js/libs/ui-shared/src/user-profile/utils.ts` using stock i18next, which only substitutes `{{n}}`, so English users see literal `{0}` and `{2,choice,…}`. Restore `{{n}}` placeholders in both UI bundles — this file and `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties` — keeping choice syntax only in the server-side base properties.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties:3138-3138`

Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text in TOTP setup — Lithuanian users see Italian text on the TOTP setup page, and the same Italian string was pasted into `totpStep1` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`. Replace both with a Lithuanian translation, e.g. "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių į savo mobilųjį telefoną:", as done for the sibling locales.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties:101-101`

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` breaks callers via `ClientPermissionsV2` V1 stubs — When both `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` and its V2 are enabled, every client deletion fails: the `ClientRemovedEvent` handler in `AdminPermissions` calls `setPermissionsEnabled`, which `ClientPermissionsV2` stubs with `UnsupportedOperationException`; `ClientResource`'s V1 endpoints and `canExchangeTo` break likewise. Keep V1 semantics for these methods or gate the V1 callers on `!ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`.

getClientsWithPermission: 'Clients' in result and per-client grants omitted — With a type-level grant, the result contains the literal `Clients` name, not a client ID, so `AvailableRoleMappingResource` NPEs on the null `getClientById` result; per-client resources, created typeless by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`, stay invisible to `findByType` and get omitted — a V1 regression. Skip the type resource and include per-client grants.

NPE when Clients type resource is missing in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) — Realms initialized before this change never get the `Clients` type resource, so `getResourceTypeResource` returns null and `policyStore.findByResource` NPEs; every client permission evaluation 500s for callers without realm-admin roles, though the sibling type-level method null-checks. Guard `resource == null`, and add a store migration creating missing type resources and scopes.

**Also found in:**
- `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:63-68`

Client-removal cleanup skipped when only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled — Since `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is an independent feature, clients deleted under it permanently orphan their resources and referencing permissions; `getClientsWithPermission` then policy-evaluates every orphan on each restricted client listing, growing cost unboundedly. Handle `ClientRemovedEvent` for V2 by deleting the removed client's resource and referencing permissions.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Passkey error response crashes when identified user has no passwordless credentials — When the passkey credential disappears between render and submit, `fillContextForm` returns early without setting `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED`, so the error page throws on undefined `${isUserIdentified}` in `passkeys.ftl`. Set `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED` and `USER_VERIFICATION` before that early return in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`, or skip `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` in `createErrorResponse` for users without passwordless credentials.

getLoginPredicate() NPEs when IDP config is null — Because `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` can return null for IDPs created or updated via the admin API, operations that previously succeeded now throw NPEs in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.create/update`, returning 500 errors. Null-check `getConfig()` before reading `OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC`.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Table widgets render empty data when use-table-widget-visualization flag is on — With the flag on, `tableResultComponent` hardcodes empty `columns` and `tableData`, discarding `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, `fieldAliases`, and the loading state. Pass the real columns and result data into `TableWidgetVisualization`, or keep the previous renderer.

fetch_error_details pairs event IDs with node data positionally, misattributing error details — Because nodestore's `get_multi` appends cache-served values last and missing nodes are filtered out, `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs each `ErrorEvent` with another error's title, message, or timestamp. Iterate `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

Unvalidated `field` query params can 500 and drop error_ids from response — Unvalidated `field` params reach `generate_restricted_fieldset`, whose plain `item[field]` lookup raises `KeyError` for any name outside the replay fieldset, and a field list lacking `error_ids` makes `.get("error_ids", [])` return empty. Restrict accepted values or always pass `fields=["error_ids"]`.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Per-process SpansBuffer subsets inflate max-flush-segments budget to P× configured cap — Redis reads, in-flight memory, and Kafka produce volume can run P× beyond the `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` cap, and `any_shard_at_limit` backpressure weakens, because `flush_segments` derives `max_segments_per_shard` from `len(self.assigned_shards)` of each per-process subset. Thread the total shard count into each `SpansBuffer` so the budget uses the global shard factor.

submit() queries cluster-global Redis memory info once per buffer instead of once — Because `iter_cluster_memory_usage` scans every cluster node and all buffers share one client, each `get_memory_info()` call in `submit` returns identical data, so fanning out over `self.buffers` runs P redundant full-cluster INFO scans per batch.
