Query the memory info once, since it is not shard-scoped.

wait_produce timer uses "shards" tag instead of "shard" like sibling metrics — Dashboards and alerts slicing flusher metrics by `shard` silently miss the `wait_produce` series, which is filed under a `shards` tag unlike `produce` and `segment_size_bytes`. Use the `shard` tag key consistently.

Monkeypatched time.sleep makes the drift-change wait a no-op, risking flake — The `(msg,) = messages` unpack in `test_basic` depends on the flusher thread winning a scheduling race, because the `time.sleep(0.1)` wait calls the monkeypatched no-op `time.sleep` and never yields. Wait via an unpatched mechanism, as `test_flusher.py` does with a real `sleep`, or an explicit signal.

join() skips terminate() for remaining processes when deadline is exhausted — Remaining flusher processes can outlive `join()` and produce segments concurrently with a new strategy instance after a rebalance, duplicating Kafka output since segments are only removed in `done_flush_segments` after produce. On deadline exhaustion, skip the wait but still call `terminate()` on each process.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: AssignmentSource.queued default is a single module-import timestamp, not per-instance — Every `AssignmentSource` built by `from_integration` gets the worker's import-time timestamp, which `to_dict()` in sync.py serializes into outbound task payloads. Default `queued` to `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance captures its actual creation time.

Constant OAuth state allows forged callbacks to link attacker installation — The `state` is `pipeline.signature`, an md5 constant identical for every user and session, so the callback check binds to nothing — an attacker's `code` and `installation_id` can be forged into a victim's in-progress pipeline. Generate per-session state with `secrets.token_hex()` and `pipeline.bind_state()`, then validate with `pipeline.fetch_state()`.

Unverified installation linked when Integration row does not yet exist — When the async installation webhook is delayed, the `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch never verifies the installer, yet `pipeline.next_step()` links the installation anyway — letting an attacker race the webhook and link to a victim org. Fail closed by returning the `error()` page instead.

Unguarded `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError when sender metadata is missing — Because this pipeline never binds `sender` and `ensure_integration` replaces metadata wholesale on re-link, the field can be absent and `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError, a 500 crash. Use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and fail closed with `error()` when it is None.

get_user_info can raise HTTPError and crash setup with a 500 — Because `get_user_info` calls `raise_for_status()`, any non-2xx from api.github.com propagates as HTTPError into a 500 mid-install rather than the graceful `error()` page. Wrap the call and return `error()` on failure, mirroring the framework's callback handling.

Unwrapped token exchange crashes pipeline with 500 on network errors — Because the `safe_urlopen` exchange is unwrapped, a ConnectionError or ReadTimeout reaching github.com crashes the pipeline with a 500 instead of rendering the installation-failed page. Catch `ConnectionError`, `SSLError`, and `Timeout` and return `error()`, as `exchange_token` does.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` breaks `metric_alert_fire` detector processing — Making `build_occurrence_and_event_data` abstract leaves `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` uninstantiable, so `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` for `metric_alert_fire` detectors instead of the old no-op. Implement the abstract members with stub results or leave `detector_handler` unset until the stateful work lands.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Monitor context returns raw config, unused schedule_type transform is dead code — The `config` copy with its `schedule_type` display transform is dead code, so issue-occurrence `event_data` embeds the raw enum. Return `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config` in the dict.

Missing external calendar ID leaves updates without a destination — Without a selected calendar, updates may target an undefined or unintended calendar ID. Fall back to the destination calendar’s external ID when `externalCalendarId` is absent.

Missing destination calendar crashes Google Meet fallback — A Meet booking without a destination calendar crashes during event creation. Optional-chain `mainHostDestinationCalendar` so a missing destination follows the non-Google fallback.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.
isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Sync endpoint returns a Fetch Response instead of token data — Provider callers expect token data, so returning a Fetch `Response` leaves `token.access_token` undefined and breaks refresh. Parse the response and return the provider-shaped result, or update callers to consume a common parsed result.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Retry cleanup deletes reminders for non-SMS methods — Email and other non-SMS reminders can be deleted when their `retryCount` exceeds 1. Restrict this branch to `WorkflowMethods.SMS` as well.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Substring origin check accepts forged resize messages — An unrelated origin embedded in `discourseUrl` can send forged `discourse-resize` messages and change the frame height. Compare `e.origin` with the exact parsed origin of `discourseUrl`.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: downsize's geometry overload breaks width/height callers — `ResizeEmoji` still passes width, height, and options, which raises an argument-count error because Ruby replaces the earlier `downsize` definition. Keep one `downsize` method that accepts both call forms, or update all callers to use a geometry string.

Image downsize geometry does not constrain both dimensions — The generated `80%>` geometry does not bound both dimensions, so images may remain above the upload-size limit. Pass explicit dimensions or use a supported percentage geometry that constrains both axes.

Oversized images trigger repeated identical conversions — Repeated synchronous ImageMagick conversions consume CPU and delay uploads, even when each conversion leaves the target unchanged. Derive a target that converges in one bounded conversion, or avoid retrying with the same target.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Exact page counts report an extra page — Exact multiples show an empty extra page. Update `totalPages` to use the ceiling of `user_count / limit`.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Concurrent registrations can exceed the device limit — Make `CountDevices` and the insert atomic, using a transaction with appropriate serialization.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Legacy create is canceled when the request context ends — A client disconnect or completed request can cancel the legacy write, dropping the safety copy for a successful unified write. Derive the bounded context from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`.

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.
BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.
The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Access-token matcher rejects the expected grant shortcut — Correctly generated token IDs are rejected, while IDs with the wrong grant can pass. Reverse the conditional so only a matching `expectedGrantShortcut` is accepted.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.
Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.
The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Opted-in table widgets receive empty visualization data — Opted-in dashboard table widgets render blank because `TableWidgetVisualization` receives empty data and metadata. Pass `result.data` and `result.meta`, and derive `columns` from the widget query.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.
test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Google Meet bookings crash when destination calendars are empty or absent — Dereferencing `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` prevents the fallback to Cal Video when no destination is available. Restore optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` in this condition.

Video booking references lose credentials required for cancellation — Without `credentialId`, `handleCancelBooking` cannot delete dedicated video meetings when bookings are canceled. Preserve `result.credentialId` for video results as well as calendar results.

Secondary hosts use the organizer's destination calendar — The Office 365, Lark, and base calendar adapters select the first entry in `event.destinationCalendar`, sending secondary hosts' events to the wrong calendar. Pass only the current credential's `destination` in `event.destinationCalendar` when calling `createEvent`.

Missing calendar IDs break destination fallback for updates and deletions — For older references without `externalCalendarId`, the `selectedCalendar` fallback resolves to `primary`, causing updates to fail for events on other calendars. Restore the configured destination fallback in both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`.

Recurring collective cancellations repeat organizer deletions and skip hosts — Looping over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and selecting the first calendar reference repeats organizer deletions while leaving secondary hosts' events undeleted. Match each occurrence's `bookingRef` to `reference.type` and `credentialId`, then delete it using the already resolved host credential.

Collective host calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination — Optional chaining on a null `evt.destinationCalendar` silently discards every collected secondary-host destination. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to an empty array before appending `teamDestinationCalendars`.

Organization creation loses all slug sources when team billing is disabled — Without `slug` or `metadata.requestedSlug`, `createTeams` rejects the organization and `publish` has no slug to publish. Invert the `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition for the direct `slug` assignment so a slug source is always persisted.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team administrators are incorrectly forbidden from adding booking guests — An `ADMIN` who is neither the organizer nor an attendee receives `FORBIDDEN` because `isTeamAdminOrOwner` requires both predicates to pass. Use `isTeamAdmin` directly, since it authorizes both `ADMIN` and `OWNER` memberships, or combine it with `isTeamOwner` using OR.

Guest email casing bypasses the blacklist — An authorized attendee can invite a blocked address by changing its capitalization because `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the original casing against lowercase entries. Normalize guest addresses before blacklist comparison and persistence.

Duplicate guest inputs and concurrent requests create duplicate attendees — Repeated emails in `uniqueGuests` create duplicate attendee rows and invitations; concurrent requests do too because `Attendee` lacks booking/email uniqueness. Deduplicate normalized inputs server-side and enforce booking/email uniqueness atomically during insertion.

Guest notifications omit the booking's persisted calendar identity — When `booking.iCalUID` is omitted, `generateIcsString` falls back to `booking.uid`, potentially creating a separate invitation instead of updating the existing calendar event. Preserve `booking.iCalUID` when constructing `evt`.

Unbounded guest additions permit quadratic notification work — An unbounded `guests` array permits large attendee inserts and concurrent notifications, with quadratic aggregate work and attachment volume because each generated ICS includes every attendee. Enforce server-side guest-count and total-attendee limits before insertion and notification fanout.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Metadata lookup by directory key rejects valid app slugs — Valid apps such as `google-calendar` and `zoom` are rejected because `appStoreMetadata` uses directory keys `googlecalendar` and `zoomvideo`. Find the entry by its `slug`, or select the app's `dirName` and use it as the key.

Synchronized OAuth refresh returns a Response instead of token data — Returning a Fetch `Response` from `refreshOAuthTokens` breaks callers expecting `.data` or direct token properties when synchronization is enabled. Decode the response and adapt it to each caller's expected shape, or normalize both branches and update the callers together.

Sync token schema strips expiry and provider-specific fields — The computed keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` are literal strings, so expiry fields are stripped, breaking consumers such as Zoom's `newTokens.expires_in` calculation. Define `expires_in` and `expiry_date` explicitly and preserve provider-specific fields.

Safe-parse result is persisted instead of Google credential fields — Persisting the safe-parse wrapper returned by `parseRefreshTokenResponse` prevents `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` from loading the credential, even with synchronization disabled. Check `result.success`, throw `result.error` on failure, and persist `result.data` as `key`.

Zoho Bigin token refresh uses the credential ID as the user ID — Passing `credentialId` as `calcomUserId` requests tokens for the wrong principal or a nonexistent user. Thread `credential.userId` from `biginAuth` into this call, retaining `credentialId` for database updates.

Zoom token sync uses an unrecognized app slug — An endpoint resolving `appSlug` cannot find this integration because Zoom's metadata and installed credential use `zoom`, not `zoomvideo`; check `packages/app-store/zoomvideo/_metadata.ts`. Pass `zoom` instead of the directory name.

Undefined Prisma client breaks Salesforce client initialization — Salesforce client initialization fails because `prisma` is neither imported nor defined in this file. Import the client from `@calcom/prisma` before calling `prisma.credential.update`.

Salesforce token refresh bypasses external credential sharing — Credentials managed by an external platform cannot refresh through this direct `fetch` request when credential sharing and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are enabled. Route the operation through `refreshOAuthTokens` with the Salesforce slug and `credential.userId`.

Salesforce client refreshes tokens unconditionally but uses stale credentials — Every Salesforce service construction adds a token request and database update, yet the connection still uses the original `credentialKey` token. Refresh only when required and initialize the connection with the refreshed credentials.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Retry bookkeeping failures abort processing of remaining SMS reminders — If cancellation deletes a loaded reminder, `prisma.workflowReminder.update` throws inside `catch`, returning HTTP 500 and skipping remaining reminders. Use `prisma.workflowReminder.updateMany` to tolerate missing rows, and catch bookkeeping failures within the per-reminder error handler.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup-code login bypasses password verification when a TOTP code is supplied — A valid `backupCode` paired with any nonempty `totpCode` grants access to a password-based account without its password. Verify `credentials.password` for `IdentityProvider.CAL` accounts regardless of second-factor fields before entering the backup-code branch.

Concurrent logins can reuse or restore single-use backup codes — Unconditional writes to `backupCodes` let concurrent requests authenticate with the same code or restore another request’s consumed code. Consume codes atomically with a conditional update matching the previously read `user.backupCodes`, and reject or retry if no rows change.

Dismissing backup codes bypasses 2FA completion and leaves settings stale — Dismissing `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` with Escape or an outside click skips `onEnable`, leaving `viewer.me` and the settings switch stale after successful enablement. Make dismissal invoke `onEnable` and reset `EnableTwoFactorModal`, or prevent dismissal until the explicit Close action.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Unsanitized feed HTML allows stored XSS in imported posts and revisions — Feed authors can execute JavaScript in the forum’s origin because `absolutize_urls` preserves scripts and event handlers, while `Post.cook` returns `raw_html` verbatim. Sanitize imported HTML with explicit tag, attribute, and URL-scheme allowlists before storing posts or revisions.

Invalid Ruby in embed template prevents existing topics from rendering — Existing embedded topics fail to display comments because the conditionless `if` makes the template invalid Ruby. Replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>`.

Feed polling aborts on RSS entries without a content field — Valid RSS entries can lack `i.content`, causing `scrub` to abort polling before later entries are imported. Fall back to `i.content_encoded` or `i.description` before scrubbing, and explicitly skip entries with no body.

Imported URLs mishandle protocol-relative and path-relative references — Imported links and images break because `prefix` concatenation misroutes protocol-relative URLs and leaves path-relative URLs unresolved. Resolve `href` and `src` against the full article URL using `URI.join` instead.

Cold article requests repeatedly download and process the entire feed — Concurrent uncached article requests each invoke `Jobs::PollFeed`, multiplying full-feed downloads and per-entry database work despite the hourly schedule. Add a feed-wide cache or lock with a polling interval so different article URLs reuse a recent poll.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Empty embed category lookup aborts migration before fallback — Installations with an empty `embed_category` setting abort the migration because `execute(...)[0]['id']` accesses a missing result. Check for an empty result before reading `['id']` so the uncategorized fallback can run.

Migrated hosts retain schemes and paths that prevent host matching — Previously allowed hosts stop working after upgrade because `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares hostnames against migrated `h` values that may retain schemes or paths. Strip schemes and paths from `h` before inserting, matching the normalization in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`.

Host validation rejects valid top-level domains longer than five letters — Valid hosts such as `example.technology` can no longer be added or edited because `validates_format_of :host` caps top-level domains at five letters. Remove the upper length limit.

Uppercase URL hostnames fail to match allowed embedding hosts — URLs with uppercase hostnames are denied during embedding authorization and topic retrieval because `where` lowercases only the stored value. Lowercase `host` before binding it to the query.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Duplicate downsize definition breaks width-and-height callers — `Jobs::ResizeEmoji.execute` still passes five arguments, so replacing `self.downsize` makes emoji resizing raise `ArgumentError`. Keep one method that accepts both argument forms, or give the geometry-string variant a distinct name.

Fixed 10 MB limit rejects attachments allowed by site settings — Attachments permitted by `max_attachment_size_kb` can no longer pass client validation because `maxSizeKB` ignores that setting. Apply the new allowance only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

Oversized animated avatars lose animation under the thumbnail policy — `OptimizedImage.downsize` discards animation before `Upload.create_for` can apply `allow_animated_avatars` when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is disabled. Select the animation setting by upload type before downsizing.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Default member limit truncates the public group membership page — Users cannot reach members beyond the first 50 because the `group-members` route fetches once and its template has no pagination controls. Add pagination to the public page alongside the default `limit` change.

Page count adds an empty page when member count is a multiple of the limit — With exactly 50 members and a limit of 50, `totalPages` enables Next to an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and preserve the intended zero-member behavior.

Removing membership leaves the user's primary group reference intact — `PostSerializer.primary_group_name` can still identify the user with the removed group because `primary_group_id` remains unchanged. Clear the matching reference when removing membership, preserving the cleanup previously performed by `Group.destroy_deletions`.

Adding an existing group member violates the unique membership index — Retrying Add or including an existing member in a batch makes `Group.add` violate the unique `(group_id, user_id)` index. Skip existing memberships before insertion, preserving the set-difference behavior of `usernames=`.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Translation cache ignores site-dependent fallback chains — Users can receive stale or another site's fallback language because `translate_accelerator.rb` caches no-argument translations without accounting for `SiteSetting.default_locale`. Include the effective fallback chain in the cache key, or partition and invalidate cached translations when the chain changes.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Rejected devices bypass the limit through premature admission caching — A rejected device authenticates on retry because `tagDeviceUI` caches its ID before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, and cache hits skip admission checks. Cache IDs only after successful persistence, and prevent requests from treating in-flight cache entries as admission.

Omitting the device ID header bypasses the anonymous device limit — Anonymous authentication succeeds without a capacity check because `TagDevice` returns nil when `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is absent. When a limit is configured, enforce admission independently of this optional client-supplied header.

Concurrent device admissions can exceed the configured limit — Concurrent requests can both observe `deviceLimit - 1` through `CountDevices` and insert distinct devices, exceeding the configured limit. Serialize capacity checks and admissions with a database-level lock or equivalent atomic mechanism that works across Grafana instances.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Request cancellation can interrupt asynchronous legacy writes — Request cancellation can stop the legacy goroutine's SQL work before replication completes, also affecting `Update`, `Delete`, and `DeleteCollection`. Apply `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before `context.WithTimeoutCause` to preserve namespace and requester values while retaining the ten-second timeout.

Legacy updates replay patches against potentially stale objects — Passing the original `objInfo` lets `d.Legacy.Update` apply patches to stale data, preserving field values that differ from the successful unified write. Pass an `updateWrapper` containing a deep copy of `res` instead of replaying the original transformation.

Unified Create and Update failures are attributed to legacy storage metrics — Calling `recordLegacyDuration` when unified `Create` or `Update` fails blames a backend that was never called and hides the actual failure in storage metrics. Use `recordStorageDuration` for both unified-storage error paths.

Legacy DeleteCollection metrics are attributed to unified storage — Using `recordStorageDuration` for the `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` result duplicates the unified observation, misattributes legacy errors, and leaves legacy collection metrics empty. Record this observation with `recordLegacyDuration`.

Resource names cause unbounded delete histogram cardinality — Using `name` as the histogram's kind label permanently retains a series for each distinct deleted resource, increasing exporter memory and scrape cardinality. Pass `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration` instead, matching the other observations.

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: TotalDocs can race with index creation and crash the process — An event can trigger `BuildIndex` while `TotalDocs` iterates the cache, crashing the process with a concurrent map iteration/write error. Protect the cache iteration in `TotalDocs` in `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go` with `cacheMu.RLock`.

Concurrent builds can overwrite an index containing processed events — A search and `handleEvent` can build separate indexes when `GetIndex` returns nil during construction, allowing a slower snapshot to replace processed events and leave results stale. Coordinate cache lookup and construction per key so callers reuse one completed index while different keys build in parallel.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Delete is hidden for Grafana list rows without a ruler DTO — Users with delete permission lose Delete in grouped and filtered lists because those rows supply only `promRule`, while the menu requires `canDelete && rulerRule`. Render deletion from the editable identifier and group, and update the callback contract to avoid requiring a ruler DTO.

Pause action remains hidden for Grafana list rules without a ruler DTO — Grafana list users cannot pause rules because the menu still requires `rulerRule` and passes it to `MenuItemPauseRule`, despite the Prometheus pause ability. Update the rendering condition and `MenuItemPauseRule` to accept the Prometheus rule or fetch the ruler DTO on demand.

Silence notifications does nothing for Grafana rules with only a Prometheus DTO — Clicking Silence notifications has no effect because `RuleActionsButtons.V2` requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` to render the drawer, but only `promRule` is supplied. Update `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` to accept a UID and pass the Prometheus rule UID directly.

Export is unavailable for Grafana-managed recording rules — Grafana-managed recording rules lose Export in the Prometheus-only list because `AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport` uses `isAlertingRule`, unlike the previous ruler-based ability. Use the Grafana rule predicate rather than the alerting-only predicate for export support.

Skipped Grafana rule checks incorrectly grant abilities — Users with Grafana create permission regain Duplicate for plugin-provided rules because an absent `rule`, including from `skipToken`, grants abilities through the OR merge in `AlertRuleMenu`. Return unsupported abilities when `rule` is absent so skipped Grafana checks cannot enable actions.

CombinedRule abilities lose the federation guard for immutable rules — Legacy list buttons now offer Edit for federated Mimir rules because `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated` to false and no longer receives `rule.group`. Preserve the group's federation state when calculating `CombinedRule` abilities.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Client-credentials tokens encode an unknown grant type — Decoding returns unknown instead of `client_credentials` because `ClientCredentialsGrantType.process` calls `generateAccessToken()` without setting `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, bypassing `createTokenResponse()`. Set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on that path before token generation.

Token ID matcher checks the wrong grant characters and inverts equality — The event expectations cannot detect incorrect grant encoding because the matcher reads the wrong characters and rejects matching grants. Validate that `items[0]` has six characters, then reject when `substring(4, 6)` does not equal `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Exception assertion races with the reader's in-flight request — The test can miss a concurrent-access error if a pending request adds to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion passes. Retain the reader thread and join it after signaling termination, before inspecting `caughtExceptions`.

Group deletion failures leave the non-daemon reader running — If `remove()` throws, the reader keeps issuing requests, potentially blocking JVM shutdown and interfering with later tests. Put `deletedAll.set(true)` and reader cleanup in a `finally` block around deletion.

Overlapping prefix and suffix matching crashes HTML validation — When the sanitizer appends a closing element, overlapping prefix and suffix matches make `substring` throw, preventing the Maven verifier from collecting remaining diagnostics. Bound `end` by each string’s remaining length after subtracting `start`.

Java-format placeholders break multivalued-size errors in both UIs — Users see literal placeholders and ChoiceFormat text because `ThemeResource` returns these strings unchanged and `setUserProfileServerError` uses i18next interpolation. Keep `error-invalid-multivalued-size` compatible with i18next placeholders and supported pluralization in both account and admin UI bundles.

ChoiceFormat normalization hides HTML in translation branches — Unchecked HTML can reach verification emails through `LinkExpirationFormatterMethod`, and the runtime sanitizer permits external HTTPS links. In `VerifyMessageProperties`, preserve and validate HTML inside ChoiceFormat branches, exempting only numeric choice operators instead of replacing entire expressions.

Lithuanian login and account OTP instructions are in Italian — Lithuanian users receive Italian OTP installation instructions from `loginTotpStep1` and the account bundle’s `totpStep1`. Replace both values with Lithuanian instructions while keeping embedded links removed.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: Global client view grants bypass client-specific permission denials — An all-clients `view` grant overrides client-specific denials through `canView(client)` and bypasses object checks in `ClientsResource.getClients()`. Separate global role-based access from policy-based grants, and evaluate object-specific permissions before accepting the all-clients fallback.

Global manage permission fails client-scope listing and viewing guards — Administrators with only all-clients `manage` cannot list client scopes or read realm default scopes, despite authorization by `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` and `canView(ClientScopeModel)`. Update `canView()` so inherited `canListClientScopes()` and `canViewClientScopes()` recognize global `manage` alongside `view`.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Passkey-only users receive an unusable password challenge in the keycloak theme — Accepting passkey-only users in `PasswordForm` leaves them unable to authenticate with the `keycloak` theme because `base/login/login-password.ftl` never renders `passkeys.conditionalUIData`. Add the passkeys macro to that base template, not just `keycloak.v2`, so those users can complete authentication.

Cache expansion republishes invalidated login results under a fresh revision — Removed login eligibility or organization associations can remain cached if another transaction invalidates `query` before its searches are copied into `IdentityProviderListQuery`. Validate the previous revision before reusing searches, or omit them and pass `startupRevision` to `cache.addRevisioned`.

Organization-disabled providers can retain stale login cache membership — Setting `hideOnLogin=true` while an organization is disabled can leave a provider cached and expose it when the organization is re-enabled, because `original.isEnabled()` already returns false. Copy `original` and `updated` into plain `IdentityProviderModel` instances before applying `getLoginPredicate()` to compare persisted eligibility.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Table visualization receives empty data and columns instead of query results — Organizations with `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled see an empty table despite populated `tableResults`. Pass the current result’s data and metadata to `TableWidgetVisualization` and derive its columns from the widget fields.

Attribute query cache key omits organization identity — Switching organizations with identical projects and date filters can briefly show the previous organization’s attributes because `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys` fetches organization-specific data. Include the organization slug in `queryKey` to preserve cache isolation.

Hidden attributes remain visible when the search is empty — `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` remain visible by default because an empty search returns `sorted` before applying `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES`. Apply the exclusion before the empty-search return.

Mismatched timestamp units place errors out of chronological order — Errors can appear before earlier recording events because `error_events` timestamps use seconds while `event` timestamps use milliseconds. Multiply `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"]` by 1000 before comparing it with `event.get("timestamp", 0)`.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Process type guard skips hung spawn workers before replacement — Hung children can resume alongside replacements and process the same shards because the `multiprocessing.Process` guard rejects `SpawnProcess` instances created by `self.mp_context.Process`. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, then kill and join the old child before replacing its handle.

Expired join deadline skips cleanup of remaining flusher processes — Old flushers can remain running during partition reassignment when `next_step.join(timeout)` or an earlier child exhausts the deadline and `join` skips subsequent children. Apply `remaining_time` only to waiting, and clean up every child even after the deadline expires.

Memory backpressure repeats cluster-wide Redis sweeps for every process — Each submission performs one synchronous cluster-wide Redis sweep per flusher process because `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` queries the shared cluster regardless of assigned shards. Fetch memory information from a single buffer instead of querying every buffer in `self.buffers`.
