GitHub installation identity check uses mutable usernames — Comparing GitHub's mutable `login` with `sender.login` lets a different account that later claims the old username pass after the original user renames their account. Persist `authenticated_user_info["id"]` and compare it with `integration.metadata["sender"]["id"]`, using GitHub's immutable account IDs.

Missing sender metadata raises KeyError during GitHub installation — An active integration from `build_integration` can lack sender state when no `OrganizationIntegration` exists, so indexing `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises `KeyError` and turns a retry into a 500. Use a guarded sender lookup and return the invalid-installation error when sender metadata is absent.

GitHub OAuth request failures escape dispatch and cause a 500 — Because `safe_urlopen` and `get_user_info` run outside the parsing `try`, connection, SSL, timeout, and `/user` non-2xx failures escape `dispatch` and produce a 500. Catch upstream request exceptions around both calls and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` instead.

OAuth token request omits the authorization redirect_uri — Omitting `redirect_uri` from `data` violates OAuth 2.0's requirement to repeat the authorization value and allows GitHub to reject the token exchange. Add the identical `redirect_uri` computed for the authorization request.

Wrong OAuth state prevents test_installation_not_found from exercising the 404 — `test_installation_not_found` exits at the state-mismatch branch because it uses `ddd023...`, so it passes without reaching the intended GitHub installation 404. Use the `9cae...` signature from `assert_setup_flow` and assert the `The GitHub installation could not be found.` response.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated — `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` when instantiating the handler registered on `MetricAlertFire`, preventing detector evaluation. Implement `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, or keep `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` on the concrete `DetectorHandler` base until its stateful implementation exists.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Optional-chain missing on mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration — Reading `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining crashes `EventManager.create` when the entry is absent. Add the `?.` to safely short-circuit.

updateEvent fallback returns undefined calendarId when externalCalendarId missing — The `.find` filter can never match when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the request ships `calendarId: undefined` and fails. Mirror `selectedCalendar`'s fallback to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` via destructuring.

deleteEvent falls back to undefined calendar when externalCalendarId is null — The same broken `.find` in `deleteEvent` forwards `calendarId: undefined` and targets nothing. Destructure `mainHostDestinationCalendar` first and combine with `externalCalendarId`, respecting the existing `defaultCalendarId` guard.

teamDestinationCalendars duplicates accumulate in handleNewBooking — `handleNewBooking` pushes `teamDestinationCalendars` for each member without deduping, so duplicates grow on collective events. Skip insertion when `user.destinationCalendar?.id` already exists in the array.

destinationCalendar falls back to empty instead of user.destinationCalendar — Without a fallback to `bookingToReschedule.user?.destinationCalendar`, reschedule emails and webhook payloads ship `destinationCalendar: []`. Mirror the sibling handlers' pattern before defaulting to an empty array.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team admin-or-owner check uses && instead of ||, blocking admins — `isTeamAdminOrOwner` wrongly rejects team ADMINs who aren't OWNERs because `&&` reduces the check to OWNER-only. Combine the two predicates with `||` so admins are authorized.

addGuests handler stores newly added guests with an empty name — Newly added guests stored with `name: ""` produce malformed headers like ` <guest@example.com>` in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and drop the attendee name in `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`. Derive a display name from the email's local part instead.

sendAddGuestsEmails uses unfiltered guests instead of uniqueGuests — `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `email-manager.ts` reclassifies existing attendees as new when `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives the un-filtered `guests` list, sending them a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests` so they only get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

addGuestsHandler TOCTOU race on attendee email uniqueness — Two concurrent calls can both pass the filter and insert duplicate attendees since `Attendee` in `schema.prisma` lacks a unique `(bookingId, email)` constraint. Re-read and re-filter inside a `prisma.$transaction` so the check and `createMany` are atomic.

isInvalidEmail persists across retries and re-appears on edit — The inline error stays visible across retries and re-appears alongside an `onError` toast because `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is never cleared. Reset it at the top of `handleAdd` so it reflects only the latest validation.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: parseRefreshTokenResponse schema uses computed keys instead of catchall — Computed keys become literal `'ZodString'` rather than a catch-all, so real provider responses with `refresh_token`/`expiry_date` fail validation and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).catchall(z.number())` so arbitrary keys are accepted.

refreshOAuthTokens returns inconsistent shapes across branches — Sync returns a `Response` while no-sync returns `refreshFunction`'s result, and `CalendarService.ts` consumers read `.data`/`.expiresIn` unconditionally, so toggling `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` crashes refresh for those four integrations. Normalize both branches to the same shape before returning.

Race condition in credential findFirst/update/create webhook handler — Two concurrent webhooks for the same `(userId, appSlug)` can both miss the lookup and race to `create`, producing duplicate or failed rows. Replace `findFirst`/`update`/`create` with a single `prisma.credential.upsert` keyed on the unique `(userId, appId)` constraint.

Webhook secret check misses headers due to missing toLowerCase on key — Node lowercases incoming header keys, so a non-lowercase `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` silently breaks verification and effectively disables the webhook. Normalize the lookup key via `.toLowerCase()` before reading `req.headers`.

Pass user id, not credential id, to refreshOAuthTokens — Passing `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` causes the admin sync endpoint to receive the credential row's id as `calcomUserId` and resolve the wrong principal (or reject). Pass `credential.userId` to the third argument of `refreshOAuthTokens`.

Salesforce refresh path returns Connection with stale access_token/instance_url — The returned `jsforce.Connection` still reads `accessToken`/`instanceUrl` from the stale `credentialKey`, so `this.conn` resolves to an expired connection while the DB holds fresh tokens. Pass `accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and `instanceUrl: accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url` when constructing the `Connection`.
Refresh token fallback writes literal "refresh_token" instead of previous token — Set the fallback to `response.refresh_token` or omit the override.

Webhook handler must not 500 on invalid JSON body or decryption failure — `safeParse` and `JSON.parse`/`symmetricDecrypt` throw on bad input and bubble up as Next.js 500s instead of structured errors. Switch to `safeParse` returning `res.status(400).json(...)`, and wrap `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` to return the same 400 on failure.

Webhook secret compared with !== is vulnerable to timing attacks — `!==` short-circuits on length and the first differing byte, letting attackers recover the secret character-by-character via request latency. Compare equal-length `Buffer`s with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Non-atomic retryCount increment risks under concurrent cron workers — Concurrent cron workers can both read the same snapshot and overwrite each other's `retryCount` write, leaving retries stuck at 1. Use Prisma's atomic `increment: 1` in both `prisma.workflowReminder.update` calls instead of `reminder.retryCount + 1`.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: TOCTOU race in backup-code consumption allows single-use code reuse — The read-modify-write of `backupCodes` is non-atomic, so two concurrent logins both pass `indexOf` before either `prisma.user.update` commits and the same code authenticates twice. Switch to an atomic update conditioned on the prior encrypted value, or store codes individually so DELETE-by-value is atomic.

Unguarded body.backupCodes dereference crashes DisplayBackupCodes render — In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, `handleSetup` calls `body.backupCodes.map` without verifying the field exists, so a malformed response throws inside the catch and leaves the user at an empty `DisplayBackupCodes`. Guard with `Array.isArray(body.backupCodes)` before mapping, or route to the error branch.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: raw post.cooked renders unsanitized HTML in embed iframe — Embedding unsanitized `post.cooked` from `Post#cook` allows `<script>` injection (ruby-readability preserves event handlers), so a malicious embeddable_host can run JS in Discourse's origin and steal session cookies. Sanitize raw_html posts through PrettyText or escape here and only unescape known-safe subtrees, using `post.cookedHtml`.

poll_feed loop aborts batch on any per-item error — Any per-item failure in `poll_feed`'s `rss.items.each` loop (e.g. `i.content.scrub` raising `NoMethodError`) drops every remaining item for that hour because `retry: false` swallows the abort. Wrap each iteration in `begin/rescue`, log the exception, and also rescue `Errno::ECONNREFUSED`/`SocketError` around `open()`.
PollFeed runs synchronously inside RetrieveTopic worker — Enqueue it instead via `Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)` so the retriever only schedules the work and returns.

Use URI.open instead of Kernel#open to avoid shell evaluation — Using `Kernel#open` to fetch the feed URL retains shell semantics and executes strings starting with `|`, including any value later typed into `feed_polling_url` in the admin UI. Switch to `URI.open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` so the input is unambiguously treated as a URI.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: SQL injection via unsanitized embeddable_hosts interpolation — The `execute` call interpolates `embeddable_hosts` setting values into raw SQL, so any host containing a quote, backslash, or `'),'` either crashes the migration or injects unintended statements. Switch to `sanitize_sql_array` with placeholders so values are bound, not concatenated.

Migration crashes when embed_category site_setting is missing — The first `execute("... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` dereferences `[0]` with no guard, so a missing `embed_category` site_setting raises NoMethodError before the `uncategorized_category_id` fallback runs. Stash the row in a local, check `cmd_tuples > 0`, and default to 0 when absent.

before_validation crashes when host is nil — `before_validation` chains two `self.host.sub!` calls, so a nil `host` raises NoMethodError before `validates_format_of` ever runs. Guard with `return unless host.is_a?(String)` so the callback is a safe no-op when the attribute hasn't been assigned.

Admin::EmbeddingController#update does no persistence, just re-renders — `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` re-renders the `OpenStruct` without persisting, so any PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` returns 200 while changing nothing. Drop the route and the action, or make it perform the work the API expects.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

findings.description: Flex container placed on .contents instead of .row breaks header fallback — In the noscript fallback template, `.title` and `.panel` are inside a regular `.row` block, so `margin-left: auto` and `order: 3` on `.panel` are no-ops and the right alignment breaks. Apply the flex declarations to `.row` instead of `.contents`, or keep `float: right` on `.panel` for non-Ember pages.

goldensDetail.text: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Duplicate self.downsize definitions make 4-arg emoji callers fail — Ruby keeps only the last `self.downsize`, so the 5-arg call from `resize_emoji.rb` raises `ArgumentError`. Delete the obsolete 4-arg definition so emoji resize jobs run.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: `update` renames group to "" when an empty name param is posted — A blank `params[:name]` is truthy in Ruby, so `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` overwrites the group's name with `""` and fails the 422 on `group.save`. Switch the guard to `params[:name].present?` to match the `alias_level` style on the line above.

add_members drops usernames with surrounding whitespace — `add_members` splits on commas but `User.find_by_username` matches `username_lower`, so a token like `" bob"` returns `nil` and that user is silently dropped while the invite appears to succeed. Trim each token with `username.strip` before the lookup.

remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb for DELETE-only route — The first `.remove_member` example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member` even though the route registers `delete "members"`, masking that the endpoint is DELETE-only and tempting readers to copy the wrong verb. Change the line to `xhr :delete, :remove_member, …` to match the `is able to remove a member` example.

totalPages reports an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit — `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which yields a phantom page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` and pushes `offset` past the data on `next`. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` so the pager only lists pages with content.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: FallbackLocaleList#[] mixes String and Symbol, defeating uniq — `Array#uniq` can't deduplicate the mixed `String`/`Symbol` identifiers returned here, so `I18n.ensure_loaded!` parses the same `\.en\.yml$` files and merges into `@translations[:en]` twice on every boot. Normalize with `locale.to_sym` before the `uniq.compact` so each locale loads only once.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Race between device-count check and insert can exceed deviceLimit — Concurrent inserts in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` bypass `deviceLimit` because `CountDevices` and the `INSERT … ON CONFLICT` run as separate statements. Wrap both in a single `WithTransactionalDbSession` at SERIALIZABLE, or push the cap into a conditional `INSERT` that aborts when the count threshold is met.

Cache device key before DB write allows bypass of device limit — `tagDeviceUI` writes to `a.localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs, so a request rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` still authenticates from cache during the TTL. Move `localCache.SetDefault` after a successful DB write (or invalidate the key on error).

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description:
Double-checked locking missing second check of cache under exclusive lock — Every goroutine queued behind the exclusive lock performs a redundant read of `assets-manifest.json` and blocks concurrent `RLock()` callers. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` after `Lock()` and return it when non-nil.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48-52`
Async legacy write goroutines inherit request context and short-circuit — Detach them with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying the timeout, so the safety net actually finishes writing.

Storage delete success metric is labeled by object name, inflating cardinality — Labeling the storage histogram with `name` instead of `options.Kind` on the delete success path creates a new Prometheus time series per object, risking Prometheus OOM. Pass `options.Kind` to `d.recordStorageDuration` so the label stays low-cardinality.

Misclassifying storage failure as legacy in DualWriterMode3.Create — A failed storage call is recorded into the legacy histogram, which corrupts the `dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds` metric used by monitoring. Change `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` to `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` so the timing reflects the call that actually failed.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-131`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:161-167`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: BuildIndex drops lock around index creation causing same-key race — Dropping the function-level `b.cacheMu` lock from `BuildIndex` lets two concurrent callers missing the cache both invoke `bleve.New` and `idx.Flush()` on the same disk directory, risking on-disk corruption. Capture the lock, ideally a per-key lock, around the full construction so only one goroutine builds a given key.

NewResourceServer blocks synchronously on Init including search indexing — `NewResourceServer` now synchronously runs `s.Init(ctx)`, which triggers `s.search.init(ctx)` to build all search indexes from `GetResourceStats` before returning. Run `Init` asynchronously (e.g. `go s.Init(s.ctx)`) so every caller—like `pkg/storage/unified/sql/server.go`—no longer blocks on indexing.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.
The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: AccessTokenContext constructor re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId — Replace `grantType` with `rawTokenId` in that null check.

AccessTokenContext constructor uses grantType instead of rawTokenId in null check — The blank-check passes `grantType` while its message names `rawTokenId`, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted silently. Pass `rawTokenId` to the `Objects.requireNonNull` argument instead.

isAccessTokenId has inverted and mis-indexed grant-type check — The `isAccessTokenId` matcher in `AssertEvents` uses `substring(3, 5)` and a non-negated equality, so the grant check always passes and every well-formed token matches. Change to `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` to fix the off-by-index and the inversion.

**Also found in:**
- `testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:30-35`
ANCHOR_PATTERN matches any tag starting with 'a', not only anchor tags — Tighten it to `|/>)` so only real ``/`` tokens match.

verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException for English file, bypassing Mojo error handling — A missing English file in `verifySafeHtml` aborts the Maven build with an unhandled stack trace because `verify` only catches `IOException`. Throw `MojoExecutionException` so the failure flows through `ThemeVerifierMojo.execute`'s normal validation channel.

santizeAnchors reports a failure but caller still adds an overlapping illegal-HTML message — When `santizeAnchors` flags an anchor mismatch, `verifySafeHtml` still sanitizes the same string, so each bad key produces two overlapping messages ('Didn't find anchor…' and 'Illegal HTML in key…'). Have `santizeAnchors` signal failure (e.g. return null) so the caller skips the redundant sanitize.

santizeAnchors strips a stale match because the matcher is anchored to the original value — In `santizeAnchors`, the matcher stays bound to the original `value` while `replaceFirst` mutates it, so the substring stripped is no longer the one just visited. Rebuild the matcher each iteration, or collect anchors first and apply them on a fresh pass.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: getEvaluationContext is dead code in ClientPermissionsV2 — Remove the method or wire it through an actual V2 token-exchange evaluator before publishing.

registerListener gate uses V1 only, dropping V2-only setups — In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the gate checks only V1's `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`, so V2-only deployments never call `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` on role/client/group removal and orphan permission resources. Match `MgmtPermissions.java:85` by checking `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ || ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: createErrorResponse calls fillContextForm without guarding null/empty authenticators — `fillContextForm` may return early (null) when authenticators are empty, skipping `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED`, `USER_VERIFICATION`, `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS`, and `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` and breaking client-side `initAuthenticate`. Guard the call with a null/empty-authenticators check and populate those attributes directly.

getForLogin misses organization invalidation guard used in getByOrganization — Login cache subsets outlive their organization because `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)` while sibling `getByOrganization` also guards on the org id. Add the `isInvalid(organizationId)` check (and call `cache.invalidateObject` for the affected subset) so removed or updated orgs evict their login IDP entries.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description:
TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty columns, data, meta, and renderer — Every org with `use-table-widget-visualization` sees a blank widget because the new branch hardcodes `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData`. Pass `widget.queries[i]?.fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta` through from the loading-state branch above.

**Also found in:**
- `static/app/views/dashboards/widgetCard/chart.tsx:164-175`
validate_timestamp/validate_age truthiness check treats age=0/timestamp=0 as absent — Replace it with `is not None` so a real zero is still validated.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: SpanFlusher silently produces zero workers for non-positive max_processes — A negative `max_processes` produces zero workers because `min(-1, ...)` and `range(-1)` yield empty dicts, so `_create_processes()` is a no-op and backpressure checks silently skip. Guard in `__init__` against `max_processes < 1` and validate `--flusher-processes` via `IntRange(min=1)`.

Avoid redundant Redis cluster memory queries in submit — Each `get_memory_info` call fans out `cluster.info()` across all Redis nodes, so looping `self.buffers.values()` issues N identical cluster-wide queries per submit. Query the cluster once via `next(iter(self.buffers.values())).get_memory_info()` and reuse the result.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at class definition — Every `AssignmentSource` instance shares the timestamp captured at class definition, so later `from_integration()` calls see a stale value. Switch `queued` to `field(default_factory=lambda: timezone.now())` so each instance records its own construction time.

OAuthLoginView swallows exceptions only after the network call — `safe_urlopen` in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` runs outside the `try/except`, so a missing `code` or network errors surface as 500s instead of the friendly page. Move the `try` above `safe_urlopen` to mirror `OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token` in oauth2.py.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler will raise TypeError on instantiation — `Detector.detector_handler` (detector.py) catches instantiation in `try/except logger.exception`, so `MetricAlertDetectorHandler`'s new `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` base raises `TypeError` (missing `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`) that's silently swallowed, blocking metric-alert detection. Restore `DetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` or stub the three methods.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Null dereference on empty destinationCalendar in Meet location fallback — Reading `integration` on undefined `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws and breaks the Meet location fallback. Guard the access with `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` before comparing.

destinationCalendar null fallback drops collective host calendars — Collective events silently lose host calendars when `evt.destinationCalendar` starts as `null` because the optional push never runs. Initialize it to `[]` and push `teamDestinationCalendars` without optional chaining.

Inverted organization slug condition stores slug in wrong billing mode — Organizations store the physical `slug` in the wrong billing mode and break the `requestedSlug` workflow. Spread `slug` only when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.

loadUsers fallback can return undefined causing TypeError on non-team bookings — Non-team bookings crash with a TypeError when `eventType.users` is undefined because callers use `users.length` and `users.slice`. Return `eventType.users || []` as the fallback.

updateEvent selectedCalendar fallback is dead and leaves calendarId undefined — `selectedCalendar` stays undefined because the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar` with a falsy `externalCalendarId` and never matches. Fall back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` for `calendarId` resolution.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:314-318`

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team admin/owner check requires both roles instead of either — Legitimate admins or owners get denied with `FORBIDDEN` because almost nobody holds both roles. Change the `&&` in `isTeamAdminOrOwner` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` to `||`.

Case-sensitive guest email checks bypass blacklist and allow duplicates — Uppercased emails bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` and create duplicate `Attendee` rows via case variants. Normalize `guest` with `toLowerCase()` before comparing against `blacklistedGuestEmails` and `attendee.email` and store the lowercased value.

Calendar update uses requester credentials instead of organizer — Guests appear in the DB but the organizer's calendar never updates when another allowed user adds them via `EventManager`. Fetch credentials with `getUsersCredentials` for `booking.userId` and build `EventManager` from the organizer instead of `ctx.user`.

Attendees committed to DB before calendar update with no rollback — A failure in `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` after `prisma.booking.update` leaves `Attendee` rows without calendar updates. Run the calendar update before the DB write or wrap both in a transaction, as in `editLocation.handler`.

sendAddGuestsEmails uses original guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests — Duplicates or blacklisted emails cause `sendAddGuestsEmails` to misclassify attendees and send the wrong email type. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

Unguarded attendees[0].name access crashes email when guest list empty — An empty `attendees` array makes `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` throw and the email fails after the DB write. Guard it with `attendees[0]?.name` falling back to `organizer.name`.

Unbounded guests array allows DB and email fan-out exhaustion — An unbounded `guests` array lets an attacker fan out hundreds of DB writes and emails via `ZAddGuestsInputSchema`. Add a `.max()` limit and normalize with `trim`/`toLowerCase` on `guests`.

Duplicate guest emails allowed in ZAddGuestsInputSchema — Duplicate emails in `guests` slip through `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` and `createMany` inserts duplicate `Attendee` rows. Enforce uniqueness on `guests` with a `Set`-based refine and normalize before filtering `uniqueGuests`.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys break token response validation — Valid token responses with expiry fields are rejected, breaking sync for every calendar provider. Replace the computed keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` with `passthrough()` and validate expiry with `refine`.

Credential key stored as SafeParse wrapper breaks Google calendar refresh — The stored credential becomes a wrapper object so the next `googleCredentialSchema` parse fails and sync breaks after the first refresh. Check `success` on the result of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` and persist `parsed.data` as `key`.

Sync OAuth refresh returns raw fetch Response instead of parsed token — Callers expecting `res.data` get `undefined` and throw on `access_token` access. Parse `response` with `json()` inside `refreshOAuthTokens` and return a normalized object with `data`.

refreshOAuthTokens receives credentialId instead of userId — The sync endpoint receives the wrong principal and fails lookup or syncs the token for the wrong user. Pass `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens` instead of `credentialId`.

Unhandled decrypt/JSON parse exception causes 500 and stack leak — A malformed payload or wrong `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` throws unhandled and leaks a 500 stack trace. Wrap `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` in `try/catch` and return 400, using `safeParse` for validation.

Salesforce token refresh incorrectly checks statusText instead of response.ok — Valid 200s are rejected as errors and some 4xx pass through because `statusText` is implementation-dependent. Check `response.ok` instead of `response.statusText` for `HttpError`.

Webhook auth missing method check and timing-safe secret comparison — Credentials can be overwritten via non-POST verbs and secret comparison leaks timing while mixed-case headers fail to match. Enforce `req.method` is `POST`, lowercase the header name from `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`, and compare with `timingSafeEqual`.

Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError on Salesforce token refresh — Every refresh throws `ReferenceError` and breaks all Salesforce calendar operations. Add `prisma` import from `@calcom/prisma` in `CalendarService.ts`.

Salesforce connection uses stale token after refresh — The persisted token is updated but the returned connection still uses the expired `credentialKey` and fails immediately with 401. Build `jsforce.Connection` from `accessTokenParsed.data` instead.

Missing refresh_token replaced with literal string corrupts persisted credential — The literal `refresh_token` is persisted and then used as a real token, causing every later refresh to fail with `invalid_grant`. Preserve the original `refresh_token` from the credential instead of assigning a placeholder string.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: SMS cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders via unscoped retryCount filter — Reminders for other channels with `retryCount` above 1 get silently pruned by this SMS cron and lose scheduled retries. Move `method` outside the `OR` so both branches are scoped to `WorkflowMethods.SMS`.

SMS retryCount not incremented when message or sendTo missing — A reminder with missing `message` or `sendTo` stays `scheduled:false` forever with unchanged `retryCount` and is refetched each run without ever reaching the deletion threshold. Add an `else` for the `message`/`sendTo` check to increment `retryCount` there as well.

Concurrent retryCount updates lose increments via read-modify-write — Concurrent runs read the same `reminder.retryCount` and both write `+1`, so one increment is lost and the deletion threshold is missed. Use `increment: 1` for `retryCount` instead of snapshot arithmetic in both update paths.

Unhandled retryCount update rejection aborts SMS reminder loop — A transient failure from `prisma.workflowReminder.update` escapes and aborts the loop, skipping remaining reminders and leaving the cron without a response. Wrap the `retryCount` increment in its own `try/catch` that only logs and continues.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Password bypass via backup code with dummy TOTP code — An attacker with only email and a `backupCode` can authenticate by adding any `totpCode` to skip the `verifyPassword` check. Always verify `credentials.password` against `user.password` before entering the `backupCode` branch.

Non-string backupCode triggers TypeError crash instead of 400 — A non-string `req.body.backupCode` makes `replaceAll` throw `TypeError` and returns 500 instead of 400. Guard with a `typeof` check for `req.body.backupCode` before `replaceAll` and return `ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode`, also check `next-auth-options.ts`.

Race condition allows backup code reuse via non-atomic check-then-update — Concurrent requests can both pass the `indexOf` check on `backupCodes` before either nulls `backupCodes[index]` and reuse a single-use code. Replace `prisma.user.update` with an atomic `updateMany` filtered on `backupCodes` or a transaction and reject if no rows were updated.

Default export named TwoFactor in BackupCode.tsx breaks identity — Duplicate `TwoFactor` displayName hides the component in DevTools and breaks HMR. Rename the default export in `BackupCode.tsx` to `BackupCode`.

Backup codes ObjectURL leak on modal unmount retains Blob memory — The last `backupCodesUrl` from `URL.createObjectURL` is never revoked if the modal unmounts without a new setup, leaking `Blob` memory. Add a `useEffect` cleanup and revoke `backupCodesUrl` on close with `URL.revokeObjectURL`.

resetState retains backup codes, secret and ObjectURL after close — Plaintext `backupCodes`, `secret`, `dataUri` and `backupCodesUrl` stay in memory after the dialog hides because `open` only hides it. Clear and revoke them in `resetState` with `URL.revokeObjectURL` and on unmount.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: Org scope misses direct members when org has no child teams — Direct members' personal bookings are excluded from insights, under-reporting org data. Remove the `teamsFromOrg.length` guard in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and always query `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` using `teamIds`.

Team scope allows missing teamId and silently returns no results — Callers get empty data with no error, masking a missing `teamId` misconfiguration. Make `teamId` required when `scope` is `'team'` in `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` and throw via `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.parse` instead of falling back to `NOTHING_CONDITION`.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in postMessage targetOrigin — `request.referer` is attacker-controlled and can break the JS string to execute code, and the full URL is rejected as a `targetOrigin`. Serialize it with `to_json` on `URI.parse(request.referer).origin` instead.

Stored XSS via unsanitized raw_html cook bypass — External feed HTML stored with `cook_method` set to `raw_html` bypasses sanitization and executes in every embed view. Sanitize `raw` via `Sanitize.clean` or route it through the normal `cook` pipeline before storing.

Inverted origin check allows spoofed postMessage origins — Any attacker origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl` is accepted while legitimate origins with a path are rejected. Compare `e.origin` to a normalized `discourseUrl` origin for equality.

PollFeed crashes on RSS items without content due to nil.scrub — Missing `i.content` raises `NoMethodError` on `scrub` and kills the hourly job. Fall back to `i.description` with `(i.content || i.description || '').to_s.scrub` before `CGI.unescapeHTML`.

Nil post.user dereference raises NoMethodError in embed view — When the author is deleted `post.user` is `nil` and the embed iframe fails to render. Guard `post.user` with safe navigation `&.` and a fallback for `small_avatar_url` and `username`.

Embed script throws TypeError when discourse-comments element missing — The script crashes with `TypeError` on pages without the placeholder div. Guard `comments` with an early return before creating the `iframe`.

SSRF and DoS via unrestricted open-uri fetch of feed URL — Fetching `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` without validation lets an attacker probe internal hosts and hang the scheduler. Validate the `URI` scheme/host against an allowlist and fetch with `URI.open` using timeouts and rescue for `OpenURI::HTTPError`.

absolutize_urls crashes on malformed URLs and builds wrong prefix for ports/host — A malformed `url` makes `absolutize_urls` crash on `URI` and breaks importing jobs, with ports and protocol-relative URLs mishandled. Wrap `URI(url)` with a rescue returning `contents` and normalize `uri.scheme`/`uri.host` using `uri.default_port`.

Synchronous PollFeed on every cache-miss embed request causes duplicate work — Every embed cache miss synchronously parses the entire feed and re-imports all items, duplicating work under concurrent loads. Remove the inline `Jobs::PollFeed` call from `perform_retrieve` and rely on the scheduled job.

TopicEmbed.import crashes on deleted post and concurrent create race — A deleted `embed.post` is `nil` and crashes `PostRevisor`, and concurrent imports race on the `create!` unique index. Guard for `nil` post recreation and use `find_or_create_by` with a `RecordNotUnique` retry.

In-place `<<` on `contents` mutates caller string and breaks frozen strings — Appending with `<<` mutates the caller's `contents` and raises `FrozenError` on frozen strings. Build a new string with `contents +` or `contents.dup` instead.

Raw embed_url as Redis key allows unbounded keys and throttle bypass — Using raw `@embed_url` as a Redis key lets attackers exhaust memory and bypass throttling by varying URLs. Hash `@embed_url` with `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest` for `retrieved_recently?` and rate-limit by normalized host.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Migration raises NoMethodError when embed_category setting is missing — A fresh install without the setting crashes with `NoMethodError` instead of migrating. Guard the `execute` result in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` with `&.`/`dig` and handle nil before `to_i`.

edit() throws TypeError when host.category is null — A host without a category throws `TypeError` and blocks editing. Guard `host.category` in `edit` and read `id` only when present, falling back to `null` or `Discourse.Category.findById`.

record_for_host case-sensitive and port-stripping lookup misses valid hosts — Case-variant referers and hosts with ports never match and valid embeds are rejected. Downcase `host` in `record_for_host` and compare `lower(host)` to `host.downcase`, handling `uri.port` when building the lookup value.

update/destroy dereference nil host instead of returning 404 — Requesting an unknown id crashes with `NoMethodError` instead of a clean 404. Guard the result of `where(...).first` in `update` and `destroy` and return `head :not_found` when `host` is nil.

Nil host causes NoMethodError in before_validation callback — Blank params crash with `NoMethodError` before validations run, so users never see a proper error. Guard `self.host` in `before_validation` and only call `sub!` when `present?`.

_hydrateEmbedded crashes on non-array _ids and leaks undefined entries — A null `_ids` payload throws `TypeError` on `map` and missing subtypes leave `undefined` in the list. Guard `obj[k]` with `Array.isArray` in `_hydrateEmbedded` and `filter(Boolean)` on results from `_lookupSubType` before assigning.

SQL injection via unescaped host string interpolation — A host containing a single quote breaks the migration and could inject SQL. Quote `h` with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` or use parameterized `execute` in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` instead of string interpolation.

Missing functional index on lower(host) causes sequential scan — Every embed request scans the whole `embeddable_hosts` table because `lower(host)` cannot use a plain index. Add a functional index on `lower(host)` in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` or store a normalized host and index it.

basePath only replaces first underscore breaking admin routes — Types with multiple underscores are routed outside `/admin/` and fail to load. Replace `type.replace('_', '-')` in `basePath` with a global regex `/_/g` or `Ember.String.dasherize` so all underscores become dashes.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

findings.description: order mixin passes wrong value to 1-indexed box-ordinal-group — Legacy WebKit/Firefox will render `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` in swapped order due to the off-by-one. Offset `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` to `$val + 1` while leaving `-ms-flex-order` and `order` as `$val`.

Invalid -ms-align-items prefix and incorrect IE10 flex alignment values — IE10 will ignore the alignment and future `flex-start`/`flex-end` values will silently fail. Remove `-ms-align-items` from `align-items` and map `$alignment` to `start`/`end` for `-ms-flex-align`.
Panel margin-left:auto ignored in legacy -webkit-box causing overlap — Add a `float: right` fallback in `.panel` or `-webkit-box-pack`/`-moz-box-pack` handling via `flexbox`.

align-items emits invalid -webkit-box-align:baseline and omits -moz-box-align — `badges.css.scss` calls `align-items` with `baseline`, but legacy Firefox gets no alignment and old WebKit receives an invalid `-webkit-box-align` value. Add `-moz-box-align` and only emit `-webkit-box-align`/`-moz-box-align` for valid values, mapping `flex-start`/`flex-end` to `start`/`end`.

goldensDetail.text: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Duplicate downsize definitions overwrite each other breaking legacy callers — The winning `downsize` arity rejects the legacy 5-argument call with `ArgumentError`, breaking callers in `resize_emoji.rb`. Remove the dead overload and make `downsize` handle both a dimensions string and `max_width`/`max_height` via `*args`.

Synchronous downsizing loop blocks worker and ignores downsize failures — Repeated `OptimizedImage.downsize` shellouts on the request thread can block the worker for seconds on large images and keeps looping even after a failure. Check the return value of `downsize` and break on failure, or cap to a single resize toward `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` as shown.

Unvalidated URL fetch with rescue nil enables SSRF and resource exhaustion — `FileHelper.download` fetches an attacker-controlled `url` with `rescue nil` hiding failures and a fixed 10 MB allowance that widens SSRF and exhaustion risk. Validate `url` scheme/host against an allowlist and raise on failure instead of rescuing to nil, checking `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` for the limit.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: add_members/remove_member require :group_id but route supplies :id — Every add or remove from Ember fails with a 400 `ParameterMissing` error. Update `add_members` and `remove_member` to read `params[:id]` (or fall back to `params[:group_id]`) to match `routes.rb`.

findMembers returns undefined instead of promise when name empty — Callers chaining `.then` on `findMembers` hit a `TypeError` when the group has no name. Return `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` for the empty `name` case so the interface stays promise-based.

totalPages off-by-one creates phantom page when count divisible by limit — The extra page leaves the next button enabled and pushes `offset` past available data. Switch `totalPages` to `Math.ceil` so it calculates correctly when the count divides evenly.

Unbounded limit/offset enables DoS via huge or negative pagination — A huge `limit` forces a full table scan and serialization while negative values produce unpredictable queries. Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum and `offset` to `>=0`, defaulting to `50`/`0` on invalid input.

Whitespace in usernames not stripped causes member lookup to fail — A leading space like in `bob, alice` makes `User.find_by_username` miss the record so the user is silently skipped. Strip each entry from `usernames` and reject blanks before the lookup.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
