Age/timestamp exclusivity check ignores a value of 0 — A valid value of 0 is falsy, so a report with both fields passes when one of them is 0. In `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`, check `is not None` on `self.initial_data.get(...)` instead of truthiness.

Test with max_segment_id=None never exercises the null guard — Because `delete_matched_rows` is patched, the `max_segment_id` None row never reaches `_make_recording_filenames`, so the test passes even without the guard. Add a test that runs `_make_recording_filenames` or an unmocked `delete_matched_rows` with None and asserts no filenames are produced.

Error details paired with wrong event IDs via zip over dict values — `nodestore.backend.get_multi` doesn't guarantee that the order of `events.values()` matches `error_ids`, and missing nodes may be omitted. This can attach the wrong title, message and timestamp to an event ID.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Hung flusher process is never killed because isinstance check excludes SpawnProcess — `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so the `isinstance` guard is likely False and a hung flusher is never killed. The old process keeps its shards while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, which can produce duplicate segments.
time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched in the test — Replace it with a deadline-based poll until `messages` is non-empty, or capture the real sleep before patching.

`break` on an expired join deadline skips `process.terminate()` for remaining flushers — Flusher processes keep running after `join()` returns, whereas the old code always terminated them after the wait loop. Remove the `break` and always call `process.terminate()` after each wait, or add a separate terminate loop after the wait loop.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: Dataclass default timezone.now() is evaluated once at import time — Every `AssignmentSource` gets the same stale process-start timestamp in `queued`, and that value goes out in the task payload. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets its own time.

First-time GitHub installs skip authenticated-user verification — A first-time install with any `installation_id` skips the authenticated-user check, so the installation can be bound to the wrong user's session. Don't call `pipeline.next_step()` here without verifying that `github_authenticated_user` matches the installation's account or sender, or reject the request.

Token exchange and user-info lookup in GitHub OAuth step lack error handling — A network failure, timeout, or GitHub API error raises an unhandled exception and returns a 500 during installation. Move `safe_urlopen` into the try block and wrap `get_user_info` in try/except, returning `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

OAuth state is a constant pipeline signature, not a per-flow secret — `pipeline.signature` is a constant, publicly derivable value, so the `state` check gives no CSRF or login-binding protection. Generate a random per-flow nonce, store it with `bind_state`, and compare it using `constant_time_compare` in the callback.

test_installation_not_found uses wrong state and asserts only generic message — The test uses a `state` that differs from the pipeline signature in other tests, so it likely fails at the state check and never reaches the missing-installation branch. Use the correct state and assert on something specific to that case, since the generic message appears on every failure path.

KeyError on missing 'sender' in integration metadata causes 500 during install — `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` raises `KeyError` when `sender` is absent, since `build_integration` writes it only conditionally, so installation returns a 500 instead of the error page. Read it with `.get()` and fall through to `error()` when it's missing.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and will fail to instantiate — `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` subclasses the abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` but only has `pass`, so `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` for every metric alert detector. Implement `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, or restore the no-op evaluate returning `{}`.

Expected occurrence uses value 6 but test evaluates 100; mock ignores value — The mock `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value` (`evidence_data={}`), so the assertion passes whatever the handler sends to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Put `value` in the mock occurrence's evidence data and build the expected occurrence with the real evaluated value, so a wrong value fails the test.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Monitor context returns raw config instead of transformed schedule_type copy — The transformed `config` copy is never used, so the occurrence's monitor context carries the raw numeric `schedule_type`. Return `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config` in `get_monitor_environment_context`.

Collective team calendars silently dropped when destinationCalendar is null — When both destination calendars are null, the optional chaining silently drops all team destination calendars, so collective hosts with connected calendars never get invited. Initialize the array instead of relying on `?.push`.

Duplicate deletes for recurring cancellation across calendar references — Each extra calendar reference re-runs the full credential and booking loop, issuing duplicate delete calls for collective cancellations. Move this block outside the reference loop and execute it once.

Use localization key for hard-coded loadUsers 500 error message — Users will see this error in English regardless of their locale, unlike neighboring `HttpError` messages that use translation keys. Replace the literal with a localization key such as `unable_to_load_users`.

Calendar credential key leaked to updateEvent error log — The fallback credential includes the raw `key` secret, and `updateEvent` logs the whole `credential` object when `bookingRefUid` is empty. Redact or omit `key` before passing it to the update path.

Unsafe access of destinationCalendar integration when no calendar exists — When no destination calendar exists the array is empty, so destructuring yields `undefined` and dereferencing `.integration` throws a `TypeError` instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

Non-calendar branch drops video credentialId — Cancellation fails because the video reference is stored without a `credentialId`, but `handleCancelBooking.ts:491` only deletes when that field is truthy. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar result types.

External calendar ID fallback compares cal.externalId to undefined — In the falsy branch the comparison always evaluates `undefined === undefined`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and `events.update` is called with a missing `calendarId`. Fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`

Org creation slug condition inverted — This flips the self-hosted behavior: billing-disabled orgs get a null `slug`, while billing-enabled orgs bypass the `requestedSlug` publishing flow. Restore the `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition for `slug`.

updateLocation drops destinationCalendar fallback for externalId/credentialId — `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never returns `externalId` or `credentialId`, so update flows now store undefined values and lose the previous destination-calendar fallback. Retain fallbacks to `evt.destinationCalendar?.[0]` for these fields.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && so team admins are denied adding guests — `isTeamAdmin` already covers owners, so `&&` makes this true only for owners and denies team admins with a `FORBIDDEN` error. Change the operator to `||` so non-owner admins can add guests as intended.

Normalize guest emails to lowercase before blacklist and duplicate checks — Case differences allow a blacklisted address to bypass the filter and an existing attendee to be re-added as a new row. Normalize `guest`, `attendee.email`, and the blacklist entries to lowercase before both comparisons.

Add guests 500s for team/collective bookings when booking.userId is null — Coercing a nullable `userId` to `0` makes `findFirstOrThrow` throw and return a 500 for team or collective bookings. Fall back to `booking.eventType?.userId` or `user.id` instead of querying id 0.

Unbounded guests array permits email fanout resource exhaustion — A single request can submit thousands of emails, each triggering a DB insert, translation lookup, and outgoing email. Cap `guests` with `.max(...)` or add a rate limit to prevent email-fanout exhaustion.

sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails metadata — Event types configured with `disableStandardEmails` still send organizer and attendee emails from this function because the metadata check is missing. Thread `booking.eventType.metadata` into `sendAddGuestsEmails` and gate the loops like `sendLocationChangeEmails` does.

AddGuestsDialog leaves isInvalidEmail true after success or dialog open — After a failed attempt, a successful add leaves `isInvalidEmail` true, so reopening the dialog still shows the stale error. Reset `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` in `onSuccess` and when the dialog opens.

Error toast can show 'undefined: ...' and bypasses fallback — Users can see `undefined: ...` when `err.data?.code` is absent, and the truthy interpolation makes the localized fallback unreachable. Show `t("unable_to_add_guests")` directly instead of prefixing raw TRPC error codes.

Missing evt.team prevents team member add-guest emails — Team-member emails are skipped because `CalendarEvent.team` isn't populated here, so the branch in `sendAddGuestsEmails` never runs. Include the `eventType.team` relation in the Prisma query and set `evt.team` from it.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531-537`

Add server-side uniqueness validation for guests array — Duplicates inside the input pass validation and `uniqueGuests` doesn't catch them, so `createMany` can insert repeated attendee rows. Add a `.refine` check for unique emails in the schema or dedupe in the handler.

sendAddGuestsEmails misclassifies existing attendees as new guests — Existing attendees whose email also appears in the raw input get the wrong email template because this branch trusts `newGuests`. Pass the filtered `uniqueGuests` from the handler so the parameter reflects actual additions.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168-168`
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-168`

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Unconditional Salesforce token refresh on every calendar operation — This adds a network round-trip and database write to every calendar operation, even when the existing token remains valid. Check the token expiry before calling `getClient` unconditionally from the constructor.

Non-atomic credential check-then-act allows duplicate concurrent writes — Two concurrent webhook calls can both pass the `findFirst` check and create duplicate credentials, or one fails on a unique-constraint violation. Use `prisma.credential.upsert` keyed on a unique `(userId, appId)` constraint instead.

Return parsed JSON with data instead of raw fetch Response — Callers read `.data` or `.expiresIn` off the returned object, but a raw Fetch `Response` exposes neither, so token refresh throws or stores `NaN` expiry. Return `{ data: await response.json() }` to match the axios-shaped result.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-96`

Google Calendar refresh stores Zod SafeParse wrapper as credential key — Storing the Zod wrapper means later schema parsing in `googleAuth` sees `{ success, data }` instead of the token fields and rejects the credential. Extract `.data` from `parseRefreshTokenResponse` before passing it to `prisma.credential.update`.

Refreshed Salesforce token not used by returned connection — The connection still uses the stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`, so the refresh has no effect on the request in progress. Update those fields from `accessTokenParsed.data` before constructing the connection.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:90-99`

Duplicate computed keys cause token schema to strip expiry fields — Both computed keys evaluate to `"[object Object]"`, so the second overwrites the first and no expiry field is ever retained; unknown-key stripping also drops `expires_in` and `expiry_date`. Replace them with `z.record(z.number())` or an explicit expiry field.

Zod schema uses fixed computed keys instead of record — The computed keys are fixed object properties, not a record, so the schema validates neither arbitrary numeric expiry fields nor extra unknown keys. Use `z.record(z.string(), z.number())` and explicit unknown-key handling to match the documented behavior.

Placeholder refresh_token overwrites real refresh token — When `refresh_token` is absent, this assigns the literal string `"refresh_token"`, which callers like office365calendar later spread back into credentials and persist. Preserve the original refresh token instead of substituting a placeholder.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11`
Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time — Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, rejecting immediately when lengths differ.

refreshOAuthTokens gets credential ID where user ID is expected — The sync endpoint receives `credential.id` as `calcomUserId` instead of `credential.userId`, which the other callers send. Pass `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Locked SMS account wrongly increments retryCount in else branch — When SMS sending is locked, `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` instead of throwing, so this `else` branch counts a lock as a send failure and increments retryCount. Pending reminders for a locked account are deleted after two cron runs without any send attempt, so they are permanently lost if the lock is later removed.

Second OR branch lacks SMS method filter, deleting non-SMS reminders — The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is missing the SMS method filter. This endpoint is meant to clean up SMS workflow reminders only, but this branch will delete any WorkflowReminder of any method (email, etc.) once its retryCount exceeds 1.

Off-by-one retry threshold deletes SMS reminders after one retry — The retry limit is off by one relative to the value being measured. `retryCount` is incremented on every failed attempt including the initial one (lines 184 and 195), but this deletion condition removes reminders when `retryCount > 1`.

Wrap retryCount update in its own try/catch to preserve best-effort catch behavior — The new awaited prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block changes the error contract: previously a scheduling error was swallowed and logged, and the loop continued to the next reminder. Now, if this retryCount update throws (e.g. transient DB failure or the reminder was deleted), the error escapes the catch and aborts the whole cron run, causing remaining reminders to be skipped and the request to fail.

Non-atomic retryCount increment permits indefinite SMS retries — `retryCount` is updated with a non-atomic read-modify-write (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) using the value read at findMany time. Two overlapping cron invocations both read the same stale value and write the same incremented result, so retryCount never reaches 2 and the reminder is retried indefinitely, defeating the new retry cap.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-186`

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup code login bypasses password verification when totpCode is supplied — A valid backup code plus any dummy `totpCode` bypasses the password check above. Verify `credentials.password` against `user.password` before trusting the backup code.

Non-atomic backup-code consumption allows double-use or resurrection — Two logins on the same code can both pass `indexOf` before either write commits, or one write can clobber another and resurrect a used code. Use an atomic update keyed on the prior `backupCodes` value.

2FA enable invalidation skipped when dialog dismissed via X/Escape after success — The X/Escape path calls `onOpenChange` directly, so `onEnable()` never runs and the parent query stays stale. Trigger `onEnable()` on close as well, or drive invalidation from `onOpenChange`.

Backup-code comparison is case-sensitive and rejects uppercase codes — Codes are generated as lowercase hex, so an uppercase entry is rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode` despite being correct. Normalize with `.toLowerCase()` before comparison and set `autoCapitalize="none"` on the input.

Backup code copy test only waits for toast, not clipboard contents — The toast appears even when the clipboard write rejects or writes empty text, so this test never catches a broken copy. Grant clipboard-read permission and assert the actual contents.

Loose 2FA switch assertion can pass when switch is not checked — `.isChecked()` returns a truthy-then-falsy value here, so the assertion can pass when the switch is not checked. Wait for `data-state="checked"` or close the backup-code dialog first.

Backup code verification should use constant-time comparison — Early-exit string comparison leaks timing information about the code and its position. Compare the submitted code against every stored code with a fixed-work loop that accumulates differences before deciding.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61-63`

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: teamId is optional for team scope in public options type — A team-scope caller can now omit `teamId` and the lookup runs with `id: undefined`, silently returning `NOTHING_CONDITION` or matching the wrong team. Keep `teamId` required for the team scope, e.g. as a discriminated union, or handle the missing value in `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`.

Prisma.sql deep-equality fails due to nested fragment construction — The service composes conditions with nested `Prisma.sql` fragments via `reduce`, so `toEqual` compares different internal `strings`/`values` arrays and the assertions fail—nested `Sql` fragments are only flattened at serialization time. Build the expected fragments with the same nested composition, or assert on the rendered `conditions.sql` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:429-431`

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Imported embed content is stored with raw HTML cook method, bypassing sanitization — Third-party feed or embed content executes in the Discourse-origin iframe because `cook_method: raw_html` bypasses `PrettyText.cook` sanitization and `best.html.erb` renders with `raw`. Route the import through the regular cooking pipeline or sanitize the HTML before storage.

Unescaped URL in imported_from link allows HTML injection — The URL is interpolated into raw HTML without escaping, and raw cooking plus `raw` rendering means a quote or angle bracket in the URL can inject markup or script. Escape the URL with `ERB::Util.html_escape` for both the attribute and link text.

PollFeed raises NoMethodError when feed item has no content element — Standard RSS feeds using `<description>` leave `i.content` nil, so the exception aborts the whole `poll_feed` loop with no retry. Fall back to `i.description` and guard against nil before calling `scrub`.

Remote topic import can abort on bad links or silently drop threads — A dead or malformed permalink aborts the entire import, and non-http(s) links silently drop that thread's posts because `TopicEmbed.import_remote` returns nil. Rescue network errors per URL and skip blank results so one bad link doesn't kill the run.
Invalid ERB tag `<%- end if %>` causes SyntaxError — This invalid ERB tag raises `SyntaxError` and returns a 500 for any already-embedded topic. Change it to a plain `end`.

Throttle key set without TTL can permanently block non-staff retrieval — A crash between `setnx` and `expire` leaves the key without a TTL, permanently blocking non-staff retrieval for that embed URL. Set the value and TTL atomically with `SET ... NX EX`.

Discourse embed postMessage origin check is substring, not exact — This substring check lets an untrusted origin embedded anywhere in the configured URL pass the trust test and send `discourse-resize` messages. Compare `new URL(discourseUrl).origin` exactly against `e.origin`.

PollFeed spec tests do not isolate each required setting — The other two settings default to values that already make the guard condition false, so removing any single check would leave its corresponding test green. Stub all other guards to passing values so only the named setting is tested.

Missing embed_url spec passes due to blank embeddable_host, not missing param — The blank `embeddable_host` causes the `ensure_embeddable` filter to fail first, so `response.should_not be_success` passes even without the `embed_url` require. Put the test in a context with a valid host and referer, then assert the specific 404.

Tests stub private retrieved_recently? guard instead of exercising Redis throttle — Stubbing `retrieved_recently?` directly means the Redis throttle is never exercised, so `retrieve`'s branch can pass with a broken guard. Arrange real Redis state or call the private method through `retrieve` so the throttle behavior is actually tested.

Concurrent TopicEmbed.import creates duplicate topic/post for the same URL — Concurrent imports from `poll_feed` and `retrieve_topic` can both pass the `embed.blank?` check, then the second `create!` raises on the unique index and aborts the job. Guard the create with a unique-constraint rescue or use a concurrency-safe find-or-create.

Update test to expect Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) instead of TopicRetriever — The controller now enqueues `:retrieve_topic` instead of calling `TopicRetriever` directly, so this mock expectation fails. Assert `Jobs.enqueue` with the job name and arguments.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: embedding.embeddable_hosts is a plain array, so pushObject/removeObject fail — The hydrated collection is a plain array, so mutating it with Ember methods throws a TypeError and leaves the UI broken. Wrap it with `Ember.A(...)` in `_hydrateEmbedded`, or use plain `push`/`filter` here.

CreateEmbeddableHosts migration crashes when embed_category is unset — When `embed_category` is unset, the inner join returns no rows and indexing nil raises, skipping the intended fallback. Check `ntuples` before indexing so unset values fall back to the uncategorized category.

Migrated embeddable_hosts URLs are not normalized before insertion — Raw SQL inserts bypass `before_validation`, so URL-form hosts keep schemes and paths that never match `uri.host`. Normalize each host before inserting, or insert through the model so validation runs.

Obsolete example no longer verifies embeddable_host blank condition — The expectation now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false, so it no longer tests the embeddable-host condition. Remove the example or set `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` and stub `has_topic_embed?` to return true.

EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy dereferences nil for missing id — A stale or double delete returns nil from `where(...).first`, which raises NoMethodError and a 500. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` to render a 404, or return early when nil.

Unconditional sub! on nil host raises NoMethodError — A nil host raises NoMethodError during `before_validation`, bypassing the intended format validation and producing a 500. Normalize `self.host` to an empty string before calling `sub!`.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: OptimizedImage.downsize signature breaks Jobs::ResizeEmoji calls — Every time an admin uploads a custom emoji, `resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls this with five positional args, so Ruby raises `ArgumentError` and the emoji is never resized. Update `resize_emoji.rb` to pass a single dimension string such as `"100x100"` instead of `100, 100`.

validateUploadedFile hardcodes 10 MB limit, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb — Non-image attachments are never downsized server-side, so admins' `max_attachment_size_kb` is silently dropped on the client and files up to 10 MB pass validation only to be rejected later. Keep the site setting for non-image types and use 10 MB only for images.

Animated GIF uploads lose animation when downsized due to temp path — `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects the animated path when the source path has a `.gif` extension, but `tempfile.path` does not reliably preserve the original suffix. Use a tempfile with a `.gif` suffix before calling `downsize`, or change `optimize` to select the animated path from `filename` or the content type rather than from `tempfile.path`.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description:
add_members and remove_member read missing :group_id param — These routes expose the id as `params[:id]`, not `params[:group_id]`, so every add/remove request raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` and returns 400. Read `params[:id]` like `update` and `destroy` do.

**Also found in:**
- `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:85-85`

add_members re-adds existing members causing RecordNotUnique — Re-adding an existing member hits the unique `(group_id, user_id)` index and returns a 500 instead of succeeding silently. Skip usernames that are already members before calling `group.add`.

Reset group members offset after deleting last member on page — The stored `offset` can point past the last member after a delete, so `findMembers()` requests an empty page while members exist on the previous one. Clamp the offset before reloading.

Default 50 member limit truncates public group member lists — Any public group over 50 members is silently truncated because the endpoint now paginates by default and the public template has no pager. Add pagination to the public page or fetch all members for that consumer.

Use DELETE verb in remove_member spec — Controller specs bypass routing, so this would still pass if the DELETE route broke or was removed. Use `xhr :delete` to match the endpoint defined in `config/routes.rb`.

totalPages overcounts pages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit — This reports an extra empty page whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, so `next` can navigate past the last member. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: I18n fallback wiring missing outside ApplicationController#set_locale — Non-HTTP contexts never trigger fallback loading, so Sidekiq jobs risk missing translations or a `NoMethodError` from `@loaded_locales` on first `I18n.t`. Wire the ensure-loaded fallback setup into the job runner and other non-controller entry points, not just `ApplicationController#set_locale`.

FallbackLocaleList#[] never stores computed fallbacks in Hash — Because the computed list is discarded, `I18n.fallbacks` stays permanently empty for every Hash API, so enumeration or inspection silently returns nothing. Store the computed fallbacks in the hash so `each`, `keys`, `key?`, `size`, and `to_a` see the configured mapping.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: RowsAffected()==0 incorrectly treats unchanged existing device as over-limit — RowsAffected can be 0 when the UPDATE matched a row but wrote identical values, such as a same-second update stored to a second-precision updated_at column or MySQL without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS. That makes an existing anonymous device look over-limit: CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and Anonymous.Authenticate now propagates it.

Device key remains cached after CreateOrUpdateDevice error — tagDeviceUI writes the device key into localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. Now that TagDevice propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached, the failed attempt leaves the key cached: a retry within the cache TTL returns early at impl.go:83, so the device is never persisted yet anonymous authentication succeeds, bypassing the device limit.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-47`

Device limit check and insert are not atomic under concurrency — The count and insert run as separate, non-transactional statements: two concurrent anonymous requests can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, exceeding the configured device limit. Wrap the count and insert in one transaction or add a DB-level constraint to enforce the limit atomically instead of check-then-act.

Synchronous TagDevice call adds DB round-trips to anonymous auth hot path — Every uncached anonymous login now blocks on a COUNT plus an INSERT/UPDATE against anon_device before the identity is returned, adding two DB round-trips to the auth hot path. Keep the normal tagging path asynchronous and perform the limit check separately, or otherwise avoid the blocking write on each uncached login.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Re-check assets cache under write lock to prevent thundering herd — Every goroutine that saw an empty cache re-reads the assets manifest and overwrites it, causing a thundering herd on first access. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` inside the lock and return it when non-nil and `cfg.Env != setting.Dev` to make cache population single-flight.

Mode3 Delete skips legacy fallback on unified-storage NotFound — Objects that exist only in legacy storage (created before mode-3 migration) can no longer be deleted and will resurface on rollback. Restore the old `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` fallback that still calls `d.Legacy.Delete` before returning.

Async legacy write may be canceled before writing to legacy storage — The mode-3 invariant (write to both stores) is silently broken when the request context cancels before `LegacyStorage.Create` finishes. Use a parent not tied to request cancellation, e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`, so only the 10s timeout cancels the legacy write; the same pattern exists in `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`.

Mode3 legacy update passes raw objInfo causing divergent writes — When the two stores are out of sync the legacy write diverges or conflicts instead of converging. Wrap the storage result as before with `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}`.

Delete passes object name instead of options.Kind to storage metric — The metric's `kind` label (metrics.go:23) gets polluted with arbitrary object names instead of the resource kind. Pass `options.Kind`.

Storage failures recorded in legacy duration histogram in Create and Update — This pollutes the legacy duration histogram with storage errors and leaves the storage histogram missing its error observations. Change `Create` and `Update` to call `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-130`

DeleteCollection legacy duration mislabeled as storage duration — Legacy-store failures and timeouts are mislabeled as unified-storage durations. Change to `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`.

TestMode3_Create never asserts async legacy Create — The test would still pass if `d.Legacy.Create` were removed or broken. Add synchronization for the async legacy write and assert it was invoked (e.g., wait for the goroutine and call `m.AssertExpectations`, or use a done channel/atomic spy), rather than only asserting the storage result.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:299-345`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Data race: TotalDocs called without cache lock after watcher starts — After searchSupport.init starts the write-event goroutine, handleEvent or BuildIndex can write b.cache while this call iterates it, causing a concurrent map iteration and write that can panic at runtime. Make TotalDocs hold cacheMu.RLock during iteration, or move this log before the watcher starts.

Postgres skip hides instrumentation server regressions — The postgres skip makes a regression in the instrumentation server path pass silently whenever GRAFANA_TEST_DB is postgres. Fix the underlying Drone-only failure, or narrow the skip to the detected Drone environment so the assertion still runs elsewhere.

Concurrent same-key builds can overwrite cache and drop events — Without the function-wide cacheMu.Lock, two same-key builds can race, and a cache overwrite taken before a handler writes an event silently drops that update until the next rebuild. Serialize builds per key with singleflight or a keyed mutex instead of relying on the removed global lock.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: GrafanaRuleListItem omits rulerRule, so managed rules cannot be paused or deleted — Without `rulerRule`, `AlertRuleMenu` receives `rulerRule={undefined}`, so `Delete` and `Pause` are disabled even when Grafana permissions allow them. Pass `rulerRule={rule}` to `RuleActionsButtons`.

Federated rule groups no longer marked immutable in deprecated alert rule abilities hook — Federated rule groups lose their immutable flag because the shared hook hardcodes `isFederated = false`. Restore the `isFederatedRuleGroup` check before delegating to the shared implementation.

Silence notifications action is a no-op when rulerRule is undefined — Guard `canSilence` on `Boolean(rulerRule)` or provide a prom-rule-based silence flow.

**Also found in:**
- `public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:44-48`
GrafanaRuleListItem is rendered without a key prop — Missing `key` causes React warnings and can mis-reconcile rows when the filtered list reorders or grows. Add `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' only checks the More button — The test never opens the dropdown or asserts menu options, so it passes even if the action menu renders nothing. Either rename it or click `More` and assert the expected options appear.

Edit button absence assertion races with async permission check — The edit button is absent while the folder permission query is loading, so this assertion can pass before the async permission check settles. Use `waitFor` or `await expect(...).rejects` to let the condition resolve first.

useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities does not guard skipToken — Passing `undefined` to `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` lets `Duplicate` be seen as `AlwaysSupported`, so cloud rules can be duplicated whenever Grafana create permission exists. Early-return `[NotSupported, false]` for `skipToken`.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Client credentials token grant type encoded as na instead of cc — Without this attribute, `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` falls back to UNKNOWN and client-credentials tokens encode `na` instead of `cc`. Set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to `context.getGrantType()` on the client session context in `ClientCredentialsGrantType.process` before generating the access token.

Constructor validates grantType twice and fails to validate rawTokenId — A null `rawTokenId` passes silently and later makes `encodeTokenId` emit a token id ending in `null`. Change the second `Objects.requireNonNull` to target `rawTokenId`.

Access token ID matcher extracts grant-type shortcut at wrong offset — The grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5, so reading `substring(3, 5)` yields part of the token type plus the first grant character (for `trltcc` it gives `tc` instead of `cc`) and never inspects the complete shortcut. Use `substring(4, 6)` and invert the condition so a mismatch returns false.

isAccessTokenId validates grant shortcut at wrong substring indexes — The encoder places the grant shortcut at indices 4–5 of the pre-colon context, so this matcher reads the wrong slice and can also throw on short contexts. Require `items[0].length() >= 6` and return `expectedGrantShortcut.equals(items[0].substring(4, 6)) && isUUID().matches(items[1])`.

Inverted condition rejects correct grant type in isAccessTokenId — Returning false when the extracted shortcut equals the expected one rejects correct grant types, so these assertion helpers only check the UUID and never verify the grant type. Invert the condition so only a genuine mismatch returns false.

OAuth2 grant type shortcut length not constrained to two characters but encoder assumes it — A custom factory returning a shortcut length other than two produces token IDs that later throw `IllegalArgumentException` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`. Enforce an exact two-character shortcut here, validate it in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, or make the encoder handle variable lengths.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:109-117`

Return 0L instead of null when delegate model is missing in getSubGroupsCount — Returning `null` here breaks the `GroupModel` contract that this method 'Never returns null', and `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` forwards that null into the REST response. Return `0L` when `model` is null.

Reader thread is never joined before asserting caughtExceptions — The assertion can pass before the reader thread finishes its last in-flight request, hiding exceptions that occur after the check. Join `reader` before asserting on `caughtExceptions` so the concurrent-deletion behavior is fully observed.

PropertyResourceBundle decodes UTF-8 properties as ISO-8859-1 — Every non-ASCII translation is decoded as mojibake before HTML comparison, so sanitize, containsHtml, santizeAnchors, and their diagnostics can misreport or garble results. Construct the bundles from a UTF-8 reader such as new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)).

Use i18next {{...}} placeholders for multivalued-size error — The account console will render literal {0}, {1}, {2}, and {2,choice,...} text for multivalued-size errors. Keep the {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} syntax in the React bundles; the identical change in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties breaks the admin console the same way.

Italian text overwrote Lithuanian totpStep1 and loginTotpStep1 translations — Lithuanian users are shown Italian instructions for totpStep1 and loginTotpStep1. Restore the Lithuanian translation for both keys in the account and login files.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties:71-71`

Anchor validation compares tags positionally instead of by membership — Reordering identical anchors or using only the second of two source anchors compares against the wrong English anchor and reports a missing tag. Check membership of each translated anchor against the full set of English anchors instead of consuming englishMatcher positionally.

totpStep1 uses Traditional Chinese in Simplified Chinese locale — Users of the zh_CN locale see the wrong character variant. Replace totpStep1 with Simplified Chinese text such as '在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：'.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: All-clients permission ignored when specific client resource exists — Granting a scope only through the all-clients permission is ignored for any client that has its own resource, so callers are incorrectly denied access. Evaluate the all-clients resource in addition to the specific resource, or fall back per scope, when the specific resource does not grant the requested scope.

getClientsWithPermission returns typed resource name instead of client IDs — Callers filtering clients by the returned set will match no client or treat "Clients" as a client id when a global all-clients permission exists. Skip the typed resource or expand it into actual client ids so the set contains only client identifiers.

Skip unsupported V2 setPermissionsEnabled call on client removal — Client removal with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled throws UnsupportedOperationException because ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled is unsupported. Skip the call when the V2 feature is enabled, and verify the role and group branches do not have the same issue.

removeDefaultClientScope permission test masked by getDefaultClientScopes call — The test passes even when removeDefaultClientScope authorization is broken because getDefaultClientScopes throws first. Fetch default client scopes with a privileged client before the try block so only removeDefaultClientScope is exercised inside it.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Passkey conditional UI shown for disabled users — Disabled users can reach the passkey conditional UI and then submit to webauthnAuth.action before the enabledUser gate. Add the isEnabled() check to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled, or skip filling passkey data in challenge() for disabled/brute-force error challenges.

Passkey conditional UI enabled for base/classic theme without template support — The classic and custom themes inherit themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/login-password.ftl, which lacks the passkeys import and conditional UI rendering, so this fix is invisible there. Update the base template to match the keycloak.v2 change or gate fillContextForm on template support.

Reauthentication test does not exercise per-user passkey branch — This currently passes because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled short-circuits on the disabled realm policy, so a broken per-user branch would go unnoticed. Set setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.TRUE) and keep the user without passkey credentials to exercise credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(...).

N+1 JPA queries in getForLogin cache-miss loop — Each cached internalId triggers a separate database lookup on the login page when the cache is cold, causing O(N) queries for realms with many IDPs. Reuse the models already loaded by `idpDelegate.getForLogin` or load them in bulk instead of calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` inside the loop.

Login cache invalidation on qualified IDP create/remove is untested — The current steps never touch login-qualified IDPs, so a broken `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` in `create()` or `remove()` would leave stale login caches and all assertions would still pass. Add a create and a remove step for a login-qualified IDP and assert all three login caches are invalidated each time.

Login cache test lacks org-linked IDP with BROKER_PUBLIC false/absent — Because every org-linked IDP sets `OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC=true`, the false/absent branch in `getLoginPredicate` is never exercised and a broken condition would not change the expected counts. Add an org-linked IDP without `BROKER_PUBLIC` and assert it is excluded from login results.

IDP cleanup uses literal alias instead of created alias — Cleanup callbacks use the literal `"alias"` instead of the generated alias, so none of the created IDPs are removed and they persist into the shared realm for later tests. Register the cleanup with `testRealm().identityProviders().get(idpRep.getAlias())::remove`.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: PR comment helpers defined on CommitContextIntegration instead of PRCommentWorkflow — `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` inherit from `PRCommentWorkflow`, not `CommitContextIntegration`, so the new helpers are unavailable on `self` and the internal `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` reference points at a class that lacks it. Move both helpers to `PRCommentWorkflow` or otherwise expose them to those subclasses.
TableWidgetVisualization receives empty columns and tableData — Wire `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the derived columns into the new component.

Fix error detail mapping by looking up events by node_id — `get_multi` does not preserve input order and may merge cache hits after uncached ids, so `zip(error_ids, events.values())` mis-associates each error's details. Iterate `node_ids` and look up each result with `events.get(node_id)`.

get_environment_info causes per-issue recommended-event lookup N+1 — `get_environment_info` issues a Snuba query and nodestore fetch per issue, so large suspect-commit sets incur an N+1 that slows PR comment generation. Fetch environments in bulk or avoid the per-issue recommended-event lookup.

Mutually-exclusive age/timestamp validation uses truthiness, allowing 0 — Truthiness checks treat valid zero values as absence, so a report with both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` bypasses the mutual-exclusion rule. Use explicit key-existence checks like `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`.

Logging full GroupEvent payload leaks sensitive event data — Logging `workflow_event_data` can serialize the full `GroupEvent`, including message text, tags, and user context into logs. Log only non-sensitive identifiers such as `event_id` and workflow/action ids instead of the event payload.

Browser report validation warning logs sensitive raw report data — `raw_report` can include sensitive query-string tokens or PII in the report `url`, `user_agent`, and `body`. Log only sanitized fields such as report type or validation error keys, not the raw report.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Per-process shard buffers bypass global max-flush-segments burst cap — Each process computes its per-shard cap from its own subset size, so with `--flusher-processes N` the total flush grows to roughly `N * max_flush_segments`, defeating the global cap. Derive the cap from the total assigned shard count across `process_to_shards_map` so aggregate volume stays constant.

Redundant get_memory_info loops issue one Redis INFO per buffer per submit — `get_memory_info()` returns cluster-wide usage for any shard subset, so the loop issues a full `INFO` scan once per buffer on every `submit` and scales with `flusher_processes`. Compute the memory info once and reuse it; the `used`/`available` ratio is invariant.

Inconsistent shard tag key on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce — This splits the same shard dimension across `shards` and `shard`, so `wait_produce` disappears from any query filtering on `shard`. Use `shard` for consistency with the other flusher metrics.

Explicit max_processes=0 conflated with None in `or` fallback — Passing `0` silently becomes `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` because `or` conflates zero with `None`, launching far more processes than requested. Use an explicit `is None` check and reject values below 1 before computing `num_processes`.

Patched time.sleep no-op causes test to race with flusher thread — The wait returns immediately because the patched `time.sleep` is a no-op, so the assertion still races with the flusher thread. Synchronize on a condition or poll for `messages` with a real deadline instead of sleeping.

Test assertion does not verify shards are distributed across processes — The total only proves no shard was lost; assigning all four to one process would still pass. Assert that every entry in `process_to_shards_map` is non-empty or check the exact expected mapping.

SpawnProcess not killed due to isinstance check for multiprocessing.Process — `SpawnProcess` is a `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so this guard is always false and hung processes are never killed before a replacement starts. Check `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` so `kill()` actually runs and orphans are not left flushing the same shards.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: AssignmentSource.queued default freezes timezone at import — The import-time timestamp is shared by every `AssignmentSource` created through `from_integration`, so staleness or dedup checks compare against a stale value. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own creation time.

GitHub OAuth state uses constant signature instead of per-session CSRF token — A constant signature means the state check can be precomputed and reused by an attacker, defeating the CSRF protection it is meant to provide. Generate a per-request random token with `secrets.token_hex()` and validate it via `pipeline.fetch_state("state")` as `OAuth2LoginView`/`OAuth2CallbackView` do.

GitHub OAuth token exchange missing redirect_uri — Omitting `redirect_uri` from the token exchange causes GitHub to reject it with `error=redirect_uri_mismatch`, so every installation fails with a generic error page. Include the same `redirect_uri` used in the authorize URL, plus `grant_type`.

Unhandled GitHub OAuth callback network exceptions return 500 — A transient network or HTTP failure in `safe_urlopen` or `get_user_info` escapes as an unhandled 500 instead of the intended error page. Wrap both calls in the try block and return `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

test_installation_not_found uses invalid state and does not test missing installation — The hardcoded `state` is rejected by `OAuthLoginView` before `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` runs, so this test no longer covers its namesake scenario. Use the valid pipeline signature and assert the actual missing-installation outcome, or rename the test to match what it checks.

KeyError when GitHub integration metadata lacks sender key — Integrations without a `sender` key exist, as `installation.py:44` guards against them; accessing it directly raises `KeyError` and returns a 500. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` or guard the missing case.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler remains abstract and cannot be instantiated — `StatefulDetectorHandler` requires abstract members that `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` does not implement (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), so instantiating it raises a `TypeError` when `Detector.detector_handler` builds the registered handler. Implement those methods or keep it as a concrete `DetectorHandler` until the abstraction is ready.

build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value parameter — The expected occurrence/event is identical no matter what value was passed to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, so a wrong or missing `value` in `evaluate_group_key_value` would still pass. Make the mock occurrence/event depend on `value` (for example include it in `evidence_data` or the event payload) or explicitly assert the builder receives it.

Test does not assert produce_occurrence_to_kafka call count — `assert_has_calls` does not enforce the total number of calls, so extra calls to `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` would go unnoticed. Also assert `mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.call_count == 2` or otherwise require an exact call list.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: updateLocation drops externalCalendarId for updated events — `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never sets `externalId`, so location changes persist references without an `externalCalendarId`, and later deletes hit `primary`. Fall back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` when `result.externalId` is absent.

Video booking references lose credentialId, so meetings are never deleted on cancel — `handleCancelBooking.ts:491` has no else branch, so an undefined video `credentialId` means the Zoom/Daily/Meet meeting is never deleted on cancellation. Restore the video fallback so `createMeeting`'s `credentialId` is persisted.

Dereference of possibly undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar — `handleNewBooking` sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` and the webhooks set `[]`, so this throws a TypeError for a Google Meet booking when the organizer has no destination calendar instead of falling back to Cal Video. Guard the dereference.

Dead selectedCalendar fallback passes undefined calendarId — The `find` only runs when the predicate's value is falsy, so it never matches and `calendar.events.update` gets an undefined `calendarId`. Fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` or match on `credentialId`.

deleteEvent destination calendar lookup always falls back to primary — The `find` can never match a falsy `externalCalendarId`, so every delete falls back to "primary" and events on secondary destination calendars are never deleted. Use the destination calendar's `externalId` as the fallback.

Collective team destination calendars dropped when organizer calendar is null — `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` a few lines above when no destination calendar exists, so the optional push silently drops every `teamDestinationCalendars` entry. Assign the merged array instead of pushing.

Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId when no matching destination calendar — Google Meet bookings with no matching destination calendar fail the patch and lose the updated description. Apply the same `|| "primary"` fallback to the `calendar.events.patch` call.

Recurring cancellation repeats deletes for each calendar reference — The recurring branch now runs once per calendar reference while still looping over credentials and `updatedBookings`, so a collective with N references deletes the same events N times. Run it once when `allRemainingBookings` is set.

Organizer email uses first destination calendar, not credential's — With `destinationCalendar` now an array of every host's calendar, an event created with host B's credential is sent with host A's email as organizer. Match the destination calendar by `credentialId` (as `selectedCalendar` does) before using its `externalId`.
