goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: addGuests updates calendar with requesting user's credentials — Calendar updates run with credentials that never created the event, so the organizer's invites are never updated when a team owner or attendee adds guests. Build `EventManager` from `booking.user`'s credentials, as the seat flow in `createNewSeat.ts` does.

addGuests handler throws unhandled P2025 when booking.userId is null — A null `booking.userId` makes id 0 throw P2025, surfacing as an unhandled 500 instead of a TRPCError. Throw an explicit TRPCError when `booking.userId` is null before querying.

isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && so team admins are wrongly denied access — `isTeamAdmin` already covers ADMIN and OWNER, so combining with `&&` reduces `isTeamAdminOrOwner` to owner-only and rejects team admins. Use `||`, or just `await isTeamAdmin(...)`.

Blacklisted guest emails bypassed via case and plus aliases — Comparing `guest` raw against lowercased `blacklistedGuestEmails` lets `Blocked@Example.com` and plus aliases bypass the blacklist, so a low-privilege attendee can inject blocked addresses. Lowercase the guest and reuse `extractBaseEmail` before comparing.

Unbounded `guests` array allows mass inserts and email fanout per request — A single caller can submit thousands of addresses, triggering as many inserts and outbound emails per request. Cap `guests` with `.max(...)` and reject oversized input.

Guest attendees can add arbitrary attendees to a booking — Any existing attendee, not just the organizer or admin, can inject arbitrary third parties into the organizer's calendar event and trigger invites without consent. Drop the `isAttendee` branch or gate attendee additions behind an organizer setting.

Guest emails are not deduplicated before createMany — `uniqueGuests` never dedupes within the incoming `guests` array, so duplicates reach `createMany` and produce duplicate rows or a constraint error. Dedupe the input server-side, since the schema has no uniqueness refinement.

sendAddGuestsEmails gets raw guests instead of the computed uniqueGuests — Passing raw `guests` makes `sendAddGuestsEmails` classify existing attendees as new, sending duplicate confirmations instead of the added-guests notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` so producer and consumer agree on what counts as a new guest.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165-168`

Duplicate guest added when email casing differs from existing attendee — The case-sensitive `attendee.email` check lets `Foo@Example.com` through when `foo@example.com` already attends, creating a duplicate row and invite. Lowercase both sides in the comparison, matching `blacklistedGuestEmails`.

Error toast leaks raw server error code and message to user — Raw server codes and messages, including Prisma and provider errors from `addGuests`, leak to the user, and this expression is always truthy so the fallback never fires. Show a generic localized message and log the code for server-side diagnostics.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Webhook looks up app metadata by slug but map is keyed by dirName — For every app whose `dirName` differs from its `slug`, the lookup returns undefined and the webhook answers 404, so credential sync silently fails for the main OAuth apps. Resolve the metadata by scanning entries for `meta.slug === app.slug`, as `getAppWithMetadata` in packages/app-store/_appRegistry.ts does, or look the app up by `dirName`.

Salesforce connection uses stale access token after refresh — The fresh token is persisted and then discarded, so the exchange can never fix an expired token and the stored credential is rotated without effect. Build the connection from `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and its `instance_url`, or drop the refresh and let jsforce handle it.

Webhook findFirst overwrites wrong credential for multi-account users — For a user with two Google or Outlook accounts, the arbitrary first row is overwritten with the synced account's keys, corrupting the other account while the intended one is never updated. The payload carries no credential identity, so the webhook needs an external credential identifier instead of `findFirst`.

Credential sync never clears the invalid flag on synced credentials — A credential previously marked broken stays excluded from `getCalendarsEvents`, which filters `!credential.invalid`, even after valid credentials are pushed, so sync can never recover the user's app. Set `invalid: false` in both the `update` and the `create`.

Shared-credential branch returns raw fetch Response without a .data property — Callers still read `res?.data`, so this branch yields undefined and throws a TypeError or silently returns expired credentials in Google's try/catch. Parse the body with `await response.json()` and return an object with a `data` property.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns safeParse envelope instead of token data — Google's refresh path assigns the envelope straight to `credential.key`, so the stored value becomes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` and every later `googleCredentialSchema.parse` fails. Return `refreshTokenResponse.data` so the persisted value keeps the expected shape.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-100`

refreshOAuthTokens receives credential id instead of user id — When credential sync is enabled, the endpoint receives a credential id where it expects a cal.com user id and refreshes the wrong user's credential. Pass the credential's `userId` like the other callers do.

Computed Zod keys collide, stripping refresh_token from token responses — Both computed keys resolve to "[object Object]", so the schema has no expiry or catch-all rule and Zod strips `refresh_token`; line 25 then substitutes the literal placeholder, which callers persist and permanently destroy the real refresh token. Declare the schema explicitly and only fall back to a placeholder when the provider genuinely returns no refresh token.

Placeholder refresh_token overwrites the real stored credential when missing — Zoom and office365calendar persist this literal string, so the real refresh token is overwritten and every later refresh fails with `invalid_grant`, forcing a reinstall. Leave the existing refresh token untouched instead of substituting a dummy string.

Salesforce OAuth refresh runs on every service instantiation — `getClient` runs from the `SalesforceCalendarService` constructor, so every booking and availability operation pays a synchronous OAuth round trip to login.salesforce.com even when the stored token is still valid. Check the `credentialKey` expiry before exchanging, or refresh lazily on a 401.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality — The `!==` comparison short-circuits on the first differing byte, so response timing leaks how many leading characters of `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` were guessed, letting an attacker recover it and inject credentials. Compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over fixed-length buffers, after normalizing a `string[]` header to one string.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Locked SMS reminders are counted as failed retries — `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` for a temporary SMS lock rather than an error, so a deliberate hold is recorded as a failed attempt. Since `deleteMany` then removes reminders above `retryCount` 1, locked accounts lose their SMS permanently; only increment when Twilio actually rejects the request, as in `twilioProvider.ts`.

Retry-count update in SMS reminder catch can abort remaining reminders — This `update` throws P2025 when the row is already gone, for example after `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` in `smsReminderManager.ts` or a parallel cron run, and the unhandled rejection aborts scheduling for all remaining reminders. Wrap it in its own try/catch or use `updateMany` so bookkeeping cannot fail the batch.

Non-atomic retryCount increment can be lost across concurrent runs — Overlapping cron runs both read the same `retryCount` and overwrite each other, so a lost increment leaves the reminder retried forever and the `retryCount > 1` cleanup never fires. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of the stale in-memory value.

Unindexed retryCount OR arm causes WorkflowReminder full scan — The `retryCount` OR arm is unindexed, so the existing `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])` no longer serves this delete and every cron tick scans the whole `WorkflowReminder` table. Move the retry cleanup into its own `deleteMany` or index `retryCount`.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup code login bypasses password when totpCode is present — Anyone with a leaked backup code and the account email gets a session without the password, since the `!credentials.totpCode` gate skips password verification in this branch. Verify `credentials.password` inside the backup-code branch, or drop that gate when `backupCode` is present.

Modal dismissal leaves stale backup-code step and cleared codes — Escape or an overlay click leaves `step` at `DisplayBackupCodes` with codes wiped, so reopening renders a stale screen with no controls. Reset `step`, `backupCodes` and `backupCodesUrl` whenever `open` goes false, not only in the button handlers.

Backup-code lookup is sensitive to input formatting and case — `indexOf` only strips dashes, so a code with any uppercase letter never matches and a valid recovery code is rejected. Normalize to `replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "").toLowerCase()` before matching, and apply the same at `totp/disable.ts:61`.

Backup code consumption is non-atomic and can be reused — The decrypt-null-write-back in the backup-code path is not atomic, so two concurrent requests can both pass `indexOf` and one code authenticates twice. Consume it with a conditional update that checks the unchanged `backupCodes` value.

2FA stays disabled when backup-codes dialog is dismissed without Close — Dismissing with Escape or an overlay click after 2FA is enabled server-side never calls `onEnable`, so the switch still shows 2FA as disabled and the modal shows stale backup codes. Invoke `onEnable()` on `onOpenChange(false)` once the codes are generated.

Backup code field validation never runs, so empty submissions give no feedback — The `required`/`minLength`/`maxLength` attributes never run because the form is `noValidate` and `formSchema` omits `backupCode`, so an empty submit sends `backupCode: ""` and shows no error. Validate `backupCode` in the schema or show an error when it is empty.

Clipboard copy test only asserts toast, not copied content — The `backup-codes-copy` handler shows the toast without checking the clipboard promise, so this test passes even when the copied content is wrong or the copy never happens. Read the clipboard back and assert it equals the dash-formatted codes shown in the dialog.

Backup code verification uses non-constant-time indexOf — `indexOf` on a live backup code reachable from the unauthenticated login endpoint leaks match position and prefix length through timing. Iterate all codes and compare equal-length buffers with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, recording the match without early exit.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58-64`

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: Public options type makes teamId optional, losing compile-time safety — A `team`-scope call that omits `teamId` now compiles and silently returns zero rows via `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse`. Keep the constructor parameter typed as `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` and make `teamId` required for the `team` variant.

Org-scope test assertion depends on unordered array order — `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` use no `orderBy`, so Postgres can return rows in any order and this assertion flaps. Assert the `teamIds` and `userIds` arrays order-independently, or add `orderBy` to the repositories.

Restore deleted caching tests for authorization and filter conditions — Deleting this block leaves no test that calls `getAuthorizationConditions()` or `getFilterConditions()` twice, so a broken memoization in `cachedAuthConditions` or `cachedFilterConditions` would pass CI. Restore both tests against the new `Prisma.Sql` return type.

Prisma.sql assertions compare internal structure instead of SQL — `toEqual` against a `Prisma.sql` template deep-compares the internal `strings`/`values` arrays, and the nested `conditions.reduce` templates partition `strings` differently, so the assertion can mismatch. Compare `conditions.sql` and `conditions.values` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:429-431`

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Unescaped feed URL interpolated into imported-from HTML footer — The feed-supplied `url` is interpolated into the href with no escaping, and the `^https?:\/\/` gate lets a quote and markup through. Since these posts render raw, build the anchor with an escaped href.

Unescaped referer injected into embed layout script — `request.referer` is only host-checked, so a crafted path breaks out of the script block and runs attacker script on the forum origin with access to its cookies. Emit only the parsed origin, JSON-escaped.

Embed view renders unsanitized raw_html cooked content (XSS) — Feeds can carry markup that bypasses the cooking pipeline via the `cook_method` shortcut, and `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites links, so scripts execute on the forum origin. Sanitize `post.cooked` before rendering it raw.

**Also found in:**
- `app/models/post.rb:130-137`

Referer check allows unauthenticated clients to create unlimited topics — The `Referer` header is client-supplied, so any non-browser client can pass the `ensure_embeddable` check and create unbounded topics by randomizing `embed_url` paths. Gate creation on a non-forgeable token or a per-IP rate limit.

nil feed item content raises NoMethodError and aborts polling — Items that only carry `<description>` leave `i.content` nil, so `nil.scrub` raises and aborts the whole poll; with no retries the run is lost. Fall back to `i.description` and skip blank content.

`end if` without a condition causes a SyntaxError in the embed/best template — `end if` with no condition is a SyntaxError, so the template fails to compile on the branch where a topic was found and `/embed/best` raises instead of rendering. Use a plain `end`.

Throttle key can persist without TTL due to non-atomic setnx and expire — A failure between the two calls leaves `retrieved:<url>` without a TTL, so `setnx` never succeeds again and `perform_retrieve` skips that URL forever. Make the set and TTL a single atomic operation.

Remote embed fetch has no timeout and reads unbounded body — A slow or oversized page pins the `retrieve_topic` worker indefinitely or exhausts memory, since `open(url).read` has no timeout and no size cap. Pass explicit timeout options and limit the bytes read.
postMessage target origin is full referer URL, not an origin — Send the parsed origin instead.

Message origin check uses substring match instead of exact origin — A substring match accepts messages from lookalike origins like `https://discourse.example.co`, letting an attacker drive `iframe.height`. Compare `e.origin` exactly against the forum origin and also check `e.source` is the embed iframe.

TopicEmbed.import races on embed_url and raises RecordNotUnique — Two workers can both see `embed.blank?`, and the unique index on `embed_url` makes the loser's `TopicEmbed.create!` raise `RecordNotUnique`, rolling back its just-created topic and post. Rescue the conflict and reuse the existing embed.

Test for feed_polling_enabled? doesn't isolate the enabled flag — `feed_polling_url` and `embed_by_username` stay at their blank defaults, so `poll_feed` is skipped regardless of the enabled flag and the test would pass even without that guard. Make the other two conditions truthy so only the flag prevents the call.

**Also found in:**
- `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18-22`
- `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:24-28`

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Migration dereferences nil when embed_category or uncategorized row is missing — Forums that never overrode `embed_category` have no such `SiteSetting` row, so `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises `NoMethodError` and the migration cannot run. Guard with `.first` and fall back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`.

Migration inserts embeddable hosts without normalization or SQL escaping — Legacy values with a scheme or path survive verbatim, so `record_for_host` never matches the bare host and embedding silently breaks after upgrade. Normalize each value like the model does and use a quoted insert so a host containing a quote cannot abort the migration.

EmbeddableHost lookup fails when referer host has uppercase letters — A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/page` keeps its case, so `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` never matches the configured host and the embed frame is rejected. Downcase the argument too.

Guard `_hydrateEmbedded` against non-array `_ids` values — The regex now matches every `_ids` key, so a null or non-array value makes `obj[k].map` throw and breaks the whole `store.find`/`findAll` for that type. Guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])` and leave the key untouched otherwise.

Missing nil check on embeddable host lookup returns 500 — A stale or already-deleted id (double-click on delete, two admins editing) makes `host.host = ...` or `host.destroy` raise `NoMethodError` and answer 500. Use `find_by!` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` so a missing record returns 404.

Uncached embeddable host lookup runs on every embed request — Each embedded page view now adds an uncached SQL round trip, and the `lower(host) = ?` predicate blocks any index on `host`. Cache the host list and compare in Ruby, or store hosts downcased in an indexed column.

Migration resolves numeric embed_category by name, losing category — A stored numeric id fails the name join, so `category_id` resolves to 0 and every host falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`, losing the category. Resolve by id when the value is numeric and by name otherwise, mirroring `TopicCreator#find_category`.

Embedded posts lose category when EmbeddableHost lookup misses — When `record_for_host` returns `false` for an unparseable URL or `nil` for no match, the embedded topic is created with `category: nil` and lands in uncategorized, where it previously went to the configured category. Fall back to `SiteSetting.embed_category`, and downcase the argument in `record_for_host`.

Vacuous expandable_first_post? test no longer exercises embeddable host — `expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts, and this example sets neither `embed_truncate` nor the `has_topic_embed?` stub, so it passes on defaults and cannot fail for the reason its name claims. Delete it; the no-embed case is already covered in the nested block.

before_validation crashes on nil host instead of failing validation — A nil host from a missing `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` makes `self.host.sub!` raise `NoMethodError` and answer 500, so `validates_format_of :host` never reports it. Assign through `self.host.to_s.sub(...)` to return a 422 instead.

Plural embedded hydration drops unresolved ids and maps null — When the side-loaded key does not match `pluralize(subType)` or is missing, every `_lookupSubType` returns undefined, the raw ids are lost, and the property becomes `[undefined, ...]`. Delete and replace the ids key only when the lookup resolved, otherwise keep the original.

Plural `*_ids` hydration stores undefined for missing records — `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for ids missing from the side-loaded collection, so `[undefined, ...]` is stored and consumers like `embeddable-host`'s `host.category.id` throw a TypeError. Filter unresolved ids before assigning.

Test requests fruit 2 but pretender fixture returns fruit 1's data — The pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` in `create-pretender.js.es6` hardcodes `fruits[0]` and ignores the requested id, so these assertions verify apple's fixture and would pass even if the store mangled the id. Look the record up by `request.params.id` or request fruit 1.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Downsize tempfile path lacks extension, collapsing animated GIFs — Without an extension, `file.tempfile.path` fails `optimize`'s `.GIF` check, so `allow_animation` does nothing and every animated GIF is collapsed to one frame. Copy the tempfile to a path carrying the original extension (as `OptimizedImage.create_for` does) before downscaling, then convert back.

API upload URL download uses hardcoded 10 MB cap instead of site settings — Hardcoding the ceiling lets any API upload URL, even non-images `FileHelper.is_image?` excludes, force a 10 MB fetch despite a smaller configured limit. Derive the cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` and `SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb` instead of a constant.

New `downsize` definition shadows width/height version and breaks caller — The `downsize` call in `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb` still passes five positional arguments to the new 3-4 arity, raising `ArgumentError` and leaving emoji un-resized. Update that caller to the `"100x100"` dimension-string form, or keep a width/height-compatible method name.

Client upload size check hardcodes 10MB instead of using configured site setting — Hardcoding 10 MB desyncs the client from the server, which still enforces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so attachments pass client-side then fail server-side. Drive the check from the same `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` setting the server uses.

Downsizing loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize failure — When `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails, all five full convert passes still run synchronously, multiplying CPU cost with no size reduction. Break out of the loop when `downsize` returns false.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Non-automatic group members silently truncated to 50 — Regular groups now return at most 50 members, and the public group page has no pager, so members past 50 are unreachable. Return all members when no `limit` param is supplied, or add pagination to `group-members.js.es6` and `members.hbs`.

Group creation ignores alias_level parameter — Any alias level picked while creating a group is silently dropped, so the group is saved with the default 0. Assign `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?` as `update` does.

remove_member bypasses Group#remove and leaves primary_group_id stale — Deleting the join row directly skips `Group#destroy_deletions`, leaving `users.primary_group_id` pointing at a group the user left and skippng the `user_count` decrement. Resolve the user and call `group.remove(user)` instead of `group.users.delete(user_id)`.

remove_member raises when user is not a group member — Removing a user who is not a member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, so a stale admin UI or a concurrent removal returns an error. Look up the membership with `group.group_users.find_by(user_id: user_id)` and no-op when it is nil.

Group members endpoint allows unbounded limit parameter — Any visitor can request an unbounded `limit` and force a full member load plus serialization of the whole group. Clamp `params[:limit]` to a maximum of 200 before applying `limit`/`offset`.

add_members re-adds existing members and raises RecordNotUnique — Re-adding an existing member violates the unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, raising `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` after earlier users in the batch were already inserted. Call `group.add(user)` only unless `group.users.include?(user)`.

totalPages computes an extra page when user_count is a multiple of limit — With exactly `limit` members, `totalPages` reports an extra page, so Next stays enabled and lands on an empty list. Use Math.ceil with a 0 guard so the counter matches the data.

Automatic group members incorrectly show remove link — `{{#unless automatic}}` cannot resolve in the member item view context, so automatic groups show a remove link whose DELETE returns 422. Reference the group explicitly via `view.parentView.model.automatic`.

**Also found in:**
- `app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6:1-4`

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Fallback chain isn't loaded for non-request translations; misses are cached — Translations outside a request (jobs, mailers, rake tasks) resolve the fallback chain against a locale that `load_locale` never loaded, raising `MissingTranslation`. Load the whole `I18n.fallbacks` chain inside `I18n.translate`/`load_locale` instead of relying on the controller filter.

I18n fallback lookup raises when SiteSetting is unavailable — `FallbackLocaleList#[]` runs on every `I18n.t` and reads `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which queries the DB and raises in boot/rake paths when it's unavailable. Guard the lookup with a rescue that falls back to `:en`, or resolve the site locale once outside the per-call chain.

Translation cache key ignores fallback site default locale — Fallback results now depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but the cache key in `translate_accelerator.rb` omits it and nothing calls `I18n.reload!` on settings changes, so stale languages persist after an admin updates `default_locale`. Include the site default locale in the cache key or clear the cache on `site_setting_saved`.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Synchronous TagDevice adds DB round trip to anonymous auth — Every anonymous request that misses the cache now blocks the auth middleware on `CountDevices` and an `anon_device` upsert, and a stalled database stalls auth with no timeout or `recover()`. Move `TagDevice` back to the fire-and-forget goroutine with its own timeout and panic recovery.

Device limit keyed on spoofable client-supplied ID enables auth DoS — `DeviceID` comes from the spoofable `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header, so random IDs fill the 30-day `updated_at` window and deny anonymous auth instance-wide for up to 30 days. Bind the quota to a server-side signal such as IP or a rate limiter instead of the client-supplied identifier.

ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 param breaks wire DI registration — Wire still registers `ProvideAnonDBStore`, whose new `int64` dependency the container cannot supply, so generation fails wherever `anonstore.AnonStore` is resolved. Remove that provider from the set in `pkg/server/wire.go` since `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now builds the store inline.

Test never exercises successful update at device limit — The test only submits nonexistent `device_id` "keep", so `updateDevice`'s UPDATE always affects 0 rows and a broken update path would still pass. Add a step re-submitting "32mdo31deeqwes" with a new IP and assert `ListDevices` returns one device with the updated `ClientIP`.

anonymousDeviceLimit inferred as undefined-only instead of number | undefined — Without an annotation `anonymousDeviceLimit` is inferred as the literal `undefined`, but `GrafanaConfig` declares `number | undefined`, so the numeric limit from the backend cannot be represented. Annotate it as `number | undefined` like the sibling `loginError` field.

Device-limit rejection bypassed by cache set before device insert — `tagDeviceUI` writes the cache key before `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, so a device rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is cached as tagged and slips through on the next request within the TTL. Set the cache entry only after the insert succeeds, or delete the key on rejection.

Device limit check races with insert, allowing too many devices — `CountDevices` and the INSERT run in separate statements, so two concurrent new devices both see limit-1 and the table exceeds `deviceLimit`. Perform the count and insert under one lock or enforce the cap inside the insert statement.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Double-check assets cache under write lock to avoid serialization — Every caller that lost the race re-runs the full manifest load while holding the global write lock, serializing bursts of requests. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` under the write lock after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` and return it if populated, so only the first caller loads.

TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, discarding recorded logs — A fresh `NewTestLogger` drops the receiver's recorded `Logs`, `InfoLogs`, and `ErrorLogs` along with the context attributes, so assertions on the original logger pass vacuously or fail spuriously. This violates the `Logger` contract in ifaces.go; return the receiver itself, or a shallow copy sharing the same sinks.

Async legacy update reuses raw objInfo instead of persisted object — For patch-based infos the two stores now diverge, and a non-idempotent `UpdatedObject` can fail or write a different object to legacy. Wrap `objInfo` in `updateWrapper{updated: res}` as the pre-PR code did.

Backgrounded legacy writes inherit request context and are cancelled — Because the request-scoped `ctx` is cancelled when the handler returns, the backgrounded legacy write aborts and the object is never persisted to LegacyStorage. Detach the context with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or keep the write on the request path; the same pattern repeats in `Delete`, `Update` and `DeleteCollection`.

Update error path records storage latency in legacy metric — A unified-storage failure is counted in the legacy metric even though the legacy update never ran. Use `recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`; `Create` has the identical mistake.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:43-48`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45-45`

DeleteCollection legacy delete records to storage metric — Legacy latency and errors land in the unified-storage metric, so the legacy metric never gets a sample for this method. Use `recordLegacyDuration`, as the other legacy goroutines do.

Delete records storage duration with object name as kind label, unbounded metric cardinality — The object `name` fills the `kind` label of `WithLabelValues(isError, mode, name, method)`, creating a new Prometheus series for every deleted object and inflating memory without bound. Pass `options.Kind`.

Delete success metric passes object name as the kind label — The object name becomes the `kind` label, giving a new series per deleted object and nonsense delete metrics. Pass `options.Kind`; also pass the request-scoped `log` instead of `d.Log` to `klog.NewContext`.

TestMode3_Create never verifies the asynchronous legacy write — Deleting the legacy goroutine, making legacy `Create` always fail, or dropping the 10s timeout would leave this test green. Synchronize on the legacy call and assert its expectations.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:215-241`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Log reads TotalDocs() concurrently with watcher goroutine writes — `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without `cacheMu` while the write-event goroutine inserts into the same map, so Go raises a fatal concurrent map read and map write error at startup. Take `cacheMu.RLock()` inside `TotalDocs` or read the count only after the watcher is quiescent.

Concurrent BuildIndex calls can duplicate index construction — Concurrent callers that miss the cache for the same key now build the same index twice, with the losing index still receiving writes that are silently lost. Restore per-key serialization across the build, or check-and-insert under the lock and return the already-cached index.

Missing s.cancel() on Init failure leaks server context and watcher — A failed startup leaves an orphaned write-event watcher consuming database events for a server object nobody holds, since the context from line 229 leaks and the watcher loops keep running. Call `s.cancel()` on the error path and give `searchSupport.init`'s watch a cancellable context.

Skipping postgres case masks eager-init behavior change in resource server — This skips the only coverage of the instrumentation-server-without-http-server path on postgres, hiding that eager init in `NewResourceServer` now runs before surrounding startup state it depended on. Fix the ordering so the caller still drives initialization instead of dropping the test.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Grafana delete ability merged into canDelete but unused by menu item — In the list view `rulerRule` is undefined, so the Delete action vanishes and the merged prom ability is dead computation. Gate the menu item and `handleDelete` on the prom case too (e.g. from `promRule.uid`), or drop the unused ability merge.

Prom-only pause ability has no effect in alert list view — Because `rulerRule` is always undefined in the list view, the Pause item never renders and the merged prom pause ability has no effect. Render a pause item based on the prom rule (or remove the rulered gate) so pause works there.

Silence notifications action renders no drawer in Grafana rule list — With only `promRule` passed and `canSilence` true from the prom abilities, the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` mount condition in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx stays false, so the click is a silent no-op. Render the drawer from the prom rule as well.

Missing Grafana prom rule reports not loading and enables Duplicate — A missing rule reports `loading: false`, so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported` and `Duplicate` only checks the global permission. Return `loading: true` (or not supported) when no Grafana prom rule is supplied so cloud rules don't offer Duplicate without `AlertingRuleExternalWrite`.

GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterViewResults is rendered without a key — Unkeyed, this child is reconciled by position, so per-item state like the open menu or pending identifier can attach to the wrong rule. Restore a stable key on the element, e.g. `key={key}` or `key={rule.uid}`.

Federated rule groups lose immutability in useAllRulerRuleAbilities — Passing only `rule.rulerRule` discards `rule.group`, so federated (Mimir) groups are reported as editable and the UI offers actions that cannot succeed. Keep the `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` detection on this path instead of the constant.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Non-default getShortcut() and missing validation break grant factories — A third-party grant factory predating this change aborts startup with `AbstractMethodError`, a null shortcut throws `NullPointerException` from `ConcurrentHashMap.put`, and a wrong-length shortcut makes every id it encodes unparsable. Validate `grantShortcut` for non-null and length 2 in `postInit`, and make `getShortcut()` a default method so existing implementations keep working.

testIncorrectGrantType passes on NPE and never asserts IllegalArgumentException — The fixture leaves `factory.sessionFactory` null, so the broad `catch (RuntimeException)` swallows a `NullPointerException` and the test passes without exercising the unknown-grant validation. Set a `sessionFactory` on the fixture and assert `IllegalArgumentException` specifically instead of catching `RuntimeException`.

Grant-shortcut check in isAccessTokenId is inverted — The comparison rejects ids that have the expected grant and accepts ones that do not, so every caller such as `expectCodeToToken` and `expectRefresh` fails on correct tokens and passes on wrong-grant tokens. Negate it and use `substring(4, 6)`, since the shortcut starts at index 4.

Inverted grant-type shortcut check in isAccessTokenId matcher — The inverted guard rejects a match and accepts a mismatch, so for `ac`, `dg`, `rt` and `ci` the check never triggers and `isAccessTokenId` degenerates into a UUID check. Negate it and slice `substring(4, 6)`.

isAccessTokenId matcher rejects matching grant shortcut instead of mismatching one — The matcher rejects a matching shortcut and accepts a mismatching one, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` pass for any grant value. Negate the condition and extract via `substring(4, 6)`.

Inverted access token grant-shortcut comparison in isAccessTokenId — The inverted comparison rejects a correct token and accepts any wrong grant, so the `isAccessTokenId` callers would pass even if the grant type were wrong. Negate it and use `substring(4, 6)`.

Inverted grant shortcut check in isAccessTokenId rejects correct tokens — The matcher rejects the token exactly when the encoded shortcut matches, so `isAccessTokenId(RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT)` and the other new expectations fail on correct tokens. Negate the condition.

isAccessTokenId extracts grant shortcut at wrong offset — The offset is off by one: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4..6, so `substring(3, 5)` yields `ta` instead of `ac` for `onrtac:…`. Slice `substring(4, 6)`.
Null check validates grantType instead of rawTokenId — Require `rawTokenId` here instead.

getSubGroupsCount may return null when cached group is unresolved — Returning null breaks the contract, and `GroupUtils` passes the value straight into `representation.setSubGroupCount(...)`, so the count can be silently absent or NPE on unboxing. Return a non-null default such as 0, or handle null in that consumer.

Reader thread not joined before asserting caught exceptions — An exception from the request in flight during the concurrent-delete window may not yet be in `caughtExceptions`, so the test can pass while the NPE still reproduces. Join the reader thread before the `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` check.

Reader thread is not joined before the exception assertion — The assertion reads `caughtExceptions` while the reader thread can still append, so a racing exception may be recorded after it passes, or the loop may exit without a read against the deleted state. Join the reader thread before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` so every raced read counts.

Reader thread can loop forever when group deletion throws — If any `remove()` throws, `deletedAll.set(true)` is never reached and the non-daemon reader thread spins in a delay-free loop, hanging the forked JVM. Set the flag in a `finally` around the delete loop and join the thread with a bounded timeout before asserting.

Choice-format blocks hide HTML from message sanitizer — Because `normalizeValue` strips the `{n,choice,...}` block before sanitizing, HTML hidden in `error-invalid-multivalued-size` on both sides is erased and passes, enabling XSS. Sanitize the block content before substituting the placeholder instead of discarding it.

Lithuanian TOTP setup message replaced with Italian text — Lithuanian users now see an Italian sentence on the TOTP setup page. Restore a Lithuanian translation of `loginTotpStep1` here and of `totpStep1` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`.

Tests never exercise allowed HTML translation branch — Both `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties` and `noHtml_de.properties` bypass the permissive branch, so breaking `containsHtml(englishValue)` would leave all tests green while legal `<b>` translations fail. Add an English/German fixture pair with an allowed tag asserting `verify()` returns empty.

Multivalued size error message uses Java MessageFormat syntax i18next cannot render — The admin console renders this key with i18next (`user-profile/utils.ts:79`), which ignores `{0}` and the `MessageFormat` choice, so users see the literal placeholder text. Keep `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in `{{n}}` form.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties:188-188`

Missing English bundle aborts verification with raw RuntimeException — A translation file without a matching `messages_en.properties` makes `verifySafeHtml` throw a raw `RuntimeException` that escapes the `IOException` catch and aborts the build. Check `Files.exists` and report the file through `messages` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: All-clients grants ignored when per-client resource exists — Any client with its own resource loses the grants an admin holds on the "Clients" type resource, so all-clients `manage`, `configure` and `view` silently stop applying. Evaluate the type resource as well and fall back to it instead of consulting it only when `resourceStore.findByName` returns null.

getClientsWithPermission matches only type resource, not per-client grants — The per-client resources from `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` carry no type, so `findByType` returns only the literal "Clients" resource and omits every real grant, leaving `getRoleIdsWithPermissions` with a null client id. Iterate the realm's clients and check `hasPermission` on each instead.

canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException on token exchange path — `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` calls `canExchangeTo` on every cross-client exchange, so enabling V2 turns each one into an uncaught exception and HTTP 500 instead of a 403. Return `false` or delegate to the existing evaluation, including the inherited 2-arg overload.

Client removal fails when both fine-grained authz features are enabled — With V1 and V2 both enabled, the `ClientRemovedEvent` branch still reaches `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` and throws, so deleting a client returns 500. Skip that branch when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is on, since V2 needs no permission cleanup.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/MgmtPermissionsV2.java:63-68`

canView(ClientModel) issues redundant per-client permission checks — `ClientsResource.getClients` calls `canView` per client, so a realm listing runs up to four resource lookups and policy evaluations each, with the type-level result never cached. Check `hasPermission(scope)` once and evaluate the client scopes in a single pass.

Missing null check on fallback resource before evaluation — When the `getResourceTypeResource` fallback also returns null, `root.evaluatePermission` dereferences a null `resource` and throws. Return `false` before the evaluation when `resource` is null.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:215-222`
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:214-222`

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Passkeys conditional UI include missing from base login-password.ftl — The base template behind every inheriting theme still lacks the passkey control, so passkey-only users reach a password page with no way to authenticate. Add the `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData/>` include to `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/login-password.ftl`.

Organization clause in shared login predicate hides linked brokers — `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` also uses `getLoginPredicate()`, so users linked to an organization IDP without `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` lose that provider from the login page. Keep the stricter predicate local to the invalidation code or add an explicit method instead of altering the shared predicate.

Login IDP cache invalidates shared entry for each new organization — Every login page then loads and copies the IDP ids of all organizations, and each new organization's first request triggers a full reload. Include `organizationId` in `cacheKeyForLogin` so entries are per-organization, or accept a per-search-key entry instead of invalidating the shared one.

Login cache test misses login-eligible IDP create/remove — Both IDPs fail `getLoginPredicate()`, so dropping the invalidation calls from `create()` and `remove()` would still pass, leaving the stale-login-list regression undetected. Add a step that creates and removes a login-eligible IDP and asserts the login caches become null for every `FetchMode`.

Discarded getForLogin results leave cached return path untested — The return half of the cached branch, resolving ids via `getById`, is never verified, so an empty or wrong returned set still passes. Collect the aliases returned by `getForLogin` and assert them against the expected set alongside the cache-entry count.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Table widget flag branch renders blank grid with empty data — Every table widget renders a blank grid once the flag is enabled, since `fields` and `result` are discarded. Feed the already-computed `result.data`, `result.meta` and `fields` into `TableWidgetVisualization`.

Error context dropped when field params are provided — Any caller passing field params gets [] for error_ids, so the new error context is silently dropped. Request the replay fields independently of the client's field list so error ids are always available.

Invalid field query param causes 500 in replay breadcrumbs — An authenticated `?field=bogus` request raises `KeyError` in `process_raw_response` and returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Filter the requested fields against the known response keys before calling it.

Report tests no longer post with application/reports+json content type — Without the browser-reporting content type DRF uses the generic `JSONParser`, so these tests would still pass if `BrowserReportsJSONParser` broke. Restore `content_type="application/reports+json"` on at least one request.

Unauthenticated endpoint logs raw unvalidated report payload — This unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint lets anyone persist arbitrary content, and browser reports carry URLs, tokens and page messages into a retained warning log. Log only non-sensitive shape information instead of `raw_report`.

Replay error events mispaired by positional get_multi zip — `NodeStorage.get_multi` dedupes ids and appends cache hits after service results, so `zip` mispairs ids with another event's data and drops trailing ones. Look events up by node id instead of relying on positional order.

Mutually exclusive age/timestamp check uses truthiness, so 0 slips through — A legal value of 0 is falsy, so `timestamp`/`age` pairs like `{"timestamp": 0, "age": 5}` pass the mutually exclusive check. Use existence checks such as `"age" in self.initial_data` in `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Per-shard buffers multiply global max-flush-segments limit by process count — With N shard processes, each shard now admits ~N× the segments per cycle, so aggregate flush capacity reaches ~N × `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` and `any_shard_at_limit` fires late, letting the queue overrun its bound. Keep the divisor global by passing the total assigned shard count to the buffer so the limit stays cluster-wide.

Spans flusher queries cluster memory once per buffer in submit — `get_memory_info()` fans out a cluster-wide `INFO` to every master regardless of `assigned_shards`, so `submit` issues one round trip per buffer and the summed totals are the same numbers counted N times. Query memory once per `submit` and reuse it across buffers.

Unhealthy flusher process is never killed due to isinstance guard — The guard never matches a `SpawnProcess`, so a hung flusher is never killed and its replacement races the old one on the same shard queues, duplicating segments and leaving orphans. Drop the `isinstance` guard or test against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`.

Flusher wait_produce timer uses inconsistent "shards" metric tag — The sibling `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` timers tag this same value as `shard`, so dashboards grouping on one shard tag silently miss this metric. Use `{"shard": shard_tag}` for consistency.

flusher_unhealthy tags shard with bare int instead of shard_tag — Every other emit site tags `shard` with `shard_tag`, the comma-joined group, so this metric's bare int lives in a different value domain and per-shard grouping can never match. Emit `shard_tag` here or use one identifier at all sites.

Assertion does not verify shard distribution across flusher processes — The sum equals 4 for any assignment of the shards, so the test passes even if round-robin placed them all in one process. Assert the per-process counts, e.g. sorted lengths equal `[2, 2]`.

Deadline break in join() leaves flusher processes alive — When the deadline expires, the `break` skips the `terminate()` for that process and every remaining one, leaving hung flushers running after `join()` returns. Move the terminate outside the deadline break so all spawned processes are killed on shutdown.

Sleep after drift change is a no-op due to patched time.sleep — `time.sleep` is patched to a no-op at line 15, so this returns immediately and provides none of the synchronization the comment claims, running the assertion before post-drift processing finishes. Synchronize on a real condition or remove the misleading sleep.

max_processes truthiness mishandles 0 and negative values — Truthiness treats a configured `0` as unset, silently running one process per shard instead of failing fast, while a negative value passes here and later raises `KeyError` on `process_to_shards_map`. Use an explicit None check and reject values below 1.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: sync_status_outbound assignment_source unused; ExampleIntegration lacks kwargs — Status-sync cycles stay broken for the kind this PR fixes, and the first caller passing `assignment_source` will hit a `TypeError` in `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound`. Update the call in `tasks/sync_status_outbound.py` and add `**kwargs` to the example integration.

AssignmentSource round-trip loses datetime type for queued — A queued `AssignmentSource` comes back with `queued` as a `str` instead of a `datetime`, and the first consumer comparing it to `timezone.now()` fails far from here. Serialize `queued` with isoformat in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

queued timestamp is shared across all AssignmentSource instances — Every `AssignmentSource` shares one import-time timestamp, so `queued` never reflects when that source was enqueued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own time.

Active-only Integration lookup blocks reinstalling inactive integrations — Filtering by `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE` makes a non-ACTIVE Integration return "Invalid installation request" even though `ensure_integration` in src/sentry/integrations/pipeline.py resets `status` to ACTIVE on reinstall. Drop the status filter so retries reach `ensure_integration`.

Pipeline state mutated before OAuth state validation — A request with a forged or invalid state still overwrites the victim's Redis-backed `installation_id` via `pipeline.bind_state`, so a later legitimate completion resolves the wrong installation in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`. Bind `installation_id` only on the first, state-less request so rejected requests cannot mutate pipeline state.

GitHub OAuth callback state uses constant pipeline signature — `pipeline.signature` is the same constant for every user and org, so the callback check accepts any attacker-computed value and gives no CSRF protection. Generate a per-request nonce with `secrets.token_hex()`, bind it via `pipeline.bind_state`, and compare the callback against the stored value as `OAuth2LoginView`/`OAuth2CallbackView` do in src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py.

Unhandled GitHub OAuth token and user info failures return HTTP 500 — An expired code, a 401 from GitHub, or a network error escapes as an unhandled HTTP 500 instead of the error page, because `raise_for_status` in src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py and `safe_urlopen` both raise. Wrap the token request and `get_user_info` in the existing try/except and fall through to `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

KeyError when GitHub integration metadata lacks sender — `integration.metadata["sender"]` only exists for webhook-created integrations, so pipeline-created ones raise `KeyError` (HTTP 500) instead of showing the failure page; `installation.py:44` guards this same key. Read it with `(integration.metadata.get("sender") or {}).get("login")` and return `error(...)` when missing.

test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found — The second request passes a wrong `state`, so `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` returns at the state-mismatch guard and the `Integration.DoesNotExist` path is never exercised. Complete the OAuth step with the correct `pipeline.signature` state and assert "The GitHub installation could not be found."

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler leaves abstract methods unimplemented — Switching `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` to `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare pass leaves `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` abstract, so instantiating it raises TypeError and `Detector.detector_handler` crashes for every `metric_alert_fire` detector. Implement the abstract members as no-op stubs until the metric-alert hook exists, or stop registering this class as the detector handler.

build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value argument — The `value` argument is never included in the returned occurrence or event_data, so no assertion actually covers it and tests with wrong or stale values still pass. Fold `value` into what `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` returns, then pass the real evaluated value at each call site so a wrong `value` reaches the hook and fails the test.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Monitor context returns raw config, discarding mutated schedule_type — The occurrence payload keeps the raw `schedule_type` key instead of the readable label, so the copy and its replacement are wasted. Return the mutated `config` in the `"config"` field.

Null destinationCalendar drops collective hosts' calendars — When an organizer has no calendar configured, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` silently skips adding `teamDestinationCalendars`. Default `destinationCalendar` to an empty array `[]` instead of `null` to preserve collective host calendars.

Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED check for organization slug — Organizations created with team billing disabled are left without a `slug`. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` so the organization receives its slug directly.

Unchecked access to mainHostDestinationCalendar causes TypeError — An empty `evt.destinationCalendar` causes `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` to throw an unhandled `TypeError` when checking `MeetLocationType`. Use optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` to guard against `undefined`.

`selectedCalendar` fallback matches against falsy `externalCalendarId` — Matching against a falsy `externalCalendarId` always evaluates to `undefined`, leaving `selectedCalendar` unset. Fall back directly to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-318`

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.
