When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses logical AND instead of OR — Because a user cannot be both an admin and an owner simultaneously, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` always evaluates to `false`. Replace `&&` with `||` so either role is permitted.

Unfiltered guests array passed to sendAddGuestsEmails — Existing attendees present in `guests` will be misidentified as new guests and sent `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Hardcoded refresh token dummy string overwrites stored credentials — Merging this result overwrites and permanently corrupts valid OAuth refresh tokens in the database. Remove the fallback assignment so `refresh_token` is omitted when absent.

Credential key updated with SafeParseReturnType instead of parsed data — Storing the wrapper object in the database corrupts the credential record and breaks subsequent calendar operations. Destructure `data` from `parseRefreshTokenResponse` so only the parsed credential payload is passed to `prisma.credential.update`.

refreshOAuthTokens receives credential ID instead of user ID — Passing a credential record ID prevents the sync endpoint from locating the Cal.com user. Pass `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens` instead of `credentialId`.

Raw fetch Response returned instead of response data expected by callers — Returning a raw `Response` lacks the `.data` property expected by callers, causing unhandled `TypeError` exceptions when accessing tokens. Parse the response body with `await response.json()` before returning it.

Header lookup fails if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME has uppercase characters — Node normalizes incoming header names to lowercase, causing lookup failures if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` contains uppercase characters. Call `.toLowerCase()` on the header key before indexing `req.headers`.

Insecure fallback to empty string for encryption key — Decrypting with an empty string compromises security when the environment variable is unset. Reject the request early if `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing instead of falling back to `""`.

Invalid `[z.string().toString()]` key in Zod schema strips response properties — Evaluating `toString()` creates a static `"[object Object]"` key, causing Zod to strip token expiry fields from the response. Chain `.passthrough()` onto `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of defining computed schema keys.

Timing attack vulnerability in webhook secret comparison — Comparing secrets with `!==` leaks timing information that allows attackers to guess the secret token. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for a constant-time comparison instead.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Retry count cleanup deletes non-SMS workflow reminders — Reminders for `EMAIL` or `WHATSAPP` with `retryCount > 1` are inadvertently deleted because `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` only scopes the first `OR` branch. Move `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the top-level `where` clause alongside `OR` so both conditions apply only to SMS reminders.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: NoMethodError when feed item content is nil — Feed items that omit content abort the scheduled poll job when `scrub` is called on `nil`. Check that `i.content` is present before calling `scrub` and `CGI.unescapeHTML`.
Syntax error from invalid `<%- end if %>` tag — ERB compilation fails and crashes the view whenever comments render. Replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>` to close the conditional block.

Test 'requires feed_polling_url' does not enable feed polling — Because `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to `false`, `execute` short-circuits early and creates a false positive even if URL validation breaks. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true` and supply `embed_by_username`.

Test does not stub feed_polling_enabled? or feed_polling_url — Because `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to `false`, `execute` short-circuits early and passes even if username checks break. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true` and configure `feed_polling_url`.

Full URL passed as postMessage targetOrigin fails origin match — Passing the full URL from `request.referer` fails origin matching or throws a `SyntaxError`, blocking `discourse-resize` messages. Pass `'*'` or a parsed origin to `parent.postMessage` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: NoMethodError when indexing query results without checking row presence — If `embed_category` or `uncategorized_category_id` returns no rows, indexing `[0]` raises `NoMethodError`. Verify the query results are present before reading `['id']` or `['value']`.

Obsolete test for blank embeddable_host in Topic#expandable_first_post? — `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks embeddable hosts, so this test passes vacuously regardless of host state. Remove this spec or update it to test `SiteSetting.embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`.

NoMethodError when host is nil in before_validation callback — A blank or missing `self.host` causes `sub!` to raise `NoMethodError`, crashing with a 500 error instead of validation failures. Guard the mutations with `if self.host.present?`.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Invalid ImageMagick resize geometry and stale tempfile size in downsize loop — Appending `\>` to `"80%"` produces invalid ImageMagick geometry, and `tempfile.size` caches the initial file size so the loop cannot terminate early. Use pixel dimensions for `OptimizedImage.downsize` and check `File.size(tempfile.path)` on each iteration.

Duplicate method definition overwrites OptimizedImage.downsize — Ruby lacks method overloading, so callers like `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` expecting the 5-parameter signature will raise an `ArgumentError`. Merge both parameter signatures into a single `downsize` method that handles either argument structure.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description:
`remove_member` expects nonexistent `group_id` parameter — Requests fail with `ActionController::ParameterMissing` because member routes provide `params[:id]` rather than `params[:group_id]`. Update `remove_member` to read `params.require(:id)`.

**Also found in:**
- `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:66-70`
- `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:84-86`

Duplicate or existing group members cause unhandled database exception — Submitting existing or duplicate usernames triggers a unique constraint violation on `index_group_users_on_group_id_and_user_id`, resulting in an unhandled 500 error. Check membership with `group.users.include?(user)` before calling `group.add(user)`.

totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit — Users can paginate to an empty page when `user_count` divides evenly by `limit`. Replace the `Math.floor` calculation with `Math.ceil`.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Device cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice validation completes — Blocked devices exceeding `deviceLimit` can bypass authentication on subsequent requests because `tagDeviceUI` returns `nil` on cache hits. Populate `localCache` only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or evict the key on error.

Outer args slice mutated in retried WithDbSession callback — Retrying the transaction on lock contention prepends duplicate `query` elements to `args`, causing execution to fail with argument mismatch errors. Pass `query` directly to `dbSession.Exec` instead of prepending it to `args`.

TOCTOU race condition in device limit check — Concurrent requests can all see the count below `deviceLimit` and insert simultaneously, exceeding the configured limit. Move `CountDevices` and the insert into a single transaction with appropriate locking.

Unbound int64 in ProvideAnonDBStore breaks Wire provider set — Wire code generation fails because it cannot resolve the unbound `deviceLimit int64` parameter registered in `pkg/server/wire.go`. Update or remove the `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` registration in `wire.go` since `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now instantiates it directly.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Context cancellation aborts asynchronous legacy write — Propagating request context cancellation aborts background writes as soon as the HTTP handler returns. Wrap `ctx` with `context.WithoutCancel` before calling `context.WithTimeoutCause`.

High metric cardinality from passing object name instead of kind — Using individual resource names causes metric cardinality explosion and excessive memory consumption in Prometheus. Pass `options.Kind` instead of `name` to `d.recordStorageDuration`.

Create storage error recorded under legacy metric instead of storage — This misattributes storage failures and latency to the legacy storage metric. Call `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration` when `d.Storage.Create` fails.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:128-130`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:165-167`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Concurrent index creation causes storage conflicts and race conditions — Concurrent calls to `bleve.New` for the same key will collide on the directory path, corrupting index files and leaking duplicate indices. Keep `b.cacheMu` locked across the entire build or synchronize creation with a per-key lock.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem — Without item identity tracking inside `rules.map`, React can hit reconciliation bugs and retain stale state as filtered results update. Pass `key={key}` to `<GrafanaRuleListItem>`.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: rawTokenId validation checks grantType instead of rawTokenId — This leaves `rawTokenId` unvalidated while checking `grantType` with a mismatched error message. Pass `rawTokenId` to `Objects.requireNonNull` instead.

Inverted condition and incorrect substring range in isAccessTokenId — Valid access token IDs are rejected because the check inspects the wrong characters and returns `false` upon matching `expectedGrantShortcut`. Invert the condition and slice indices 4 to 6 after verifying `items[0]` length.

Return of null from getSubGroupsCount can cause NullPointerException — Callers auto-unboxing the return value to `long` will throw a `NullPointerException` when `model` is null. Return `0L` instead of `null` to satisfy the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount` contract.

Background reader thread is not joined before assertions — Assertions can run while the reader thread is still active, missing late exceptions and causing false test passes. Store the thread in a variable and call `join()` before checking `caughtExceptions`.

Unescaped hyphen in `[a-zA-Z-_]` creates unexpected character range — The regex treats `Z-_` as an ASCII range instead of a literal hyphen, preventing hyphenated locale codes from matching. Move the hyphen to the end of the character class as `[a-zA-Z_-]` or escape it.

Unsupported MessageFormat syntax used in i18next message property — Using Java `MessageFormat` syntax in `error-invalid-multivalued-size` breaks i18next localization, displaying raw placeholders and choice expressions directly to users. Switch back to `{{0}}` interpolation placeholders and replace the choice format with static wording.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties:3138-3138`

Unconstrained end index calculation causes StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — Overlapping prefix and suffix matches can cause `length - end` to fall below `start`, throwing a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` in `substring()`. Constrain `end` in the loop condition using `sanitized.length() - start` and `value.length() - start`.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: Client removal fails with UnsupportedOperationException under V2 authz — `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled()` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, aborting client deletion when V2 fine-grained authorization is enabled. Guard this call by checking whether `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is disabled.

canManage(ClientModel) checks role directly instead of calling canManage() — Callers granted permission to manage all clients are denied managing individual clients that have a dedicated resource in `resourceStore`. Replace the `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` check with a call to `canManage()`.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.
The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Falsy age or timestamp bypasses field mutual exclusion validation — Falsy values like `0` cause `self.initial_data.get()` to treat present fields as absent and bypass mutual exclusion checks. Move this cross-field validation into `validate` and check presence using `in self.initial_data`.

Error IDs misaligned with event payloads when zipping with events.values() — Pairing `error_ids` with `events.values()` misaligns or drops data when entries are missing or unordered. Look up each payload directly from `events` using its corresponding `node_id` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Expired deadline skips terminating remaining flusher processes — Breaking early leaves subsequent entries in `self.processes` running as orphaned background processes. Remove the early `break` check so each process is terminated even after `deadline` expires.

Patched time.sleep makes wait a no-op — Because `time.sleep` is patched to a no-op earlier in the test, this returns immediately and introduces race conditions. Synchronize on an event or use an unpatched sleep instead.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: assignment_source added to sync_status_outbound instead of sync_assignee_outbound — Callers in `sync_assignee_outbound.py` pass `assignment_source` to `sync_assignee_outbound`, which will fail because the parameter is missing there. Move `assignment_source` from `sync_status_outbound` to `sync_assignee_outbound`.

AssignmentSource.queued evaluated at class definition time — Every `AssignmentSource` instance receives the same static startup timestamp instead of its actual creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` on `queued` so it evaluates dynamically at instantiation.

OAuth state uses static pipeline signature enabling CSRF — An attacker can bypass CSRF validation and link an arbitrary GitHub account to a victim session because `pipeline.signature` is predictable. Generate a cryptographically secure random token, store it with `pipeline.bind_state`, and validate the callback `state` against it.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Original monitor config returned instead of modified copy — The updated schedule display is discarded because the untransformed configuration dictionary is returned. Return `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

updateLocation recreates calendar references with undefined externalCalendarId/credentialId — These fields are always undefined because `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`, so `editLocation.handler.ts` recreates the booking's references without them and later reschedules/cancels lose the Google event. Fall back to `evt.destinationCalendar` or return both fields from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`.

Team destination calendars dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null — When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, the optional chain silently drops `teamDestinationCalendars`, so COLLECTIVE bookings create no calendar events for hosts that do have destination calendars. Assign with a spread over `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` instead.

Video booking references created with null credentialId, breaking seat-cancellation updates — Video results now get a null `credentialId`, but seat cancellation in `handleCancelBooking.ts` relies on `reference.credentialId` to load the credential and update the meeting, so removed attendees stay in the call. Drop the `isCalendarType` guard and always store `result.credentialId`.

Destructuring destinationCalendar without guard throws on null/empty array — When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and `.integration` throws, breaking the Google Meet without Google Calendar case this check exists for. Add optional chaining to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Dead fallback in updateEvent always yields undefined when externalCalendarId is falsy — In the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy by definition, so `find` can never match and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined, making updates without an external calendar fail instead of using the booking's destination calendar. Fall back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:314-318`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:314-317`

Inverted billing condition: slug set on cloud instead of self-hosted — The dropped negation means self-hosted organizations are created without a `slug` while cloud organizations get one immediately, bypassing the `requestedSlug` reservation flow that holds the slug until the organization is published. Restore the negation in the ternary.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Adding guests to seated bookings overbooks slots and skips BookingSeat creation — Attendees get created without seats, so they can't be managed or cancelled per-seat and become invisible in seat-based views. Reject seated bookings early, as the fix does, or create `BookingSeat` rows after checking remaining capacity.

EventManager built with caller's credentials instead of organizer's — When the caller is an attendee or team admin, their credentials get used against the organizer's external calendar event and the update fails, so new guests never appear on it. Build the `EventManager` from `booking.user` instead of `ctx.user`.

Team admins rejected: isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner only passes for owners — Team admins who are neither organizer nor attendee get a FORBIDDEN error, contradicting the intent of `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already covers admins and owners, combine the checks with `||` instead of `&&`.

Guest emails with uppercase characters bypass the guest email blocklist — A guest like 'Spam@x.com' gets added and emailed despite being blocked. Compare `guest.toLowerCase()` against `blacklistedGuestEmails`, matching `checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked` which lowercases both sides.

Team bookings build CalendarEvent without team, so team hosts miss guest emails — Additional team-member hosts never receive the guests-added email, and subjects fall back to the organizer's personal name. Populate `team` on `evt` from the booking's event type team, fetching its name and accepted members as `handleNewBooking` does.

Unbounded guests array allows mass attendee/email abuse — A single request can insert thousands of attendee rows and send mass emails to arbitrary third parties through Cal.com's mail infrastructure. Cap the `guests` array with `.max(10)` and consider a per-request limit in the handler.

isInvalidEmail banner never cleared on success, persists across dialog opens — The stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner reappears the next time the dialog opens after a successful add. Reset it with `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` in `onSuccess` and at the start of a passing validation in `handleAdd`.

Booking-ID oracle: distinct NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN errors leak booking existence — Any authenticated user can probe this mutation to enumerate valid booking IDs across the system by comparing the two error responses. Scope the lookup to bookings the caller can access, or return `booking_not_found` for unauthorized IDs too.

Duplicate emails in guests array create duplicate attendee rows — Duplicate attendee rows cause repeated guest emails and duplicate calendar updates, even from concurrent requests. Dedupe the `guests` input case-insensitively in the handler as shown, or add a unique constraint on `Attendee`.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests — Guests already on the booking receive a fresh 'confirmed' invitation with an .ics file even though nothing changed for them. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Sync-mode refresh responses rejected by strict webexRefreshedTokenSchema — Sync-mode responses only carry an access token and expiry, but `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` demands literal `scope`, `token_type`, and `refresh_token` fields, so every webex refresh rejects and no token is ever persisted. Validate the response with `parseRefreshTokenResponse` like the other adapters do.

Credential key stores parseRefreshTokenResponse wrapper instead of parsed token — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `{ success, data }` safeParse wrapper, so the credential key becomes that wrapper instead of the token, and Google Calendar breaks on the next call after its first refresh. Store `parsedToken.data` as the key, matching the other consumers.

Broken computed keys make token schema strip expiry_date and real refresh_token — The computed keys evaluate to the literal key `[object Object]`, so `z.object` strips `expiry_date` and the real `refresh_token`, and persisting the result wipes the user's stored refresh token. Use a passthrough schema that captures the numeric expiry and never write a placeholder `refresh_token`.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27`

refreshOAuthTokens is passed credential id instead of the user id, risking cross-user token sync — Passing `credentialId` as the `userId` argument makes the sync endpoint return another user's OAuth tokens, which would be persisted into this user's credential — a cross-user leak. Pass `credential.userId`, as the other integrations do.

Token refresh success check relies on environment-dependent statusText — `statusText` is empty for HTTP/2 and in runtimes that drop the reason phrase, so a valid 200 response fails this check and the whole refresh rejects. Test `response.ok` (or `response.status === 200`) instead.

Non-atomic find-then-create can create duplicate credentials for same user+app — Concurrent webhooks can both pass `findFirst` and each run `create`, leaving duplicate `Credential` rows — `schema.prisma` has no unique constraint on (`userId`, `appId`). Use a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or add a unique constraint and upsert with a `P2002` fallback.

getClient performs blocking token refresh and DB write on every service construction — `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed for every calendar operation, including availability checks on booking-page loads, and each construction now pays a blocking refresh POST to Salesforce plus a `prisma.credential.update` even when the stored access token is still valid. Check expiry first and refresh only when needed, as other providers do.

New access token saved but stale token used for jsforce connection — The connection keeps running on the stale `credentialKey.access_token` captured before the refresh, while the fresh token is only written to the database and never used. Pass `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` to the `jsforce.Connection`.

Sync branch returns raw fetch Response instead of parsed token payload — Callers written for the non-sync shape — Google's `res?.data`, zoho's `tokenInfo.data`, hubspot's token fields — crash or misread the raw fetch Response. Await `response.json()` and return the parsed body so both branches honor the same contract.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-96`
- `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-191`

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !==, leaking it via timing — This endpoint can overwrite any user's OAuth credentials, and the `!==` comparison leaks the secret byte-by-byte through response timing, letting an attacker forge webhook calls. Compare hashed buffers with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` and fail closed when the header is missing.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Unindexed retryCount disjunct forces full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run — The OR branch filters on `retryCount`, which has no index on `WorkflowReminder`, so every cron run degrades to a full scan instead of using the `method`/`scheduledDate` composite index. Add an index on `retryCount` or scope the branch with the same `method` filter.

Non-atomic retryCount increment loses updates across overlapping cron runs — Overlapping cron runs read the same `retryCount` snapshot and both write value+1, losing increments, so a repeatedly failing reminder can stay below the cleanup threshold and retry forever. Use an atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in the update data.

Catch-block retryCount update can throw and abort remaining reminders — The update inside the catch can itself throw — e.g. `P2025` when a reminder was concurrently deleted — aborting the loop so remaining reminders are skipped and the cron request fails. Wrap it in its own try/catch or use `updateMany`, which doesn't throw on missing rows.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup-code login bypasses password verification — A leaked backup code alone then grants full account access, since the password check is skipped when a `backupCode` is posted with any dummy `totpCode`. Verify `credentials.password` inside the backup-code branch before authenticating.

twoFactorLostAccess state persists after modal is closed or cancelled — Reopening the modal then shows the backup-code screen with stale `backupCode`/`totpCode` values instead of the default TOTP view. Reset `twoFactorLostAccess` and the form values when the modal closes or opens.

Non-string backupCode throws TypeError instead of returning 400 — A truthy non-string `backupCode` (number, object, array) passes the guard and `replaceAll` throws an unhandled TypeError, surfacing as a generic 500. Check `typeof req.body.backupCode === "string"` and return the 400 `IncorrectBackupCode` response otherwise.

2FA switch assertion passes a Promise to expect and never fails — The unawaited Promise from `isChecked()` is always truthy, so the assertion can never fail and this test proves nothing about the 2FA switch. Await `expect` on the `[data-state="checked"]` locator or use `toBeChecked()` instead.

Closing backup code dialog asserts nothing, test passes if dialog stays open — A broken close button would go unnoticed, because the follow-up switch assertion still passes behind an open modal and the next step discards the dialog. After the click, assert the dialog is gone, e.g. `toBeHidden()` on `backup-codes-close`.

Dialog close via ESC/overlay skips onEnable() and resetState(), leaving stale 2FA state — ESC or overlay clicks skip both `onEnable()` and `resetState()`, leaving `viewer.me` stale in `two-factor-auth.tsx` so 2FA still shows disabled and the modal reopens on backup codes. Trigger `onEnable()` from the dialog's close path too, not just the Close button.

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write race — Two concurrent logins can both pass the `indexOf` check, leaving a consumed code valid or letting the same one authenticate twice. Make the write conditional — `updateMany` matching the previously read `backupCodes` — and fail when no rows change.

Backup code comparison is case-sensitive while stored codes are lowercase hex — Stored codes are lowercase hex from `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, so a valid code typed with uppercase is wrongly rejected with `IncorrectBackupCode`. Compare both sides lowercased, here and in `disable.ts`.

Backup-code comparison is not constant-time, leaking match info via timing — Response times reveal how many leading characters of a submitted `backupCode` match a stored one, which is enough to reconstruct a code that together with the password authenticates the account. Compare hashes with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers instead of `indexOf`.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58-64`

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: Public options type marks teamId optional, but schema requires it for scope "team" — A call site omitting `teamId` for scope "team" now type-checks but fails `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` validation at runtime, silently degrading to empty results instead of a compile-time error. Split `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` into a discriminated union so `scope: "team"` requires `teamId`.

toEqual on composed Prisma.Sql compares internals, not rendered SQL — These assertions can never pass: `toEqual` deep-compares `Prisma.Sql` internals (`strings`/`values`), and fragments composed by `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` keep nested `Sql` objects inside `values`, never matching the flat literal template. Build the expectation with the same composition the service performs, or assert on `conditions.sql`.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:332-343`
- `packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:429-431`

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Imported HTML is persisted unsanitized, enabling stored XSS — Untrusted HTML from the feed or article lands in post content as-is, so script and event-handler payloads execute on the forum origin, and the `embed.imported_from` footer interpolates `#{url}` unescaped. Sanitize the fragment with a Nokogiri tag/attribute whitelist before persisting and escape the URL.

Invalid `<%- end if %>` causes syntax error compiling embed/best template — Every `embed/best` request 500s once a topic exists because the compiled template has an unmatched `if`, and controller specs don't render views, so tests stay green. Replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>`.

Unthrottled enqueue of RetrieveTopic jobs for unknown embed URLs — Since the 60-second throttle lives inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, every unauthenticated request — and each open tab's 30-second reload — enqueues a `Jobs.enqueue` call and runs `topic_id_for_embed` forever when the article can't be imported. Check the throttle before enqueueing or dedupe pending retrievals per embed_url.

NOT NULL column with default rewrites hot posts table under exclusive lock — Adding `cook_method` with a default on PostgreSQL < 11 rewrites every `posts` row under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads and writes to the site's hottest table for the deploy. Add it nullable, backfill in batches, then apply the NOT NULL constraint.

Non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE can leave throttle key with no TTL — If the worker dies between `$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire`, the key `retrieved:<embed_url>` persists forever and that embed URL is never imported again, leaving the widget stuck on 'Loading Discussion...'. Set the TTL atomically with `SET key value EX 60 NX` or a MULTI/EXEC pipeline.

String#scrub unavailable on Ruby 2.0 and i.content may be missing — `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError on the pinned Ruby 2.0 (`String#scrub` arrived in 2.1) and when feeds carry only `description`, so with `retry: false` the hourly job dies and imports never work. Use `(i.content || i.description).to_s` instead.

feed_key is dead code; feed modification check never wired into polling — Nothing ever calls `PollFeed#feed_key`, so the feed-modification check was never wired in and the hourly job unconditionally re-imports the whole feed. Either skip re-polling when the digest is unchanged or remove `feed_key` and the now-unused `require 'digest/sha1'`.

Test for feed_polling_enabled? passes even without the guard due to other defaults — This test still passes if the `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` guard were removed, because unstubbed `feed_polling_url` and `embed_by_username` default to '' and short-circuit execution. Stub both settings so execution actually reaches the condition under test.

Embed layout leaks full referer URL into cacheable response body — The full `request.referer`, including path and query string that can carry tokens or session ids, is echoed into responses `EmbedController#best` marks cacheable, so a shared cache can serve one embedder's URL to another. Send only the referer origin as the postMessage targetOrigin, or skip caching these responses.

Origin check uses substring containment, allowing forged origins — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` accepts any origin string contained anywhere in `discourseUrl`, letting a forged frame send resize messages that control the embed iframe's height. Compare origins strictly, e.g. a prefix match, rather than with `indexOf` containment.

Test doesn't enable feed_polling_enabled? so feed_polling_url check is never reached — `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` short-circuits at `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` (false by default in site_settings.yml) before reading `feed_polling_url`, so this test would pass even without the guard it claims to cover. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true and `embed_by_username` present so the `feed_polling_url` condition is actually exercised.

**Also found in:**
- `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:24-28`

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: SQL injection via unquoted host value interpolated into INSERT — The `embeddable_hosts` setting is admin-entered with no format validation, so a crafted value runs as arbitrary SQL during the migration — staff-level settings access escalates to full database execution. Wrap `h` with `connection.quote` instead of interpolating it.

Migration inserts unnormalized hosts with scheme/path, breaking host matching — Rows migrated with a scheme or path never match `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, so embedding silently breaks on upgraded sites until each host is re-saved. Strip scheme and path from `h` before the INSERT, mirroring the model's `before_validation` normalization.

Serializer emits only embeddable_host ids with no root-level records to hydrate from — The store's `_hydrateEmbedded` resolves the emitted ids against a root-level `embeddable_hosts` collection that no server payload includes, so hosts hydrate to undefined and the admin table cannot render or edit them. Emit the records as a sideloaded root collection with `embed_in_root: true`.

Migration crashes indexing empty result when site_settings rows are missing — Discourse only stores `site_settings` rows for non-default values, so on fresh installs these selects return zero rows and indexing `[0]` aborts `db:migrate`. Guard both lookups with `cmd_tuples > 0`, as the `embeddable_hosts` query below already does.

record_for_host can't match hosts stored with a port suffix — The validation accepts a `:8080`-style port but `before_validation` never strips it, and the comparison targets a port-less URI host, so a saved host can never match and embedded comments stay refused. Strip the port when comparing, or reject ports in the validation.

**Also found in:**
- `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2-2`

Update/destroy 500 on missing embeddable host instead of 404 — A stale tab or a concurrent delete leaves `host` nil, so both actions raise `NoMethodError` instead of returning a clean 404. Raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is missing.

NoMethodError when host is nil in before_validation — An API call omitting `host` makes `self.host.sub!` raise `NoMethodError` — a 500 — instead of letting `validates_format_of` reject it with a 422. Skip the trimming when `host` is nil so validation can run.

delete() swallows destroyRecord rejections with no error handler — A failed `destroyRecord` (server error or the 500 the admin controller returns for a concurrently deleted record) is swallowed silently, leaving the row in the table as if it succeeded. Attach `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, as `save()` already does.

Blank-embeddable-host test no longer discriminates (false && false passes trivially) — With the setup moved into the neighboring test, the assertion reduces to `false && false`, so it passes for any implementation that returns false — even a broken one. Set `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` and stub `has_topic_embed?` here so hosts are the only variable.

Case-sensitive bind value fails to match downcased stored hosts — A referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/x` keeps its casing through `URI(...).host`, so it never matches hosts stored lowercased and embedding is denied. Normalize the bind value with `host.downcase` so both sides compare equal.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Over-limit image stored when OptimizedImage.downsize fails or makes no progress — When the convert subprocess fails, `tempfile.size` never shrinks, so the command runs five times and the oversized image is still stored since `Upload.create_for` never revalidates the limit. Check the `OptimizedImage.downsize` return value and fail the upload when no progress is made.

4-arg downsize overrides 5-arg version, breaking ResizeEmoji caller — `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb` still calls the old 5-argument form, so every emoji resize now raises an `ArgumentError` and the background job fails. Make `downsize` accept both signatures or update that caller.

Animated GIFs flattened by downsize since tempfile path lacks file extension — The extensionless Rack tempfile path means `OptimizedImage.optimize` never takes the animated branch and its `convert` keeps only the first frame, silently flattening oversized GIFs. Copy the upload into a `Tempfile` carrying the filename's extension before downsizing.

Downsize loop runs all 5 attempts even when convert fails or file shrinks — A failed convert leaves the file unchanged, so all five synchronous `OptimizedImage.downsize` calls still execute in the request thread and can pin workers or exhaust CPU under concurrent uploads. Break out of the loop when `tempfile.size` stops shrinking.

Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores per-type site settings — On sites with a smaller configured limit, non-image files under 10MB pass client validation, consume upload bandwidth, and are then rejected by the server citing a different limit. Keep reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` instead of hardcoding it.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: add_members crashes with RecordNotUnique when re-adding an existing member — A double click on Add resubmits the input (the UI never clears it), and `group.add` pushes unconditionally onto `group_users`, which has a unique index — so re-adding raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and returns a 500. Skip usernames already present in `group.users` before calling `group.add`.

Deleting group member bypasses GroupUser destroy, so user_count counter cache drifts — The stale count shows up in the admin groups list and on the group page and never self-corrects, because `group.users.delete` removes the join row without destroying `GroupUser`, so its `user_count` counter cache never fires. Use `group.remove` instead, which destroys the record.

Unvalidated limit/offset params cause PostgreSQL errors and unbounded limit — Anyone can send `?offset=-1` to this public endpoint and get a 500, since PostgreSQL rejects negative `OFFSET`/`LIMIT`; `limit` is also uncapped. Clamp both params to non-negative values and cap `limit` before applying them.

totalPages off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit — The pagination controls enable 'next' on the real last page; clicking it loads an empty member list ('2/2' with no rows). Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead of the floor-plus-one form so `totalPages` matches the actual page count.

findMembers clamps offset to user_count, which can yield an empty page — `offset == user_count` is always past the last row, so the server returns an empty page — reachable after removing a member while on page 2. Clamp the offset to the start of the last page instead, rounded down to a multiple of `limit`.

Public group members page shows only first 50 members, no pagination — The backend now caps results at 50 and returns pagination metadata, but this route ignores it, so large groups silently lose the rest of their member list. Add pagination or a load-more here, or raise the limit for this consumer.

**Also found in:**
- `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26`

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Fallback locales not loaded when I18n.locale is set outside requests — Emails and background jobs translate with only the switched-to locale loaded, so sites with a non-English `default_locale` fall straight back to English or show 'translation missing' instead of the configured chain. Call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` wherever `I18n.locale` is switched outside the request cycle, e.g. in `Jobs::Base`.

Fallback chain uses runtime SiteSetting.default_locale not reflected in accelerator cache key — Changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` at runtime keeps serving stale fallback translations, since the accelerator's LRU key ignores the site default. Include the fallback base in the cache key or bust the cache when the setting changes.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Device-limit gate bypassed when X-Grafana-Device-Id header is omitted — Since `TagDevice` returns early when the client-controlled `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, simply omitting it bypasses the gate and the limit never applies to the unbounded traffic it is meant to cap. Enforce a server-side fallback identity (e.g. from IP/User-Agent) or reject requests missing the header.

Device cached before DB write, so limit rejection is bypassed on retry — Because `SetDefault` caches the device before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs, a rejected request succeeds on retry via a cache hit without touching the database — rejection silently becomes access. Cache the device only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or evict the key on error.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-47`

Device limit check has a check-then-act race allowing limit bypass — `CountDevices` and the insert run in separate sessions without locking, so concurrent requests with distinct device IDs all see the count below the limit and all insert, letting one burst push far past the cap. Enforce it atomically, e.g. a locking read in one transaction or a conditional insert.

anonymousDeviceLimit typed as number | undefined but backend always sends a number (0 = no limit) — `undefined` never arrives: the Go DTO field `AnonymousDeviceLimit` always serializes a number, `0` when no limit is set, so consumers checking for `undefined` or treating any number as a real limit will misbehave. Type the field as `number` and document that `0` means unlimited.

Panic in TagDevice now escapes Authenticate after removing defer/recover — Panics raised inside `TagDevice`, for example while parsing request headers, now escape `Authenticate` and fail the request with a 500 instead of being swallowed as before. Wrap the synchronous call in a defer/recover that logs and treats the panic as a tagging failure.

Authenticate leaks internal ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel in HTTP response — Returning the raw `ErrDeviceLimitReached` sentinel makes it the response message for unauthenticated requests, disclosing to anonymous users that a device limit exists and is exhausted. Log the real cause server-side and return a neutral authentication failure instead.

AnonymousDeviceLimit leaks internal capacity config via unauthenticated /api/frontend/settings — The endpoint is served without authentication, so this publishes the internal capacity setting to any visitor, and no frontend consumer of the value appears in this PR. Omit it from the payload or include it only when anonymous access is enabled.
