goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: TestLogger.FromContext returns a detached logger, losing captured logs — Logged records go to a throwaway instance, so assertions on `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs` silently see nothing, breaking the contract in `ifaces.go` that `logger_middleware.go` relies on. Return `f` instead of a fresh `NewTestLogger()` so the result shares the receiver's captured `Logs`.

Legacy DeleteCollection skipped when unified storage delete fails — After a partial unified deletion, objects removed from unified storage keep their legacy rows, so the stores diverge and a rollback resurrects them. Run `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` asynchronously even when `d.Storage.DeleteCollection` errors, as before.

Async legacy write derives timeout from cancellable request context, aborting immediately — The apiserver cancels the request context right after the handler returns, so the spawned goroutine's legacy write aborts with `context canceled` and mode 3 never records to legacy storage. Derive the timeout from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` and avoid reusing request-scoped validation closures.

Mode 3 async legacy update drops updateWrapper, causing stale legacy writes — Without `updateWrapper`, the legacy store recomputes the update against its own possibly stale object, silently diverging from unified storage — and backfill propagates that. Wrap `res` in `updateWrapper` alongside `objInfo`, as modes 1 and 2 do.

Mode 3 Delete no longer falls through to legacy delete on NotFound — Objects that exist only in legacy storage are never removed: the client gets a 404 while the legacy copy survives and resurrects the object after a rollback. Fall through to `d.Legacy.Delete` when `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)`.

Mode 3 tests never assert the legacy-storage write actually happens — The legacy mock expectation is never asserted, so the tests pass even if `d.Legacy.Create` is removed or always fails. Wait for the goroutine and assert the call (e.g. via `AssertExpectations`), including a case with a pre-canceled parent context.

Mode 3 dual-write tests never verify the legacy write — Because `doPlaylistTests` reads everything through unified storage, a broken or failing legacy write is invisible and these subtests pass regardless. Verify the legacy side directly, for example by querying legacy storage after each write.

Create(): storage error path records metric as legacy instead of storage — Storage create failures are counted in the legacy metric, inflating its error rate while the storage metric under-reports. Record with `d.recordStorageDuration` here, matching the success path.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-131`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129-129`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:128-129`

Delete() passes object name instead of options.Kind to storage duration metric — Passing `name` puts object names in the same label other call sites fill with `options.Kind`, breaking per-kind metric aggregation. Use `options.Kind` here too.

DeleteCollection goroutine records legacy latency with recordStorageDuration — Legacy delete-collection latency and errors land in the storage metric, which over-reports while the legacy metric stays empty. Call `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Index-build failure in eager Init aborts server boot on existing index path — Any server with file-backed indexes now fails to boot on every restart, since `BuildIndex` calls `bleve.New` which errors with 'path already exists' on a directory persisted from a previous run. Make `BuildIndex` reopen or reuse the existing index, or remove the stale `cfg.IndexPath` first.

TotalDocs reads b.cache without cacheMu lock, racing with BuildIndex map writes — This log call can trigger a fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' panic, because `TotalDocs` iterates `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu.RLock` while `BuildIndex` writes it concurrently. Take `cacheMu.RLock` inside `TotalDocs` (the metrics collector needs the same fix) before logging `total_docs`.

Constructor synchronously consumes Init, breaking consumer-owned init — The constructor now blocks on the index build and hard-fails, while callers like `client.go` still expect a cheap, late-failing constructor; worse, the internal `sync.Once` makes their later `Init` a no-op under an internal context. Drop `Init` from `NewResourceServer`, or update all consumers and let `Init` use the caller's context.

Concurrent BuildIndex calls for same key race without per-build serialization — Two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same key now both build: file-backed indexes fail on `bleve.New`'s file lock, memory-only ones leak an index and split writes across instances. Hold `cacheMu` for the whole build so the loser blocks and then hits the cache.

Postgres skip silently drops instrumentation-server coverage and masks a failure — A real, possibly PR-introduced failure (eager `Init` building the search index) is being hidden: the test now skips before exercising the instrumentation server on postgres, so any regression there passes silently. Root-cause and fix the postgres failure, or narrow the skip with a linked issue.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Silence menu item is a no-op: RuleActionsButtons gets no ruler rule to wire silence flow — Users with silence permission click the menu item and nothing opens, since `RuleActionsButtons` renders `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only when a ruler rule is present, and the list view no longer fetches one. Wire the flow to the prom rule (or a prom-based drawer) and gate the item on the same condition.

isFederated hardcoded to false, federated rule groups lose immutability guard — Federated Mimir rule groups are no longer treated as immutable, so Edit/Delete/Pause become supported through `useAlertRuleAbility` once datasource ruler permissions pass. Keep the `isFederatedRuleGroup` check in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` or thread the group into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` until the TODO is implemented.

`prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule()` doesn't narrow `promRule` — `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule()` is a plain boolean check, not a type predicate, so `promRule` stays `Rule | undefined` where `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` is required — a type error here and in `RuleActionsButtons.V2`, whose `promRule.uid` can also read undefined. Export a narrowing guard such as `isGrafanaPromRule` or validate at the boundary so both call sites narrow.

skipToken rules still report supported=true for globally-permitted Grafana prom rule abilities — When the rule is `skipToken`, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` still yields supported for abilities backed by a global permission, so Mimir rules render the Duplicate item without the datasource write permission the ruler path requires. Return NotSupported for every ability while the rule is skipped, so skipped rows produce [false, false].

Cloud rule tests don't exercise permission gating; mocked hook hides buttons — These tests pass even if the new Mimir gating logic is broken, since the stubbed `useIsRuleEditable` omits `isRulerAvailable`, making every ability NotSupported and hiding Edit/Delete regardless of permissions. Let the real hook run, or add `isRulerAvailable: true` to the stub and assert the buttons track permission changes.

Negative Edit-button test passes regardless of which ability hook is consulted — The assertion holds no matter which hook drives the edit decision — `useRulerRuleAbility` stays at its [false, false] default, the same result the denied permission yields — so removing the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` call would still pass. Pin the other hooks to allow so only `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` denying makes the button disappear.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: testIncorrectGrantType passes via incidental NPE, not grant-type validation — Catching `RuntimeException` swallows an incidental NPE: `before()` never calls `factory.postInit()`, so `sessionFactory` stays null and the unknown shortcut throws before the intended `IllegalArgumentException`. Assert on `IllegalArgumentException` and initialize the factory so the validation path actually runs.

Constructor guard re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId — A null `rawTokenId` slips through this duplicate `grantType` check and later yields a corrupt token ID like "onrtna:null" in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` instead of failing fast. Make the second check require `rawTokenId`, matching its message.

isAccessTokenId grant check uses wrong substring and inverted polarity, so it never fails — The wrong `substring` bounds and inverted polarity turn this check into a no-op, so token IDs with a wrong or missing grant type still match the event. Use `substring(4, 6)` and return false on mismatch.

Sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads still lack the null guard — The same concurrent-deletion race still throws an NPE through the unguarded `modelSupplier.get()` calls in the three `getSubGroupsStream` overloads, so the fix is only partial. Apply the same null check, or a shared null-safe accessor, at all four call sites.

Reader thread may finish no reads before deletes complete, passing vacuously — On a slow or loaded machine all 100 deletes can finish before the reader thread's first call, so the loop exits having read nothing and the assertion passes vacuously — the race is never exercised. Gate the delete loop on a latch that the reader signals once running.

getSubGroupsCount() returns null, violating GroupModel never-null contract — Callers relying on the `GroupModel` contract ("Never returns null" in server-spi) that unbox the result to a primitive `long` will now hit a fresh NullPointerException. Return a fallback such as `0L`, or document the contract change on the interface.

Reader thread not joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty — A request still in flight when `deletedAll.set(true)` runs can append to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed, hiding the very NPE this test guards against. Keep a reference to the reader thread, join it after the delete loop, then assert.

JS console uses i18next {{n}} interpolation, but new value uses Java ChoiceFormat — The console renders this value with i18next, which ignores single braces and has no choice format, so users will see raw placeholders instead of the attribute name and counts. Use the `{{n}}` form without the choice, as also needed in the account-ui messages file.

Common prefix/suffix scans can overlap, causing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — When the prefix scan overlaps the suffix scan, the `sanitized.substring` and `value.substring` calls throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Clamp `end` so suffix and prefix never overlap, for both strings.

Uncaught RuntimeException when English reference file is missing or unresolvable — The RuntimeException from reading the English reference escapes `verify()`, aborting the whole run at the first missing file instead of recording a per-file diagnostic. Skip with a message in `messages` when the reference file is missing or unresolvable.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: NPE in hasPermission when Clients type resource does not exist — When the realm's admin-permissions client predates this PR, `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` no-ops and `getResourceTypeResource` returns null, so `findByResource` throws an NPE and every client view or update turns into a 500. Add a null check returning false, mirroring the 1-arg `hasPermission`.

Client delete fails when both fine-grained authz versions enabled: V2 cleanup throws — When both feature flags are on, the handler in AdminPermissions.java selects `MgmtPermissionsV2` and `setPermissionsEnabled` throws, so deleting any client fails and rolls back. Make the guard skip cleanup when the V2 flag is active instead of checking the V1 flag.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77-95`
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77-96`

Per-client resource lacks type so all-clients policies are ignored in evaluation — An all-clients grant silently stops applying once any per-client permission for that client exists, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never sets a `type`, so `DefaultPolicyEvaluator` skips type-scoped policies. Set `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` on the resource so those policies participate in evaluation.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:136-144`

testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants all scopes at once, masking wrong-scope regressions — Because every scope is granted at once, `ClientPermissionsV2` could evaluate the wrong scope and the test would still pass: negatives still throw and post-grant operations still succeed. Create one permission per scope (`MAP_ROLES`, then `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`), or assert intermediate negative states between grants.

V2-enabled cleanup skipped: guard ignores ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 — With V2 enabled and the old flag off, removal cleanup is silently skipped while V2 keeps creating per-object permission resources, so stale policies can re-apply to a future object reusing the id. If V2 doesn't clean this up elsewhere, include `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` in the guard.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Login cache invalidation skipped when org-aware wrapper masks IDP login eligibility — When the organization is disabled, the org-aware wrapper's `isEnabled()` makes `getLoginPredicate()` false, so updates like removing `BROKER_PUBLIC` or hiding or disabling the IDP skip invalidation and stale `.idp.login` caches serve a hidden broker after re-enabling. Evaluate the predicate on the unwrapped model, e.g. via `idpDelegate.getByAlias()`.

Login cache uses empty-string sentinel that collides with empty organizationId — When a call passes an empty-string `organizationId`, the wrong result lands under the `""` key and later `null`-filter lookups skip the re-fetch, returning an empty list until invalidation. Use a non-colliding sentinel like `getByOrganization`'s `-1.-1`, or normalize empty strings to `null`.

isEnabled re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean lacks test coverage — If this `isEnabled()` filter broke, the suite would still pass, since `testCacheIDPForLogin` calls `getForLogin` directly and never renders through the bean. Add a test path that exercises `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, or assert on the models it resolves.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: TableWidgetVisualization renders hardcoded empty data under flag — Organizations with the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag see completely empty table widgets because the hardcoded props discard the fetched `result.data` and `result.meta`. Pass the real data, meta, and derived columns until the new visualization is wired up.
Error timestamps (seconds) compared against rrweb event timestamps (ms) — Convert error timestamps to milliseconds (rrweb convention, see src/sentry/replays/testutils.py) before merging.

Hidden attributes are shown when search query is empty — When the user isn't searching, the early return skips the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter entirely, so `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are rendered — the exact case the hiding was added for. Apply the filter before the empty-query early return.

Mutual-exclusion validators treat falsy 0 as absent, accepting age+timestamp together — `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` test presence with truthiness, but 0 is valid for both fields, so a report with `age: 0` plus a timestamp is accepted with 200 instead of rejected with 422. Check membership explicitly, e.g. `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`.

None max_segment_id fixture is mocked out, leaving the fix untested — The `None` fixture never reaches the fixed code because the mocked `delete_matched_rows` is the only caller of `_make_recording_filenames`, so reverting the fix would still pass. Cover the `None` case with an unmocked test of `delete_matched_rows`.

Error IDs paired with wrong event data due to positional zip of nodestore results — A backend that omits missing IDs or returns rows out of order silently pairs each error ID with the wrong event data, since the positional zip assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi()` preserves order and completeness. Look up by key with `events.get(node_id)` instead of `events.values()`.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: submit() queries cluster memory info once per buffer, duplicating blocking Redis INFO calls — The blocking cluster-wide Redis INFO round-trip in `buffer.get_memory_info()` runs once per buffer on the consumer loop, so duplicated I/O grows with process count while the resulting ratio is unchanged. Every buffer shares the same Redis cluster, so query it once and reuse the result.

record_stored_segments runs one sequential Redis pipeline per buffer in submit — A batch submit that previously took one Redis round trip now takes one sequential pipeline per buffer, so latency grows with process count. Aggregate the zcard sampling into a single pipeline over all assigned shards instead of calling `record_stored_segments()` per buffer.

N flusher processes each use the full max-flush-segments budget — Each buffer computes `max_segments_per_shard` from its own shard subset, so total flush work reaches N times `max-flush-segments` and Redis backpressure only trips at N times the intended backlog. Divide the global budget across processes, deriving the per-shard page size from the total shard count.

`max_processes or ...` treats explicit 0 as missing, silently maximizing parallelism — Passing `--flusher-processes 0` silently spawns one process per shard, the opposite of the requested limit, because the truthiness test swallows 0. Use an `is not None` check and validate a minimum of 1 on the option.

Patched-out sleep makes flusher wait a no-op — This wait never happens because the test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op earlier, so the race the comment targets stays unfixed. Poll until `messages` is non-empty instead of sleeping.

Test only checks total shard count, not distribution across processes — If the mapping ever assigned all four shards to a single process, `total_shards` would still equal 4 and every assertion would pass. Assert the distribution itself, for example that each of the two processes received shards in `process_to_shards_map`.

Hung thread-based flusher is duplicated on restart instead of being stopped — Threads cannot be killed, so skipping `kill()` still leaves the hung thread polling its shards while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second one, and both produce duplicate segment payloads. Stop or disable the old thread first, or skip the restart and surface the failure.

Metric tag key `shards` inconsistent with `shard` used elsewhere — Dashboards or alerts querying one emit site will miss or split the data because the other flusher metrics tag the same value as `shard`. Use `shard` here too so all four emit sites agree.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: AssignmentSource dict with datetime `queued` breaks Celery enqueue and round-trip — The raw datetime in `queued` isn't JSON-serializable, so enqueueing fails; over a JSON hop, `from_dict` swallows the `TypeError` and returns None, silently dropping the source so the inbound assignment syncs back to the same integration — the cycle this PR prevents. Serialize `queued` in `to_dict` and parse it in `from_dict`.

AssignmentSource.queued defaults to import-time timestamp, not construction time — Every `AssignmentSource` gets the same stale timestamp from module import instead of its actual queue time, corrupting `queued` for all consumers, including `to_dict` payloads sent to the sync task. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead of a bare default.

OAuth state uses deterministic pipeline.signature, enabling CSRF — An attacker can derive the constant `state` and forge a callback that binds their own GitHub code as `github_authenticated_user` in a victim's pipeline, defeating the user-match check. Generate a random uuid4 token per pipeline and bind it into the pipeline state instead.

Missing sender key in integration metadata causes unhandled KeyError — Older integrations can lack a `sender` key in `integration.metadata`, so the check raises an unhandled `KeyError` — a 500 instead of the graceful `error(...)` page other paths return. Read it with `.get()` and treat a missing sender as an invalid installation request.

gettext applied to variable in error() prevents extraction of error strings — The literals passed by callers never sit inside a `_(...)` call, so makemessages cannot extract them and users get untranslated English in every locale. Wrap each literal in `_()` at the call sites and drop the `_(error_short)` re-wrap in `error()`.

Unwrapped get_user_info call raises unhandled exception on GitHub API failure — Any GitHub API failure makes `get_user_info` raise as a generic 500, so the postMessage failure handshake never fires — unlike the wrapped token exchange right above. Wrap the call in try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on exception.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated — Detectors using this handler now raise `TypeError` when instantiated in `process_detectors`, since `StatefulDetectorHandler` leaves `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` unimplemented. Implement them as no-op stubs until the stateful detector abstraction is built for metric alerts.

build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value parameter, weakening fixtures — Because the expected occurrence never reflects the actual value, these fixtures still pass if `evaluate_group_key_value` forwards the wrong value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Use `value` in the occurrence (e.g. `evidence_data`) with the true per-group value at each call site, or drop the parameter.

**Also found in:**
- `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:190-192`

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: get_monitor_environment_context returns untransformed monitor config — The monitor context sent with the incident occurrence carries the raw `schedule_type` enum instead of the readable display value, because the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` rather than the transformed copy. Return the enriched `config` local instead.

Null credentialId destinations fall back to "primary" instead of configured externalId — Matching the destination by `cal.credentialId === credentialId` never matches `DestinationCalendar` rows with a null credentialId (nullable in schema.prisma:159, and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents:375-381 explicitly handles such destinations by passing every matching credential). Those bookings now fall back to `"primary"` instead of the configured `destination.externalId`, creating the event on the wrong calendar — previously the code used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly.

Inverted condition writes slug on billing instances and omits it on non-billing ones — The ternary rewrite inverted the condition. The old `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` included `slug` only when team billing is DISABLED; the new `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` includes it only when billing is ENABLED — the exact opposite.

Unguarded access to mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration crashes bookings without destination… — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without a null guard, but `destinationCalendar` is explicitly `null` (handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067) or `[]` (confirm/webhook/paypal handlers) when no destination calendar exists, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. Any booking with Google Meet as location and no destination calendar — the exact case this fallback exists for — now throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the booking fails with a 500.

Unguarded dereference of possibly-undefined destinationCalendar element throws TypeError — Unguarded dereference of a possibly-undefined element: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array — both now produced by callers (handleNewBooking passes `null` when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar; webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts and confirm.handler pass `[]`). Line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, throwing a TypeError whenever the location is Google Meet, whereas the replaced code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) evaluated safely and fell back to Cal Video.

Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition sets slug on wrong path — The rewrite of `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` into `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the condition: when team billing is disabled organizations are now created with a null slug (Team.slug is nullable, so no crash, but the org has no usable slug for routing/lookup), and when it is enabled the real slug is written immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug approval metadata flow. Restore the original negated condition.

Inverted condition sets org slug only when team billing is enabled — At line 151 the condition was inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, which is inconsistent with the unchanged `requestedSlug` metadata line at 153. This logic inversion affects when the org slug (identity) is set directly vs. deferred for verification.

createEvent ignores destination calendars with null credentialId and falls back to "primary" — createEvent now resolves the target calendar only via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. DestinationCalendar rows with a null credentialId — a case this PR explicitly still supports in EventManager by filtering credentials by integration type and calling createEvent for each — never match, so the event is silently created on `"primary"` instead of the configured destination calendar's externalId, which the old code used whenever it was set.

createEvent posts to first destination calendar regardless of credential match — Office365CalendarService (and likewise LarkCalendarService:128-129/164-165 and BaseCalendarService in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-164) only ever consult `destinationCalendar[0]`, but with the new multi-destination collective flow a secondary host's credential is paired with the first host's `externalId` (often a Google calendar id), so the POST targets `/me/calendars/<wrong-id>/events` and fails — the event is never created on that host's calendar (CalDAV variants filter out all calendars and create nothing). Match the destination whose credentialId equals the current credential, as GoogleCalendarService.createEvent attempts to do.

Per-destination externalId is never used to steer event creation — The new `externalId` parameter is declared and passed per-destination from EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (`createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`), but it is only echoed back in the return object — it is never forwarded to the calendar service. GoogleCalendarService re-derives the target calendar from credentialId, but the other services updated in this PR (office365, lark, BaseCalendarService) still select only the FIRST element of `event.destinationCalendar`.

createEvent uses first host's destination calendar, skipping other hosts' calendars — BaseCalendarService.createEvent assumes destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar) is the calendar relevant to the current call, but with the new array model EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents creates one event per destination using each host's own credential. For any non-first host (collective events push team members' destinationCalendars after the organizer's), filtering that host's calendars by the first host's externalId matches nothing, so the event is never created on that host's calendar.

createEvent uses first destination calendar instead of matching credentialId — office365calendar's createEvent still has signature (event: CalendarEvent) and picks the target calendar from destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId). It does not hold up what the other changed hunks now assume: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 makes credentialId a required part of the createEvent contract precisely so each service selects the destination entry matching its own credential (Google's implementation does this), and handleNewBooking.ts now pushes every COLLECTIVE host's destinationCalendar into the array, with EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents invoking createEvent once per host's credential.

Lark createEvent ignores credentialId and always writes to first host's destination calendar — larkcalendar's createEvent has the same disagreement with the rest of the PR: it takes only (event: CalendarEvent) and derives calendarId from destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId), ignoring the credentialId that CalendarManager now passes per the new Calendar interface contract (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221). Since handleNewBooking.ts now produces arrays containing every COLLECTIVE host's destinationCalendar, Lark will write each host's event to the first host's calendar (or throw "no calendar id" when the first entry is absent even though a destination matching this credential exists), instead of the calendar belonging to the credential being used.

Undefined or stale credential passed to updateEvent for calendar references — `credential` is declared outside the new per-reference loop (line 479-480) and is only assigned when a reference's credentialId resolves; `this.calendarCredentials` contains only the organizer's personal and team credentials (getAllCredentials), so secondary hosts' references rely on the DB fetch, and when that fetch returns null or a credential without `app.slug` the loop silently reuses the previous reference's credential — updating the wrong account/calendar — or stays `undefined`, causing a TypeError at `credential.appName` in CalendarManager.updateEvent. Reset `credential` to undefined at the top of each iteration and skip (or fail) the reference when resolution fails.

Recurring cancellation reuses organizer credentials and duplicates delete calls — The recurring-event deletion block was moved inside the new per-reference loop but ignores the current `reference` and its resolved `calendarCredential`, instead re-iterating all of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's credentials only). For multi-reference bookings introduced by this PR the block runs once per calendar reference — duplicating every delete call (subsequent passes hit 404/410) — and secondary hosts' calendar events are never deleted because their credentials are not in the organizer's user credentials, leaving stale events on their calendars.

Video references persisted without credentialId, leaking video rooms on cancellation — New bookings' video references are persisted without a credentialId because the video branch now writes `undefined` instead of `result.credentialId`, which `createMeeting` populates (packages/core/videoClient.ts:78); handleCancelBooking.ts:491-503 only calls `deleteMeeting` when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so every booking created after this change leaks its video room (e.g., Daily) on cancellation. Restore `result.credentialId` as the value for non-calendar results.

updateLocation stores calendar references with null routing data from updateEvent — updateLocation now builds calendar references from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-322) returns neither field — only `createEvent` was updated to return them — and the old fallbacks to `evt.destinationCalendar` were removed, so the references persisted by editLocation.handler.ts:120 are stored with null credentialId and null externalCalendarId. Have `updateEvent` return `credential.id` and the `externalCalendarId` parameter, mirroring the `createEvent` changes, so updateLocation's references keep their routing data.

Sequential per-destination awaits make collective booking latency scale with host count — The new per-destination loop awaits each `prisma.credential.findUnique` and each `createEvent` sequentially, so a collective booking performs one full Google/Office365 network round trip per host in series, making booking-creation latency grow linearly with host count. Build the per-destination promises and settle them with `Promise.all`, as the adjacent other_calendar loop (lines 399-405) already does.

updateEvent fallback compares externalId against falsy externalCalendarId, always undefined — This is a dead/ineffective fallback that regresses the previous `destinationCalendar?.externalId` behavior.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:314-317`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317-317`
- `packages/core/EventManager.ts:379-381`
- `packages/core/EventManager.ts:376-381`

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: EventManager uses caller's credentials instead of booking organizer's — The EventManager is constructed from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` — the calling user's credentials — instead of the booking organizer's, even though the query already fetches `booking.user` with `credentials: true` (never used). When an attendee or team admin (both authorized by this handler's gate) adds guests, `updateAllCalendarEvents` finds no matching credential in `this.calendarCredentials` (EventManager.ts:846/872) and silently skips or soft-fails the update, so the organizer's calendar event never receives the new attendees.

Unhandled Prisma P2025 when booking.userId is null due to `|| 0` fallback — `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws an unhandled Prisma P2025 error when `booking.userId` is null (schema.prisma:554-555 defines `userId Int?`). The `|| 0` fallback converts null into a guaranteed not-found lookup, so any authorized caller on a user-less booking gets a raw INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of a handled TRPC error.

isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner restricts permission to owners only, excluding admins — The `isTeamAdminOrOwner` check combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, but `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270), so the conjunction is satisfied only by owners. A team ADMIN who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee is wrongly denied with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to a team booking, breaking the feature the variable name (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`) says it supports.

Case-sensitive email comparisons let blacklisted and duplicate guests bypass filters — The guest filter compares un-normalized guest emails against normalized values: `blacklistedGuestEmails` entries are `.toLowerCase()`d, but `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the raw guest string, so a blacklisted email submitted with any uppercase character (e.g. "Spam@X.com" vs blacklist "spam@x.com") bypasses the blacklist entirely. The sibling check `guest === attendee.email` is likewise case-sensitive, so a case-variant of an existing attendee's email passes the duplicate filter and is created as a second attendee record.

Unbounded guests array allows email-bombing and mass Attendee insertion — The `guests` array has no `.max()` bound, and the handler authorizes plain booking attendees (not just organizers) to call it. One mutation with thousands of emails inserts that many `Attendee` rows via `createMany` and fans out emails to the organizer plus every existing attendee plus every new guest (sendAddGuestsEmails, email-manager.ts:539-547), enabling email-bombing and unbounded DB growth by any booker.

Missing booking status check allows adding guests to pending/cancelled bookings — The permission gate checks user identity but never `booking.status`, so guests can be added to pending or cancelled bookings (the UI even renders the add_members action for past unconfirmed bookings via BookingListItem.tsx:553, and the API accepts any status directly). The new email templates hardcode ICS `status: "CONFIRMED"` (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:15, organizer-add-guests-email.ts:19), so attendees receive CONFIRMED calendar invites for events that are not accepted.

Team members never get add-guests email: caller builds event without team — The `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)` branch in `sendAddGuestsEmails` is unreachable: its only caller (`addGuestsHandler`) builds the `CalendarEvent` without a `team` property, and `formatCalEvent` only clones the event and strips `platformClientId`. Team members therefore never receive the add-guests notification email this branch is written to send, silently dropping the side effect for team bookings.

onSuccess fails to reset isInvalidEmail, leaving stale error banner — The mutation's `onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but never resets the `isInvalidEmail` flag (only the Cancel button does). After a failed validation is fixed and the add succeeds, reopening the dialog shows the stale `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error banner even though no invalid email is present.

Dead fallback: message is always truthy, so 'unable_to_add_guests' never shows — When `err.data` is missing the toast shows 'undefined: …' instead of the intended `unable_to_add_guests` message. Base the fallback on the actual message part (e.g. `err.message || t("unable_to_add_guests")`).

Case-sensitive duplicate guest check allows same-email attendees — The duplicate check `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` compares emails case-sensitively, and attendee emails are stored as typed at booking time. Adding `john@x.com` to a booking that already has `John@x.com` creates a second `Attendee` row for the same person, producing duplicate invites and ICS attendees.

Pass uniqueGuests instead of raw guests to sendAddGuestsEmails — The handler passes the raw `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails, but email-manager's sendAddGuestsEmails assumes its `newGuests` parameter contains only the guests actually added (it uses newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to decide between the "You're scheduled" email and the "new guests added" email). The handler already computed `uniqueGuests` (filtered against existing attendees and the blacklist) for the DB write at lines 74–106; passing the unfiltered list means that when a user re-submits an email that is already an attendee (allowed by the client validation, which only checks uniqueness among entered emails), that existing attendee wrongly receives the full AttendeeScheduledEmail booking confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notification.

addGuests schema allows duplicate guest emails, causing duplicate rows or P2002 — The server schema omits the uniqueness refinement the dialog applies client-side (AddGuestsDialog refines z.array(z.string().email()) for uniqueness), and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only removes emails already on the booking or blacklisted — it never deduplicates within the input array. A direct mutation call with `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` passes zod and reaches `createMany`, inserting duplicate Attendee rows for the same booking (or, if the DB enforces uniqueness on bookingId+email, throwing an unhandled P2002).

**Also found in:**
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-106`

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Metadata lookup uses slug to index a map keyed by dirName — The metadata lookup `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` indexes a map that is keyed by app dirName, not by slug (apps.metadata.generated.ts:98 keys entries as `googlecalendar:`, and _appRegistry.ts:17 indexes the same map with `app.dirName`). For every app whose slug differs from its dirName — google-calendar, office365-calendar, msteams, lark-calendar, zoom — the lookup returns undefined and the webhook responds 404 "App not found", and the caller cannot work around it because the earlier `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })` only accepts the slug.

Wrong app slug passed to refreshOAuthTokens: "zoomvideo" should be "zoom" — The appSlug passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `"zoomvideo"`, but the Zoom app's actual slug is `"zoom"` (zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16 and getZoomAppKeys.ts:11 both use "zoom"). When credential sharing is enabled, the sync endpoint receives an app identifier that matches no App row, so it cannot resolve the user's Zoom credentials and Zoom token refresh fails.

Refresh parses direct Salesforce response with stripping minimum schema, dropping instance_url — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` chooses the stripping `minimumTokenResponseSchema` whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, but Salesforce never calls `refreshOAuthTokens` — the parsed response always comes from the direct `login.salesforce.com` token endpoint. In sharing mode the full Salesforce response is parsed with the minimum schema, so the credential update saves `{access_token, refresh_token}` and drops `instance_url`/`signature`/`scope`; the next instantiation builds the jsforce connection from the DB key and loses `instance_url`, breaking Salesforce.

Persisted Google credential is the safeParse envelope, breaking future parses — The refreshed credential persisted to the database is the zod safeParse result envelope, not the parsed data: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{success, data}` and `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` stores that whole envelope via `prisma.credential.update({data: {key}})`. On the next service construction, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws a ZodError because the envelope lacks scope/token_type/expiry_date/access_token/refresh_token at the top level, permanently breaking the user's Google Calendar integration after the first routine token refresh — in default (non-sharing) deployments.

Credential sync path returns raw fetch Response, breaking OAuth refresh at all call sites — When credential sync is enabled this function returns the raw `fetch` Response of the sync endpoint, but the call sites it wraps were written against provider-specific response shapes and immediately break: googlecalendar reads `res?.data` (gaxios shape) so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError (swallowed by the catch, silently reusing the stale token); zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`) and zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) throw TypeError on undefined `.data`; hubspot expects the SDK `HubspotToken` so `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined (NaN expiryDate, `setAccessToken(undefined)`, and the Response object is persisted to Prisma at CalendarService.ts:193-200). OAuth refresh is broken for these apps in any sharing-enabled deployment; the helper must return a normalized shape all callers agree on (or parse the JSON once and let each adapter map it).

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-96`
- `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-191`

Invalid computed keys strip all but access_token; fake refresh_token saved — The "minimum" schema's computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (ZodString has no custom toString, and the duplicate object-literal key is overwritten), so the schema effectively validates only `access_token`. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so in the credential-sharing path the parsed output contains only `access_token` — refresh_token, expiry_date, instance_url, etc. are all stripped.

Computed keys collapse to "[object Object]", stripping fields from parsed token — The computed catch-all keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal property name `"[object Object]"` (zod 3.x ZodString has no toString override, and the second key overwrites the first), so the intended "any numeric property is the expiry" / "allow other properties" semantics do not exist and `z.object`'s default strip mode removes every field except `access_token` from the parsed data. In sharing mode this corrupts persisted credentials: salesforce stores a key without `instance_url` (next instantiation builds the jsforce connection with `instanceUrl: undefined`) and office365calendar never receives the transformed `expires_in`, so its stored expiry stays expired and every getToken triggers a new refresh.

Computed schema keys collapse, stripping refresh_token and breaking credentials — The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"` (Zod schemas don't override `toString`, and z.object has no wildcard shape keys), so the duplicate key collapses and the declared validations — "any property with a number is the expiry" and "allow other properties" — never run. The schema is effectively just `{access_token: string}`, and since z.object strips unknown keys, `data` contains only `access_token`; the injected dummy `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` then overwrites consumers' real refresh tokens (e.g. office365calendar's spread at CalendarService.ts:264 saves `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` to the DB, permanently breaking the credential in sharing mode).

Computed key `[z.string().toString()]` collapses to "[object Object]"; schema silently drops… — The comments on lines 7-10 do not describe what the schema does. "Assume that any property with a number is the expiry" — the computed key `[z.string().toString()]` does not create a wildcard for numeric properties; zod schemas have no `toString` override, so this evaluates to the single literal key "[object Object]" (which the second, identical computed key then overwrites).

Computed schema keys collapse to duplicate "[object Object]", stripping unvalidated token fields — The computed schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (zod schemas don't override toString), and since they are duplicate keys the second silently overrides the first — so minimumTokenResponseSchema actually only requires `access_token: z.string()`. The intended validation ("any property with a number is the expiry") does not exist, and zod's default key-stripping drops every other field from the parsed token response, so unvalidated/partial token data flows into stored credentials in sharing mode.

Fabricated "refresh_token" placeholder overwrites real stored refresh token — When the parsed data has no `refresh_token` (always the case in sharing mode, since the broken minimum schema strips it), this function injects the literal placeholder string `"refresh_token"` into the data, and callers persist it over the real stored token: zoomvideo (VideoApiAdapter.ts lines 120-122) writes `key.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` so the next refresh POSTs the literal and fails with invalid_grant (integration permanently broken until re-auth) and computes `expiry_date = NaN` from the undefined `expires_in`; office365calendar (CalendarService.ts line 264) spreads the placeholder over the real refresh token. Preserve the previously stored refresh_token instead of fabricating one.

Constructor eagerly refreshes Salesforce token on every instantiation, discarding result — The constructor now triggers an unconditional POST to `login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` plus a `prisma.credential.update` on every service instantiation, and `getCalendar` (packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts line 47) builds a new service per credential per operation with no caching — so every availability check and booking involving a Salesforce credential pays a blocking network roundtrip and a DB write even while the stored token is still valid. The fetched token is additionally never used: line 106 constructs the jsforce connection with the stale `credentialKey.access_token`, so jsforce still refreshes on demand and refresh traffic is doubled.

Race in check-then-insert credential upsert allows duplicate credential rows — The upsert is a check-then-act sequence (`credential.findFirst` followed by `create`) with no transaction and no unique constraint on (userId, appId) — the code's own comment confirms no compound unique exists. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same userId+appSlug (retry storms and duplicate deliveries are normal for webhooks) both observe no existing credential and both insert, leaving duplicate credential rows that make the app appear installed twice and cause the same calendar/video integration to be loaded twice.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality, leaking it via timing — The webhook secret is authenticated with a plain `!==` string comparison (req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET). String equality in V8 short-circuits at the first differing byte, so response timing leaks how many leading bytes of the shared secret an attacker guessed, allowing progressive recovery of the secret — and this secret gates an endpoint that writes attacker-supplied keys directly into any user's credential row.

refreshOAuthTokens called with credentialId instead of owner userId — The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is documented and used as the owner's `userId` (it is sent as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint), but this call site passes `credentialId` — which is `credential.id` (line 53), the credential row's id, not a user id. With credential sharing enabled the sync endpoint is invoked with the wrong identifier, so it either fails to find the user or syncs tokens onto the wrong user's credential.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: SMS lock treated as permanent failure, deleting valid pending reminders — A transient SMS lock makes `twilio.scheduleSMS` return `undefined` (see `twilioProvider.ts`, `checkRateLimitAndThrowError.ts`), so two locked cron runs push `retryCount` past 1 and the `deleteMany` permanently drops valid pending reminders. Increment only on permanent failures like invalid phone numbers, not quota-lock states.

Unprotected reminder update in catch block can abort scheduling of remaining reminders — If this `prisma.workflowReminder.update` rejects — e.g. `P2025` when an overlapping run's `deleteMany` already removed the row — the exception escapes and aborts scheduling for every remaining reminder. Wrap it in its own try/catch, or use `prisma.workflowReminder.updateMany`, which doesn't throw on zero matches.

Unindexed OR in deleteMany forces full table scan on every cron run — The unindexed `retryCount > 1` OR branch — no schema index covers it — defeats the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index, forcing a full `WorkflowReminder` scan on every cron run. Delete the row in the scheduling loop once the increment reaches 2, or add a partial index.

retryCount delete branch lacks SMS method filter, can delete non-SMS reminders — EMAIL reminders and future-dated rows can be deleted, since the new `retryCount > 1` branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter or `scheduledDate` bound, contradicting the comment's stated contract. Restore the method filter in this branch or update the comment.

Retry give-up threshold is off by one, deleting reminders after 2 attempts — Because `retryCount` is incremented on every failed attempt including the first, `gt: 1` gives up after only two attempts — one initial send plus one retry — and deletes the reminder. Use `gt: 2` to allow three total attempts, or stop counting the first failure.

Retry counter uses read-modify-write instead of atomic increment, allowing lost updates — Overlapping cron runs both read the same `findMany` snapshot and write the same `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, a lost update that undercounts failures and lets a permanently failing reminder retry indefinitely — the exact behavior this change was written to eliminate. Use the atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` at both sites.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Existing 2FA users permanently lack backup codes; enable endpoint never generates them — Every pre-existing 2FA user has `backupCodes` = null, so the lost-access login path always fails with `MissingBackupCodes` and their only recourse is disabling 2FA. Generate codes in the enable endpoint when `backupCodes` is null, or add a regeneration path for already-enabled users.

Backup code login skips password verification, allowing single-factor auth — Any non-empty garbage `totpCode` skips the password gate, so a stolen backup code plus a wrong password authenticates — turning a static downloaded secret into single-factor login. Verify the password inside the backup-code branch, or only allow the skip when the TOTP path is actually taken.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:128-131`

2FA switch assertion is vacuous: unchecked Promise is always truthy — The un-awaited `isChecked()` Promise is always truthy, so `toBeTruthy()` never fails and the test cannot catch an unchecked switch. Replace it with `toBeChecked()` (or the `data-state="checked"` visibility check) and drop the FIXME.

Backup-codes test never verifies the actual codes; passes on malformed output — The checks pass even when generation is broken: the download check compares only the filename, and `toast-success` fires without awaiting the clipboard write. Assert the rendered codes (10 entries matching `XXXXX-XXXXX`) or the downloaded file's contents.

Backup code check-then-act race lets one code mint multiple sessions — Between reading `backupCodes` and writing the consumed array sit a bcrypt check and a rate-limit call, so two concurrent requests can both pass `indexOf` and mint sessions from one code. Consume it atomically, e.g. an `updateMany` filtered on the stored codes being unchanged.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:128-149`

Dialog close at backup-codes step skips onEnable() and leaves stale state — Closing the dialog via X, Escape, or outside click skips `onEnable()` and `resetState()`, so the parent never invalidates `viewer.me` and re-opening resurrects the stale codes step. Handle `onOpenChange` to enable and reset at this step.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:134-136`

Backup code verified with non-constant-time indexOf, leaking timing data — `indexOf` compares the submitted secret with plain equality on an unauthenticated endpoint, leaking match position and prefix length via timing, unlike the adjacent TOTP and bcrypt paths. Use `timingSafeEqual` over fixed-length digests of each code instead.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58-64`

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: toEqual fails against nested Prisma.Sql fragments the service returns — Because `toEqual` compares `strings`/`values` structurally, these assertions never match the nested `Sql` fragments the service composes, so three tests fail — invisibly, since this fork's CI can't run the integration job. Compose the expected value the same way (or compare `conditions.text`), or flatten in the service via `Prisma.join`.

Org/team-scope SQL array parameters are never executed by any test — Only the user-scope path ever executes, so the org/team authorization SQL — including its `ANY(${array})` parameters — has no execution evidence, and a wrong column name or unsupported array serialization would ship silently since hand-written SQL is only validated at execution. Add executing tests for those scopes via `getBaseConditions`, mirroring `insightsRouting.integration-test.ts`.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Unescaped embed URL interpolated into raw HTML footer causes stored XSS — Because the footer post is stored with `cook_method: raw_html` and rendered raw, any quote or `<` in `url` becomes stored XSS; `embed_url` only passes a host check and RSS `<link>` values get no URI parsing. HTML-escape the URL before interpolating it into the I18n link argument.

raw_html cook method bypasses the whitelist sanitizer, enabling stored XSS — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` persists unsanitized external HTML as `cooked`, so any `<script>` in the feed — including entity-encoded or MITM-injected over http — executes on the Discourse origin for every viewer. Run imported content through the whitelist sanitizer before storing it.

PollFeed crashes on nil content and String#scrub missing on Ruby 2.0 — `i.content.scrub` crashes the poll job in two ways: `i.content` is nil for feeds without `content:encoded`, and `String#scrub` doesn't exist on the project's pinned Ruby 2.0.0 (.ruby-version.sample), so with `retry: false` the hourly import dies silently. Guard nil content and use a 2.0-compatible scrub or drop it.

Nil post in TopicEmbed.import crashes feed imports on stale embeds — If the topic or post backing an embed is deleted — nothing cleans up `topic_embeds` — `embed.post` is nil, so the next poll crashes in `revise!` via `PostRevisor.new(nil)`, aborting the `rss.items.each` loop and permanently stopping all imports. Guard `embed.post` and destroy or skip stale rows.

Best-of embed view crashes on posts from deleted users (post.user can be nil) — `UserDestroyer` nulls `posts.user_id` while keeping the posts (lib/user_destroyer.rb), so a best-of post from a deleted user raises NoMethodError here — a permanent 500 for that article's embedded comments. Fall back to a placeholder avatar and username when `post.user` is nil.

Embed assets not precompiled, breaking /embed/best in production — With `config.assets.compile = false` in production (config/environments/production.rb), `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` raises "embed.css isn't precompiled" and every `/embed/best` request returns a 500; `embed.js` can't be served at all. Add both assets to the precompile list in config/application.rb.

SSRF: open-uri follows redirects, defeating the embeddable host check — `invalid_host?` checks only the initial `embed_url` host, but `open(url)` follows redirects, so a redirecting URL on the embeddable host lets unauthenticated callers make the server fetch arbitrary internal targets and import their content into a publicly readable topic. Disable redirect following or re-validate each hop's host.

Poll feed has no error handling; nil content aborts every import — With `retry: false`, any transient failure in `open`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, or `i.content.scrub` aborts the run mid-iteration, and feeds whose items lack `<content>` (plain RSS 2.0 uses `description`) crash on nil every hour. Wrap the fetch/parse and each item in error handling, falling back to `i.description`.

Invalid ERB closer `<%- end if %>` breaks template compilation — `<%- end if %>` compiles to the incomplete Ruby statement `end if`, so the template fails to compile and every `embed/best` render — the feature's main success path — raises an ActionView error. Close the `if`/`else` block with plain `<%- end %>`.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs by treating them as root-relative paths — `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs, and `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips their leading slashes, turning `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` into a broken path on the embed host; the same applies to `img` `src`. Only rewrite values that don't start with `//`.

postMessage origin check uses substring match, allowing spoofed origins — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured URL — e.g. an attacker-controlled `http://forums.com` matches `forums.company.com` — so a third-party window can spoof the channel and set arbitrary iframe heights. Compare `e.origin` for exact equality against the normalized origin of `discourseUrl`.

Guard-condition specs are vacuous: sibling settings not stubbed, so tests always pass — Each test stubs only one of the three guards in `execute`, leaving siblings like `feed_polling_url` and `embed_by_username` at unsatisfied defaults, so `poll_feed` is never called regardless — deleting any requirement wouldn't fail these specs. Stub the sibling settings to satisfying values in each test.

Spec never reaches action: embeddable_host not stubbed, so 404 path untested — Without `embeddable_host` stubbed, the `ensure_embeddable` filter raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` before the action runs, so `params.require(:embed_url)` is never reached and the test passes even if that line is deleted. Stub `embeddable_host` (and a matching referer) and assert the actual 404 status.

Non-atomic setnx/expire can leave throttle key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval — If the process dies between `$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire` in `retrieved_recently?`, the `retrieved:` key is left without a TTL and nothing ever clears it, permanently blocking that URL's retrieval and leaving its embed stuck loading. Set the key and TTL atomically in one command.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Migration inserts legacy embeddable hosts without stripping scheme and path — The migration inserts legacy `embeddable_hosts` values verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing the model's `before_validation` normalization that strips `https?://` prefixes and paths.
