The new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = uri.host`, so rows migrated as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (formats the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` accepted by parsing `URI(h).host`) never match any referer, silently breaking embedding on upgraded sites until an admin re-saves each row.

Host comparison is case-sensitive on the referer side — `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the stored column while the referer's `uri.host` is left as-is, so a mixed-case referer (e.g. 'http://Eviltrout.com/page') or a mixed-case admin-entered host never matches even though the `lower()` shows case-insensitive matching was intended. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, so validly configured hosts get falsely rejected and embedding fails for those sites.

Hosts saved with a port are never matched because record_for_host drops the port — A host saved with a port (explicitly permitted by the validation regex `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` and preserved by `before_validation`, which strips only protocol and path) can never be matched, because `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` — which excludes the port in Ruby — against the stored value via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. An admin who enters e.g. `example.com:8080` gets a permanently dead configuration: `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` returns false for every referer and embed_url from that host, so `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` reject all embedding from it.

Plural _hydrateEmbedded branch throws on null/non-array and keeps unhydrated keys with undefined… — The new plural branch of `_hydrateEmbedded` has no failure handling, unlike the guarded singular branch: `obj[k].map` throws a TypeError if a `_ids` key holds null or a non-array, and when `_lookupSubType` finds nothing for an id, the original key is still deleted and the model receives an array containing `undefined` entries — `hydrated || []` is dead code because `.map` always returns a truthy array. Since the regex change now routes every `_ids` key in every `__rest_serializer` payload through this branch (not just known associations), any such key that is null or whose ids aren't side-loaded in root either breaks hydration with an exception or silently corrupts the record's data.

Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting row is absent — `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError when the `embed_category` site_settings row is missing or its value doesn't match any category name (PG::Result#[] returns nil for zero rows). This is the default state for nearly every install — Discourse only writes a site_settings row when a setting is explicitly changed, `embed_category` defaults to '' (which can never join on `c.name`), and fresh installs have an empty site_settings table — so `db:migrate` aborts with `undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass` and blocks deploys.

Update and destroy crash with 500 when embeddable host id is missing or stale — `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil when the id doesn't exist (e.g., the record was deleted in another admin tab or the request uses a stale/invalid id), and the result is used without a guard: `save_host(nil)` does `nil.host = ...` in update, and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`. Both actions crash with NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 404.

update/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) when embeddable host id does not exist — `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil when no host with that id exists (e.g. a double-delete from a stale admin UI or a PUT to a deleted id). Both `update` (save_host(nil) → `nil.host = ...`) and `destroy` (`nil.destroy`) then raise NoMethodError and answer with an unhandled 500 instead of a 404 for a missing resource.

update action ignores params and persists nothing, contradicting its name — The `update` action is named and invoked as an update — the route is `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` and the frontend controller's `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` — but the action ignores all request parameters and persists nothing; it only re-renders the serializer. A caller reading the name (or issuing the PUT) expects changes to be saved.

update/destroy raise NoMethodError on nil when host id doesn't exist — `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` with no nil check. When the id doesn't match a record (stale id after a concurrent deletion by another admin, or a direct API request), this raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a 404 — and in the JS delete flow the destroyRecord promise rejects unhandled, leaving the row stuck in the UI.

before_validation calls sub! on nil host, causing 500 instead of validation error — The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!` without a nil guard. A create/update request with `host: null` (params[:embeddable_host][:host] is nil) raises NoMethodError on nil before `validates_format_of` can run, turning invalid input into an unhandled 500 instead of a rendered validation error.

"is false if embeddable_host is blank" test no longer tests anything — The test "it is false if embeddable_host is blank" verifies nothing after this PR's restructuring. It now sits outside the 'with an emeddable host' describe block, so besides no host being fabricated, `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` is left false and `has_topic_embed?` is never stubbed true (the topic is Fabricate.build with no topic embed).

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

findings.description: .panel lost float: right, breaking header layout in non-flexbox browsers (IE9) — In IE9 (supported via `ie9-hax.js.es6`), `.contents` never becomes a flex container, so `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)` are inert and the panel stacks below the logo, overlapping `#main-outlet`. Restore `float: right` on `.panel` — floats on flex items are ignored, so flex-capable browsers are unaffected.

goldensDetail.text: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Shell injection: unsanitized type param reaches shell via tempfile path — An API request with shell metacharacters in the unsanitized `type` param achieves arbitrary command execution: the `FileHelper.download` tempfile basename embeds `type` and reaches `convert_with`'s interpolated shell string via `OptimizedImage.downsize`. Whitelist `type` and use array-form process spawning.

Duplicate downsize definition shadows the 5-arg version and breaks ResizeEmoji — Custom emoji are never resized: `Jobs::ResizeEmoji`'s 5-argument call raises `ArgumentError` against the surviving 4-parameter `downsize`. Delete the duplicate definition and pass a dimensions string from `resize_emoji.rb`.

Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores per-type site settings for file size validation — The hardcoded `maxSizeKB` lets attachments above `max_attachment_size_kb` pass client validation only to fail server-side in `Validators::UploadValidator#maximum_file_size`, and blocks valid uploads when admins raise limits past 10MB. Read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:244-248`

Downsize retry loop ignores failures and wastes CPU on intermediate ImageOptim passes — Large uploads now spend tens of seconds of sequential CPU: each iteration's `ImageOptim` pass is overwritten by the next `convert`, and a failed `downsize` still burns all 5 attempts. Break on failure and optimize only once, after the loop.

Browser-uploaded animated GIFs lose animation when auto-downsized — Rack multipart tempfiles lack the `.gif` extension, so `optimize`'s animation check never matches and browser-uploaded animated GIFs are flattened to a static first frame despite `allow_animation`. Base the animated decision on the upload filename rather than the tempfile path.

Downsize loop capped at 5 iterations may not reach the allowed image size — Five 80% passes leave a 10MB image near 3.3MB when `max_image_size_kb` is 1024, so `Upload.create_for` still rejects it despite the comment's promise. Loop until under the limit, breaking when the size stops shrinking.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: remove_member passes an integer to association delete, raising AssociationTypeMismatch — Rails' collection `delete` type-checks arguments, so the bare integer in `group.users.delete(user_id)` raises `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` and removes no one. Load the `User` record first, delete the `group_users` join record directly, or call the model's `remove`.

Group member routes deliver params[:id] but controller requires params[:group_id] — As member routes under `resources :groups`, the id arrives as `params[:id]`, so `params.require(:group_id)` in `add_members` and `remove_member` raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` and every request fails (the specs pass `group_id:` directly, masking it). Read `params[:id]` or rename the route param.

**Also found in:**
- `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65-76`
- `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:84-90`

Members endpoint caps list at 50; public page has no pager so rest unreachable — The unconditional 50 default leaves the public page — `group/members.hbs` iterates `members` with no pagination controls — showing only the first 50 of a larger group, the rest unreachable. Add pagination there or fetch without the cap.

**Also found in:**
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12`

findMembers clamps offset with stale user_count, leaving an empty page after removal — Removing the last member of the last page makes `findMembers` clamp the offset with the stale previous-load `user_count`, landing the admin on an empty page with no way forward. Recompute the offset from the fresh response meta, or step back a page when `members` is empty.

Unbounded limit/offset params cause 500 errors on public members endpoint — Unbounded `params[:limit]` and `params[:offset]` now reach the query for any visible group, so a negative `offset` raises `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` and a 500 from this public endpoint. Clamp both to a minimum of 0 and cap `limit` at a sane maximum.

{{#if id}} hides members of the "everyone" group whose id is 0 — The persisted `everyone` group has `id` 0 (`Group::AUTO_GROUPS[:everyone]`), so `{{#if id}}` treats it as unsaved and hides its member list and count. Detect a new group explicitly — e.g. a computed `isNew` via `Em.isNone(id)` — instead of relying on truthiness.
totalPages counts phantom page when user_count is exact multiple of limit — Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` in `totalPages`.

add_members raises RecordNotUnique when adding an existing member — Because `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, `group.add(user)` on an existing member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and a 500 — easy to hit since the selector isn't cleared after an add (see the `addMembers` TODO). Guard with a `GroupUser` existence check or rescue and skip duplicates.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Fallback locale list crashes I18n.t when default_locale is nil or DB unavailable — When the settings container is empty or the DB is unreachable, `SiteSetting.default_locale` returns nil or raises, so `to_sym` crashes every `I18n.t` call — lib/tasks/db.rake already guards this exact read. Guard the read with a `:en` fallback and rescue so the list degrades instead.

Stale translation cache: fallback depends on default_locale but accelerator cache key does not — Translation results now depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but the cross-request LRU cache in `translate_accelerator.rb` still keys only on key, locale, and backend, so users keep stale translations after an admin changes the default. Add `default_locale` to the cache key or clear the cache when it changes.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Unauthenticated device tagging can exhaust the global cap and break anonymous auth — An attacker can fill the global cap with arbitrary `X-Grafana-Device-Id` values via `TagDevice`, locking out every genuine new anonymous device for ~30 days. Throttle or bound anonymous device creation per client IP.

Wire provider set still registers ProvideAnonDBStore under old single-arg contract — `pkg/server/wire.go` still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` with no provider for a bare `int64`, so wire generation breaks. Remove the stale entry and regenerate the wiring.

Device-limit error path leaves stale cache entry, letting over-limit devices through on retry — `tagDeviceUI` caches the device key before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` and never evicts it on failure, so an over-limit device is denied once and then granted for 29 minutes. Delete the `localCache` entry when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

Device-limit check is a check-then-act race; concurrent requests can exceed the cap — `CountDevices` and the subsequent insert run in separate DB sessions with no transaction or lock, so concurrent first-requests can all pass the check and exceed the cap. Wrap the count and write in a single transaction or enforce the limit atomically.

ErrDeviceLimitReached returned raw, surfacing as generic internal auth error — The auth middleware only renders `authn.Error` values, so a raw `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` surfaces as an indistinguishable internal fault on every request. Return the sentinel as an `authn.Error` with a status code and reason.

Dropped recover lets TagDevice panics fail anonymous requests — The old goroutine's `recover()` guaranteed a tagging panic only logged a warning; without it, panics now surface as a generic 500 on anonymous requests. Keep a recover around the synchronous `TagDevice` call.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Double-checked locking misses cache re-check under write lock, serializing cold-start rebuilds — Concurrent cold-start callers each rebuild the assets while serialized on `entryPointAssetsCacheMu`, causing a thundering herd under the write lock. After acquiring the lock, re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` so only the first caller builds.

TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh instance instead of the receiver — Because `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs via `FromContext`, tests injecting a `TestLogger` record nothing — the log lands in a throwaway instance. Return `f` instead of `NewTestLogger()`, matching the receiver-based behavior of `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` in `logger.go`.

Async legacy writes use request context that cancels when handler returns — This defeats mode 3's stated purpose (legacy write as a safe measure) and only passes tests because local file/unified storage finishes within the response-write window. Apply the timeout to a detached context instead, e.g. `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), time.Second*10, ...)` (the same pattern Delete at line 110, Update at 135, and DeleteCollection at 163 must use).

Fire-and-forget goroutines break legacy write ordering across dual stores — Mode 3 now performs every legacy write in a fire-and-forget goroutine (same pattern repeated at lines 108-114, 134-141 and 161-167). Dual-write correctness assumes operations reach LegacyStorage in the same order they were applied to Storage, but goroutine execution order is not guaranteed: a delete(name) followed by a create(name) can leave the object present in legacy storage while unified storage reports it deleted, and two sequential updates (A then B) can leave legacy holding A's stale state.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:134-141`

Delete returns early on NotFound from unified storage, orphaning legacy-only rows — Delete now returns immediately when `d.Storage.Delete` fails with any error, including NotFound, whereas the removed code tolerated NotFound and still called `d.Legacy.Delete` to clean up legacy-only rows. Objects that exist only in legacy storage (the migration drift this dual writer exists to reconcile) become undeletable: the caller gets a 404 and the legacy row is orphaned forever, reappearing if reads ever fall back to legacy.

Data race: async legacy Create mutates obj during response serialization — Mode 1 explicitly guards this exact scenario with `created.DeepCopyObject()` before its async write (dualwriter_mode1.go:51). Pass `obj.DeepCopyObject()` into the goroutine.

Mode 3 tests never assert the asynchronous legacy half of the dual write — dualwriter_mode3.go now performs Legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection in fire-and-forget goroutines, but every TestMode3_* function returns after the synchronous Storage call and asserts only on its result — no AssertExpectations/AssertCalled or call-count check exists anywhere in the package, and nothing waits for the goroutines. If all the `go func() { d.Legacy.X(...) }` blocks were deleted from the implementation, every one of these tests would still pass (TestMode3_Delete/TestMode3_DeleteCollection don't even configure a legacy expectation).

Shared mock.Mock makes Get/List tests unable to pin reads to Storage — TestMode3_Get (and TestMode3_List) cannot detect which backend served the read, because legacyStoreMock and storageMock wrap the same shared mock.Mock and dispatch to the same method names — the `m.On("Get", mock.Anything, name, ...)` expectation set via setupStorageFn is matched identically by d.Legacy.Get. If Mode3's Get/List were changed to read from LegacyStorage instead of Storage (mode 3's core read contract, and the difference between mode 2 and mode 3), these tests still pass.

Async legacy Update re-derives object instead of writing unified storage result — Mode 2 still enforces replication with `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}` (dualwriter_mode2.go:298), as did this file's previous implementation. Wrap the unified-storage result: `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}, ...)`.

Create/Update storage error paths record duration under legacy metric — On unified-storage failure, Create records the failure with `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` using the storage start time — the error and elapsed time land in grafana_dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds for a call that never touched legacy storage, and grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds never sees its own failures. Update's error path has the identical defect at line 129.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-131`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129-132`

DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records latency on the storage metric instead of the legacy metric — It must call `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)` like the legacy goroutines in Create (line 56), Delete (line 113), and Update (line 140).

Delete success path records object name instead of kind in storage duration metric — The Delete success path passes the object `name` where every other call site in this file passes `options.Kind`, so the kind label of grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds receives the object's name (e.g. "foo") instead of the resource kind. Per-kind aggregation breaks, and each distinct object name creates a new histogram series (buckets × is_error × mode × method), growing label cardinality without bound as objects are deleted.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:2-7`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock; concurrent BuildIndex crashes process — If any goroutine is in `BuildIndex` while this log line runs, `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` reads `b.cache` without `b.cacheMu` and the runtime fatally crashes the process. Have `TotalDocs` in `search/bleve.go` take `b.cacheMu.RLock()` before iterating.

Unsynchronized concurrent same-key index builds can duplicate work and corrupt file-backed indexes — Removing the function-wide lock leaves `getOrCreateIndex` unsynchronized, so concurrent same-key builders each scan and the loser's cached index silently drops documents; file-backed builds can corrupt the on-disk index. Add per-key sync — `singleflight` in `getOrCreateIndex`, or a cache re-check under the write lock in `BuildIndex`.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:307-307`
- `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:85-90`

NewResourceServer now blocks on full Init and hard-fails, breaking the constructor contract — Every caller now blocks construction on the full index build and hard-fails on any init error — one consumer already broke and was skipped rather than adapted. Revert `NewResourceServer` to returning immediately, leaving init to the separate `Init` path.

Postgres skip silences failing integration test instead of fixing it — This skip hides a real postgres failure exactly when this PR rewrites the init path it tests, so regressions go undetected. Fix the cause — `addStorageServerToConfig` hardcodes grafanatest credentials instead of parsing the connection string — or scope the skip to Drone.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Delete and Pause actions silently dropped when only promRule is provided — Grafana rules in the new list view lose Delete and Pause even though `showDeleteModal` only needs the identifier, because AlertRuleMenu gates both items on `rulerRule`. Gate them on the prom-rule abilities and `identifier` instead.

Silence action is a no-op: drawer requires a ruler rule that is never passed — Clicking Silence sets `showSilenceDrawer` but renders nothing: the drawer mounts only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is truthy, and this call site passes only `promRule`. Render a prom-rule-based silence drawer or hide the menu item when no drawer can render.

Federated rules wrongly shown as editable: federated check dropped in delegation — Federated Mimir rules now expose Edit, Delete, Pause, Restore and Duplicate because `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated` to `false` instead of computing `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. Restore the check before delegating.

**Also found in:**
- `public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:243-245`

skipToken does not skip: undefined rule still yields supported abilities — Cloud rules show a Duplicate item gated only by Grafana create permission, bypassing the datasource-scoped check, because the `skipToken` path still computes `MaybeSupported` as `AlwaysSupported`. Return `NotSupported` for every action when `rule` is undefined.

Menu actions test grants delete permission but never asserts the Delete item — The test grants delete permission but never asserts Delete, so it passes with the action missing. Either assert Delete and fix the `rulerRule` gate in AlertRuleMenu, or drop the delete permission and rename the test.

Undefined rule (skipToken) yields enabled Duplicate ability instead of disabled — With `rule` undefined, `loading` is false so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported`, letting AlertRuleMenu's OR show Duplicate on cloud rules with only `AlertingRuleCreate`. Early-return `NotSupported` for every action on the skip path.

Dropped federated rule group check makes federated rules editable/deletable — Federated Mimir rule groups now evaluate as editable and deletable for every `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` consumer because the delegation to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated` to `false`. Restore `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` in the wrapper.

Federated Mimir rule groups incorrectly shown as editable/removable after refactor — Federated Mimir rules now offer Update, Delete, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently because the delegation to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated` to `false`. Pass a federated flag or keep `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` in the wrapper until real support lands.

Delegation to useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops federated-rule immutability check — Read-only federated Mimir rules now report Update, Delete and Pause as supported to every `useAlertRuleAbility` consumer because `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated` to `false`. Pass a federated flag derived from the combined rule's group into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Inverted grant-type comparison in isAccessTokenId accepts wrong grant types — Wrong or missing grant types encoded in token IDs pass undetected, since the check returns false only on a match. Negate the `equals` in `isAccessTokenId` so mismatched segments are rejected.

UMA grant shortcut "pg" never used: RPT token creation never sets GRANT_TYPE attribute — RPTs encode "na" and report no grant info because `AuthorizationTokenService` builds them without `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. Set the attribute on the clientSessionCtx in the UMA path before token creation.

`ClientCredentialsGrantType` never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` — Set the attribute on the clientSessionCtx before `generateAccessToken()`, mirroring `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/tokenexchange/StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:236-240`

Grant type shortcuts are not validated for the 2-char, no-':' format — A custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` following its own javadoc can register a 3-char or ':'-containing shortcut, producing token IDs the decoder in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` rejects or misparses. Validate length and content at registration and fix the `getShortcut()` javadoc.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:100-118`
- `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29-33`

testIncorrectGrantType passes via swallowed NPE instead of validation error — The test never reaches the unknown-grant validation it is named for: `before()` skips `postInit`, so `getGrantTypeByShortcut` throws a null-sessionFactory NPE that the broad `catch (RuntimeException)` swallows. Catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically and initialize the factory.

getSubGroupsCount returns null when underlying group is deleted, violating non-null contract — Unboxing callers following the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` never-null contract will NPE. Return 0L for a concurrently deleted group, as the JPA layer does with its `Objects::nonNull` filter.

Reader thread not joined before asserting, so late exceptions go unobserved — The thread can still be mid-read when `deletedAll.set(true)` flips, so a `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` failure may land after the assertion already passed. Keep the Thread reference and `join()` with a timeout before asserting `caughtExceptions`.

**Also found in:**
- `tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:136-149`
Missing English reference file crashes build with unchecked RuntimeException — Report it as a `messages` entry instead.

Overlapping prefix/suffix stripping can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — If `sanitized` is a prefix of `value`, `start` and `end` can overlap so `start + end` exceeds `sanitized.length()`, and `sanitized.substring()` throws a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` that escapes `verify()` and fails the build. Stop the `end` loop once `start + end` reaches the length bound.

error-invalid-multivalued-size uses MessageFormat placeholders the JS i18n bundle cannot render — i18next cannot evaluate `{2,choice,...}`, so users see literal braces and translators get a convention unlike every other locale. Restore `{{0}}` here and in the matching admin-ui `messages_en.properties`, leaving choice plurals to the base themes.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties:3138-3138`

Italian text pasted into Lithuanian totpStep1 message — Lithuanian users see Italian on the account and login TOTP setup pages — the same string was pasted into `loginTotpStep1` in the login `messages_lt.properties`. Replace both with the Lithuanian translation.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties:71-71`

totpStep1 in zh_CN bundle uses Traditional Chinese instead of Simplified — Simplified-Chinese users get Traditional script (`手機`, `應用程式`) on the TOTP page, clashing with every other key in this bundle. Rewrite `totpStep1` in Simplified forms, matching adjacent keys like `totpStep2`.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: Existing admin-permissions servers never get the `Clients` type or new scopes — Creating any client permission fails — `getScope` throws, `getOrCreateResource` throws `ModelException` — and every client permission evaluation NPEs via the null type resource. Because `init()` returns early when `getAdminPermissionsClient()` exists, add a migration creating the missing type resource and scopes.

getClientsWithPermission adds type-level 'Clients' name, not per-client IDs — Per-client resources from `getOrCreateResource` carry no type, so `findByType` matches only the type-level resource and `granted` collects the literal `Clients` — `AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions` then NPEs calling `realm.getClientById`. Set the resource type at creation, as V1's `ClientPermissions` does, or resolve per-client resources by name.

NPE when Clients type resource is missing in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) — When the type resource is absent, `getResourceTypeResource` returns null and `policyStore.findByResource` throws, turning every `canManage`/`canView`/`canConfigure`/`canMapRoles` client check into a 500 instead of a denial. Add a null check returning false, as the `hasPermission(String)` overload does.

Client removal listener calls setPermissionsEnabled that throws under AUTHZ_V2 — With `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` enabled, the `ClientRemovedEvent` handler reaches `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` — every client deletion fails. Make the listener V2-aware: skip the call or perform V2-appropriate cleanup when that flag is on.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195`
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195`

V2 canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, crashing token exchange — `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` calls `canExchangeTo` for every non-self audience client, so with V2 enabled cross-client token exchange returns a 500 rather than evaluating or denying. Implement the evaluation — the now-dead `getEvaluationContext` shows the intent — or return false.

Type-level all-clients fallback re-evaluated for every client and scope check — In the `ClientsResource.getClients` listing, each `canView` repeats the identical type-level fallback up to three times — thousands of full policy evaluations per request in large realms. Compute the fallback once per request or collapse scopes into a single `hasPermission` call.

All-clients permission fallback skipped once a per-client resource exists — Granting `view` on one client then `manage` for all clients leaves `canManage` returning false and a 403 despite the realm-wide grant, contradicting the `ClientPermissionEvaluator` javadoc. In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, evaluate the all-clients resource whenever the per-client evaluation fails to grant the requested scope.

testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient doesn't verify per-client scoping — Every operation in `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` targets `myclient`, so a regression where one client's permission authorizes all clients would still pass. Add a negative check against a second client, as `testManageOnlyOneClient` does, and grant scopes separately.

**Also found in:**
- `tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:191-247`

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description:
PasswordForm advertises passkey support that base theme's password page cannot render — Base-derived themes lack the `passkeys.conditionalUIData` include in their `login-password.ftl`, so `configuredFor` admits passkey-only users the rendered page cannot serve — they get neither passkey UI nor a password field. Add the include to the base template or drop the `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` clause.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/PasswordForm.java:51-54`

Passkey conditionalUIData macro 500s password page when required vars unset — For users without a passwordless credential, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` returns null before setting `isUserIdentified` and `userVerification`, so `passkeys.ftl` interpolation throws and the login flow dies with a 500. Guard the include on those variables or default them in the macro.

Registered passkey credential IDs leaked to unauthenticated visitors — Before authentication, anyone submitting a known username now receives hidden inputs listing that user's passkey `credentialId` values and authenticator labels. Restrict the `authn_select` form — and the `authenticators` attribute behind it — to genuine re-authentication sessions.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/PasswordForm.java:50-57`

Login-cache invalidation on create/remove of login-available IDP is untested — A stale login IDP could keep being served from the cache until expiry without this test failing. Add steps that create and remove a login-available IDP and assert all three `cacheKeyForLogin` entries are invalidated.

testCacheIDPForLogin never asserts on getForLogin's returned stream — The cache-hit path of `getForLogin` skips the `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` mapping, so a hit and a miss can return different models unnoticed here. Assert the count and aliases returned by a second, cache-hit call for each `FetchMode`.

Test never exercises the cached-query merge branch of getForLogin — Broken merge logic in `getForLogin` would still pass because the test queries only one search key per `FetchMode`, never triggering the cached-query merge. Query the same `FetchMode` under a second organization and assert both search keys are served correctly.

getLoginPredicate() may NPE when identity provider config is null — If an IDP has null config, `getLoginPredicate()` throws an NPE. Guard the `idp.getConfig()` access before reading `OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC`.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Feature flag branch renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty data — With the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag on, every dashboard table widget renders blank because the branch passes hardcoded empty `columns` and `tableData`, ignoring computed values like `result.data` and `result.meta`. Pass real data — columns from `fields`, `tableData` from the query results — so the flag can be enabled safely.

Unconditional Snuba replay-instance query wastes an RPC when error context is disabled — Every request with error context disabled still pays a wasted `query_replay_instance` RPC plus `process_raw_response` work, since their only consumer `error_ids` is discarded. Evaluate `disable_error_fetching` before querying and skip both calls when it is set.

Null max_segment_id fixture change is neutralized by mocked delete_matched_rows — Because `delete_matched_rows` is patched out, `_make_recording_filenames` never runs, so the null `max_segment_id` fixture verifies nothing — the test passes whether the None-guard is correct, removed, or inverted. Add a test calling `_make_recording_filenames` with a null `max_segment_id` that asserts no recording filenames are produced.

test_basic drops application/reports+json content type, so custom parser is never tested — With `application/reports+json` dropped, every request uses the default `JSONParser`, so `BrowserReportsJSONParser` is never exercised — the suite would pass even if the parser broke. Keep at least one test, like `test_basic`, posting with that content type.

get_multi result zipped positionally with error_ids, mispairing error data — `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `get_multi` returns values in input order, but it returns a dict with no ordering contract, so `id`, title, and message can be mispaired and the `None` filter silently shifts alignment. Look up each node by its generated `node_id` instead.

Mutual-exclusion validators miss falsy zero values for age and timestamp — A report with both `timestamp` and `age` set to 0 slips past the truthiness checks in `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`, even though zero is a legitimate value for both. Use explicit presence checks like `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None`.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Per-process SpansBuffer shards the max-flush-segments cap, multiplying it N× — Because each buffer budgets from its own shard subset, one process per shard means N× the `max-flush-segments` cap fetched from Redis and produced to Kafka each cycle, and the higher `any_shard_at_limit` threshold delays the `MessageRejected` backpressure in `submit()`. Have `SpansBuffer.flush_segments` compute the per-shard budget from the total shard count.
Redundant cluster-wide Redis INFO queries per buffer in submit() — Call `get_memory_info()` on any one buffer instead of iterating `self.buffers.values()`.

Shard distribution test passes even if all shards go to one process — The check is vacuous: `total_shards` only sums shard counts, and `process_to_shards_map` is pre-seeded with an entry per process index, so a regression in `process_index = i % self.num_processes` would go uncaught. Assert each process's shard list is non-empty (the expected 2/2 split).

wait_produce timer uses `shards` tag key instead of `shard` — Per-shard dashboards and alerts that aggregate by `shard` silently miss every `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` sample, which splits the dimension into a second tag key unlike the sibling `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` timers. Use the `shard` key here.

max_processes=0 treated as unset; negative value crashes with KeyError — Use an `is not None` check and reject non-positive values.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:59-66`
- `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:60-66`

Expired join deadline skips terminate() for remaining flusher processes — On expiry the `break` skips `process.terminate()` for every remaining flusher, so a hung one never observes `stopped` and keeps producing on possibly reassigned shards; since segments are only removed via `done_flush_segments` after produce, racing flushers can emit duplicate span batches. Terminate each remaining process instead of breaking.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: queued datetime is not serialized, so from_dict rebuilds it as a str — Because dataclasses don't validate, the JSON round-trip through Celery silently leaves `queued` a `str`, handing consumers like `sync_assignee_outbound` an object that violates the declared `datetime` type. Serialize it to an ISO string in `to_dict` and parse with `datetime.fromisoformat` in `from_dict`.

Dataclass default `queued` is evaluated once at import time, not per instance — Every `AssignmentSource` built by `from_integration` records the worker process's startup time as `queued`, so all instances share one stale timestamp. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to capture the actual operation time.

sync_status_outbound declares assignment_source but no caller passes it; breaks ExampleIntegration — Any caller following this abstract signature and passing `assignment_source=` hits a TypeError against `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound`, while the method that actually receives it at runtime only absorbs it via `**kwargs`. Remove it here and declare it on `sync_assignee_outbound`.

OAuth state is a constant signature, not a per-session nonce; forgeable callback — `pipeline.signature` is the same public constant for every session (md5 of view class names in `src/sentry/pipeline/base.py`), so an attacker can forge a callback and bind their GitHub identity to a victim's install. Generate a per-session `state` with `secrets.token_hex()`, persist it via `pipeline.bind_state("state", state)`, and compare with `pipeline.fetch_state("state")`.

Unguarded access to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError — `ensure_integration` overwrites `metadata` on pipeline finish and the pipeline path never sets `sender`, so this read crashes the installation page with a 500. Read it as `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and fail closed on a missing sender, as `src/sentry/integrations/github/installation.py` does.

Unhandled exception in OAuthLoginView when GitHub get_user_info fails — `get_user_info` raises on non-2xx (`raise_for_status` in `src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py`), so a degraded GitHub API or rejected token crashes with a 500 instead of the error page. Wrap the call in a try/except, like the token-exchange parsing above, and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found behavior — The hardcoded `state` never matches `pipeline.signature`, so the request fails at the state check before the not-found branch; the generic assertion keeps the test green even if that handling is removed. Capture the real state from the redirect's `Location` and assert "The GitHub installation could not be found."

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description:
MetricAlertDetectorHandler raises TypeError: abstract methods not implemented — MetricAlertFire auto-registers this handler, so every detector with type='metric_alert_fire' now crashes process_detectors with a TypeError instead of the old no-op behavior. Implement StatefulDetectorHandler's four abstract members, or keep the class on DetectorHandler with a stub evaluate until the stateful metric-alert work lands.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:163-170`

build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores value, so expected occurrences are identical for any value — The new value plumbing into build_occurrence_and_event_data is entirely unverified: tests hardcode 6 where 10, 100, or 8 is evaluated, and the helper's identical expectations would mask any wrong value. Fold `value` into the occurrence (e.g. `subtitle` or `evidence_data`) and fix the mismatched literals.

Expected occurrence built with wrong group key, so fingerprint never matches — Since `build_fingerprint` embeds the group key, the expectation built with `"val1"` can never match the actual occurrence for the `"group_key"` group, so the `DetectorEvaluationResult` assertion always fails. Pass `"group_key"` instead.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Monitor context uses raw config, discarding computed schedule_type display — Incident occurrence event data always receives the raw `schedule_type` because the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the transformed local `config`. Return the local `config` so the `get_schedule_type_display()` value is actually used.

Missing destination calendar crashes Google Meet fallback — Without a destination calendar, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws before event creation can continue. Guard the missing entry to preserve the fallback behavior.

Organizer email uses the first destination for every calendar update — Updates to calendars other than the first can use the wrong organizer email. Select the destination matching `externalCalendarId`, falling back to the first destination.

Hidden-notes message is hard-coded in English — Users in other locales will see the hard-coded English text. Replace `"Notes have been hidden by the organizer"` with the surrounding user-facing translation mechanism.

Missing calendar ID leaves updates without a destination — When `externalCalendarId` is absent, `selectedCalendar` resolves to no destination and can leave the update targeting an undefined calendar ID. Fall back to a valid event destination or the primary calendar.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Concurrent requests can add duplicate attendee emails — Concurrent requests can both pass this check and create duplicate attendees. Enforce uniqueness atomically or add a database constraint and handle conflicts.

Email casing bypasses blacklist and duplicate checks — Case differences can let guests bypass the blacklist or be added twice. Normalize the submitted and stored addresses before comparing them in `uniqueGuests`.

Emails are sent for guests who were not added — Guests who were not inserted can receive normal scheduled emails, making notifications inconsistent with the attendee list. Pass the emails actually inserted to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

Case-sensitive attendee email check denies valid attendees — An attendee whose account email differs only by case can be incorrectly denied authorization. Compare normalized addresses in `isAttendee`.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Credential sync returns a response shape callers cannot consume — Callers may read an absent `data` property or treat the `Response` wrapper as token data when sync is enabled. Parse and normalize the endpoint response to the shape each caller expects.

Concurrent webhook deliveries can create duplicate credentials — Concurrent deliveries can both create credentials for the same user and app, violating the one-credential-per-user/app invariant. Use an atomic upsert or add a unique constraint to the `Credential` schema.

User ID 0 bypasses credential sync — A valid `userId` of `0` skips the sync path and uses the local provider refresh instead. Check explicitly for null or undefined so every valid ID uses the configured endpoint.

Webhook secret comparison leaks matching prefixes through timing — Direct string comparison can leak matching secret prefixes through timing. Validate equal lengths, then compare the webhook secret with a constant-time function.
Missing encryption key falls back to an empty string — Fail fast when `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing instead of attempting decryption.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Retry cleanup deletes reminders regardless of method or retry policy — A reminder that fails twice is deleted on the next scheduler run, including non-SMS reminders. Restrict `retryCount` cleanup to SMS reminders and preserve reminders until the retry policy marks them exhausted.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup codes are exposed in the API response — Anyone who captures this response can use the plaintext backup codes to access the account. Avoid returning `backupCodes` in a generally observable response, or protect delivery from logging and recording.
Concurrent requests can reuse the same backup code — Replace the unconditional `prisma.user.update` with an atomic conditional update that only consumes the code if the stored set is unchanged.

Security-area modal omits backup code when disabling 2FA — The security-area modal cannot disable 2FA with a backup code because it omits that value. Update its call to `disable` to pass the backup code.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: Zero-valued filter IDs are ignored — ID 0 is treated as absent, so the requested SQL predicate is omitted. Check `eventTypeId` and `memberUserId` against `undefined` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Imported feed HTML is stored without sanitization — An attacker controlling a feed item can inject executable markup that runs on every embedding page. Sanitize `contents` with an allowlist before passing it to `PostCreator`.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Missing embed_category causes the migration to raise — If `embed_category` is absent, indexing the empty query result raises and aborts the migration. Check for an empty result and use the uncategorized-category fallback.

Mixed-case request hostnames fail allowed-host lookup — Mixed-case request hostnames can fail to match because hostnames are case-insensitive. Normalize the parsed hostname before passing it to `where`.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Downsize rejects the existing width/height call form — Emoji resize jobs fail with `ArgumentError` because `resize_emoji.rb` still uses the five-argument form. Preserve compatibility in `OptimizedImage.downsize` or update the caller to pass a dimensions string.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Automatic-group removal test uses the wrong HTTP method — The PUT request misses the DELETE route for `remove_member`, so this test may not exercise the automatic-group guard. Send DELETE and assert 422.
Exact multiples produce an extra member page — When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, the UI exposes a nonexistent page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` to calculate the page count.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Concurrent registrations can exceed the device limit — Concurrent calls can both pass `CountDevices` and insert distinct IDs, exceeding the configured cap. Make the capacity check and insertion atomic with a transaction and appropriate locking or a database constraint.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Legacy create is canceled with the request context — Request cancellation can abort the legacy write after the unified-store write succeeds, leaving the stores inconsistent. Use `context.WithoutCancel` before adding the timeout.

Create returns before the legacy write completes — Callers can receive success before the legacy write completes or fails, breaking consumers that rely on the legacy representation. Preserve synchronous completion or provide an explicit completion guarantee and update consumers.

Successful delete metrics use the object name as the kind label — Successful deletes use a different metric label, fragmenting or misattributing measurements. Pass `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration`.
Success case does not verify the asynchronous legacy write — The test would pass even if `Legacy.Create` were omitted or broken. Synchronize with the asynchronous call and assert that it occurs.
DeleteCollection records legacy duration as storage duration — Call `recordLegacyDuration` for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`.

Storage create failures are recorded as legacy operations — This attributes a `Storage.Create` failure to the legacy backend. Call `recordStorageDuration` to record the operation against the backend that ran.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129-129`
