goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.
BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.
The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Access token ID matcher checks the wrong grant shortcut — Correct token IDs can be rejected, while IDs with a different grant can pass. Check `substring(4, 6)` and reject only when it differs from `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Access token ID matcher checks the wrong grant shortcut — Correct token IDs are rejected because `substring(3, 5)` includes the token-type character and only one grant character. Check `substring(4, 6)` instead.
Access token matcher rejects the expected grant shortcut — The matcher rejects tokens that contain `expectedGrantShortcut`. Negate the equality check so it rejects only a mismatch.

Reader thread may not run or finish before the test passes — The deletion loop can finish before the reader makes a request, so the test may miss concurrent-read regressions. Use a latch to confirm a read occurred and wait for the reader to finish before asserting.

Missing English bundle aborts theme verification — A missing English bundle throws an unchecked exception, so `verify()` aborts instead of reporting diagnostics. Add the read failure to `messages` and return, or route it through the verifier’s normal error handling.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: Missing Clients resource causes authorization check failure — A missing Clients resource can cause a runtime failure instead of denying access. Return false when `getResourceTypeResource` returns null, before calling `findByResource`.

Client listing assertion does not verify all authorized clients are returned — A nonempty result still passes when authorized clients are omitted. Assert the expected client set or size, including the surviving fixture client.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.
The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Feature-enabled tables render with no columns or data — Enabled organizations see a blank table because `TableWidgetVisualization` receives no columns or rows. Pass the current result’s data and metadata, and use its columns.

Missing nodestore events misassociate error details — When `get_multi` omits missing nodes, zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can attach details to the wrong event. Iterate the returned mapping by key or look up each requested node ID directly.

Zero-valued age and timestamp bypass mutual-exclusion validation — Reports with both fields set to zero bypass the mutual-exclusion check because `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` use truthiness. Check whether each field is present in `self.initial_data` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: Assignment source payload contains a non-serializable datetime — A raw `queued` datetime can make JSON serialization fail and prevent inbound assignment changes from being enqueued. Convert it to a supported representation in `to_dict()` or omit it.
Missing sender metadata raises KeyError during installation setup — Guard the `integration.metadata` lookup and treat a missing sender or login as an invalid request.

Inactive integrations return an invalid-installation error — Inactive installations are rejected instead of continuing through the existing flow. Handle their status before the active-only lookup or route them through the missing-installation path.

GitHub login comparison is case-sensitive — Different casing can reject the same GitHub account because usernames are case-insensitive. Normalize both values from `github_authenticated_user` and `integration.metadata` before comparing them.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Video booking references lose credential IDs needed for cancellation — Video bookings fail the credential-ID guard in `handleCancelBooking`, leaving external meetings undeleted on cancellation. Preserve `result.credentialId` for video results as well.

Legacy destinations without credentialId fall back to the primary calendar — Legacy destinations supported by `createAllCalendarEvents` lack `credentialId`, so this lookup silently sends their Google events to `primary`. Retain a configured-destination fallback for the legacy credential-selection path.

Recurring collective cancellations delete the first host's events repeatedly — The `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` loop repeatedly deletes the first host's events while leaving other hosts' events undeleted. Use `calendarCredential` and select each occurrence's reference by matching `credentialId` and `reference.type`.

Missing organizer destination drops collective cohost calendars — When the organizer has no destination, optional chaining on `evt.destinationCalendar` silently discards connected cohosts' destinations. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` before appending `teamDestinationCalendars`.

Missing destination calendar crashes Google Meet booking creation — With no destination calendar, reading `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a `TypeError` for Google Meet bookings instead of using the Cal Video fallback; check `handleNewBooking` for the null case. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` in this condition.

Cohost calendar events use the organizer's destination calendar — Office 365, Lark, and base CalDAV services select the first `destinationCalendar` entry, so cohost requests can fail or target the organizer's calendar. Pass `createEvent` an event containing only the current `destination`, or update those providers to match destinations by credential.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-76`

Missing calendar IDs break destination fallback for updates and deletions — When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this lookup cannot recover a configured destination, so updates fail and `deleteEvent` can leave non-primary events untouched. Resolve the appropriate configured destination in both expressions instead of searching by the missing `externalCalendarId`.

Reversed billing condition assigns organization slugs at the wrong stage — Billed organizations must retain `requestedSlug` until publication, while non-billed organizations need `slug` immediately. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` for the `slug` assignment and leave the metadata condition billing-enabled.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team administrators are incorrectly forbidden from adding guests — An `ADMIN` who is neither the organizer nor an attendee receives `FORBIDDEN` because `isTeamAdminOrOwner` requires both checks to pass. Use `isTeamAdmin` alone, which accepts both `ADMIN` and `OWNER`, or combine it with `isTeamOwner` using OR.

Guest email blacklist can be bypassed with capitalization or aliases — Comparing unchanged guest input against lowercased `blacklistedGuestEmails` lets callers invite blocked addresses by changing capitalization. Normalize submitted addresses before comparison and apply the base-email normalization used by `handleNewBooking`.

Guest invitations lose the stored iCalendar identity and update sequence — Without `booking.iCalUID` and `booking.iCalSequence`, `generateIcsString` can produce a separate event or an update recipients ignore as stale. Preserve `booking.iCalUID` and persist an incremented `booking.iCalSequence` for the invitation.

Added-guest notifications ignore event-type email-disable settings — `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends notifications despite event-type email-disable settings. Pass event-type metadata from the handler and apply the host and attendee email-disable predicates used by `sendScheduledEmails` and `sendLocationChangeEmails` before queuing notifications.

Unbounded guest arrays cause excessive database and email attachment work — Each address in `guests` adds a database attendee and an email whose ICS includes the attendee list, allowing unbounded fanout and quadratic attachment work per request. Add a server-side size limit to `guests` before insertion and notification generation.

Guest insertion permits duplicate attendee emails, including concurrent requests — `uniqueGuests` checks only existing attendees, so repeated input addresses or concurrent requests can make `createMany` insert duplicates and trigger duplicate notifications. Deduplicate submitted emails and enforce atomic per-booking email uniqueness at the write boundary.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-78`

Existing attendees receive fresh booking confirmations when guests are added — When a request mixes existing and new attendees, passing `guests` makes `sendAddGuestsEmails` send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to existing attendees instead of a guests-added notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` as the second argument so only newly added attendees receive booking confirmations.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Fabricated refresh token overwrites the stored Office 365 refresh token — A successful Office 365 response can omit `refresh_token`, so fabricating it destroys a valid stored token. Leave `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` absent when no replacement is returned, preserving the stored token during merging.

Salesforce token refresh uses an unimported Prisma client — Successful Salesforce refreshes can throw `ReferenceError` in production because `packages/prisma/index.ts` initializes the global `prisma` only outside production. Import `prisma` explicitly from `@calcom/prisma` before updating the credential.

Sync refresh returns a Response where callers expect provider token objects — With synchronization enabled, callers of `refreshOAuthTokens` expecting `res.data.access_token`, `response.data.error`, or `HubspotToken` receive an unparsed `Response`, causing refresh failures or undefined token fields. Normalize the sync result and update consumers to a consistent contract while preserving support for fetch-based callers.

Token refresh persists the parse result instead of credential data — Writing the `parseRefreshTokenResponse` result directly stores a wrapper without top-level tokens, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse` fails even with sharing disabled. Check `success`, handle parsing failures, and assign `.data` to `key` before persisting.

OAuth refresh passes a credential ID instead of the owning user ID — Sync requests can target the wrong user because `refreshOAuthTokens` sends its third argument as `calcomUserId`, but `credentialId` comes from `credential.id`. Pass the owning `credential.userId` instead, using `null` for team-owned credentials so the helper falls back to normal refresh.

Concurrent first deliveries can create duplicate app credentials — Simultaneous deliveries can both reach `prisma.credential.create` and insert duplicate user/app credentials; check the `Credential` model for the missing uniqueness constraint. Serialize lookup and creation per user/app pair, or add a matching unique key and atomic upsert.

Salesforce initialization always refreshes tokens but uses the stale token — Each initialization incurs an OAuth request and database write even for valid tokens, yet the connection still uses the original `credentialKey.access_token`. Refresh only when necessary and initialize the connection with the refreshed token.

Webhook secret comparison leaks timing information — Direct equality against `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` can expose secret information through timing differences on this credential-writing endpoint. Validate that the supplied header is a single string, then compare fixed-length cryptographic digests with `timingSafeEqual`.

Token response schema uses literal keys and strips additional properties — Ordinary token responses miss the documented handling because `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` create literal property names, while `z.object` strips additional fields. Explicitly validate supported expiry fields and preserve additional token properties as required by the contract.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: SMS cleanup deletes retry-exhausted reminders of other methods — Email or WhatsApp reminders with `retryCount > 1` can be deleted regardless of their scheduled date. Move `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside `OR` so both deletion conditions apply only to SMS reminders.

Retry bookkeeping failures abort processing of subsequent SMS reminders — If Prisma remains unavailable after a processing failure, `prisma.workflowReminder.update` can throw from the per-reminder catch and prevent subsequent reminders from being processed. Add separate error handling around the retry update so bookkeeping failures cannot escape that catch.

Deleted reminders can make the SMS error handler throw — An overlapping scheduler invocation can delete an in-flight reminder, causing `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the error handler to throw and interrupt remaining reminders. Use `prisma.workflowReminder.updateMany` with `reminder.id` so an already-deleted row does not cause another failure.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup-code login bypasses password verification when a TOTP code is supplied — A valid `backupCode` plus any nonempty `totpCode` allows authentication without a password or verified TOTP. Ensure the backup-code branch verifies the password rather than letting an unverified `totpCode` suppress that check.

Concurrent backup-code logins can reuse codes or restore consumed codes — Concurrent requests can authenticate with the same code or overwrite each other's `backupCodes` changes, restoring consumed codes. Make consumption atomic by conditioning the update on the original encrypted `user.backupCodes` value and rejecting or retrying conflicts, or serialize verification and consumption in a suitable transaction.

Dismissing backup codes leaves the parent's 2FA status stale — Dismissing `EnableTwoFactorModal` with Escape or an outside click leaves the settings switch and badge showing 2FA as disabled after successful enablement. Refresh the parent's user query immediately after success, or make every dismissal from `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` run the Close button's completion and reset logic.

Backup-code copy test passes without verifying clipboard contents — Users could lose recovery access while this test still passes because `EnableTwoFactorModal` shows the success toast without checking `clipboard.writeText`. Read the clipboard after clicking `backup-codes-copy` and assert that it contains the displayed backup codes.

Backup code download test passes for empty or incorrect file contents — An empty file or incorrect recovery codes still pass because `download.suggestedFilename()` checks only the filename. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes.

Backup-code verification leaks secret-dependent timing — Plaintext comparisons in `backupCodes.indexOf` and its early exit expose secret-dependent timing during authentication. Compare fixed-length buffers or digests with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, handle invalid lengths safely, and scan every entry before deciding whether authentication succeeds.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:60-63`

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Unescaped imported URLs allow HTML injection into posts — Quotes or markup in `url` can inject attributes or elements into imported posts because the prefix check allows them and `raw_html` preserves them. HTML-escape `url` in both the link attribute and text before interpolating it into `I18n.t`.

Unsanitized feed HTML becomes executable content in imported posts — Malicious feed HTML can execute on the forum's origin because `TopicEmbed.import` selects `raw_html` and `Post.cook` bypasses sanitization; `CGI.unescapeHTML` does not remove scripts or event handlers. Sanitize feed content before passing it to `TopicEmbed.import`, including on updates.

**Also found in:**
- `app/models/post.rb:131-133`

Invalid Ruby in embed template prevents comments from rendering — Rails cannot compile `<%- end if %>`, so the existing-topic branch of `EmbedController.best` fails instead of displaying comments. Replace it with `<%- end %>`.

Concurrent imports can fail on duplicate embed URLs — Concurrent imports can both pass `embed.blank?`, then collide on `embed_url`, raising `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and aborting a feed run. Rescue the conflict outside the rolled-back transaction and retrieve the winning `TopicEmbed` and post, or serialize imports per URL.

RSS items without content abort the polling run — Description-only RSS items make `i.content.scrub` raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire polling run with retries disabled. Fall back to `i.description` and explicitly handle items with neither field before calling `scrub`.

Per-article throttling causes repeated full-feed imports — Each distinct missing `@embed_url` triggers a synchronous full-feed import through `Jobs::PollFeed`, multiplying network requests and database work across article visits. Throttle polling with a shared feed-level key and let individual retrievals reuse the result.

Embedded post dates ignore the active locale — Readers on non-English forums still see English-style dates because `post.created_at.strftime` fixes the ordering and month abbreviation. Use `l` with a locale-defined date format.

Missing embed_url example fails at host validation instead — This test still passes if `params.require(:embed_url)` is removed because `ensure_embeddable` rejects the default blank `embeddable_host` first. Configure an allowed host and matching referer, then assert the intended missing-parameter status rather than any unsuccessful response.

Negative prerequisite tests short-circuit because polling is disabled — These tests can miss regressions because `execute` exits on the default false `feed_polling_enabled?` before checking `feed_polling_url` or `embed_by_username`. Enable polling and make every other prerequisite valid so each example isolates its named requirement.
Protocol-relative links and images are rewritten to the article host — Resolve both link and image URLs against the source URI with `URI.join`, or handle double-slash prefixes separately.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Unquoted host settings allow SQL injection during migration — An apostrophe in persisted `h` can break the SQL statement or inject SQL executed with migration privileges. Quote `h` with the database adapter or use a parameterized insert.

Host validation rejects valid top-level domains longer than five letters — The `host` validation rejects valid embedding domains such as `example.technology` and `example.museum`, which the previous hostname comparison supported. Remove the obsolete five-character top-level-domain limit.

Mixed-case URL hostnames are incorrectly rejected — Legitimate mixed-case URLs fail embedding authorization and topic retrieval because `URI.host` preserves case while `lower(host)` normalizes only the stored value. Compare against `host.downcase` and add mixed-case URL and configuration tests.

Empty embed category query result aborts the migration — An unset or stale `embed_category` produces no rows, so indexing the first result raises `NoMethodError` and aborts the migration before the `category_id` fallback. Read the row safely and fall back to the uncategorized category when no match exists.

Migrated embeddable hosts retain schemes and paths that prevent matching — Previously working scheme-prefixed hosts stop authorizing embedding because `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares against `URI(url).host`, while these SQL inserts bypass model normalization. Strip the scheme and path from `h` consistently with the model before storing migrated entries.

Allowed hosts with ports never match request URLs — A saved `host` such as `example.com:8080` passes validation but never matches because `uri.host` excludes the port, causing embedding to be rejected. Either reject port-qualified entries or normalize and match them consistently.

Saving Uncategorized clears the displayed host category — The server replaces a null chooser value with `uncategorized_category_id`, but `Category.findById(null)` clears the displayed category until reload. Resolve the category from the saved `host` object's returned `category_id` instead of `categoryId`.

Host-absence test passes without exercising the expansion prerequisites — The test passes even if `expandable_first_post?` ignores host presence because `embed_truncate` and a topic embed are missing. Replace it with the intended no-host behavior, or enable those prerequisites if host absence should still prevent expansion.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Fixed 10 MB upload limit ignores configured attachment size limits — Attachments permitted by `max_attachment_size_kb` can be rejected, while files exceeding smaller configured limits upload only to fail server-side validation. Apply the relaxed `maxSizeKB` limit only to images and retain `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments.

Duplicate downsize definition breaks width/height calls — Ruby replaces the earlier `downsize` definition, so width/height calls fail at `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize`, and calls with a fifth argument raise an argument-count error. Give the geometry-based method a separate name or make `downsize` explicitly support both argument forms.

Oversized animated avatars use the thumbnail animation setting — Oversized animated avatars are permanently flattened when `allow_animated_avatars` is enabled but `allow_animated_thumbnails` is disabled, before `Upload.create_for` can apply the avatar setting. Pass `SiteSetting.allow_animated_avatars` to `OptimizedImage.downsize` for avatar uploads, matching `Upload.create_for`.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description:
Pagination hides custom group members beyond the first 50 — Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages, or preserve the endpoint's complete-list behavior for custom groups.

**Also found in:**
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-11`

Removing a member leaves their primary group pointing to the removed group — `users.primary_group_id` becomes stale because `group.users.delete` bypasses the cleanup in `Group.destroy_deletions`. Clear the removed user's primary group when it matches this group, within the same transaction.

Adding an existing group member violates the unique membership index — Clicking Add again can raise a database exception because `Group.add` inserts another membership against the unique `(group_id, user_id)` index. Check `group.users.exists?` before adding each user so repeated submissions succeed.

Stale member responses can overwrite the latest group page or refresh — Out-of-order responses let `self.setProperties` replace the latest member page or membership refresh with stale data. Track a request sequence token for each group and apply a response only if it belongs to the latest request.

Automatic-group removal test does not verify membership is preserved — A `remove_member` implementation that deletes membership before returning 422 would still pass because this test checks only `response.status` without establishing membership. Create an automatic group with a real member, attempt removal, and assert both rejection and preserved membership.

Automatic-group addition test does not verify membership stays unchanged — Because `add_members` skips unresolved usernames, using an uncreated `l77t` and checking only `response.status` cannot detect membership changes before rejection. Create a real nonmember, submit that user's username, and assert both the 422 response and continued absence from the group.

Exact multiples of the page limit create an extra empty page — With 50 members and a limit of 50, `totalPages` becomes 2, enabling navigation to an empty page. Use `Math.ceil` instead of `Math.floor` plus one to count only populated pages.

Member pagination can remain on an empty page after membership shrinks — Removing the last member on a page can leave `removeMember` displaying an empty page because `Math.min` uses stale `user_count` and permits `offset` equal to the total. Clamp `offset` to the last nonempty page using the updated total, and refetch when necessary.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Site-dependent fallbacks leak cached translations across sites — Ukrainian users can receive another site's cached fallback because the accelerator cache key omits `SiteSetting.default_locale`; check the accelerator's cache-key construction. Include the site default locale or complete fallback chain in that key.

Locale-specific pluralization breaks incomplete Ukrainian translation hashes — Ukrainian entries such as `too_many_mentions` and `too_many_mentions_newuser` have only `one` and `other`, so counts selecting `few` or `many` raise `I18n::InvalidPluralizationData`. Add the required categories to those translation hashes before enabling `I18n::Backend::Pluralization` globally.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Missing device header bypasses the anonymous device limit — Requests without `X-Grafana-Device-Id` receive an anonymous identity even when all device slots are occupied because `TagDevice` returns nil for an empty header. Enforce device admission for these requests rather than treating a tagging no-op as successful admission.

Environment-only anonymous device limit configuration is ignored — Setting only `GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT` leaves `AnonymousDeviceLimit` at zero because environment overrides apply only to existing INI keys, and `conf/defaults.ini` lacks `device_limit`. Add `device_limit = 0` to its anonymous-auth section so environment-only configuration works.

Rejected devices remain cached and bypass the device limit on retry — A rejected device can authenticate on retry because `tagDeviceUI` populates `localCache` before persistence, letting subsequent `TagDevice` calls skip the store check after `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. Cache only successfully persisted devices, or remove the cached entry before returning the error.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-46`

Non-atomic device admission allows concurrent requests to exceed the limit — Concurrent requests can both pass `CountDevices` and insert distinct devices, exceeding `deviceLimit`. Make counting and admission mutually exclusive across server instances using a database lock and a suitably isolated transaction.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Concurrent cold-cache requests redundantly reload the manifest — Repeated manifest decoding wastes work, and queued writers delay cache readers. Recheck `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring the write lock and return it when non-nil outside development mode so only the first request initializes it.

Request cancellation can abort background legacy writes — Request cancellation can interrupt legacy replication because `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` inherits the HTTP request lifetime, affecting `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, and `DeleteCollection`. Derive each bounded background context from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` to preserve namespace and identity values without inheriting cancellation.

Legacy update recomputes changes against potentially divergent state — Reevaluating `objInfo` against divergent legacy state can produce different PATCH results or fail after `Storage.Update` succeeds. Pass an `updateWrapper` containing `res` to `Legacy.Update` so legacy storage receives the committed authoritative object.

Detached legacy writes reorder mutations and can resurrect deleted objects — Independent goroutines can run `Legacy.Create` after a subsequent `Legacy.Delete`, resurrecting deleted objects, or apply updates in reverse order even for sequential requests. Preserve per-object mutation ordering across legacy operations, or keep those writes synchronous.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:108-113`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:134-140`

Shared mocks let mode-3 tests pass when the wrong backend is called — The shared `mock.Mock` lets `Legacy.Create` satisfy expectations intended for `Storage.Create`, so incorrect backend selection can pass. Use separate mocks throughout the mode-3 tests and configure the unified-storage error case on the storage mock.

Update success test never verifies the asynchronous legacy write — Removing the legacy-update goroutine would still pass because the success test only checks the synchronous result from `dw.Update`. Use a separate legacy mock, wait for its `Update` call with a bounded completion signal, and assert the invocation and arguments.

Successful deletions use object names instead of kind in storage metrics — Passing `name` to `recordStorageDuration` creates a metric series per object and separates successful deletions from failures labeled with `options.Kind`. Pass `options.Kind` instead, matching the error and legacy paths.

Mode 3 metrics attribute operations to the wrong storage backend — Recording `Storage.Create` and `Storage.Update` failures with `recordLegacyDuration`, and legacy `DeleteCollection` observations with `recordStorageDuration`, hides primary-store errors and misattributes secondary failures. Use `recordStorageDuration` for primary errors and `recordLegacyDuration` for background collection deletion.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:165-166`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Concurrent builds for the same key can overwrite indexes with newer writes — When `GetIndex` returns nil during an ongoing build, `Search` and `handleEvent` can create separate indexes, letting a later publication discard newer write events. Serialize cache lookup, building, and publication per key while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

Startup document count can race with index cache writes — After the write-event consumer starts, `s.search.TotalDocs()` can race with cache writes and crash startup with a concurrent map iteration/write error. Protect cache iteration in `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` with `cacheMu.RLock`, or snapshot entries under that lock before counting.

Unconditional PostgreSQL skip disables instrumentation server coverage — Calling `t.Skip` when `dbType` is PostgreSQL prevents Drone from detecting instrumentation server startup failures for targets without an HTTP server. Fix the PostgreSQL test setup or server startup issue instead of bypassing the behavioral check.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Delete menu still requires a ruler object missing from Grafana list rows — Users with delete permission cannot delete rules from the new list because `GrafanaRuleListItem` no longer supplies `rulerRule`. Render and invoke deletion using the existing rule identifier instead of requiring `rulerRule`.

Pause and Resume disappear for Grafana rules without ruler data — Neither Pause nor Resume appears once ruler loading is removed because the menu still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. Update the pause menu item and its rendering guard to accept the Prometheus rule or its UID and paused state.

Silence notifications action never opens the drawer for Prometheus rules — Clicking Silence notifications only updates state because `RuleActionsButtons.V2` renders `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only for a Grafana alerting ruler rule. Update the drawer and its rendering guard to use the Prometheus rule UID supplied through `promRule`.

Export is unavailable for Grafana-managed recording rules — Grafana-managed recording rules lose Export because `AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport` uses `isAlertingRule`, unlike the ruler-based ability. Base export support on `Boolean(rule)` rather than the alerting subtype.

Federated rule groups lose mutation restrictions in the delegated hook — Existing consumers can now receive update/delete abilities for immutable federated groups because `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hard-codes `isFederated` to false. Pass federation state through from `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`, or retain its `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` restriction.

**Also found in:**
- `public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:243-245`

Skipped Grafana rule ability checks can incorrectly grant actions — Users with Grafana create permission can see Duplicate for data-source rules whose own ability denies it because `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` treats `undefined` as eligible. Return neutral abilities for `skipToken` in `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` and its singular wrapper so skipped checks cannot grant actions.

**Also found in:**
- `public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:308-318`

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Client-credentials tokens encode an unknown grant instead of cc — Client-credentials tokens encode `na` because `ClientCredentialsGrantType.process` calls `generateAccessToken()` without the `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` attribute normally set by `createTokenResponse()`. Set that attribute before generating the access token so its encoded context identifies the actual grant.

Incorrect-grant test passes on an unrelated NullPointerException — Catching `RuntimeException` lets the test pass on a `NullPointerException` from uninitialized `sessionFactory`, even if unknown-grant validation is removed. Initialize `sessionFactory` with an empty provider stream and assert `IllegalArgumentException` specifically.

Invalid-width grant shortcuts produce token IDs that cannot be decoded — Custom shortcuts longer than two characters make `encodeTokenId` produce IDs that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects with `IllegalArgumentException`. Validate that `gtf.getShortcut()` returns exactly two characters before registration, including dynamic paths, and document this constraint on the factory interface declaring `getShortcut()`.

**Also found in:**
- `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30-31`

Grant matcher checks the wrong substring and accepts mismatched grants — Tokens with incorrect grants pass event assertions because `substring(3, 5)` reads the wrong segment and equality rejects matches rather than mismatches. Check the prefix length before using `substring(4, 6)`, and return false when it differs from `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Duplicated grantType check allows null rawTokenId — `AccessTokenContext` accepts a null `rawTokenId`, which `encodeTokenId` serializes as the literal suffix `:null` rather than preserving the original value. Change `Objects.requireNonNull` to check `rawTokenId` instead of checking `grantType` again.

Concurrent group-read test can pass without observing reader failures — The `caughtExceptions` assertion can miss failures from an in-flight `groups()` call, and the reader may perform no reads before `deletedAll` is set. Coordinate reader startup and overlap with deletion, retain and join the reader thread, then assert `caughtExceptions` is empty.

MessageFormat syntax breaks validation messages in both React UI bundles — Attribute names and bounds remain uninterpolated, and choice expressions appear literally because `ThemeResource.getLocalizationTexts` returns strings without MessageFormat processing. Keep i18next-compatible `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}` placeholders and avoid ChoiceFormat syntax in `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in both React UI bundles.

Choice-expression removal bypasses translation anchor validation — Translations can bypass anchor restrictions because `value.replaceAll` hides choice branches from validation, while `LinkExpirationFormatterMethod` renders them into emails and the runtime sanitizer allows off-site links. Validate every branch’s contents instead of discarding entire choice expressions.

Malformed HTML fixture masks regressions in forbidden-tag validation — `verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected` can pass even if `POLICY_SOME_HTML` allows `div`, because repairing the malformed closing tag still triggers a validation error. Give `key` a well-formed forbidden element so the test isolates the tag restriction.

Lithuanian OTP setup instructions are in Italian in login and account bundles — Users selecting Lithuanian receive the first OTP setup step in Italian through `loginTotpStep1`. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation and correct `totpStep1` in the account `messages_lt.properties` bundle too.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties:101-101`

Overlapping prefix and suffix scans crash malformed HTML verification — Overlapping scans make `sanitized.substring` throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` for malformed HTML such as `

x

`, aborting verification instead of reporting it. Bound `end` by the unmatched lengths remaining after `start` in both `sanitized` and `value`.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: All-clients manage permission does not grant coarse visibility — Callers with only all-clients `manage` can manage client scopes but cannot list them because `canListClientScopes()` and `canViewClientScopes()` inherit the `view`-only check in `canView()`; client listing also returns 403 without `query-clients`. Include all-clients `manage` in coarse visibility checks while preserving resource-specific checks for individual clients.

All-clients view grants bypass resource-specific denials — Administrators can read explicitly denied clients because `canView(ClientModel)` returns early and `ClientsResource.getClients` skips individual checks when `canView()` accepts all-clients `view`. Keep the admin-role shortcut separate from fine-grained grants, and evaluate client-specific policies before falling back to all-clients permissions, including during list filtering.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78-82`
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:77-82`

Removal-denial test can pass when only the scope lookup is forbidden — The test stays green even if removal authorization breaks because `getDefaultClientScopes()` can throw the accepted `ForbiddenException` before `removeDefaultClientScope()` runs. Fetch the scope ID through the privileged `realm.admin()` client before the try block, then assert `ForbiddenException` only around the restricted client's `removeDefaultClientScope()` call.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Legacy login theme leaves passkey-only users at a password-only dead end — Accepting passkey-only users in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` blocks authentication with the legacy `keycloak` theme because `base/login/login-password.ftl` lacks passkey controls. Add the passkeys import and `conditionalUIData` invocation to that template so these users can sign in.

Organization-aware eligibility leaves stale login cache membership on update — When an organization is disabled, `getById` makes `original` fail `getLoginPredicate()`, so changing `hideOnLogin` or `linkOnly` can preserve stale cache membership that reappears when the organization is enabled. Reload `original` through `idpDelegate.getById` before comparing eligibility.

Login cache refresh can resurrect stale organization results — Concurrent invalidation can make `query` stale before this branch copies it into an entry with a newer revision, restoring outdated organization results. Preserve `query` only if its revision remains valid; otherwise, cache only the freshly loaded search.

Login cache test never asserts returned provider identities — Discarding every `getForLogin` result lets this test pass even if the method populates the cache but returns `Stream.empty()`. Collect and assert provider identities on the initial lookup, a repeated cache hit, and after invalidation.

Cleanup targets a literal alias and leaves identity provider fixtures behind — Deleting the literal `alias` leaves the `idp-alias-*` fixtures behind, risking duplicate-alias failures in other tests. Register cleanup with `idpRep.getAlias()` here and for the additional provider created later in this test.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Feature-enabled dashboard tables discard fetched results — Organizations with `use-table-widget-visualization` see empty dashboard tables even when queries return data. Pass the fetched rows, metadata, and corresponding columns to `TableWidgetVisualization` instead of empty placeholders.

Attribute query cache is shared across organizations — Switching organizations with matching query options reuses the previous organization's cached attributes from `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys`. Include `organization.slug` in `queryKey` and its memo dependencies to isolate the caches.

Zero-valued age and timestamp bypass mutual-exclusion validation — Requests containing both `age=0` and `timestamp=0` pass validation despite the mutual-exclusion requirement. In `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`, check key presence in `self.initial_data` rather than truthiness.

Falsy custom cell results incorrectly trigger fallback rendering — Valid `renderTableBodyCell` results such as `null`, `''`, and `0` trigger fallback rendering, potentially exposing values callers intended to hide. Check `cell !== undefined` here and use the same explicit check in the corresponding header renderer.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Memory backpressure repeats cluster-wide Redis queries for every worker — Synchronous Redis queries add latency to every `submit` because `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info` ignores `assigned_shards` and queries the entire configured cluster for each buffer. Collect memory information from a single buffer instead of repeating the cluster query for every worker.

Patched sleep leaves the flusher output assertion scheduling-dependent — The output assertion can race with worker shutdown because this test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op and `step.join()` sets `stopped` before waiting. Use an actual synchronization primitive to wait for the expected message before calling `step.join()`.

Process type check skips killing hung SpawnProcess workers — A hung worker can survive alongside its replacement and produce duplicates because `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` excludes the `SpawnProcess` objects created by `self.mp_context.Process`. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` or explicitly exclude `threading.Thread` before calling `process.kill()`.

Shutdown deadline skips worker cleanup and leaves spawned processes alive — Workers blocked in Redis or Kafka can remain alive after `join` returns because the deadline-triggered `break` skips their cleanup. Separate deadline-limited waiting from a cleanup pass that terminates every remaining live subprocess, including `SpawnProcess` workers.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: Inbound assignment suppresses sync to other issues in the same integration — An inbound assignment from one Jira issue leaves another linked issue’s assignee stale even when outbound sync is enabled because `sync_source.integration_id` matches both. Carry the originating external issue identity and suppress updates only to that issue.

Empty-array test passes a dictionary instead of a list — `test_from_dict_empty_array` would still pass if `AssignmentSource.from_dict` mishandled empty lists, leaving that case untested. Pass `[]` instead of `{}` and retain the dictionary case in a separately named test if desired.
AssignmentSource reuses an import-time queued timestamp — Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own creation time.

Predictable OAuth state allows attacker-controlled GitHub account linking — An attacker can link their GitHub account to a victim’s pending setup because `pipeline.signature` is predictable, not session-specific. Generate a cryptographically random OAuth state for each authorization attempt, store it in pipeline state, and validate the callback against that value.

Missing sender metadata crashes GitHub reinstallation — Reinstallation can raise `KeyError` because `build_integration` only populates `integration.metadata["sender"]` when setup state includes sender metadata. Check for the missing key and return a controlled error, or obtain authoritative installer information before comparing logins.

Short error messages lose their translation extraction sites — Translation extraction cannot resolve `error_short` in `_(error_short)`, leaving user-facing errors untranslated in newly generated catalogs. Wrap each short-message literal in `_()` at its definition or call site, including the default and both callers.

OAuth token request failures bypass installation error handling — A transport or HTTP failure in `safe_urlopen` escapes installation error handling and produces a server error instead of the failure response. Move the token request inside the `try` block and catch the expected outbound-request exceptions.

Missing-installation test passes on OAuth state rejection — This test can pass without reaching the installation lookup because `OAuthLoginView` returns the asserted error when `state` is invalid. Use the actual pipeline state and assert the installation-not-found response so broken missing-installation handling fails the test.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: Metric alert handler cannot be instantiated because it remains abstract — Accessing `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` for `metric_alert_fire` because `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` leaves `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` abstract. Implement these members before registration, or retain the concrete no-op `DetectorHandler` until they are available.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Collective bookings drop team calendars when no default calendar exists — For collective events, a null `evt.destinationCalendar` makes the optional push discard every team destination, leaving hosts without calendar events. Initialize it to an empty array before pushing `teamDestinationCalendars`.

Legacy destination events omit the external calendar ID — Legacy destinations lose the external calendar needed for later updates and deletes because `EventManager.create` reads only `result.externalId`. Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument to `createEvent`, matching the credential-specific branch.

Calendar references lose `externalId` and `credentialId` after location edits — After a location edit, `CalendarManager.updateEvent` results lack `externalId` and `credentialId`, so every updated calendar reference is persisted without both fields. Return those fields from `updateEvent` or copy them from the booking reference being updated.

Hangout patch uses an undefined calendarId after the primary-calendar fallback — When insertion falls back to `primary`, the Hangout patch still uses bare `selectedCalendar`, sending an undefined `calendarId`. Apply the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` fallback to the patch.

Rescheduling a collective booking leaves stale host calendar events — The `newBookingId` branch still uses `.find` and deletes only the first old event, leaving stale events on other hosts' calendars after a collective reschedule. Iterate over every old calendar reference and delete each with its own credential and external calendar ID.

Recurring cancellations duplicate deletions and skip additional hosts — The recurring branch repeats deletions across organizer credentials while selecting only each booking's first reference, so additional hosts' events can remain. Scope deletion to `calendarCredential` and the updated-booking reference matching the outer `reference`.

Credential-less destinations incorrectly create events in primary — A destination without `credentialId` cannot match the numeric lookup, so `createAllCalendarEvents` inserts into `"primary"` instead of the selected calendar. Preserve that path by falling back to the `externalId` of the destination whose `credentialId` is null or undefined.

Prisma errors expose internal database details to clients — `PrismaClientKnownRequestError.message` can expose queries, schema details, and database diagnostics to clients when user loading fails. Log the detailed error server-side and return a generic `HttpError` message, propagating only messages explicitly safe for clients.
Missing destination calendar throws before Cal Video fallback — Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

Event creation drops the destination calendar for secondary hosts — Secondary-host calls can combine the organizer's calendar ID with the secondary host's credentials because the new `externalId` argument never reaches adapters that select `destinationCalendar[0]`, causing failed or missing events.
