Pass the current destination through the adapter contract or make each adapter select the destination matching `credential.id`.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72-76`

Non-calendar references lose their credential ID — Non-calendar and video references now persist `credentialId: undefined`, losing the credential needed for later credential-specific operations. Preserve `result.credentialId` in the non-calendar branch while keeping calendar-specific `externalCalendarId` handling.

Update and delete fallbacks look up a destination by a falsy ID — When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, searching for a destination with that same value finds no normal calendar, so update and delete pass an undefined `calendarId`. Use the appropriate destination calendar's `externalId` here and in the delete path.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:314-320`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:314-317`

Paid collective bookings only create the organizer's calendar event — A one-element destination array before `EventManager.create` leaves only the organizer with a calendar event after payment for a collective booking. Load all collective hosts' destination calendars in both payment-success paths before creating events and references.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:175-179`

Organizations created without team billing cannot be published — With team billing disabled, omitting both `slug` and `requestedSlug` leaves new organizations unable to pass the publish check in `publish.handler.ts`. Restore the negated condition for `slug` and keep `requestedSlug` when billing is enabled.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Guest insertion bypasses seat capacity and bookingSeat requirements — This unconditional attendee insertion also applies when `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot` is set, bypassing the seat-capacity check and creating attendees without the required `bookingSeat` relation even though seated events disable guests. Reject seated bookings here or delegate to the seated-booking flow that checks capacity and creates the seat reference.

Add Guests remains available for cancelled, rejected, and past bookings — After authorization, the handler never rejects CANCELLED, REJECTED, or already-past bookings before mutating them, allowing guests to be added and CONFIRMED invitations to be sent for inactive events; the new action is also included in the actions rendered for past confirmed bookings. Validate booking status and timing before the write and hide the action for ineligible bookings.
EventManager uses attendee credentials instead of the organizer's — Build the manager from the organizer/`booking.user` credentials already associated with the booking.

Calendar update failures are discarded when adding guests — Calendar update failures are discarded: `updateEvent` catches provider rejections and returns `success: false`, while `updateCalendarAttendees` returns no results, so this handler sends emails and returns success with a stale calendar after the database insert. Return the update results from EventManager and inspect them here, with an explicit recovery path for failed updates.

sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type host and attendee email settings — `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally sends host and attendee messages and has no event-type metadata parameter, so `disableStandardEmails.all.host` and `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee` are ignored even though the handler has that metadata available. Thread the metadata into this function and apply the same host/attendee guards used by the neighboring email senders.

Unbounded guest additions allow excessive database and email work — The guests array has no size bound, but every accepted address drives attendee insertion and translation work and the resulting full attendee list drives calendar updates and concurrent email fanout. An authorized attendee can therefore force unbounded database and email work in one request or across repeated additions; enforce reasonable per-request and per-booking guest caps before inserting or sending.

The `CalendarEvent` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` never populates `team`, so its… — Load the event type's team members and populate `evt.team` before sending so team bookings notify the intended hosts.

Hard-coded tooltip text bypasses localization — The tooltip content is hard-coded as English `"Remove email"`, bypassing the translation mechanism used by the surrounding UI (and `t` is already available in this component). Users of other locales will still see this tooltip in English; pass a translated string instead.

Calendar update failures leave guest additions partially committed — The attendee rows are committed before this awaited external calendar update, and a rejection here has no rollback or compensation. The client receives an error and emails are skipped even though the guests remain persisted; a retry then finds no new unique guests and cannot complete the missed work.

Unordered attendees can put a blank guest name in the organizer subject — This assumes `attendees[0]` is the booking's named primary attendee, but the handler builds this array from a Prisma `include` with no `orderBy`, so its order is not guaranteed. A newly added guest can be first, and those guests are created with an empty name, producing a blank (or otherwise arbitrary) attendee name in the organizer's subject.

Case-sensitive attendee matching allows duplicate guest attendees — Existing-attendee deduplication uses case-sensitive `guest === attendee.email`. A case variant of an already registered attendee email passes this filter and can create a second attendee record for the same mailbox, causing duplicate calendar/email recipients.

Team admin permission check incorrectly requires ownership — `isTeamAdmin` already accepts both ADMIN and OWNER, but ANDing it with `isTeamOwner` reduces this permission to owners only, so non-attendee team admins receive FORBIDDEN despite the bookings UI treating them as authorized. Use `isTeamAdmin` alone or OR the two role checks.

Mixed-case guest emails bypass the blacklist — Blacklist values are normalized to lowercase, but each incoming `guest` is compared without the same normalization. Since the email validator preserves case, an address such as `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a configured `blocked@example.com` blacklist entry and is added.

Concurrent guest additions can create duplicate attendees — The existing-attendee check and insertion are a non-atomic check-then-act sequence. Two concurrent requests for the same new guest can both read the booking before either update commits and then both insert that guest.

Duplicate guest emails can create duplicate attendees and invitations — `uniqueGuests` filters existing attendees but never deduplicates the request itself, so a direct request containing the same new address twice inserts duplicate Attendee rows and sends duplicate invitations; the Attendee model has no booking/email unique constraint to stop this. Deduplicate normalized addresses before `createMany` and enforce booking/email uniqueness atomically to also close concurrent-request duplicates.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:3-6`

Mailer receives raw guests and misclassifies existing attendees — The mailer receives raw `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee included in a mixed request is misclassified as newly added and receives `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the add-guests notification despite not being inserted. Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Metadata lookup uses app slugs instead of directory names — `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by `dirName` (`googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`), but this indexes it with the database `slug` (`google-calendar`, `zoom`), so valid sync requests for those apps return 404 before credentials are written. Select `dirName` in the Prisma query and use it for the metadata lookup, or find the metadata entry by `meta.slug`.
Two concurrent webhook requests can both observe no credential and both execute `create`… — Make the check-and-create idempotent with serialization or an appropriate uniqueness/upsert strategy.
The documented sync payload of an access token plus expiry cannot satisfy Lark's… — Define a common parsed token result and adapt those callers while preserving their existing credential fields.
Zoom passes its directory name `zoomvideo` as `appSlug`, while its app and stored credentials use… — Pass `"zoom"` instead.

The refreshed Salesforce token is written to Prisma, but the new `jsforce.Connection` below still… — Build the connection from `accessTokenParsed.data`, or update `credentialKey` before constructing it.

Unconditional token refresh adds a Salesforce request and DB write per client — Every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction now performs a blocking Salesforce token request and a database update before any operation, even when the saved access token is still valid. This adds an external round trip and write to every calendar operation and can consume Salesforce API limits; only refresh when expired or let jsforce refresh on demand.

Updating credentials preserves the stale invalid flag — Updating only `key` preserves an existing credential's automatically-set `invalid` flag, so a successful webhook delivering repaired credentials still leaves that credential excluded by paths such as `getCalendarsEvents`. Set `invalid: false` when the replacement keys are successfully stored.

Provider-fallback team refreshes incorrectly use the sync response schema — The parser chooses the sync schema from global configuration even when `refreshOAuthTokens` took its provider fallback for a team credential (`userId === null`). With sync configured, provider-native team responses therefore bypass app-specific validation and transforms such as Office365's `expires_in` conversion, breaking refreshes; select the schema using the refresh path actually taken or pass an explicit sync-response flag.

Webhook secret comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks — The webhook secret is authenticated with a direct string `!==` comparison. String comparison can exit at the first differing character, exposing match-dependent timing on a secret that authorizes creation and replacement of stored app credentials.

Computed Zod keys strip token fields during credential sharing — These computed properties do not declare a Zod index signature: `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` evaluate to ordinary object keys (both normally `[object Object]`, with the second overwriting the first). Consequently, in credential-sharing mode the default `z.object` behavior strips the actual numeric expiry (`expiry_date`/`expires_in`) and other token fields instead of preserving them.

Missing refresh tokens are replaced with a hardcoded placeholder — Do not substitute the literal string `"refresh_token"` when a refresh response omits this credential. The sync-endpoint path explicitly permits access-token-only responses, and callers subsequently persist this parsed data; for example, Office365 merges it over the existing credentials, replacing a valid refresh token with the placeholder.

The sharing branch always returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, while the fallback returns each… — That contract is incompatible with several changed callers: Google expects a gaxios response with `.data` and then dereferences `token.access_token`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM expect an Axios response with `.data`; HubSpot treats the result directly as a token object. With syncing enabled, these paths either throw during refresh or persist an empty/invalid token object.

Refreshed Google credentials are persisted as a safe-parse wrapper — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the safe-parse result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credentials. Persisting `key` directly therefore replaces Google's credential JSON with that wrapper.

OAuth refresh passes the credential ID instead of the user ID — The third argument is the helper's `userId`, but this call passes `credentialId` (assigned from `credential.id` at line 53). The sync request consequently sends the credential row ID as `calcomUserId`.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Retry cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders before their scheduled date — Future-dated EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders can be permanently removed by the SMS cron. Apply `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to both `OR` branches so the `retryCount > 1` cleanup cannot match other delivery methods.

SMS reminders without recipients never increment retryCount — When `smsReminderNumber = null`, an `SMS_ATTENDEE` reminder skips the `message && sendTo` branch, leaving `retryCount` at 0 and causing reprocessing until its scheduled date. Increment `retryCount` on the no-recipient path so undeliverable reminders can be retired.

Concurrent SMS failures can undercount retries and exceed the retry limit — Concurrent scheduler runs can record several failed attempts as one, letting delivery attempts continue beyond the retry limit. Replace `reminder.retryCount + 1` with an atomic database increment in both failure paths instead of using the stale `findMany` snapshot.

Retry-count update failures can abort SMS reminder processing — A failure from `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the error handler escapes and skips the remaining `unscheduledReminders`, whether the row was removed by cleanup or the update otherwise failed. Catch persistence errors separately and tolerate missing rows so the original scheduling error cannot abort the run.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup-code login bypasses `verifyPassword` and both authentication factors — A valid `backupCode` plus any non-empty `totpCode` authenticates without the CAL account password or authenticator. Require `verifyPassword` before accepting either second factor, regardless of additional credential fields.

Escape or outside dismissal leaves stale 2FA state after enablement — Because `onEnable()` no longer runs here, `viewer.me.invalidate()` is reached only by the custom Close button; Escape or outside dismissal leaves 2FA shown as disabled after server enablement. Invalidate on successful enablement and separate that from closing, or route every exit through completion.

Clipboard failures falsely trigger the recovery-code success toast — A rejected `writeText` promise, such as denied clipboard permission, still shows the success toast and falsely tells users their recovery codes were copied. Await the write, show success only when it resolves, and show an error toast when it rejects.

Backup code field has no effective submission validation — Because the form uses `noValidate` and `register("backupCode")` has no rules, an empty submission bypasses native validation and returns `SecondFactorRequired` without a visible error. Add React Hook Form rules to the registration or validate explicitly in lost-access mode before calling `signIn`.

Backup-code mode persists after the modal is canceled or dismissed — Canceling or dismissing while using a backup code leaves `twoFactorLostAccess` set, so the next opening shows the backup-code form instead of the default TOTP form. Reset `twoFactorLostAccess` on every close path, not only after a successful disable.

Backup-code recovery message directs logged-out users to settings — Before credentials are authorized, the user has no session and cannot reach settings, making the `missing_backup_codes` recovery instruction unusable; no standalone regeneration flow is added. Provide logged-out guidance or add that flow.

Backup-code disable path logs a misleading login error — The `console.error` message refers to “backup code login” although this handler disables 2FA, sending operators debugging a missing encryption key toward the wrong flow. Describe the backup-code disable operation instead.

Empty backup codes incorrectly fall through to TOTP validation — Treating `backupCode` by truthiness sends an empty submission to TOTP validation; from the backup-code view, cleared `totpCode` then yields `SecondFactorRequired` with no visible error. Detect backup-code submissions explicitly and reject missing or empty strings with backup-code-specific validation.

This check would still pass if copying backup codes were broken — Waiting only for `toast-success` does not prove anything was copied: the component does not await `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)`, so rejected or no-op writes and incorrect contents still satisfy the test. Read the clipboard and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes.

This verifies only that some download occurs with the hard-coded filename — Checking only `suggestedFilename()` allows empty, malformed, or incorrect backup-code downloads to pass. Read the downloaded file and compare its complete contents with the formatted codes displayed in the dialog.

Close sequence does not verify the backup-code dialog closes — The checked settings switch can remain visible to Playwright beneath an open modal, so this sequence can pass without the backup-code dialog closing. After clicking close, assert that the dialog or its backup-code content is hidden.

Non-atomic `backupCodes` updates permit reuse and restore consumed codes — Checking and rewriting the decrypted `backupCodes` list separately lets concurrent requests reuse one code; with different codes, the last write can restore the other as unused. Consume the code and authorize login only in an atomic, retrying serializable or row-locked transaction.

Backup code verification uses timing-sensitive string equality — Because `indexOf` uses ordinary string equality and can stop at the first mismatch, verification time may reveal how much of a guessed authentication secret matches. Compare the normalized fixed-length code with every stored code using equal-length buffers and `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, while retaining rate limiting.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58-64`

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: Flat Prisma.Sql expectations fail against nested SQL fragments — `toEqual` compares the flat expectation's `strings` and `values` with the service's nested fragments, so equivalent rendered SQL still fails. Build the expectation with matching `Prisma.Sql` nesting or compare rendered SQL and parameters, including the org-scope and combined `eventType`/`memberUser` filter assertions.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Nil RSS item content aborts the entire feed polling pass — RSS items that provide only `description` leave `i.content` nil, so `.scrub` raises and aborts the whole feed pass, with `retry: false` preventing Sidekiq retries. Use `i.content || i.description` and skip items with no usable content.
The `start_with?('/')` guard leaves ordinary relative links and images such as `images/a.png`… — Resolve relative references with `URI.join(url, value)` for both links and images.

Rolled-back spam posts still reach embed creation — `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even after `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` rolls back its save, and that unsaved object is still `present?`; `TopicEmbed.create!` then receives nil `topic_id`/`post_id` and raises instead of skipping the blocked item. Require `post.persisted?` and no creator errors before creating the embed.

Remote embed fetch permits SSRF via unchecked redirects — `import_remote` opens the user-supplied `embed_url` after `TopicRetriever` checks only the initial hostname, while open-uri follows redirects without reapplying that check. An allowed-host URL that redirects to loopback or private-network services can therefore trigger internal requests; validate scheme, port, resolved addresses, and every redirect target, or disable redirects.

Unbounded embed downloads can exhaust Sidekiq worker memory — `open(url).read` buffers the entire response with no byte limit in a job reachable through attacker-selected embed URLs. A large response on the allowed host can exhaust a Sidekiq worker's memory; stream with a strict maximum size and explicit open/read timeouts.

Cache-miss embeds can flood Sidekiq before validation and throttling — Unknown embeds enqueue a Sidekiq job before `TopicRetriever` performs host validation or its Redis throttle, so repeated cache-miss requests using unique query-string variants can grow the queue even when every job is later rejected or throttled. Deduplicate, rate-limit, and validate `embed_url` before enqueueing.
Non-null default column addition rewrites and locks the posts table — Add it nullable without a default, backfill in batches, then add the default and constraint separately.

Embed stylesheet is not precompiled for production — Production precompilation does not generate `embed.css` because it is absent from `config.assets.precompile` in `config/application.rb:61`, while production disables runtime compilation, so this layout cannot load its stylesheet. Add `embed.css` to the precompile list.
Port filtering strips meaningful non-default ports from rewritten URLs — Omit the port only when it is the default for `uri.scheme`.

Disqus imports lose the original thread publication date — The new import call drops the previous `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` option, and `TopicEmbed.import` never forwards a timestamp to `PostCreator`, so every imported Disqus thread is dated at import time rather than its original publication date. Thread `created_at` through `import_remote` and `import` into `PostCreator`.

Post dates ignore locale-specific date formatting — The user-visible post date is hard-coded with `strftime("%e %b %Y")`, giving every locale the same day-month-year ordering and English month abbreviations. Unlike the surrounding embed labels, this bypasses I18n; use `I18n.l` with a localized date format instead.

Concurrent imports of the same previously unseen URL can both pass the `embed.blank?` check and… — The unique `embed_url` index then makes one transaction fail with `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Because that race is not handled, a PollFeed run can abort before processing its remaining items, or a RetrieveTopic job can fail, instead of returning the embed created by the other caller.

Non-atomic throttle setup can leave a key without an expiry — The throttle key is created with SETNX and given its TTL by a separate EXPIRE command. If the process dies or the second command fails after SETNX succeeds, `retrieved:<url>` has no expiry; subsequent throttled calls will always consider it recently retrieved, permanently preventing retrieval of that URL.

Scheme-relative URLs are incorrectly rewritten to the article host — Scheme-relative (`//host/path`) links and image sources are rewritten to the article's host. `start_with?('/')` is true for these values and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` removes both slashes, so `//cdn.example/a.png` becomes `https://blog.example/cdn.example/a.png` rather than `https://cdn.example/a.png`.

Embed controller spec still expects direct TopicRetriever calls — Retrieval now happens through `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, but `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` still expects the controller to call `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` directly. Those calls never occur in this action, leaving the example's mock expectations unsatisfied.

Full referer URL is an invalid postMessage target origin — `request.referer` is normally a full URL such as `http://eviltrout.com/2013/...`, but `postMessage`'s second argument must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not a URL with a path. Sending this resize message raises a `SyntaxError`, so the `discourse-resize` listener in `embed.js` never receives the height and the iframe is not resized.

Raw HTML posts bypass sanitization and enable stored XSS — Returning `raw` for `raw_html` bypasses `PrettyText`'s sanitizer; `PollFeed` HTML-unescapes remote feed content and `embed/best` renders `post.cooked` with `raw`, so a malicious feed or article can persist scripts or event handlers that execute for Discourse readers. Sanitize imported HTML and its URL attributes with an allowlist before using `raw_html`, or keep it in the normal cooking pipeline.

Origin substring check lets untrusted sites resize the iframe — This substring test does not authenticate the sender's origin. For example, with `discourseUrl = "https://community.example.com/"`, a message from the distinct origin `https://community.example.co` passes because that origin is a prefix of the configured URL, allowing that sender to issue `discourse-resize` messages and manipulate the iframe height.

feed_polling_enabled? spec leaves other prerequisites unset — The enabled-setting test leaves `feed_polling_url` and `embed_by_username` blank, so `poll_feed` remains skipped even if the `feed_polling_enabled?` check is removed. Stub the other two prerequisites to valid values so the disabled flag is the only condition preventing polling.

**Also found in:**
- `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18-22`
- `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:24-28`

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Failed plural hydration deletes ids and leaves undefined entries — If an id has no matching side-loaded collection, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined, but this still stores an array of undefined entries and deletes the original `*_ids`; `hydrated || []` cannot help because `map` always returns an array. Preserve the original ids unless hydration resolves them, matching the singular branch's behavior.
Blank categoryId overwrites the saved category with undefined — Resolve the category from `host.get('category_id')` after the save response instead.

expandable_first_post? ignores missing embeddable hosts — An embedded topic with `embed_truncate` enabled now returns true even after the last allowed host is deleted, whereas the previous host-presence guard returned false. Restore an `EmbeddableHost` presence check so disabling embedding also disables the full-post expansion control.

Feed imports lose embed_category when no EmbeddableHost matches — Feed polling calls `TopicEmbed.import` directly, so a feed entry without a matching `EmbeddableHost` now passes a nil category and is filed under Uncategorized instead of the previously configured `embed_category`. Provide an explicit feed-category fallback or migration rather than relying exclusively on a matching host record.

Missing-host spec also lacks a referer, so it does not isolate the host guard — The 'missing host' example also supplies no referer. Since the new guard checks `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`, the nil referer independently produces a non-success response; the test would still pass if a valid referer were incorrectly accepted when no host records exist.

Missing embed_category site setting crashes the migration — `embed_category` can have no row in `site_settings` when it has never been overridden. The query then returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `['id']` raises, aborting the migration before the intended `category_id == 0` fallback can run.

Legacy hosts are inserted without stripping URL schemes and paths — Legacy settings accepted values such as `https://example.com/1234`, but this inserts them verbatim while `record_for_host` later queries only `example.com`, disabling those existing embeds after upgrade. Normalize each legacy value with the same scheme/path trimming as the model before inserting it.

Saving without a host crashes in normalization before validation — Saving a record with an omitted `host` parameter calls `sub!` on `nil`, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard the normalization when `host` is blank, or convert it to a string, before running validation.

The model accepts and preserves an optional port such as `example.com:3000`, but `uri.host`… — The lookup therefore searches for `example.com`, so the port-specific record does not match its own referer. Compare a consistently normalized host-and-port authority, or reject ports when writing.

Mixed-case URLs can fail the embeddable host lookup — `lower(host)` normalizes only the database column; the bind value from `uri.host` retains its input case. Uppercase or mixed-case URLs can therefore fail the exact comparison despite hostnames being case-insensitive and the validator accepting them.

Update and destroy crash when the embeddable host no longer exists — Both actions immediately dereference the nullable `where(...).first` result. A stale update or delete after another admin removes the host causes `save_host(nil)` to fail at `host.host=` or destroy to fail at `host.destroy`, producing an unhandled 500.

Embeddable hosts lack case-insensitive uniqueness enforcement — The new host-to-category mapping has no uniqueness enforcement: the model validates only format and the table has no unique index. Concurrent admin creates can therefore both commit the same normalized host, potentially with different categories, after which `record_for_host(...).first` silently chooses one mapping for access and topic categorization.

**Also found in:**
- `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2-3`

Blank-host example no longer isolates blank-host behavior — The setup enabling `embed_truncate` and stubbing `has_topic_embed?` was moved into the nested context, so this example returns false because truncation is false by default and the topic has no embed. It passes whether blank-host handling is correct or broken.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Every resize retry runs a redundant full ImageOptim pass — Skip optimization during intermediate downsizing passes and run it only once after the final image is produced.

Extensionless upload tempfiles flatten oversized animated GIFs — Direct multipart GIFs use Rack's extensionless `RackMultipart` tempfile, so `OptimizedImage.optimize` does not match `/\.GIF$/i` and selects `downsize_instructions`, whose `#{from}[0]` keeps only the first frame; every oversized animated GIF uploaded through the normal browser path is flattened even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled. Choose the animated converter from the original filename or detected image format rather than the tempfile path.

Unescaped tempfile paths enable shell injection during GIF downsizing — For large API-downloaded GIFs, this new call sends a tempfile path containing the unvalidated `type` parameter to `convert_with`, which joins it unquoted into a backtick command; an API user can include shell metacharacters in `type` to execute commands, whereas GIFs previously bypassed the similar orientation command. Shell-escape both paths with `Shellwords.escape` and avoid using raw `type` as a tempfile prefix.

Duplicate downsize definition breaks width/height callers — This second `downsize` definition replaces the width/height version above it; Ruby does not overload methods by arity. Existing callers such as `ResizeEmoji` still invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which now raises `ArgumentError` because the surviving method accepts only `(from, to, dimensions, opts = {})`.

This overload forwards arbitrary geometry strings unchanged, but the new controller caller passes… — For GIFs taking the animated branch, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to gifsicle's `--resize-fit`, which requires explicit pixel dimensions and does not accept percentage geometry. The resize therefore fails (and the controller retries the same invalid conversion), leaving large animated GIFs oversized.

**Also found in:**
- `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67-67`

Upload validation ignores per-type file size site settings — The client now validates every image and attachment against a hard-coded 10 MB instead of the corresponding `max_<type>_size_kb` site setting. It therefore rejects files that the configured server limit permits, or accepts files that `Upload.create_for` will reject, and the error message reports this incorrect limit.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Omitting offset in members raises NoMethodError — Requests that omit `offset` now call `to_i` on `nil`, raising `NoMethodError` instead of returning the first page as the endpoint previously did. Restore the zero fallback with `(params[:offset] || 0).to_i`.

Adding an existing group member violates the unique membership index — Adding a username that is already in the group blindly pushes another join row, violating the unique `group_users(group_id,user_id)` index and returning a 500; the unchanged selector makes clicking Add twice a direct trigger. Make insertion idempotent by ignoring duplicate input and existing memberships before calling `group.add`.

Removing a group member leaves the cached user count stale — Deleting through `group.users` removes the join row without running `GroupUser`’s destroy callbacks, so its `counter_cache: "user_count"` is not decremented and serialized group counts remain stale after a refresh. Destroy the join record through `Group#remove` or explicitly reset the group’s `group_users` counter after deletion.

Bulk member addition runs an unbounded series of user lookups — Bulk-adding N members performs N separate `User.find_by_username` queries in series, with no bound on the comma-separated input, replacing the previous bulk username lookup. Split the names once, fetch all matching users with a single `User.where(username: names)` query, and iterate over that result.

Remove-member links are shown for automatic groups — The item view's context is each `member`, and `GroupUserSerializer` does not expose `automatic`, so this `unless` renders removal links even for automatic groups. Bind the condition to the parent group controller's `automatic` flag so the action is hidden when membership changes are forbidden.

Unbounded members limit can load and serialize an entire large group — The action passes an arbitrary `params[:limit]` directly to ActiveRecord and serializes the result, allowing one request to load an entire large visible group's membership; the rewrite newly exposes this behavior for non-automatic groups too. Clamp `limit` to a reasonable maximum before querying.

Automatic-group removal spec uses PUT instead of DELETE — The automatic-removal test uses `xhr :put`, but `remove_member` is exposed as `DELETE members`; PUT is the `add_members` route. It therefore does not exercise the HTTP operation used to remove members and can pass despite a regression in DELETE removal handling.

totalPages adds an extra page when user_count is a multiple of limit — `totalPages` is one too high whenever `user_count` is a positive exact multiple of `limit`. For example, 100 users with a limit of 50 produces 3 pages instead of 2; Next from page 2 then sets `offset` to 100 and displays an empty third page.

Every `findMembers` response unconditionally replaces the member list and pagination state, while… — Sequence the requests and ignore obsolete responses, or prevent another page load until the current one completes.

The offset is clamped using the cached `user_count` before the request, so a reload after removal… — With 51 users on the page at offset 50, removing its sole member leaves 50 users, but this still requests offset 50; the server returns `total: 50` with no members and the model stores that out-of-range offset, leaving an empty page. Reconcile the offset with the refreshed total (and refetch a valid page when necessary) instead of relying only on the stale count.

**Also found in:**
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:45-48`

Default limit truncates public non-automatic group member lists — The new 50-member default also truncates the public group-members page, whose route calls `findMembers` only once and whose template has no pagination controls; groups that previously displayed more than 50 non-automatic members now hide the rest. Add pagination or continued loading to the public members route, or preserve the prior retrieval behavior for that caller.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Fallback cache key omits the tenant-dependent default locale — A fallback lookup can return another tenant's translation, or a stale one after the default locale changes, because the accelerator cache key ignores `SiteSetting.default_locale`. Add the fallback chain or default locale to the key in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`, or invalidate these entries when it changes.

Fallback chains stay unloaded outside ApplicationController — Missing keys can remain untranslated in `PostAlerter` and `Jobs::Base`, since only `ApplicationController#set_locale` calls `ensure_loaded!` to load `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`. Load the fallback chain in the shared translation path, or update every consumer that sets or temporarily changes `I18n.locale`.

**Also found in:**
- `app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159-159`

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Untagged anonymous requests bypass the configured device limit — A missing `X-Grafana-Device-Id` makes `TagDevice` return `nil` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, so over-limit clients still receive an anonymous identity. Reject these requests or enforce the limit with a server-generated device identity.

Cached failed device tags let over-limit devices authenticate on retries — Over-limit devices can authenticate on retries because `tagDeviceUI` caches the key before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` and leaves it after store rejection; for 29 minutes, `TagDevice` returns `nil` instead of `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. Evict the key on store errors or populate `localCache` only after a successful create/update.

Non-atomic device admission lets concurrent requests exceed the limit — Concurrent first requests can all pass the `CountDevices` check before any insert/upsert commits, leaving more active devices than `s.deviceLimit` allows. Make admission and the write atomic with transaction locking, or serialize this critical section.

updateDevice retries prepend the query repeatedly and corrupt Exec arguments — Retries after SQLite `ErrLocked` or `ErrBusy` shift every `Exec` argument because the callback prepends another query to captured `args`. Build a fresh slice per `WithDbSession` invocation or call `Exec(query, args...)` without mutating `args`.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Missing post-lock cache recheck causes repeated cold-start manifest loads — Concurrent cold-start requests serialize on the write lock and each reread and reparse the manifest, even after an earlier request populated the cache. Recheck `entryPointAssetsCache` after locking and return it outside development mode to prevent redundant loads.

SetDualWritingMode cannot select mode 3, leaving new tests on mode 1 — New subtests can silently exercise `Mode1`, and fresh deployments cannot enable `Mode3`, because `SetDualWritingMode` initializes unset modes to `Mode1` and handles only 1↔2 transitions. Add explicit `Mode3` transitions and assert the selected mode.

Legacy update resolves changes against the wrong old object — Patch/apply can produce different legacy contents whenever the stores differ because the original `objInfo` makes `d.Legacy.Update` resolve against its own old object instead of unified `res`. Pass an `updateWrapper` containing `res` and the upstream preconditions.

Unbounded legacy create goroutines can exhaust memory and connections — When legacy storage is slow, request-rate writes accumulate untracked goroutines and database work for up to the timeout, potentially exhausting memory or connections. Replace per-request spawning around `d.Legacy.Create` with a bounded worker queue that applies backpressure.

Unified-storage errors skip legacy collection deletion — A transient unified-storage failure now leaves the entire legacy collection untouched instead of preserving best-effort dual deletion. Attempt `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` even when `d.Storage.DeleteCollection` fails, while returning the original unified-storage error.

Successful Mode3 writes do not verify the asynchronous legacy write — Dropping the legacy `Create` goroutine would still pass because `m.On(...)` only stubs the call and the goroutine is never awaited; `Delete`, `DeleteCollection`, and `Update` have the same gap. Synchronize on legacy completion and assert its invocation and arguments so a lost write fails.

TestMode3_Get cannot distinguish legacy and unified storage reads — Sharing `m` between `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` lets a legacy `Get` satisfy the unified expectation and return `exampleObj`, so a regression still passes. Use separate mocks, verify the unified-storage call, and assert legacy `Get` was never called.

Async legacy writes can be canceled when the request handler returns — The API server can cancel the request `ctx` when the handler returns, aborting a legacy safety write after unified storage has committed. Derive each write's timeout from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` to detach cancellation while retaining namespace and identity values.

Legacy writes can execute out of order and leave stale state — Independently scheduled legacy writes let a later update or delete overtake a create or older update; `legacyStorage.Update` can then return not found, and the delayed create can leave stale pre-update state. Serialize operations per object or use one ordered queue instead of scheduling each request independently.

Storage NotFound errors skip legacy deletion in mode 3 — An object missing from unified storage but still present in legacy storage can no longer be cleaned up because every `d.Storage.Delete` error returns before `d.Legacy.Delete`. Preserve the `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` fallback and attempt legacy deletion as before.

Unified-storage create failures are recorded as legacy metrics — Recording this failure in `DualWriterLegacyDuration` loses the unified-storage failure and attributes its latency to a backend that was never called. Use `recordStorageDuration` on this path instead of `recordLegacyDuration`.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129-129`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-130`

Legacy delete-collection results are recorded in the wrong metrics — Recording the asynchronous legacy result in the unified-storage histogram mixes legacy latency and errors into storage metrics while omitting them from legacy metrics. Call `recordLegacyDuration` with `startLegacy` instead of `recordStorageDuration`.

Delete metrics use object names as the kind label — Using object `name` as the Prometheus `kind` label misaggregates per-kind delete metrics and creates an unbounded time series for every object name. Pass `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration`, matching the error path.

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Unlocked TotalDocs call can race with Bleve cache writes — An event can write `b.cache` while `TotalDocs` iterates it without `cacheMu`, causing a fatal concurrent map iteration/write once the event goroutine is running. Add read locking or take a locked cache snapshot in `TotalDocs` before using it in this log call.

Parallel index builds can hide failures through the shared startup error — Each startup goroutine assigns the shared outer `err` in `search.go`, so a successful `BuildIndex` can overwrite another goroutine's failure and make `group.Wait` report success despite missing indexes. Use a goroutine-local error in the closure and return it instead.

Watcher starts after search indexing and misses events from the interim — Delaying `initWatcher` until the search build completes disconnects the server broadcaster during that window, so writes from other instances are missing from watch replays and `mostRecentRV` stays stale. Start the watcher before the index build, or buffer and replay events from the pre-build resource version.

Initialization failure leaks watch goroutines and lifecycle resources — If watcher setup fails after `search.init` starts its background watch, this return discards the server without cancellation or lifecycle cleanup, leaving resources no caller can stop. Call `s.cancel()` and `s.Stop` before returning the error, and log any stop failure.

Postgres skip message contradicts the unconditional skip — Because this branch skips every Postgres run, including local ones, the `t.Skip` message is false and prevents the local execution it describes. Gate the skip on Drone/CI, or state that Postgres is skipped everywhere.

Postgres skip disables startup and metrics integration coverage — The Postgres `t.Skip` removes that backend's startup and `/metrics` assertions, so an instrumentation-server regression would leave the test skipped instead of failing. Resolve the Drone-specific failure without disabling the Postgres case so this integration coverage remains effective.

Same-key BuildIndex calls are no longer serialized — Overlapping `BuildIndex` calls for one key can both populate an index, with file-backed calls sharing a directory; the last finisher overwrites `b.cache[key]`, leaving the other caller with an uncached index. Serialize construction per key or use singleflight, then reuse the completed index before replacing the cache entry.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Grafana recording rules incorrectly lose export support — Users cannot export Grafana recording rules from the prom-only list, although `RuleFormType.grafanaRecording` is supported. Change `ModifyExport` to use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` with `exportAllowed`, retaining alerting-only guards for actions that need them.

Singular Grafana ability mocks cannot control AlertRuleMenu — Mocking `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` cannot change the abilities rendered by `AlertRuleMenu`, which consumes `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, making the new guidance and mocks misleading. Remove the singular-hook recommendation and mock the plural hook instead.

More button test never opens or verifies the action menu — The test would still pass if `AlertRuleMenu` lost every action or the More button never opened it. Click `moreButton` and assert the silence, copy-link, duplicate, and export menu items, or rename the test to cover trigger rendering only.

Skipped Grafana-prom rules can incorrectly enable Duplicate — For cloud rules, `skipToken` becomes an undefined `rule`, so `Duplicate` falls back to `rulesPermissions.create`; `canDuplicate` in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` can then allow duplication despite the ruler ability forbidding it. Return `NotSupported` with `false` when `rule` is absent, or make both Grafana wrappers neutral for `skipToken`.

**Also found in:**
- `public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:397-405`

CombinedRule adapter drops federated-group immutability checks — Federated rules can now expose update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent-delete as supported because this `CombinedRule` delegation drops `rule.group` and the delegated hook hard-codes `isFederated` to false. Preserve the federated-group check in the adapter or pass it into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.

**Also found in:**
- `public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:242-245`

Prom-only Grafana rules hide Delete despite delete permission — Users with delete permission still see no Delete action for prom-only Grafana rules because `GrafanaRuleListItem` supplies no `rulerRule`, even when `canDelete` is true. Allow the Delete item to use the prom-rule identifier instead of requiring `rulerRule`.

Prom-only rule silence action does not open a drawer — Clicking Silence notifications for a prom-only rule only sets `showSilenceDrawer`; `RuleActionsButtons.V2` renders `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only after `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` succeeds, but receives no `rule` here. Add a prom-rule drawer path or hide the silence action for this caller.

Missing key reconciles Grafana rule rows by position — Without `key`, React reconciles these stateful `GrafanaRuleListItem` rows by position, so delete, silence, or clone state can attach to a different rule as asynchronous results arrive. Restore `key={key}` to preserve rule identity.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: This lazy registration path does not preserve the shortcut-uniqueness invariant checked in postInit — If a grant discovered after startup reuses an existing shortcut, line 113 overwrites grantsByShortcuts for the old grant while the old grant remains in grantsToShortcuts; both grants can then encode the same context and tokens from the old grant decode as the new one. Validate collisions before modifying either map and publish the two mappings atomically, including when concurrent lazy lookups occur.

This test does not reach the intended unknown-grant `IllegalArgumentException` — Since `ac` is absent from the fixture map and `sessionFactory` was never initialized, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` dereferences the null session factory during its lazy refresh and throws `NullPointerException`; `catch (RuntimeException)` treats that as success. The test would therefore remain green if the intended validation were broken.

Abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories — Adding getShortcut() as an abstract SPI method breaks existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() calls it for every registered grant factory, so a custom provider compiled against the previous interface will fail startup with AbstractMethodError; rebuilding also fails until the method is added.

Client credentials and UMA token IDs use the na fallback — The grant type is propagated only through `createTokenResponse`, but `ClientCredentialsGrantType.process` (lines 140-141) and the UMA flow in `AuthorizationTokenService` (lines 357-358) generate access tokens directly without setting `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. Their token IDs therefore use the `na` fallback instead of `cc` or `pg`; set the grant attribute on these direct paths or move propagation into the shared access-token creation path.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/tokenexchange/StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237-237`

getShortcut Javadoc specifies the wrong shortcut length — This contract describes a “3-letters” shortcut, but all shortcut implementations added here return two characters and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` decodes exactly two grant characters as part of a six-character prefix. An implementer following this Javadoc could return a three-character shortcut whose encoded token ID is then rejected.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-81`
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:109-117`

Constructor validates grantType twice and allows a null rawTokenId — The constructor checks `grantType` twice, allowing `rawTokenId` to remain null so `encodeTokenId` emits a literal `null` suffix instead of rejecting the invalid context. Change this check to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

Access-token matcher extracts the wrong grant shortcut — `substring(3, 5)` reads the last token-type character and first grant-type character rather than the grant shortcut at indexes 4–5, allowing events with the wrong grant to pass the new assertions. Read `substring(4, 6)` after validating the six-character prefix.

Access token matcher uses the wrong grant shortcut offsets — The grant shortcut is at offsets 4 and 5 of the six-character context, but `substring(3, 5)` reads the second token-type character and only the first grant-type character. For example, `onrtac` produces `ta` instead of `ac`, so the assertion is not comparing the grant field.

Grant shortcut is extracted from the wrong token ID offset — The new comment says the grant shortcut starts at the fourth character, but the encoder layout is two session-type characters, two token-type characters, then two grant-type characters; the encoder therefore extracts it with `substring(4, 6)`, starting at the fifth character. This comment documents the wrong offset (and the adjacent extraction uses that same wrong offset); align it with the encoder’s `substring(4, 6)` layout.

Access token matcher reads the grant shortcut at the wrong offset — The grant shortcut is read from the wrong position. The encoder/decoder layout places it at character indices 4 and 5 (the decoder uses substring(4, 6)), but this matcher reads indices 3 and 4.

Access token ID matcher does not validate the expected grant — DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId places the two-character grant shortcut at indexes 4–5, after the two-character session and token types. This extracts indexes 3–4 instead, so it checks the last token-type character plus only the first grant character rather than the generated grant field.

Access token matcher rejects IDs with the expected grant shortcut — The matcher returns false when the extracted shortcut equals `expectedGrantShortcut`, so valid IDs are rejected whenever the extracted text accidentally matches, and correcting the bounds alone would reject every valid ID. Negate the equality test so a mismatch returns false.

Deleted cached groups cause getSubGroupsCount to return null — The `null` violates `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()`'s contract, can cause a `NullPointerException` when unboxed, and reaches responses through `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`. Return `0L` when `model` is `null`, or skip the stale group.

Worker thread is not joined before exceptions are asserted — The main thread can assert while the worker's final `groups(...)` request is still in flight, missing a later exception and letting the regression test pass despite the failure it should catch. Keep the worker reference, join it after setting `deletedAll`, and only then assert that `caughtExceptions` is empty.
Arbitrary HTML inside a choice branch is never inspected because the whole expression becomes… — A translation such as `{0,choice,0#minutes|1#minute|1

Unbalanced translation anchors pass verification after tag stripping — A translation with the same opening anchor as English but no closing `` has its opening tag removed and then compares clean, because the loop has no remaining target match and never validates balance. This accepts malformed HTML and can leave the rendered link swallowing subsequent content; reject unbalanced target anchors before stripping matched tags.

Bundle read errors bypass verify()'s MojoExecutionException contract — Preserve the prior contract by allowing these `IOException`s to reach `verify()`'s existing catch (or explicitly wrapping them in `MojoExecutionException`); handle a missing English bundle as a validation message if that case is expected.
Overlapping affixes crash the illegal HTML diagnostic — Limit the suffix scan to the characters remaining after the prefix (`min(lengths) - start`) before taking either substring.

Server error placeholders use unsupported Java MessageFormat syntax — The account UI formats these server errors with default i18next, which does not interpolate single-brace `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` or Java `{2,choice,...}` syntax, so English users see the placeholders literally. Retain `{{0}}`-style parameters and use i18next-supported pluralization for this bundle.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties:3138-3138`

Lithuanian login and account TOTP instructions contain Italian text — The new instruction is Italian, so the Lithuanian login TOTP page displays the wrong language; the identical text was also added to `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`. Replace both occurrences with Lithuanian text.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties:101-101`

TOTP instruction uses Traditional Chinese in the Simplified Chinese bundle — The new value is written in Traditional Chinese (`在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`) even though this is the Simplified Chinese (`zh_CN`) bundle and adjacent messages use Simplified Chinese. Use Simplified Chinese wording, for example `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`, so the TOTP instruction matches the selected locale.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: Missing Clients resource breaks permissions for existing admin-permissions clients — An existing admin-permissions client created before this PR has no `Clients` resource because `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns when that client already exists, so `getResourceTypeResource` returns null and `findByResource` dereferences `resource.getId()`. Backfill the new resource and scopes for existing realms and handle a missing aggregate resource before querying policies.

V2 canExchangeTo throws on every cross-client token exchange — `AdminPermissions.management(...).clients()` resolves to this V2 implementation whenever V2 is enabled, and `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` calls `canExchangeTo` for every exchange to a different target client. The unconditional exception turns such token-exchange attempts into server errors; implement V2 evaluation or deny/delegate without throwing.
When V2 is enabled without V1, this guard skips `ClientRemovedEvent` cleanup, leaving the new… — Add V2 resource and policy cleanup independently of the V1-only listener.

Per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never have `type`… — Store `Clients` as their type, including for existing resources, or query using the actual resource storage scheme.

All-clients grants add "Clients" as a client ID and trigger an NPE — The built-in all-clients resource also has type `Clients`, so a matching all-clients permission adds the literal name `Clients` as a client ID; `AvailableRoleMappingResource` then dereferences `realm.getClientById("Clients")` and throws a null-pointer exception. Exclude the aggregate resource and expand an all-clients grant to actual client IDs.

canView() ignores the all-clients manage permission — An administrator granted only the all-clients `manage` scope still gets `canView() == false`, so `ClientsResource.getClients` rejects the request at `requireList()` unless the administrator also has an unrelated query role. Include `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` in this check, matching the manage-implies-view behavior of `canView(ClientModel)` and `canView(ClientScopeModel)`.

All-clients grants are skipped when a client-specific resource exists — The all-clients permission is considered only when the client has no resource of its own. If a client has any client-specific permission (for example CONFIGURE), resource is non-null and an all-clients MANAGE or VIEW grant is never evaluated, so valid global grants stop applying to that client.

CONFIGURE test does not check permissions on a different client — This test grants CONFIGURE only on `myclient`, but every post-grant operation still targets `myclient`; the later denied operations only distinguish CONFIGURE from MANAGE. If `canConfigure` ignored the supplied client and applied that permission to every client, the entire test would still pass.

OnlyOneClient test does not check that other clients stay forbidden — The “OnlyOneClient” role-mapping test never verifies that another client remains inaccessible after these grants. An implementation that ignores the client argument when evaluating MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE would still fail the pre-grant checks and pass both post-grant calls.

View-all-clients test accepts an incomplete client list — `not(empty())` does not verify the claimed ability to list and view all clients: the test would still pass if the all-clients VIEW permission exposed only `myclient`, since the subsequent protocol-mapper check also uses only that client. Compare the returned client IDs with the complete set obtained through the privileged realm admin (or at least assert access to multiple otherwise-unpermissioned clients).

V2 setPermissionsEnabled breaks client removal cleanup — This override conflicts with the changed `AdminPermissions` client-removal listener. That listener calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` on every `ClientRemovedEvent`; with V2 enabled, `clients()` returns this class, so the call always throws `UnsupportedOperationException` and can cause client deletion to fail.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:89-92`
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:89-91`

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
