canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Base login-password template lacks conditional passkey authentication UI — Users of themes inheriting the base `login-password.ftl` cannot authenticate with a passkey because it omits the form for `passkeys.conditionalUIData`. Add the conditional WebAuthn form and initialization there, matching the `keycloak.v2` template.

Disabled organizations suppress required IDP login-cache invalidation — For a disabled organization, `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` tests organization-effective `original` state, so hiding an IDP or making it link-only or private can skip invalidation; re-enabling the organization then serves the stale IDP. Evaluate the raw stored IDP from `idpDelegate.getById`, not organization-effective `isEnabled`.

Login cache key conflates null and empty organization IDs — Because `searchKey` maps null and empty organization IDs to the same value, the first cached `ORG_ONLY` or `ALL` query can serve the other input, returning organization providers for a blank ID or dropping them for null. Encode null distinctly from an empty string.

Cold login-cache fill refetches every IDP through `getById` — With a cold IDP cache, each new mode/organization query adds N single-ID database lookups to the initial delegate query. Retain the models returned by `idpDelegate.getForLogin`, or bulk-load them, instead of refetching every ID through `getById`.

Login IDP cache test never exercises cache hits — The `query != null` branch in `getForLogin` can return wrong providers or throw while this test still passes, because every query is cold or follows invalidation and intermediate checks only inspect `IdentityProviderListQuery`. Repeat an identical mode/organization query without invalidation and assert its returned providers.

Login cache test does not exercise private organization-linked providers — Because every organization-linked provider sets `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`, removing the new organization/public clause in `getLoginPredicate()` leaves all expected counts unchanged. Add an enabled, organization-linked private provider and assert its exclusion from login results and the cache.

Cleanup registers a nonexistent alias and leaks the created providers — Cleanup targets the literal alias `alias`, so none of the generated providers is removed; the later registration repeats the mismatch for `idp-alias-20`, leaking providers into subsequent tests or failing cleanup. Register cleanup with each provider's actual alias.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Disabled error context still triggers a replay Snuba query — Even when `enable_error_context=false`, the endpoint executes `query_replay_instance` and processes its response before checking the flag, adding an unnecessary Snuba query to every opted-out summary request. Move the flag check before the Snuba call and skip replay lookup entirely when error context is disabled.

Trace attribute query cache is shared across organizations — The React Query key omits `organization.slug` even though the fetch URL depends on it, so identical filters in two organizations share cached attribute keys and can show the previous organization's schema. Include the organization or full endpoint path in `queryKey`.

Raw browser reports are exposed in validation-failure logs — Avoid logging `raw_report` in this new validation-failure warning. Browser report bodies and URLs can contain sensitive document or blocked-resource URLs, query parameters, and page-specific content, so this creates an additional warning-level copy of untrusted sensitive data in application logs.

Paginated batches repeat replay-wide errors on unrelated breadcrumbs — `error_events` contains every error in the replay, but `gen_request_data` yields all remaining entries after each paginated segment batch. Subsequent pages therefore repeat errors and attach them to unrelated breadcrumbs; scope errors to the current page's segment/time range instead of flushing the full replay-wide list on every page.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:134-139`

Error details can be associated with the wrong error ID — `get_multi` returns a mapping keyed by node ID, but zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` treats it as an ordered positional result list. If backend result order differs from `error_ids`, or an entry is omitted for a missing node, an event's title/message/timestamp can be assigned to the wrong error ID; filtering `None` after the zip cannot restore alignment.

Falsy age and timestamp values bypass mutual-exclusion validation — Both cross-field validators use truthiness, so a report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes validation despite the fields being mutually exclusive. Test explicit key presence in `initial_data` rather than the values' truthiness.

The feature-flagged path renders hard-coded empty columns and data instead of the actual `result`… — Organizations with `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled will see an empty table even when rows were returned. Pass the real result data and derived columns to `TableWidgetVisualization`, or retain the existing renderer until that mapping exists.

Hidden attributes remain visible when the search query is empty — `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` is checked only in the search-filtering branch. Because the no-search path returns `sorted` earlier, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` remain visible normally and disappear only while searching.

Falsy custom cell values incorrectly trigger fallback rendering — The renderer contract reserves `undefined` for fallback rendering, but `if (cell)` also discards valid falsy React nodes. In particular, a custom body renderer returning the number `0` will unexpectedly render the default field formatter instead of zero.

Mixed timestamp units break chronological error merging — The merge compares nodestore error timestamps in seconds with outer RRWeb event timestamps in milliseconds, so real errors compare earlier than the first breadcrumb and are emitted at the beginning instead of in chronological order. Normalize both timestamps to the same unit before sorting and merging, and cover the path with a realistic 13-digit RRWeb timestamp.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Memory backpressure repeats cluster-wide scans for every shard buffer — `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` ignores `assigned_shards` and scans every master, so this loop repeats the cluster-wide fan-out once per flusher process during every `submit` on the consumer thread. Fetch memory info once and compute the totals from that shared result.

Per-process metrics polling causes N sequential Redis round trips — `record_stored_segments()` runs a blocking Redis pipeline for each flusher process on every `submit`, replacing one all-shards poll with N sequential round trips on the consumer thread. Keep one all-shards buffer for this poll or batch every queue-size `ZCARD` into one pipeline.

Produce metrics use inconsistent shard tag keys — A common shard filter or aggregation cannot match all produce-phase metrics because `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` tags `shard_tag` as `shards`, while the other two metrics use `shard`. Use `shard` consistently across all three metrics.

max_processes=0 is silently treated as an unset value — Passing `max_processes=0` through `--flusher-processes` unexpectedly enables one process per shard because the truthiness fallback treats it like `None`. Default only when `max_processes is None`, reject nonpositive counts, and constrain the CLI option with `click.IntRange(min=1)`.

Shard count assertion does not verify distribution across processes — The summed count still passes if process 0 owns every shard and process 1 owns none, so broken distribution can go undetected. Assert `flusher.process_to_shards_map` equals the expected per-process mapping, such as `{0: [0, 2], 1: [1, 3]}`.

Hang recovery skips killing spawn-based flusher processes — On Linux, the spawn context creates a `SpawnProcess`, so the `multiprocessing.Process` guard skips `kill()` and `_create_process_for_shards` can start a replacement while the hung worker keeps flushing the same shards. Guard with `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` or the spawn context's process type.

Expired join deadline skips termination of remaining flusher workers — Because `next_step.join(timeout)` can consume the whole deadline, the timeout `break` can exit before any `terminate()` and skip every later worker, leaving hung daemons flushing after shutdown. Attempt termination for every process even after the deadline, bounding only the graceful waits.

Negative max_processes causes a KeyError during flusher startup — A negative `max_processes` leaves `process_to_shards_map` empty, so startup raises `KeyError` on `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]`. Reject values below 1 before computing `num_processes`, and restrict `--flusher-processes` with `click.IntRange(min=1)`.

Intended flusher delay is a no-op under the sleep monkeypatch — The test's `time.sleep` monkeypatch makes `time.sleep(0.1)` return immediately, providing no processing delay before the test reaches `join()`. Use real waiting or synchronization instead of the no-op sleep.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound rejects assignment_source — A keyword call valid under the base contract raises `TypeError` because `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound` in `src/sentry/integrations/example/integration.py` does not accept `assignment_source`. Update that override to accept the optional argument, or remove the unused parameter from the base signature.

Empty-array test passes an empty dict instead of an array — The test still passes if `AssignmentSource.from_dict([])` raises instead of returning `None`, because `test_from_dict_empty_array` actually supplies `{}`. Rename it for empty-dict handling, or pass `[]` to exercise the array behavior its name claims.

Queued timestamp default is evaluated once at import time — Every `AssignmentSource` created without `queued` gets the same stale import-time timestamp because `timezone.now()` runs when the class is defined, making serialized queue times incorrect. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` for `queued` and import `field` from `dataclasses` so each instance gets a fresh value.

Predictable OAuth state allows authorization code injection — Because `pipeline.signature` is a deterministic MD5 of static view class names, its OAuth `state` is shared across installations and users, enabling authorization-code injection into a victim's pipeline. Generate a random nonce per attempt, bind it in pipeline state, and validate the callback against it.

Installer verification is skipped when the integration does not yet exist — When `Integration.DoesNotExist` advances the pipeline, `build_integration` creates the integration from `installation_id` without consuming `github_authenticated_user`; a delayed or missing webhook then lets any authenticated GitHub user attach another user's installation. Require trusted installer evidence before either the new or existing integration path advances.

Variable-based gettext leaves short installation errors untranslated — Because `_(error_short)` translates a variable, gettext cannot extract its literals; `Invalid installation request.` remains untranslated, and existing translations can disappear when catalogs regenerate. Mark each literal for translation at its definition or call site, then pass the value without wrapping `error_short` in `_`.

OAuth state comparison leaks timing information — Normal string comparison can expose prefix-dependent timing for the OAuth `state` CSRF credential. Convert the request value to a string and use `django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare` instead of `!=` when checking `pipeline.signature`.

Missing-installation test is short-circuited by invalid OAuth state — The invalid `state` makes `OAuthLoginView` reject the callback before `GitHubInstallation` handles the unknown `installation_id`, so this test passes even if missing-installation handling is broken. Complete OAuth with the pipeline's real signature and assert `The GitHub installation could not be found.`

Ownership verification uses mutable GitHub login instead of immutable user ID — Persisting only GitHub's mutable `login` lets another account claim an installer's old username after a rename and satisfy the ownership check, although `/user` and webhook `sender` both provide an immutable `id`. Bind the numeric user ID and compare it with `integration.metadata['sender']['id']`, keeping `login` only for display.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:500-505`

OAuth token request failures bypass installation error handling — With `safe_urlopen` outside the `try`, connection, DNS, TLS, and timeout failures escape `dispatch`, producing a 500 instead of the installation-error response. Move the token request into the handled path, catch the HTTP client's request exceptions, and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` when the exchange fails.

Missing sender metadata raises KeyError during GitHub reinstall — An active integration without `metadata.sender` raises `KeyError` on reinstall, although `build_integration` can legitimately omit it, producing a 500 instead of an installation-failure response. Read the sender defensively and reject or reconstruct the installation when trusted sender metadata is absent.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated — `Detector.detector_handler` now raises `TypeError` when instantiating the handler registered on `MetricAlertFire`, breaking metric alert evaluation. Implement `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` on `MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, or retain the previous concrete `DetectorHandler.evaluate` implementation.

Expected occurrence fingerprint uses the wrong group key — The equality assertion fails even when production code is correct because `evaluate_group_key_value` returns a fingerprint for `group_key`, while the expected occurrence uses `val1`. Build the expected occurrence with `group_key`, or pass that key to `evaluate_group_key_value`.

Mock occurrence builder ignores value, masking incorrect measurement forwarding — Occurrence and Kafka assertions can pass even when `evaluate_group_key_value` forwards the wrong measurement because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value`. Expose `value` in returned data such as `evidence_data` and correct expected measurements, or spy on the hook and assert its `(group_key, value, new_status)` calls.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Monitor context discards the display-ready config copy — Consumers receive the raw stored `schedule_type` instead of the display-ready value because the returned context rereads `monitor_environment.monitor.config`. Return the local `config` for the `"config"` entry.

EventManager throws when destination calendar array is empty/null — Any Google Meet booking with an empty or null `evt.destinationCalendar` throws on `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` because the optional chaining was lost during the array refactor in `EventManager.ts`. Add optional chaining to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` so the `TypeError` is avoided.

updateEvent selectedCalendar fallback predicate is self-referential — The `find` predicate in `updateEvent`'s fallback searches for the falsy `externalCalendarId` the ternary just rejected, so `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and Google rejects the `update` call. Replace it with `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` so the fallback picks a real calendar.

deleteEvent fallback searches for the falsy externalCalendarId and loses destination calendar — The `find` predicate in `deleteEvent`'s fallback searches for the falsy `externalCalendarId` the ternary just rejected, then the `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` masking silently routes deletion to `primary`. Use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` so the original destination calendar is honored.

Collective booking silently skips team destination calendars when organizer has none — When both `eventType.destinationCalendar` and `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are null, `handleNewBooking.ts` initializes `evt.destinationCalendar` to `null`, and the optional-chained `push` drops every team host calendar silently. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to `[]` so collective bookings actually populate host calendars.
Lark createEvent signature missing credentialId parameter — Add the `credentialId` parameter and pick the matching `DestinationCalendar` like `GoogleCalendarService` does.

createEvent signature is missing the second credentialId parameter — The `Calendar` interface in `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts` and `CalendarManager` require `createEvent` to accept a `credentialId`, but Office365's `createEvent` in `Office365CalendarService.ts` still takes only `event`. Add the `credentialId` parameter and filter `event.destinationCalendar` by it like `GoogleCalendarService` does.

Organization slug is dropped when team billing is disabled — The slug condition in `create.handler.ts` is inverted: `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` drops the slug when team billing is off, making new organizations unsluggable. Restore the negation `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` unless this reversal was intentional.

createAllCalendarEvents fetches missing credentials serially — `createAllCalendarEvents` awaits `prisma.credential.findUnique` sequentially per destination in `EventManager.ts`, so N missing host credentials issue N serial DB round-trips before any createEvent work begins. Collect missing ids and fetch with one `findMany` run before dispatching creates in parallel.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/core/EventManager.ts:493-554`
- `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:416-484`

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires OWNER role due to redundant AND — `isTeamAdmin` already covers ADMIN and OWNER, so ANDing it with `isTeamOwner` collapses the gate to OWNER-only, wrongly blocking ADMIN team members in `addGuests.handler.ts`. Drop `isTeamOwner` (matching other handlers) so the name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` matches the behavior.

Case-sensitivity bypass: guest blacklist not compared case-insensitively — `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but compared against raw `guest`, so `ATTACKER@BAD.COM` bypasses a stored `attacker@bad.com` and the user gets the invite. Lowercase `guest` (or the whole `guests` array) before the `includes` check.

OrganizerAddGuestsEmail subject throws when attendees is empty — Reading `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` throws when `attendees` is empty, aborting the organizer email. Guard it with optional chaining and fall back to `this.calEvent.organizer.name` (or team name) so the subject always renders.

onSuccess branch fails to reset stale isInvalidEmail state — A stale `isInvalidEmail` survives dialog reopen because `onSuccess` never clears it, so users see a leftover red banner over an empty input. Add `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` inside `onSuccess` to mirror the cancel-button reset.

BAD_REQUEST message says emails_must_be_unique_valid when cause is 'no new guests remain' — Throwing `emails_must_be_unique_valid` when every guest was already present mislabels the failure. Use a key like `no_new_guests_to_add` so the i18n copy matches the actual bad-request cause.

TOCTOU race in addGuests allows duplicate attendees and bypasses blacklist — Concurrent calls slip past `booking.attendees` filtering and the non-transactional `createMany` writes duplicate rows, and case-variant emails bypass the exact-match check. Wrap the filter and insert in `prisma.$transaction` (re-querying attendees inside it), add a `@@unique([bookingId, email])` constraint, and compare lowercased emails.

sendAddGuestsEmails invoked with raw input guests not uniqueGuests — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input, so the email manager's `newGuests.includes` check sees attendees who weren't actually added. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead so notifications match the booking update.

Duplicate attendee dedupe ignores email case-insensitivity — Strict equality between `guest` and `attendee.email` lets `USER@EXAMPLE.COM` duplicate `user@example.com`, producing extra attendee rows and duplicate emails. Normalise with `guest.toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase()` before the dedupe filter.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites missing refresh_token with literal string — In credential-sync mode the schema strips `refresh_token`, so the guard always writes the literal `"refresh_token"` to `Credential.key`. Subsequent Google and Microsoft refreshes then return `invalid_grant`.

refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response on sync branch without parsing — Callers like `googlecalendar`, `hubspot`, `larkcalendar`, `zoho-bigin`, and `zohocrm` read `.data`/`.access_token` off the raw `Response` and throw. Await `.json()` and return `{ data }` so the sync branch matches the legacy shape.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:1-20`

refreshOAuthTokens raw fetch Response breaks callers — Callers in `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, and `office365calendar` read `.data`/`.access_token` from the raw `Response`, throwing on `token.access_token`. Await `.json()` (or reshape to the `{ res, tokens }` shape) so `parseRefreshTokenResponse` gets a parsed body.

statusText check fails on HTTP/2 responses — Salesforce serves over HTTP/2 where reason phrases arrive empty, so `response.statusText !== "OK"` rejects legitimate 200 responses with a spurious `HttpError`. Use `response.ok` (or a numeric status range) instead.

zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId — `refreshOAuthTokens` posts its third arg as `calcomUserId`, but this caller passes `credential.id` (`credentialId`) instead of `credential.userId`. Pass `credential.userId` so the sync endpoint receives the user identifier it expects.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality — An attacker can recover the secret through timing because `!==` short-circuits on the first differing byte. Replace it with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after the lengths match.

Race condition in credential findFirst/create creates duplicate Credential rows — Two concurrent webhook deliveries can both miss the `findFirst` and call `prisma.credential.create`, producing duplicate Credential rows. Wrap the pair in `prisma.$transaction` or use `prisma.credential.upsert` keyed on `userId`+`appId`.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: scheduleSMSReminders deleteMany OR clause is not scoped to SMS method — Without an outer `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter on `deleteMany`, the second OR branch (`retryCount > 1`) would silently purge EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders if any future code path ever sets that field on them. Wrap both OR branches in an SMS filter so the deletion scope matches the handler.

retryCount update is a lost-update race between concurrent cron workers — Two concurrent cron workers can each read `retryCount` as 0 and write 1, losing an increment and delaying the `deleteMany` gate at `retryCount > 1` by one cycle. Replace the JS read-then-write in `prisma.workflowReminder.update` with `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` so the write is atomic.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Save download and assert backup codes body matches 10 formatted codes — Asserting only `download.suggestedFilename()` lets empty backup codes slip past, since that name comes from the hardcoded `download="cal-backup-codes.txt"` attribute in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx. Save the download and assert the body matches the 10 formatted `XXXXX-XXXXX` codes.

copy backup codes test never asserts clipboard contents — Waiting solely on `toast-success` lets a silent failure in `navigator.clipboard.writeText` pass, since the toast is unconditionally fired from EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx. Read the clipboard and assert it equals the 10 formatted backup codes shown to the user.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Raw request.referer interpolated into JS string breaks out of context — Raw `<%= request.referer %>` interpolation into a JS string lets an attacker with a single quote or `</script>` segment in the URL execute script in the parent page. Wrap with `j`/`json_escape` so the referer cannot break out of the JS context.
URL interpolated raw into href attribute and link text enables XSS — Wrap both occurrences in `CGI.escapeHTML(url)` and prefer double-quoted attributes.

PollFeed runs synchronously on every embed cache miss — Running `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline makes each cached-miss embed view pay the cost of a full RSS import. Enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)` instead and only return early on the existence check.

postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of origin comparison — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin whose string appears inside `discourseUrl`, allowing attacker-controlled origins to resize the iframe. Compare `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin` to match only the parsed origin.

Synchronous PollFeed in embed render path — Invoking `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline in `perform_retrieve` blocks the embed render on a full RSS fetch and import per cache miss. Drop the synchronous call and let the scheduled `PollFeed` job reconcile topics, relying only on the embed_url existence check.

postMessage origin check uses unsafe substring match — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` matches any origin substring contained in `discourseUrl`, so attackers on a shorter matching origin can resize the iframe. Replace with `e.origin === new URL(discourseUrl).origin` for an exact parsed comparison.
"is 404 without an embed_url" test sits outside "with a host" context — Move it inside the context and stub referer so only the embed_url path is exercised.

Layout echoes full request.referer (incl. query string) into JS context — Echo only the scheme and host from `URI(request.referer)` through the `j` helper so embedding-site query secrets never reach the response.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: SQL injection via string interpolation in INSERT — Interpolating `h` and `category_id` into the `INSERT` lets a stray `'` in legacy `site_settings.value` terminate the SQL literal. Use parameterized placeholders so the values cannot break out.

Migration breaks on host values containing a single quote — Single quotes in legacy `embeddable_hosts` values break the interpolated `INSERT` and abort the upgrade. Sanitize `h` (e.g. doubling quotes) or switch to parameterized insertion.

expandable_first_post? dropped embeddable_hosts guard — After dropping the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check, `expandable_first_post?` returns true even when no `EmbeddableHost` rows exist and embedding is actually dead. Add `EmbeddableHost.exists?` so the flag reflects runtime capability.

destroy action crashes with NoMethodError when host id is missing — `host.destroy` runs without a nil check, so a bad id raises `NoMethodError` and returns 500. Raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless host` before destroying.

expandable_first_post? test with blank embeddable_host no longer tests anything meaningful — With the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil` setup removed, "is false if embeddable_host is blank" only asserts defaults and would miss a regression reintroducing that dependency. Rename it or delete it.

before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil — `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally, so a missing `:host` param from `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` blows up as a 500. Guard with `self.host.to_s.sub!` or skip when blank.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

findings.description: order:2 on .extra-info-wrapper requires flex parent added in same PR — Without a flex container parent, the new `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` is a no-op and the wrapper falls back to source order. Convert its parent to `@include flexbox()` or drop the order rule to match the described position.

order mixin uses raw value for 1-based legacy -box-ordinal-group — The legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties use 1-based ordering while `order` is 0-based, so reusing `$val` in `order()` causes off-by-one placement on legacy engines. Add `$val + 1` to the box lines so modern and legacy align.

goldensDetail.text: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Duplicate downsize redefines signature and breaks ResizeEmoji caller — Every `ResizeEmoji` job raises `ArgumentError` because the duplicate `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` shadows the 5-arg signature used at `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14`. Remove the obsolete first definition so the new contract is unambiguous.

OptimizedImage.downsize called with a percentage string after signature change — `OptimizedImage.downsize` receives `"80%"` here while the new signature expects a `"WxH"` pixel string, breaking the resize loop. Add a `downsize_percentage` helper or convert the source resolution into `"WxH"` before calling.

validateUploadedFile hardcodes 10MB, ignoring per-type SiteSetting limit — `validateUploadedFile` runs for both image and attachment uploads, so a hardcoded `10 * 1024` discards `SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb` client-side and users only learn the cap when the server rejects the upload. Restore the `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup or only apply 10MB for images.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description:
Group member PUT/DELETE routes missing :id segment — `delete "members"` and `put "members"` resolve as collection actions, so calls like `Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + id + '/members.json')` miss the route. Add `on: :member` so they generate `/admin/groups/:id/members`.

**Also found in:**
- `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65-96`

totalPages off-by-one when user_count is a multiple of limit — `totalPages` computes one extra page whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, so `showingLast` stays true on the last real page. Replace `Math.floor(...) + 1` with `Math.ceil(...)` so the count matches reality.

Race condition between next/previous clicks corrupts displayed model state — Out-of-order responses from `findMembers` overwrite `offset`, `user_count`, and `members` of the faster click, so the rendered page no longer matches `currentPage`. Guard `next`/`previous` against re-entry (e.g. a `loadingMembers` flag) and drop stale responses in `setProperties`.

**Also found in:**
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20-38`

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: FallbackLocaleList#[] crashes when default_locale is nil — `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` before `.compact`, so a nil default locale raises `NoMethodError` instead of being filtered. Apply safe navigation so `.compact` can drop the nil.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: updateDevice misreports stale device as ErrDeviceLimitReached — A device record aged 30-61 days won't match `updatedDevice`'s WHERE clause but still exists in the table, so callers can't tell stale from 'limit reached' and returning users get a wrong rejection. Check existence for the device first, then apply the `updated_at` window to distinguish the two outcomes.

CreateOrUpdateDevice count+insert race can exceed device limit — `CreateOrUpdateDevice` reads `CountDevices` then conditionally inserts with no transaction or row lock, so concurrent new-device callers both see room and exceed `deviceLimit`. Wrap the count+insert in a serializable transaction, or use a SQL row-level constraint as the limiter.

Anonymous Authenticate now blocks on TagDevice on the auth hot path — Anonymous auth now blocks synchronously on `TagDevice` -> `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, adding a guaranteed `CountDevices` round-trip and an extra COUNT scan per request when `deviceLimit > 0`. Keep the tag async for non-limit branches; only the `ErrDeviceLimitReached` case needs a synchronous read.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Double-check cache after acquiring write lock to avoid duplicate decode — Concurrent cold-cache callers each redundantly run `readWebAssetsFromFile` inside the critical section, serializing what used to be parallel work and inflating `/` and `/api/frontend/settings` startup times by N. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` right after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` and return it when set so only the first caller decodes.

instrumentContext lacks test coverage for new ContextualLoggerMiddleware — `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` ships in `contextual_logger_middleware.go` with no test coverage, so a regression in `instrumentContext` (e.g., dropping `pCtx.User` or `pCtx.DataSourceInstanceSettings`) would slip past `metrics_middleware_test.go`, which only checks Prometheus counters. Add a decorator test that captures the downstream log line and asserts `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID`.

DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records duration under wrong metric name — The async legacy goroutine after a unified-store `DeleteCollection` records its latency under the storage histogram, polluting dashboards. Call `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead.

DeleteCollection legacy goroutine uses storage duration recorder — The legacy `DeleteCollection` goroutine records latency via `d.recordStorageDuration`, attributing Legacy timings to the unified-storage series. Switch to `d.recordLegacyDuration` so the storage/legacy split stays accurate.

Mode3 Create: storage error recorded to legacy metric — Create's storage-error branch writes into the legacy metric via `d.recordLegacyDuration`, misattributing a UnifiedStorage failure. Use `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` so dashboards see the failure on the correct series.

recordLegacyDuration used instead of recordStorageDuration on storage Update error — Update's storage-error branch calls `d.recordLegacyDuration` for a Storage failure. Use `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` to keep the storage/legacy split faithful.

Delete success path logs object name instead of resource kind — Delete's success branch passes `name` where `options.Kind` is expected, putting object identity under the kind label. Replace `name` with `options.Kind` so per-kind dashboards group correctly.

Mode3 Update dispatching to Legacy asynchronously breaks prior sync guarantee — `DualWriterMode3.Update` previously called `Legacy.Update` synchronously with an `updateWrapper`; now it fires a goroutine using unwrapped `objInfo`, so callers can't rely on read-after-update from Legacy. Revert to synchronous legacy update or document the new async guarantee.

TestMode3_Create does not assert the legacy Create was actually invoked — `TestMode3_Create` registers a `legacyStoreMock.Create` expectation but never verifies it was met, so removing the legacy goroutine would still pass. Add `m.AssertExpectations(t)` so the dual-write contract is actually enforced.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:189-241`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:297-355`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: BuildIndex lost full-function lock, races on same on-disk bleve dir — The narrow lock around only `b.cache[key] = idx` lets two `BuildIndex` callers race on the same on-disk bleve directory and corrupt the index. Hold an exclusion across the whole build via a per-key mutex or singleflight so the second caller waits for the first.

Init initializes search before watcher, dropping events emitted during search.init — Starting `s.search.init` before `s.initWatcher` lets events emitted during search init be discarded, since no consumer is attached yet. Run `s.initWatcher` first (or open the event queue before `s.search.init`) so those events are buffered.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Menu actions test does not assert Pause or Delete visibility — The test asserts only 4 menu items and never checks Pause or Delete, so a regression in `grafanaPauseAbility` or `grafanaDeleteAbility` in `AlertRuleMenu` would slip past CI. Add explicit expectations for Pause/Delete visibility (or document their absence) so the suite enforces the contract.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: isAccessTokenId reads wrong substring for grant shortcut — The matcher in `isAccessTokenId` extracts `substring(3, 5)` but the encoder's 2+2+2 layout puts the grant at indices 4-5, so the predicate compares the wrong field. Use `substring(4, 6)` to read the actual grant shortcut.

isAccessTokenId substring offset and predicate are inverted — `isAccessTokenId`'s comment, offset, and predicate disagree with the encoder's 2+2+2 layout where the grant occupies the last two chars. Realign the comment to `5th char`, slice `substring(4, 6)`, and invert the equality check.

isAccessTokenId must slice substring(4, 6) for grant-type field — `isAccessTokenId` reads `substring(3, 5)` while the encoder emits a 2-char session, 2-char token, and 2-char grant, placing the grant shortcut at indices 4-5. Switch to `substring(4, 6)` so the matcher inspects the real grant field.

isAccessTokenId returns false when grant shortcut matches, breaking token-id assertions — A token whose grant shortcut equals the expected value currently fails to match because `isAccessTokenId` returns false on equality, breaking `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, and `expectAuthReqIdToToken`. Return `isUUID().matches(items[1])` when grants match and false otherwise.

Constructor null check on rawTokenId mistakenly re-checks grantType — The second `requireNonNull` re-checks `grantType` instead of `rawTokenId`, letting a null reach `encodeTokenId` where `':' + getRawTokenId()` becomes `"null"`. Pass `rawTokenId` to the check instead.

Reader thread is never joined before assertion, so exceptions can be missed — Any NPE raised by an in-flight `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` call lands in `caughtExceptions` after `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` returns, so the test can pass while the bug it targets still happens. Capture the spawned `Thread reader`, call `reader.start()`, and add `reader.join()` between `deletedAll.set(true)` and the assertion, matching the repo's latch/join convention.

Test bypasses getSubGroupsCount() fix and never joins reader — Calling `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` with `briefRepresentation=true` typically skips subgroup-count computation, so `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` and its null-handling branch may never execute. Verify the brief path on `GroupAdapter`; if it skips the count, switch to a full-representation or per-group GET that forces it.
verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException — Rethrow as `MojoExecutionException` so callers and Maven see the documented type.

containsHtml misses uppercase HTML tags, wrongly applying POLICY_NO_HTML — `containsHtml()`'s regex `<[a-z]+[^>]*>` misses uppercase tags, so English sources with `<A HREF>` are misread as `POLICY_NO_HTML` and translations get flagged `Illegal HTML`. Compile the pattern with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE`.

**Also found in:**
- `misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:139-143`

substring wrap-around causes StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in verifySafeHtml — In `verifySafeHtml()` the independent forward `start` and backward `end` scans can both reach `value.length()`, making `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. Clamp `start` to `value.length() - end` before building the diagnostic message.

loginTotpStep1 has Italian text instead of Lithuanian translation — `loginTotpStep1` in `messages_lt.properties` currently holds Italian text, breaking the Lithuanian locale. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation consistent with neighbouring `_lt` entries.
totpStep1 uses Traditional Chinese characters in Simplified Chinese locale — Switch the wording to Simplified characters consistent with the surrounding entries.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: getClientsWithPermission leaks the 'Clients' type-resource name into callers — Filter out entries where `resource.getName()` equals `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`.

ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws on client removal under fine-grained authz — `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, yet the `AdminPermissions` listener calls it on `ClientRemovedEvent` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, so client removal in V2 mode always fails. Implement V2 cleanup there, or gate the listener to fire only under V1 via an `instanceof ClientPermissions` check.

ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ listener triggers V2 setPermissionsEnabled UnsupportedOperationException — `AdminPermissions`'s `ProviderEventListener` calls `setPermissionsEnabled(false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent` under `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`, but the V2 impl `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Restrict the branch to the legacy/V1 path with an extra V2 feature check so it skips V2.

ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate skipped V1 cleanup on role/client/group removal — Gating the three `AdminPermissions` cleanup listeners behind `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` silently breaks the V1 cleanup contract, leaving orphan permissions whenever the feature is off (the default). Keep the V1 handlers registered unconditionally and gate only the V2-only additions.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: PasswordForm.setups webauthn context even when user has no passkeys registered — `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` lets zero-passkey users through, so `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` leaks `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` onto the prior form and `login-password.ftl` renders a dead webauthn button. Guard `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` on a non-null result from `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`, or skip the call when no authenticators exist.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hard-coded empty columns and tableData — `TableWidgetVisualization` ignores the computed `fields`, `fieldAliases`, `eventView`, and `result.data`/`result.meta`, so every dashboard table widget renders blank. Wire those props through `TableWidgetVisualization` instead of hard-coded `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`.

Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization receives empty placeholder props — With `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, `<TableWidgetVisualization>` receives empty `columns` and `tableData` instead of the real `result.data`, `result.meta`, and `fieldAliases` already in scope, so every dashboard table renders blank. Pass those computed props through to `TableWidgetVisualization` the same way `StyledSimpleTableChart` gets them.

validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthy checks, accept age=0/timestamp=0 combo — `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` use truthy `.get()` checks, so a payload with `age=0` and `timestamp=0` slips past both and accepts a spec-violating report. Switch to explicit presence via `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: SpanFlusher.join leaks orphaned flusher processes when the deadline expires mid-loop — Each unvisited `process` after the deadline holds Redis connections and KafkaProducer clients until the parent exits. Split the loop so all `multiprocessing.Process` instances are terminated in a second pass over `self.processes.values()`.

Unused _create_process_for_shard misroutes single shard to whole-process restart — `_create_process_for_shard` has no callers and routes a single shard through `_create_process_for_shards`, misusing a whole-process restart. Wire it into the per-shard restart path or delete the dead helper.

Avoid calling get_memory_info() once per local SpansBuffer; they share cluster client — Repeating `buffer.get_memory_info()` per entry multiplies `cluster.info()` traffic across shared `SpansBuffer` clients. Call it once from a single buffer (e.g., `next(iter(self.buffers.values()))`) and reuse the result.

wait_produce timer uses tag key `shards` while sibling metrics use `shard` — The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer tags with `"shards"` while the other three metric sites use `"shard"`, silently splitting the dashboard series. Change `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` to `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` for that timer.

Use `is None` instead of truthiness check for max_processes default — `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` silently rewrites an explicit 0 into the shard count. Use `max_processes is None` to keep 0 as a real value and constrain the CLI option with a minimum.

Flusher shard distribution test only checks total count — Asserting only `total_shards == 4` lets a regression like `process_index = 0` starve a process while passing. Require every `process_to_shards_map` list to be non-empty and balanced within one shard.

SpansBuffer flush shard_factor uses per-process shard count instead of global — `shard_factor = max(1, len(self.assigned_shards))` is computed per process, so `max_flush_segments` multiplies by `num_processes`. Either divide by the global `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` or document that the setting is now per-process.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: AssignmentSource.queued default is a shared module-load timestamp — Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to record per-instance times.

Unsafe metadata access raises KeyError on legacy Integrations — Reading `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises `KeyError` for legacy `Integration` rows written under the prior metadata contract, surfacing as HTTP 500. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value as a mismatch, and ensure the metadata writer stores `sender.login` going forward.

Use constant_time_compare for OAuth state CSRF token check — The `!=` comparison leaks per-character timing of `pipeline.signature`, defeating the CSRF check. Replace it with `django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare` (already used in `auth/superuser.py` and `integrations/github/webhook.py`), passing empty strings when either side is `None`.

Helper passes bare-string error_short so xgettext never extracts it — `xgettext` only scans literals passed to recognized translation functions, so callers passing bare `error_short=` strings (and the default `"Invalid installation request."`) will never be extracted. Define module-level `_("...")` constants such as `ERR_INTEGRATION_PENDING_DELETION_SHORT` and use them as the `error_short` default and at call sites.

test_installation_not_found exercises OAuth state mismatch, not 404 branch — `test_installation_not_found` now exits at the `OAuthLoginView` state-mismatch check, so the `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch in `GitHubInstallation` never runs and the assertion stays green if it is removed. Drive the callback with the pipeline's real signature (stub the GitHub token exchange and pull `state` from the init step's redirect) so the test reaches `GitHubInstallation`.

OAuthLoginView: token-exchange network errors escape the try/except — `safe_urlopen` on the token-exchange call sits outside the surrounding `try/except Exception`, so `ReadTimeout`, `ConnectionError`, etc. from `SafeSession.request` bubble up as an HTTP 500 instead of the designed dialog. Move the call (along with `safe_urlread` and `parse_qsl`) inside the `try` block.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434-436`

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: Reintroduce duplicate detector group key detection instead of silent overwrite — The dict aggregation silently overwrites earlier results, losing state updates while still emitting a Kafka occurrence for the survivor. Reintroduce explicit duplicate detection in `process_detectors` or `evaluate`/`evaluate_group_key_value` to log 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' and pick a deterministic winner.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler missing build_occurrence_and_event_data implementation — `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` and its `@abc.abstractmethod` `build_occurrence_and_event_data` is unimplemented, so instantiation via `Detector.detector_handler` will raise `TypeError`. Add the method returning `(IssueOccurrence, dict[str, Any])` or drop the abstract inheritance until it is ready.

Wrong value passed to build_mock_occurrence_and_event for group_2 — Since `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores its `value` parameter, passing `6` still passes despite the data packet's `group_vals={"group_2": 10}`. Use the matching values (`10` here, `100` in `test_results_on_change`, `8` in `test_dedupe`) so the per-group_key contract gets verified once `value` propagates into the occurrence.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Dead config translation in get_monitor_environment_context — The function builds and rewrites a local `config` copy but returns the untouched `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, so the translation is dead. Switch the `"config"` value to the local `config` so the rewritten `schedule_type` actually reaches the monitor context.

Team collective destination calendars lost when primary calendar is null — Attendees lose team destinations and bookings fall back to a single calendar. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` from `teamDestinationCalendars` when it is `null` instead of gating `push` with optional chaining.

Hard-coded English calendar note bypasses localization — Attendees see English text regardless of locale. Wrap `calEvent.additionalNotes` with the translation helper used nearby like `getTranslation` instead of the hard-coded literal.

TypeError on undefined destinationCalendar in Google Meet fallback check — Bookings crash with a TypeError when no destination calendar exists. Guard `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` with optional chaining like `evt.destinationCalendar` previously did.

Inverted fallback makes selectedCalendar undefined when externalCalendarId falsy — The fallback never matches and leaves `selectedCalendar` undefined, so events land on the wrong calendar or fail. Resolve `externalCalendarId` from `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` instead of searching `destinationCalendar` for the falsy value.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:314-318`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:313-318`

Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED check sets slug on wrong path — Organizations get a direct `slug` when billing is enabled and break the request flow. Restore the `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` guard for `slug` so `requestedSlug` is used when the flag is on.

Calendar.createEvent credentialId breaks existing implementations — All calendar integrations fail type checks and keep writing to `destinationCalendar[0]`. Update `Calendar.createEvent` implementors to accept `credentialId` and select the matching `destinationCalendar` entry.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125-130`
- `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72-78`
- `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125-132`

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.
