For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Calendar sync uses caller credentials instead of organizer credentials — Using `ctx.user` credentials for `EventManager` means an attendee invite fails to update the organizer's `destinationCalendar`. Load credentials with `getUsersCredentials` for `booking.userId` instead.

DB attendees persisted before external calendar update without compensation — Persisting with `prisma.booking.update` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` leaves orphaned attendees if the calendar call fails. Update the calendar first or add compensation, following `editLocation.handler` ordering.

Organizer lookup throws unhandled 500 when booking.userId is null — When `booking.userId` is null, `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` with `|| 0` throws an unhandled 500. Check `booking.userId` first and throw a `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND` if missing, using `findFirst` instead.

Case-sensitive blacklist and duplicate checks allow bypass via casing — `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lowercased but `guest` and `attendee.email` comparisons stay case-sensitive, so `Admin@example.com` bypasses the block and duplicates slip in. Normalize both sides with `toLowerCase()` and `trim()` before checking `blacklistedGuestEmails` and `booking.attendees`.

Team permission check requires both admin and owner instead of either — Using `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` denies admins who aren't owners and vice versa. Change `isTeamAdminOrOwner` to use `||` to match the `||` pattern in `teams/get.handler` and `confirm.handler`.

Unguarded attendees[0].name access crashes email when attendees empty — An empty list makes `attendees[0].name` throw and the organizer email never sends. Guard `this.calEvent.attendees[0]?.name` and fall back to `this.calEvent.organizer.name`.

handleAdd sends empty and unnormalized emails without trimming/lowercasing — Empty strings and case-variant duplicates in `multiEmailValue` pass the client check but fail or duplicate on the server. Normalize with `trim()` and `toLowerCase()`, filter empty entries, and initialize `multiEmailValue` as `[]` before validation.

Unbounded guests array enables resource exhaustion — An unbounded `guests` array lets one request create many database rows and trigger many emails. Cap `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with `.max(25)` and enforce the same limit in the handler.

Race condition creates duplicate Attendee rows on concurrent addGuests — Concurrent calls compute `uniqueGuests` from stale `booking.attendees` and both `prisma.booking.update` with `createMany` insert duplicate rows. Use `prisma.$transaction` with `Serializable` isolation and `skipDuplicates` or add a unique index on `bookingId` and `email`.

Duplicate guest emails pass validation causing unique-constraint violation — Duplicate addresses in `guests` pass `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` and make `createMany` hit a unique-constraint error. Add a `.refine` that checks `new Set` size on lowercased and trimmed emails or dedupe with a `Set` before insert.

sendAddGuestsEmails uses unfiltered guests instead of uniqueGuests — Passing `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of `uniqueGuests` emails existing and blacklisted addresses as if new. Call `sendAddGuestsEmails` with `uniqueGuests` so its `newGuests.includes` check matches the persisted attendees.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Literal placeholder for missing refresh_token corrupts credential — Most providers omit `refresh_token` on refresh, so storing the literal corrupts the credential and the next refresh fails with `invalid_grant`. Preserve the existing token instead of hardcoding a placeholder, or delete the field as in the fix.

Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError in Salesforce CalendarService — The integration throws a `ReferenceError` at runtime on every construction because `prisma` is not defined in this file. Add an import for `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` or use a dynamic import as shown.

Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens — The sync endpoint receives the wrong identifier and cannot locate the correct credential because `credentialId` is passed where `userId` is expected. Pass `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens` instead of `credentialId` to match `calcomUserId` like other callers.

Malformed minimumTokenResponseSchema rejects all valid token refresh responses — When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` every valid response is rejected because `minimumTokenResponseSchema` requires literal `ZodString`/`ZodOptional` keys and strips unknowns. Replace the computed keys with `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` as in the fix.

Google credential update persists SafeParseResult wrapper instead of data — The stored `key` becomes the wrapper `{success, data, error}` so later credential use fails. Unwrap the `parseRefreshTokenResponse` result, check `success`, and persist only `data` before `prisma.credential.update`.

Lark refresh validates sync OAuth response as Lark envelope and fails — Sync responses contain `access_token` not the Lark `{code, msg}` envelope, so `handleLarkError` always throws. Branch on the shape: only call `handleLarkError` for `code`-bearing payloads and normalize `access_token` responses separately.

Sync branch returns fetch Response instead of provider token shape — Callers like Google read `token.access_token` via `res.data`, so a raw `Response` causes `TypeError` and breaks sync for all providers. Parse `fetch` JSON and normalize to `{data, ...token}` so `refreshOAuthTokens` matches provider shapes.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-189`
- `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-94`
- `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204-217`
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-97`

Unauthenticated credential sync fetch allows arbitrary token injection — A compromised or spoofed sync endpoint can inject arbitrary `access_token` values that are then trusted for any `userId`/`appSlug`. Sign the `fetch` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and validate the response strictly.

TOCTOU race in app-credential webhook causes duplicates or unhandled P2002 — Concurrent webhooks for the same `userId`/`appId` both see no row and try to create, causing duplicates or an unhandled `P2002`. Use an atomic `upsert` on `userId_appId` with fallback handling for `P2002` instead of `findFirst` then `create`.

Webhook secret compared with !== allows timing attack — Direct `!==` comparison leaks the secret through timing differences. Compare `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after length-check and buffering.

Insecure fallback to empty string for credential encryption key — A missing `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` falls back to `""`, so decryption proceeds with an empty AES key. Fail fast with a 500 when the key is unset instead of calling `symmetricDecrypt` with a default.

Salesforce connection uses stale tokens instead of refreshed access token — The database is updated but the returned `jsforce.Connection` still uses the expired `credentialKey` tokens, so calls fail until next instantiation. Build the connection from `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`/`instance_url` with fallback to `credentialKey`.

Unhandled parse/decrypt exceptions crash webhook with 500 instead of 400 — Invalid bodies or bad `keys` payloads throw `ZodError`/`SyntaxError` and surface as 500s. Use `safeParse` for `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema` and wrap `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` in try/catch to return 400 on failure.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:56-60`

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: SMS retry cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders due to missing method filter — Any `EMAIL` or `WHATSAPP` reminder with `retryCount` > 1 gets deleted alongside SMS. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that `retryCount` branch to keep cleanup SMS-only.

Empty message or missing recipient skips retry increment causing infinite retry — The reminder is re-fetched every cron run and never ages out toward deletion. Increment `retryCount` in the skipped `message`/`sendTo` branch so it can eventually be pruned.

Stale retryCount increment overwrites concurrent updates — Concurrent runs can overwrite each other and keep `retryCount` stuck at 1 so cleanup never triggers. Switch both updates from `reminder.retryCount + 1` to atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

Unhandled error in catch-block update aborts SMS reminder loop — A transient failure of `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` aborts the loop and skips remaining reminders. Wrap that update in its own try/catch and log instead of rethrowing so iteration continues.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup codes Blob URL never revoked on close/unmount leaks memory — Every repeated setup leaks a `Blob` URL and retains memory for the page lifetime. Revoke `backupCodesUrl` with `URL.revokeObjectURL` in a cleanup effect and in `resetState`/onClose, or switch to a data URL.

Backup-code branch throws on missing encryption key instead of 500 JSON — Uncaught throw crashes the request instead of returning JSON like other branches. Return `res.status(500).json()` with `ErrorCode.InternalServerError` when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing.

Default export name TwoFactor mismatches BackupCode file and import — Mismatched name confuses DevTools and collides with the real `TwoFactor` component. Rename the default export to `BackupCode` to match the filename and import.

Required backupCode param breaks existing 2-arg disable callers — Callers in `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` and the duplicate `TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts` still call `disable` with two arguments and will break. Make `backupCode` optional or update the consumers to the new three-argument contract.

Backup code download only checks filename, not file content — Checking only `suggestedFilename` misses empty or corrupted downloads. Read the file via `download.path()` and assert it contains 10 lines matching the backup code format and the decrypted codes.

Backup code copy check only verifies toast, not clipboard — Toast alone doesn't prove `navigator.clipboard` was written. Grant `clipboard-read`, read with `navigator.clipboard.readText()` via `page.evaluate` and assert it equals the joined codes.

Backup-code login bypasses password verification via dummy totpCode — Attacker can add a dummy `credentials.totpCode` to skip the password check and log in with only a `credentials.backupCode`. Verify `credentials.password` with `verifyPassword` before entering the backup-code branch regardless of `totpCode`.

Backup code can be reused via race and leaves null holes — Concurrent use of the same `backupCodes` entry can both succeed before the write, and `null` holes leak remaining count. Remove the entry with `splice` and make the check-and-update atomic with `updateMany` or a transaction on `prisma.user`.

backupCode.replaceAll assumes string and throws TypeError on non-string input — Non-string `req.body.backupCode` throws `TypeError` on `replaceAll` instead of returning `IncorrectBackupCode`. Validate `typeof`, trim, and length before `indexOf` and return 400 on invalid type.

Backup code verification uses non-constant-time indexOf comparison — `indexOf` with early exit leaks timing information about the correct code. Compare all `backupCodes` with `timingSafeEqual` on fixed-length buffers without early return.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58-64`

Backup code validation is case-sensitive and rejects uppercase input — Generator stores lowercase hex, so uppercase input incorrectly fails validation. Normalize `credentials.backupCode` with `toLowerCase()` and `trim()` after `replaceAll` before lookup.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:60-63`

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: Public options type allows team scope without teamId — A missing `teamId` silently passes type-checking and later returns no rows via `1=0`, hiding caller bugs. Restore `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` as a discriminated union requiring `teamId` only for `scope: "team"`.

Falsy filter IDs (0) silently ignored due to truthiness check — A filter value of `0` for `eventTypeId` or `memberUserId` is dropped, returning broader results than intended. Check `this.filters` with `!= null` in `buildFilterConditions` instead of truthiness.

Combined auth+filter test lacks negative cases and allows OR bug — The test passes even if `getBaseConditions` uses `OR` or drops a condition entirely. Add bookings that match only auth and only filter and assert only the doubly-matching one is returned.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Embed crashes with TypeError when #discourse-comments is missing — `comments` is null when the container is absent, so `comments.appendChild` throws and the whole embed script stops. Guard `comments` with an early return before creating `iframe`.

XSS via unescaped request.referer in postMessage targetOrigin — An attacker-crafted Referer breaks out of the single-quoted string and executes script in the embed context. Escape `request.referer` with `j` and pass only its origin to `postMessage`.

Unsafe Kernel.open on feed URL enables SSRF and command execution — `open` on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` can reach internal hosts and execute commands via leading `|`. Switch to `URI.parse` with an http/https allowlist and fetch via `URI.open` or `Net::HTTP` with timeouts.
PostRevisor crashes when TopicEmbed post was deleted — `embed.post` is nil after deletion, so `PostRevisor.new` raises. Guard with `post.present?` and recreate or skip the update.

Unbounded RSS feed iteration imports every item on each poll — Processing every `rss.items` triggers a `TopicEmbed.import` transaction per entry and overloads the hourly job on large feeds. Cap the iteration to recent items and skip already-imported URLs.

TopicEmbed.import_remote uses Kernel.open without open-uri and raises ENOENT — Plain `open` without `open-uri` treats the URL as a local file and raises `ENOENT` on a cold worker. Require `open-uri` and `digest/sha1` here and fetch with `URI.open` with rescued network errors.

absolutize_urls raises URI::InvalidURIError and aborts import — An invalid URL that passes the regex makes `URI` raise `URI::InvalidURIError` and aborts the whole import. Rescue in `absolutize_urls` and return `contents` unchanged for that item.

Dead code: feed_key computed but never used, feed fetched unconditionally — `feed_key` is computed but never read, so the intended conditional fetch never happens and the feed is polled every run. Remove the dead method or wire it to an `If-Modified-Since` check.

Hard-coded strftime %b forces English month names, ignores locale — `strftime` with `%b` always renders English months regardless of locale. Replace `post.created_at` formatting with `I18n.l` and a locale `format`.

Unescaped URL in embed link enables XSS with raw_html — `url` is interpolated into HTML without escaping and stored as `raw_html`, so characters like `<` break markup and enable XSS. Escape `url` with `ERB::Util.html_escape` before building the `I18n.t` link.

perform_retrieve races past exists? checks and bubbles unhandled network errors — `perform_retrieve` races past `exists?` and lets `open` errors from `fetch_http` bubble up and fail the job. Rescue `OpenURI::HTTPError`, `SocketError` and `URI::InvalidURIError` around `PollFeed` and `fetch_http` and handle `RecordNotUnique`.

Falsy height 0 ignored due to truthiness check in resize handler — `e.data.height` of `0` is falsy and skips the resize, so a collapsed embed never shrinks. Check `typeof e.data.height` against `undefined` and `null` instead of truthiness.

feed_polling_url test not isolated from other preconditions — `feed_polling_enabled?` stays false in this test, so `poll_feed` is blocked regardless of `feed_polling_url`. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` and `embed_by_username` to present to isolate the URL check.

embed_by_username test is vacuous without stubbing other required settings — `feed_polling_enabled?` and `feed_polling_url` remain falsy, so `poll_feed` never runs even without the username check. Stub both to truthy values to make the test fail only for `embed_by_username`.

Spec mocks TopicRetriever instead of actual Jobs.enqueue side effect — The controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue` for `:retrieve_topic`, so mocking `TopicRetriever` never verifies the real side effect. Expect `Jobs.enqueue` with `embed_url` instead.

Stubbed retrieved_recently? hides broken redis throttle and no_throttle — Stubbing `retrieved_recently?` bypasses the real `$redis` throttle, so a broken `setnx`/`expire` logic goes undetected. Exercise `retrieve` with a fake `$redis` and verify `perform_retrieve` and `no_throttle` behavior directly.

Insecure postMessage origin validation allows bypass via substring match — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` accepts any substring match, so an attacker origin contained in `discourseUrl` passes. Compare `e.origin` with strict equality to the normalized `discourseUrl`.

postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer URL so browser drops message — `request.referer` includes the path, so the `parent.postMessage` targetOrigin never matches `e.origin` and the browser drops the resize. Send only the origin from `URI.parse(request.referer)` or `*`.

PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on nil RSS item content — `i.content` can be nil, so `i.content.scrub` raises and crashes the job with no retry. Coalesce `i.content` or `i.description` to a string with `to_s` before scrubbing and ensure `i.title` is stringified.

Stored XSS via unsanitized raw_html bypass in Post#cook — Returning `raw` for `cook_method` `raw_html` stores unsanitized HTML that `post.cooked` renders verbatim, enabling stored XSS from a feed. Sanitize `raw` through `WhiteListSanitizer` in `cook` or at import.

TOCTOU race in TopicEmbed.import allows duplicate topics on concurrent imports — The `where(embed_url:)` check and `TopicEmbed.create!` can both succeed concurrently, raising `RecordNotUnique` and leaving duplicate topics. Wrap `Topic.transaction` with a rescue for `RecordNotUnique` and reload the existing `TopicEmbed`.

**Also found in:**
- `app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-30`

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Embed category fallback to SiteSetting lost when host not found — Topics created from unknown hosts get a `nil` category instead of the configured default. Fall back to `SiteSetting.embed_category` when `eh.try(:category_id)` is `nil` for `PostCreator`.

Host lookup lowercases column but not parameter, missing uppercase hosts — Uppercase referrers like `EVILTROUT.COM` never match the lowercased column. Downcase the parameter with `host.downcase` or use `lower(?)` in the `where` clause.

Case-sensitive scheme stripping and host lookup reject uppercase hosts — `HTTP://` prefixes are not stripped and uppercase referrers fail the lookup, incorrectly rejecting valid embeds. Use a case-insensitive `/^https?:\/\//i` and downcase the lookup param with `host.downcase`.

**Also found in:**
- `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-18`

Embeddable hosts migration stores raw URLs instead of normalized hostnames — Migrated hosts with schemes or paths never match `host_allowed?` lookups against normalized hostnames. Normalize `h` like `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` does or create records through the model so callbacks run.

Unchecked category lookup crashes migration with NoMethodError on nil — An empty `site_settings` result makes `[0]['id']` raise `NoMethodError` and abort the migration. Check for an empty result before indexing and fall back to `uncategorized_category_id`.

Unsafe [0] access on empty query result raises NoMethodError — When the category query returns no rows, `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` crashes the migration. Guard the result with a nil check or safe navigation before calling `[]` and `to_i`.

Plural _hydrateEmbedded maps misses to [undefined] with dead fallback — Missing ids from `_lookupSubType` pollute embedded arrays with `undefined` and the `hydrated || []` fallback never runs. Filter falsy results from the `map` and assign `hydrated` directly.

Singular _hydrateEmbedded leaks *_id key when hydration fails — Failed lookups leave stale `*_id` keys like `category_id` that pollute attributes passed to `klass.munge` and `_build`. Move `delete obj[k]` outside the `if (hydrated)` so it always runs.

Plural _ids hydration throws TypeError on null/non-array value — A `null` or missing `*_ids` value throws a `TypeError` on `obj[k].map` during hydration. Guard `obj[k]` with an `Array.isArray` check and fall back to `[]` before mapping.

expandable_first_post? returns true without embeddable_hosts configured — Posts appear expandable even when embedding is not configured, breaking the previous contract. Restore the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check in `expandable_first_post?`.

Blank-host test for expandable_first_post? is vacuous — The test always passes even if `expandable_first_post?` is broken because it never enables truncation or embedding. Set `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` to `true` and stub `has_topic_embed?` to `true` before asserting `false` with no hosts.

Update and destroy allow nil host causing 500 instead of 404 — A missing `id` makes `host` `nil` and `save_host`/`host.destroy` raise `NoMethodError` as a 500. Guard `host` and raise `Discourse::NotFound` before saving or destroying.

Nil host raises NoMethodError in before_validation callback — A `nil` or blank `host` crashes `before_validation` on `self.host.sub!` before validation can run. Guard the callback with `self.host.present?` or `to_s` before stripping.

Single underscore replace fails to normalize multi-underscore admin types — Types with multiple underscores are not normalized and `basePath` incorrectly returns `/`. Change `type.replace('_', '-')` to a global replace with `/_/g`.

SQL injection via string interpolation of host in migration INSERT — A host value containing a quote breaks the `INSERT` and allows SQL injection during the migration. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` or a parameterized `execute` for `h`.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: SVGs incorrectly routed to bitmap downsize and rasterized — `FileHelper.is_image?` returns true for SVGs, so `OptimizedImage.downsize` rasterizes vectors through ImageMagick and corrupts them instead of preserving them like `Upload.create_for` does. Exclude `.svg` files from the bitmap downsize guard.

Duplicate self.downsize definition overwrites 5-arg overload — The second `downsize` definition overwrites the first, so callers like `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` passing five arguments now raise `ArgumentError`. Merge them into a single variadic method that builds `WxH` when given two dimensions.

Downsize loop ignores failure and burns up to 5 blocking conversions — When `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails the file never shrinks but the loop still runs five expensive blocking conversions on the request thread. Check its return value and `tempfile.size` and break when it fails or stops decreasing.

Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores per-type SiteSettings max_size — A fixed `maxSizeKB` ignores `Discourse.SiteSettings` per-type limits, so uploads are incorrectly allowed or blocked and the error shows the wrong size. Restore the lookup for `max_${type}_size_kb` instead of hardcoding 10MB.

Invalid 80% geometry makes OptimizedImage.downsize silently fail — `OptimizedImage.downsize` receives `80%`, which produces an invalid `convert -resize` and `gifsicle --resize-fit` geometry and fails silently without shrinking the file. Compute explicit `WxH` dimensions from `FastImage.size` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `app/models/optimized_image.rb:149-151`

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description:
add_members requires :group_id but route provides :id causing ParameterMissing — Requests from `Discourse.Group` hit `config/routes.rb` with `:id`, so `params.require(:group_id)` always raises `ParameterMissing`. Require `:id` in `add_members` (and `remove_member`) to match the member route.

**Also found in:**
- `config/routes.rb:49-50`

findMembers returns undefined instead of promise when name is empty — Callers chaining `.then` on `findMembers` will throw when `name` is empty because `undefined` is not a promise. Return `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to keep the promise contract.

Automatic group delete guard reads member context instead of group — Automatic groups incorrectly show the delete control because `automatic` resolves against `member` where it is always falsy. Resolve the flag from the group via the parent view/controller instead of the bare `automatic`.

Wrong HTTP verb in remove_member spec (PUT instead of DELETE) — The test never exercises the real route defined in `config/routes.rb` so a broken `DELETE` endpoint would go undetected. Change `xhr :put` to `xhr :delete` for `remove_member` to match the actual mapping.

Add_members automatic group test checks status only, not membership — A misplaced guard could mutate membership yet still return `422` and the test would pass. Reload `Group` after the request and assert `users.count` is unchanged.

Off-by-one in totalPages when user_count divisible by limit — An exact multiple of `limit` creates a phantom empty page and lets `next()` advance past the data. Compute `totalPages` with `Math.ceil` on `user_count`/`limit` instead of `Math.floor` plus one.

Unvalidated limit/offset allows zero and unbounded pagination — A `limit` of `0` breaks pagination math and SQL while a huge value is unbounded, yielding empty or heavy queries. Clamp `limit` to `1..200` and `offset` to `>=0` before use.

Next pagination offset allows empty last page when count divisible by limit — When `user_count` is a multiple of `limit`, `next()` can step to `user_count` and show an empty page. Cap `offset` at the last valid start `(Math.ceil(user_count/limit)-1)*limit`.

**Also found in:**
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23-24`

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls to_sym on nil/blank default_locale — When `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil or empty, `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises or yields `:""` that bypasses `compact` and breaks `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. Guard `FallbackLocaleList#[]` with `presence` before `to_sym` so only a real locale enters the fallback chain.

Synchronous ensure_loaded! in set_locale blocks Puma threads — Holding the global `LOAD_MUTEX` and scanning `I18n.load_path` inside `set_locale` serializes Puma threads and blocks the request on file I/O during cold starts. Deduplicate with a memoized guard around `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` or preload supported locales at boot.

Cache poisoning stores missing translation before fallbacks loaded — A `translation-missing` string from `translate_no_cache` gets frozen into `@cache` when fallbacks aren't loaded, so later hits keep returning the poisoned value. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded in `translate` before caching and avoid caching missing translations.

I18n translate skips fallback chain causing missing translations — Outside `ApplicationController#set_locale`, `translate` loads only `config.locale` via `load_locale`, so jobs and mailers miss site-default and `:en` fallbacks and return missing strings. Load the full chain in `ensure_loaded!`/`translate` by iterating `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` and calling `ensure_loaded!` for each.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Premature cache insertion bypasses device limit enforcement — A blocked device gets cached as successful, so the next request skips the limit check in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` and is incorrectly allowed. Move `SetDefault` on `localCache` to after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds instead of before it.

updateDevice BETWEEN window uses device.UpdatedAt instead of time.Now() — Mismatched active windows let a counted device miss the update and incorrectly return `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, or let an expired device match. Build the window in `updateDevice` from `time.Now()` like `CreateOrUpdateDevice` does, not from `device.UpdatedAt`.

Anonymous device tagging bypass via cancellable request context — A client disconnect cancels `ctx`, so `TagDevice` returns `context.Canceled` and `Authenticate` still returns success without counting the device, letting the limit be bypassed. Tag with `context.WithoutCancel` plus a timeout, or treat cancellation as a tagging failure instead of success.

Synchronous TagDevice blocks anonymous auth and fails on device limit — Anonymous auth previously never failed and had no DB latency, but now every call blocks on `TagDevice` and can be rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, breaking callers that expect success. Keep tagging async best-effort in `Authenticate` or update `authn.Service` to explicitly handle that error.

TOCTOU race between CountDevices and insert bypasses device limit — Concurrent logins can both see `CountDevices` below `deviceLimit` and then insert, so the limit is exceeded because the check and insert are not atomic. Enforce the limit atomically with a transaction and locking or a single conditional insert, as checked against `database.go`.

Synchronous TagDevice blocks anonymous auth on hot path — Every anonymous login now waits for `TagDevice` DB work, so a slow database stalls all anonymous auth on this path. Make `Authenticate` non-blocking again by tagging in a background goroutine with a timeout and handling `ErrDeviceLimitReached` there.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit lacks existing device update check — The test would still pass if `updateDevice` incorrectly rejected existing devices at the limit, leaving the update path uncovered. Extend `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` to re-tag the original `DeviceID` and assert `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds and the row remains.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Cache corrupted with nil on failed asset load — A transient failure overwrites a valid `entryPointAssetsCache` with `nil` and poisons all later reads. Only assign `entryPointAssetsCache = result` when `err == nil` and `result != nil`.

Exclusive RWMutex held across blocking file and HTTP I/O — `GetWebAssets` serves the hot frontend path, so holding `entryPointAssetsCacheMu` across `readWebAssetsFromFile`/`readWebAssetsFromCDN` stalls every concurrent request. Compute the `result` outside the lock and only acquire it to publish `entryPointAssetsCache`.

Global cache leaks per-request CDN prefix across orgs — The first caller's CDN prefix baked via `SetContentDeliveryURL` is returned to every later org, serving wrong asset URLs. Key `entryPointAssetsCache` by `license.ContentDeliveryPrefix()` or cache unprefixed assets and apply `GetContentDeliveryURL` on a per-request copy.

Missing double-checked locking and cache clobbered with nil on failure — Without a second check after acquiring `entryPointAssetsCacheMu`, concurrent callers duplicate work and a failed load can clobber a good `entryPointAssetsCache` with `nil`. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` under the write lock and only publish `result` when `err == nil`.

FromContext panics on nil logger and discards context on fallback — A nil `d.l` crashes and falling back to `d.New()` drops the plugin name so logs lose correlation. Check `d.l` for nil in `FromContext` and return `d` or a wrapped logger that preserves context instead.

Shared MetricsMiddleware instance races on next client assignment — Concurrent decorations overwrite the shared `imw.next` so requests can be routed to the wrong `next` client. Create a fresh `MetricsMiddleware` per `NewMetricsMiddleware` call by copying fields and setting `next` instead of mutating the singleton.

Nil request dereference panic in ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods — A nil `req` makes `instrumentContext` dereference `req.PluginContext` and crash `QueryData` and the other endpoints. Add a `req == nil` guard that delegates to `next` as `LoggerMiddleware` does.

TestLogger.FromContext returns new instance instead of receiver — Calls go to a fresh `NewTestLogger()` so assertions on the injected `TestLogger` see zero `Calls` and hide broken logging. Make `FromContext` return `f` or a wrapper that shares `Calls`, as used in `logger_middleware.go`.

Async legacy Create uses original object losing storage-defaulted fields — The legacy copy loses server-defaulted fields like `UID` and `ResourceVersion` and permanently diverges if fallback is needed. Pass the storage-returned `created` object to `d.Legacy.Create` and reuse `res` via a wrapper for `d.Legacy.Update` instead of `obj`/`objInfo`.

Legacy async create derives timeout from cancelled request context — The derived timeout is immediately cancelled when the request `ctx` returns, so legacy `Create`/`Update`/`Delete` almost never runs and stores drift. Derive the timeout from `context.WithoutCancel` or `context.Background` instead of the request `ctx` in `context.WithTimeoutCause`.

Nil CreateOptions dereference panics in DualWriterMode3 Create — Callers may pass nil `options` or `listOptions`, so dereferencing `options.Kind` panics on every mode-3 write/read. Guard `options` and `listOptions` for nil before logging and default `Kind` to an empty string.

Unbounded fire-and-forget goroutines for legacy writes in mode 3 — Burst writes can exhaust memory and crash Prometheus as each legacy copy grows goroutines and cardinality without limit. Bound the goroutines with a queue or semaphore and record legacy duration using `options.Kind`.

Create error test targets legacy mock instead of unified store — The test passes accidentally because `ls` and `us` share the same `mock.Mock` and `mock.Anything` matches either store. Set up `storageMock` to return the error in `setupStorageFn` and use separate mocks instead of `setupLegacyFn`.

Global prometheus registry reuse causes duplicate collector panic — The second `NewDualWriter` call panics when the shared global `p` tries to register duplicate collectors. Create a fresh `prometheus.NewRegistry` inside each `t.Run` as `TestMode3_Get` does.

Create failure records legacy duration instead of storage duration — Storage errors are hidden and legacy dashboards are polluted because the failure is recorded against the wrong store. Call `d.recordStorageDuration` with `startStorage` on the storage error path instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-132`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-130`

DualWriterMode3 Delete metrics use wrong kind and swapped storage/legacy series — Deletion reports the object `name` as the kind and conflates storage and legacy latencies. Use `options.Kind` in `Delete`'s `d.recordStorageDuration` success path and call `d.recordLegacyDuration` for the `DeleteCollection` legacy callback.

Delete success path uses object name instead of kind for metric label — Using `name` as the kind label creates per-object series that can OOM Prometheus and mislabels the kind. Record both branches with `options.Kind` via `d.recordStorageDuration`, guarding for nil `options`.

Delete success metric uses object name instead of options.Kind — The success and error branches never join the same metric series because one uses `name` and the other uses `options.Kind`. Change the success `d.recordStorageDuration` call to use `options.Kind` as well.

DeleteCollection legacy latency recorded as storage metric — Legacy delete-collection latency is inverted into the storage histogram and hides real storage results. Call `d.recordLegacyDuration` with `startLegacy` in the `DeleteCollection` callback instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.

TestMode3_Update does not verify async legacy Update was called — The success expectation on `Legacy.Update` is never verified because the call is now async, so removing the dual-write still passes. Use separate mocks for `Storage` and `Legacy` and wait with a deadline to assert the legacy call was made.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:17-78`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:189-241`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Synchronous Init blocks startup without timeout and poisons server on failure — Startup can hang forever building the index and a transient `GetResourceStats`/`ListIterator` failure permanently poisons `s.initErr` because `sync.Once` never retries. Wrap `s.Init` in a timeout, call `s.cancel` on error and reset `s.once`/`s.initErr` or make init retryable.

NewResourceServer synchronously blocks on Init and hard-fails — Callers expect `NewResourceServer` to return immediately with best-effort init, but now pay full `GetResourceStats` index-build latency and must handle a nil server. Restore background `s.Init` with `go` or add a timeout and update all callers for failable blocking construction.

Watcher started after search init misses writes during index build — Writes occurring while the index builds are lost and the search index goes stale. Start `s.initWatcher` before `s.search.init` to buffer events, or otherwise buffer writes during the build.

Integration test vacuously passes on postgres due to unconditional skip — The `t.Skip` hides real failures for `StorageServer` on Drone where `dbType` is postgres, so a broken `/metrics` server still looks green. Remove the skip once `pkg/server/module_server_test.go` is fixed for postgres or replace it with a postgres-aware readiness check.

Concurrent BuildIndex race leaks index and increments metric on error — Concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same `NamespacedResource` both create Bleve indexes via `bleve.New` and the loser leaks its handle while `IndexTenants` increments even on error. Guard the cache-miss check with `b.cacheMu` or a per-key lock/singleflight and only bump metrics after success.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:96-104`

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Federated rules lose immutability due to hardcoded false — Federated groups would become editable and deletable despite being immutable. Restore the `isFederated` check using `isFederatedRuleGroup` instead of hardcoding `false` so `immutableRule` includes it.

TypeError on empty Prometheus groups crashes rule list view — An empty response throws a `TypeError` and blanks the list view. Guard `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` with optional chaining on `.map` or fallback to `[]` before mapping.

Non-Grafana rules incorrectly gain Duplicate via Grafana permission OR — Data source and cloud rules incorrectly show Duplicate when Grafana create is allowed. Gate the Grafana branch on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule` or make `skipToken` return `[NotSupported, false]` so `canDuplicate` doesn't OR in `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`.

Grafana pause/delete menu items hidden in list view by rulerRule guard — Pause and Delete stay hidden in the list view even when Grafana permissions allow them. Allow `canPause`/`canDelete` to render from `promRule` via `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule` or update `rulerRule` guards and `MenuItemPauseRule` to accept `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`.

Silence drawer gated on ruler rule blocks prom-only Grafana rules — Silence never opens for prom-only Grafana rules even when allowed. Make `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` accept `promRule` or gate `showSilenceDrawer` on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)` instead of `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`.

RBAC tests assert buttons absent while mocking permission granted — Inverted expectations let the suite pass even if permission checks are removed. Mock `useIsRuleEditable` as not editable/removable for `not.toBeInTheDocument` or assert `toBeInTheDocument` when mocking granted and cover both branches.

More button test never opens menu or verifies action items — The test passes even if `AlertRuleMenu` hides or shows wrong actions. Click `moreButton` and assert the menu via `byRole` and its items like `silence`, `duplicate`, and `export` under different permissions.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Context grantType NPE on null formParams and missing copy constructor — Cloning `Context` no longer compiles and any null `formParams` crashes before `UNKNOWN` fallback applies. Guard `formParams` with a null check for `grantType` and restore the `Context(Context)` copy constructor.

Invalid token ID decoding throws 500 instead of returning UNKNOWN context — Invalid or unknown `encodedContext` bubbles as an unhandled `IllegalArgumentException` and surfaces as 500 during introspection/revocation. Return an `UNKNOWN` `AccessTokenContext` for bad length or unknown shortcuts instead of throwing, and handle unknown `grantType` in `encodeTokenId` without `IllegalStateException`.

Non-atomic lazy update of grant shortcut maps races and breaks invariant — Concurrent requests for the same unknown grant can insert duplicate shortcuts and violate the size invariant checked in `postInit`. Replace the check-then-act on `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` with `computeIfAbsent`/`putIfAbsent` as shown.

Abstract getShortcut() breaks SPI backward compatibility — Existing custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations will fail to compile or throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime. Make `getShortcut()` a `default` method returning `"na"` and rely on the `UNKNOWN` fallback in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider`.

Off-by-one substring in isAccessTokenId extracts wrong grantType characters — `isAccessTokenId` never validates the actual grant and mismatches `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` which encodes `grantType` at 4-6. Use `items[0].substring(4, 6)` and negate the comparison so only the expected shortcut passes.

Incorrect grant shortcut offset and inverted check in isAccessTokenId — Wrong offset makes `isAccessTokenId` check the tail of `tokenType` plus one char of the grant, so validation disagrees with encoding. Change to `items[0].substring(4, 6)` with a length guard and reject on mismatch to match the `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` contract.

Inverted grant-shortcut comparison rejects correct token IDs — `isAccessTokenId` accepts every wrong grant and rejects the correct one, so the test never catches mismatched tokens. Negate the check to `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` and fix the offset to 4,6.

getSubGroupsCount returns null for deleted group violating Never-null contract — This risks unboxing NPEs and inconsistent API responses, diverging from `isUpdated()` which throws `IllegalStateException`. Make deleted-group handling consistent in `getSubGroupsCount` and add the same null guard to `getSubGroupsStream` overloads that dereference `modelSupplier.get()` directly.

**Also found in:**
- `model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:271-275`

Background reader thread not joined before assert leaks and busy-spins — Exceptions added after `assertThat` are missed and the `Thread` leaks beyond the test while busy-spinning on `deletedAll`. Join the reader with a timeout before checking `caughtExceptions` and add a sleep/backoff in the loop.

Missing English bundle throws unchecked exception crashing mojo — The build crashes instead of reporting a diagnostic because `verify()` only declares `MojoExecutionException` for the other path. Wrap the `IOException` for `bundleEnglish` as `MojoExecutionException` or add to `messages` and return.

JS placeholder mismatch: {{}} vs ChoiceFormat {} breaks plural and translations — The JS formatter does not understand Java `ChoiceFormat` so the plural never resolves and users see raw choice syntax. Keep `{{}}` interpolation for `error-invalid-multivalued-size` and check `messages_es.properties`, `messages_pl.properties`, and `messages_nl.properties` for mismatched placeholders, or update them together with a JS plural.

English ChoiceFormat plural not propagated to other locale files — Other locales will show the wrong plural or stale fallback because they still ship `value(s)` without a choice form. Propagate the `ChoiceFormat` for `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to all login/admin `messages_*.properties` as done for `messages_sk.properties`, or document the plural key.

Regex character class hyphen interpreted as range breaks hyphenated locales — Hyphenated locales never map to `_en.properties` so `bundleEnglish` compares a file to itself and misses illegal HTML. Move or escape the hyphen in the `replaceAll` pattern, e.g. `[a-zA-Z_-]*` or `[-a-zA-Z_]*`.

santizeAnchors fails on duplicates, order, whitespace and misses fewer anchors — Translations with duplicate or reordered anchors trigger false mismatches and stripped tags remain, while missing anchors go undetected. Collect anchors from `santizeAnchors` with `ANCHOR_PATTERN` into normalized multisets, compare them, and strip via `appendReplacement` with `key`/`file` in the diagnostic.

Wrong language: Italian string in Lithuanian messages bundle — Lithuanian users will see Italian text because `loginTotpStep1` in `messages_lt.properties` does not match its locale. Replace it with the Lithuanian string and check `account/messages_lt.properties` for the same mismatch.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties:101-101`

Illegal HTML diff trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — `value.substring` can throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when overlapping prefix/suffix makes `start` exceed `value.length()-end` and `sanitized.length()-end`. Cap `end` so `start+end` stays below both lengths before slicing `value` and `sanitized`.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: Missing resourceId check allows cross-client permission bypass — A scope granted on one client can authorize a different client because the loop ignores `permission.getResourceId()`. Filter by `resource.getId()` equals `permission.getResourceId()` as in `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` before checking scopes.

ClientPermissionsV2 setPermissionsEnabled throws aborting cleanup on removal — Any `ClientRemovedEvent` aborts the transaction because `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now calls `setPermissionsEnabled` which throws. Make `setPermissionsEnabled` a no-op in `ClientPermissionsV2` as it has no per-client flag.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77-92`
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:74-96`

Per-client resource lookup uses wrong owner ID and misses permissions — Valid per-client grants are never found and are incorrectly denied because `resourceStore.findByName` uses `server.getId()` as owner. Use `server.getClientId()` or the 2-arg `findByName` in `hasPermission` to match `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:237-247`

getClientsWithPermission includes generic Clients resource as fake clientId — Callers expecting only real IDs will receive a spurious `Clients` entry and misbehave. Skip the resource where `resource.getName()` equals `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` before checking `hasGrantedPermission`.

O(N) per-resource permission evaluation without batching or caching — Realms with many clients pay a per-resource `root.evaluatePermission` call that hits policy stores repeatedly. Batch the evaluation or cache the `EvaluationContext` in `getClientsWithPermission` instead of calling `hasGrantedPermission` per iteration.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Re-auth conditional passkeys allow cross-user discoverable credential — A discoverable credential from a different user can satisfy re-authentication and bypass its intent. Restrict `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` to when `context.getUser()` is null or verify the credential belongs to that user in `action()`.

Re-auth hidden username lost due to new LoginFormsProvider instance — The challenged form loses its hidden state and renders the username field during re-auth. Reuse the single `LoginFormsProvider` from `context.form()` across `fillContextForm` and `challenge` so attributes stay together.

PasswordForm.configuredFor uses wrong realm and can NPE on null context — `configuredFor` checking `session.getContext().getRealm()` instead of the `realm` parameter returns the wrong state and throws when context is null. Check `realm.getWebAuthnPolicyPasswordless()` directly and guard `session.getContext()` and `getAuthenticationSession()` for null.

Stale getForLogin cache not invalidated on org linkage changes — Users see wrong login brokers until expiry because `getForLogin` remains cached after linkage changes outside `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`. Invalidate the login cache in `InfinispanOrganizationProvider` on link/unlink/disable and add `isInvalid` checks for `organizationId` as shown.

Organization-aware isEnabled incorrectly used for login cache invalidation — Login cache invalidation can be skipped because `getById` returns a wrapped model whose `isEnabled` includes `OrganizationModel.isEnabled`. Load the original via `idpDelegate.getById` so `getLoginPredicate` evaluates the raw flag.

Private org brokers excluded from login predicate breaking cache invalidation — Private org brokers never pass `getLoginPredicate` due to the `BROKER_PUBLIC` check, so `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` skips invalidation and `IdentityProviderListQuery` stays stale with missing options. Make the predicate context-dependent or explicitly invalidate `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` entries for that `organizationId`.

NPE in getLoginPredicate when IdentityProvider config is null — `getLoginPredicate` throws `NullPointerException` when `getConfig` is null during `create`/`remove`/`update`. Guard with `getConfig() != null` before reading `BROKER_PUBLIC` as shown.

Missing null guard causes NPE on update/remove of non-existent IdP — A missing IdP makes `update` and `remove` throw `NullPointerException` instead of handling it gracefully. Guard the results of `getById` and `getByAlias` before calling `registerIDPInvalidation` and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`.

Race on getForLogin cache update drops other organization entries — Concurrent `getForLogin` misses for different orgs can overwrite each other and drop entries from `IdentityProviderListQuery`. Serialize the read-modify-write on `cacheKey` or use a per-organization key as shown.

testCacheIDPForLogin lacks negative checks for login predicate filtering — The test can pass even if `getLoginPredicate` is broken because it only checks counts. Add explicit absence checks for disabled, hidden, and non-`BROKER_PUBLIC` aliases in each `FetchMode` result.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: None error_ids from null response crashes fetch_error_details — Passing `None` to `fetch_error_details` crashes on iteration and fails the request. Normalize `error_ids` with `or []` at extraction and inside `fetch_error_details` to handle null arrays.

Visualize contract change breaks yAxes and fromJSON consumers — Callers in `exploreParams.tsx` still read `Visualize.yAxes` as an array and `visualizes.spec.tsx` expects a single `Visualize` from `fromJSON`, so they get undefined or type errors. Add a compatibility getter for `yAxes` returning `[this.yAxis]` or migrate all callers to `yAxis` and the new array return.

Feature-flag table visualization renders empty with hard-coded data — Enabling `use-table-widget-visualization` shows an empty table because `TableWidgetVisualization` receives hard-coded empty `columns` and `tableData`. Pass through `fields` and `result.data`/`result.meta` like `StyledSimpleTableChart` does.

Invalid browser report aborts entire batch with 422 instead of best-effort skip — A single malformed report now fails the whole batch with 422 and drops valid reports. Change `BrowserReportSerializer` handling to log and `continue` instead of returning an error to keep the endpoint best-effort.

Mutual-exclusion validation bypassed when age or timestamp is 0 — When `age` or `timestamp` is `0` the truthiness check passes and both fields are accepted, violating the Reporting API invariant. Check membership with `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` in `validate_age` and `validate_timestamp`.

fetch_error_details misassigns payloads via zip with events.values() — Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` misaligns payloads when order or length differs and corrupts the returned errors. Look up each `node_id` via `events.get(node_id)` while iterating `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` instead.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: SpanFlusher yields 0 or -1 workers with empty shards or negative max_processes — An empty `buffer.assigned_shards` or negative `max_processes` leaves `num_processes` at `0` or `-1`, so no flushers run and spans stall silently. Validate `max_processes` and fall back to `1` when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty instead of using `or`.

Thread flusher restart leaks old thread causing duplicate flush — The old thread keeps running alongside the new one, causing duplicate flushes and races on shared `Values`. Stop and `join()` the existing thread before overwriting `self.processes`, handling both `Thread` and `Process` paths.

O(N) Redis round-trips per submit due to per-shard buffer fan-out — Each `submit()` fans out to every shard buffer, adding `N` Redis round-trips on the hot path. Throttle metrics collection in `buffer.record_stored_segments()` or batch the calls to avoid the per-message amplification.

Joined shard list as metric tag creates unbounded cardinality — Every distinct shard combination creates a new metric series and can overwhelm the backend. Replace `shard_tag` with a low-cardinality tag such as `num_shards` or `process_index`.

Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard` in flusher timers — Queries on one name miss data emitted under the other, splitting the dashboards. Standardize `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` to use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` to match `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`.

Patched time.sleep no-ops flusher wait causing race in test_basic — The `time.sleep(0.1)` after `step.poll()` returns instantly when `time.sleep` is monkeypatched, so the assertion races. Wait on a condition or `threading.Event` and poll until `messages` arrive instead of sleeping.

test_flusher_processes_limit does not verify flushing with shared processes — `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks counts, so broken sharding or dead flush still passes. Submit spans for each shard in `step.submit()` and assert all are produced via `messages`.

CLI --flusher-processes default 1 disables shard-based autoscaling — Forcing `flusher_processes` to `1` prevents `SpanFlusher` from scaling to `buffer.assigned_shards` and keeps the deployment single-process. Use `default=None` for `--flusher-processes` so the `max_processes` fallback in `flusher.py` applies.

join() breaks loop on deadline expiry without terminating remaining processes — Processes after the deadline never reach `terminate()` and leak as daemon children. Remove the `remaining_time` early `break` in `join()` and always terminate each process after its wait.

Truthiness check treats max_processes=0 as missing — Using `or` conflates `0` with `None`, so an explicit `0` incorrectly falls back to sharding. Check `max_processes is not None` in `self.max_processes` before using `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: sync_status_outbound assignment_source breaks subclasses without **kwargs — Add `assignment_source` with `**kwargs` to `sync_status_outbound` in `ExampleIntegration` and `vsts` like `jira` does.

test_to_dict assertion too loose to detect stale or string queued — `test_to_dict` passes even when `queued` is a stale import-time `datetime` or ISO string, hiding a broken `to_dict`/`from_dict` round-trip in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. Assert `queued` is a fresh timezone-aware `datetime` and that the round-trip restores it from both `datetime` and string forms.

to_dict/from_dict queued type mismatch after Celery JSON serialization — `from_dict` keeps `queued` as a string after Celery JSON serialization, so `AssignmentSource.queued` has the wrong type. Make `to_dict` emit an ISO string and `from_dict` parse strings back to `datetime`.

AssignmentSource.queued shares single import-time timestamp — Every `AssignmentSource` without an explicit `queued` reuses the import-time `datetime`, breaking per-event ordering. Use `field` with `default_factory=timezone.now` for `queued` instead of calling `timezone.now()` at definition.

sync_status_outbound task not forwarding assignment_source for cycle checks — `sync_status_outbound` implementations never receive `assignment_source` because the task still drops it, disabling cycle checks. Update the task to accept `assignment_source_dict` and forward `AssignmentSource.from_dict` to `sync_status_outbound` like `sync_assignee_outbound` does.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:382-394`

Deterministic OAuth state enables GitHub CSRF bypass — An attacker can predict `pipeline.signature` and forge a callback that passes the `state` check. Generate a per-request random value with `secrets.token_urlsafe`, store it via `pipeline.bind_state`, and validate it with `constant_time_compare`.

New GitHub install skips authenticated user validation — Anyone who obtains an `installation_id` can claim a fresh install without proving they installed the app. Require `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` before `pipeline.next_step()` in the `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch.

Empty installation_id string bypasses installation verification — A request with `?installation_id=` passes as `""` and advances through the `Integration.DoesNotExist` path without verification. Change the `installation_id is None` check to `not installation_id` to reject empty strings.

GitHub OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri required by authorize step — GitHub rejects the token exchange when `redirect_uri` was sent on authorize but missing from `data`, so valid installs fail. Include the same `absolute_uri(reverse("sentry-extension-setup"))` value as `redirect_uri` in `data`.

Non-constant-time OAuth state comparison enables timing attack — The `!=` check on `pipeline.signature` leaks timing information that can be used to guess `state`. Replace it with `hmac.compare_digest` or `constant_time_compare` after coercing both sides to strings.

test_installation_not_found uses invalid OAuth state bypassing Integration lookup — The second request uses a mismatched `state` so the test never reaches the `Integration` lookup and passes for the wrong reason. Use the pipeline's valid `state` for the request and assert the error comes from the missing `Integration`, or split into separate tests for `state` mismatch and missing install.

Unhandled exceptions in GitHub OAuth token exchange and user-info fetch — Failures in `safe_urlopen` or `get_user_info` escape as 500s instead of returning the install error. Wrap the token exchange and the `get_user_info` call in try/except and return `error` on exception.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434-436`

Unchecked sender login lookup raises KeyError instead of error response — A missing `sender` in `integration.metadata` raises `KeyError` as a 500 instead of the expected install error. Read `login` via `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value as invalid.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler missing required StatefulDetectorHandler methods — Instantiation will fail with `TypeError` for `metric_alert_fire` detectors because `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` remains abstract. Implement required `StatefulDetectorHandler` members such as `build_occurrence_and_event_data` or keep it as `DetectorHandler` until ready.

event_data passed to Kafka producer without JSON-serializability check — Failures only surface during serialization inside `produce_occurrence_to_kafka`, making non-serializable values hard to debug. Normalize `event_data` returned by `build_occurrence_and_event_data` to JSON-safe types before queuing.

TestEvaluate expects hardcoded HIGH/6 occurrence ignoring actual packet value — Expectations always use `6`/`HIGH` so `evaluate` could ignore the packet's real `group_vals` and priority and still pass. Derive expected occurrences in `TestEvaluate` from the `DataPacket` values instead of the hardcoded helper.

**Also found in:**
- `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:175-195`

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: IndexError when previous_checkins is empty for threshold > 1 — Accessing `previous_checkins[0]` on an empty result raises `IndexError` and aborts incident creation. Guard `previous_checkins` before assigning `starting_checkin` or fall back to `failed_checkin`.

Monitor environment context returns original config ignoring display transform — The transformed `schedule_type` is dead code so consumers receive the raw integer and evidence display breaks. Return the local `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config`.
